articleTitle: Youngest Woman Grandmaster’: 11-year-old British-Indian chess prodigy Bodhana Sivanandan gets Guinness record
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bodhana Sivanandan Guinness World Record
description: The 11-year-old from London achieved the feat at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, last week.
body_raw: British-Indian chess player Bodhana Sivanandan has added another record to her growing list of achievements after Guinness World Records recognised her as the youngest female chess player to earn the Woman Grandmaster WGM title. The 11-year-old from London achieved the feat at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, last week. Her latest recognition takes her tally to three Guinness World Records titles, adding to two records she set when she was 10. Those earlier records were for being the youngest chess Woman International Master and the youngest female player to defeat a grandmaster in a chess tournament. Guinness World Records said Bodhanas latest achievement came after its 2027 edition had already gone to print, so it could not be included in this years book. Her two previous records, however, feature in the new edition. Bodhana has already received certificates for the two earlier records, while the certificate for her latest achievement is yet to arrive. The announcement also drew praise online, with several users celebrating the youngsters achievement and acknowledging the role played by her family and coaches. Eleven years old and a title. Chess teaches what every kid needs slow down, look at the whole board, check your move before you play it. Congratulations to her and her family, one user commented. Check the post 11-year-old UK chess prodigy Bodhana Sivanandan has achieved the GWR title for youngest chess player to achieve the Woman Grandmaster WGM title following her history-making performance at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand pic.twitter.comuZ11U946Qk - Guinness World Records GWR October 2, 2026 What an incredible achievement at such a young age. Credit also to her trainers and, of course, her parents for the guidance and support behind the scenes, another wrote. Bodhana, who holds the Woman FIDE Master title, has family roots in Trichy, Tamil Nadu. Her father, Sivanandan Velayutham, works in the IT sector and moved to London with his family in 2007. Bodhana was born and raised in London, where she has emerged as one of the most prominent young names in British chess. Her talent had already brought her to 10 Downing Street in August 2023, when she was invited by then-British Prime Minister Rishi Sunak as he prepared to announce a financial package for chess in the UK. Interestingly, chess was never something her family had planned for her. Bodhana started playing chess when she was just five years old. We had no plans to make her play chess. She just stumbled across a chessboard at home and started to play, her father told The Indian Express last year. While chess has become a major part of her life, Bodhanas routine is not limited to the game. Her parents have also placed considerable importance on her education, and she took up both piano and violin a couple of years ago. For now, though, chess remains her favourite. I like chess more than playing the piano and violin because theres no grading in piano, and in chess you can keep improving, she said.

articleTitle: University student found injured, stripped in Ahmedabad, dies in hospital
articleFeaturedImageAlt: DCP Bhagirath T Gadhvi, Zone-6, Ahmedabad City Police
description: According to the FIR, Solanki was a third semester student of the B.Voc. (Finance) course at Silver Oak University, Gota.
body_raw: A 21-YEAR-OLD university student was found critically injured and without clothing on the premises of a society in the Isanpur area of Ahmedabad on Friday night. The youth was dressed by locals and taken to a nearby hospital, but died during treatment. The police on Saturday identified the deceased as Jigar Sailesh Solanki, originally from Bhavnagar. Police have filed a murder case and launched a probe to trace the unidentified assailants. A statement issued by Zone-6 DCP Bhagirath T Gadhvi said, An FIR has been registered regarding the death of 21-year-old Jigar Sailesh Solanki, who was beaten and sustained fatal injuries to various parts of his body inflicted by an unknown person. The incident occurred on the night of October 2, 2026, between 915 and 1030 pm, within the compound of Tirthbhumi Apartments. According to the FIR, Solanki was a third semester student of the B.Voc. Finance course at Silver Oak University, Gota. He had been living in a PG accommodation earlier but around two-and-a-half months ago, he and his paternal cousin had moved into his maternal uncles home in Isanpur. On the night of the incident, he had left home on his motorcycle to meet a friend. Later, he was found in a critically injured condition at Tirthbhumi Apartments. Signs of physical assault were observed on his body, including several injuries. He was transported to LG Hospital for treatment via the 108 emergency service, where the attending doctor declared him dead during treatment, the police statement said. In a video statement, DCP Gadhvi said Solanki had been conscious at the time he was found by some residents of the society. He managed to give them his name and contact information of his family members, with which the residents managed to inform his family. However, they could not glean any information as to who attacked him. DCP Gadhvi told mediapersons, We sent his body for panel postmortem and according to the inquest panchnama, most of the injuries are on his Solanki back and thighs, where he appears to have been repeatedly struck with a stick, but we are waiting for the autopsy report as there may be internal injuries that may not have come to the attention of police personnel on the scene. The police managed to find the clothes of the deceased near the scene of crime and a forensics team as well as the dog squad were called in to help investigate the same. The Crime Branch is also aiding in the investigation, said the senior officer. On the basis of Solankis statement, an FIR was registered at the Isanpur police station against unidentified persons under Section 1031 of the BNS. DCP Gadhvi said, We are investigating through technical means as well as human sources regarding who could be responsible. We have not yet found any particular reason or motive.

articleTitle: Government approves 5 Centres of Excellence to support Classical languages
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The Centres will focus on four broad areas - providing dedicated institutional platforms for advanced research, scholarly work and academic engagement; preservation and digitisation; wider dissemination of Classical Language heritage; and strengthening regional academic ecosystems.
description: “The establishment of these five Centres marks a significant step towards strengthening the institutional ecosystem for the study, research and preservation of India’s Classical Languages,” the Ministry said in a statement
body_raw: The Ministry of Education Saturday approved the establishment of five Centres of Excellence CoEs for studies in five Classical languages, namely Assamese, Bengali, Marathi, Pali and Prakrit. The establishment of these five Centres marks a significant step towards strengthening the institutional ecosystem for the study, research and preservation of Indias Classical Languages, the Ministry said in a statement The Centres will focus on four broad areas - providing dedicated institutional platforms for advanced research, scholarly work and academic engagement preservation and digitisation wider dissemination of Classical Language heritage and strengthening regional academic ecosystems. The Centre of Excellence for classical Assamese will be established at Tezpur University, Assam for classical Bengali at Visva-Bharati University, West Bengal for classical Marathi at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, Pune, Maharashtra for classical Pali at Central University of Odisha, Odisha and for classical Prakrit at Central University of Gujarat, Gujarat. The initiative reinforces the governments efforts to preserve and promote Indias rich linguistic and literary heritage while strengthening institutions of higher education as centres of research and scholarship, the Ministrys statement further read.

articleTitle: FIR filed over alleged illegal deletion of 778 voters in Bengaluru’s Malleswaram
articleFeaturedImageAlt: sir, blo
description: The police have named G S Vasanthalakshmi, a BJP member, as accused No. 1, who was allegedly associated with the preparation or submission of the disputed applications.
body_raw: Amidst the ongoing Special Intensive Revision SIR of the electoral rolls in Karnataka, the Bengaluru police have registered a case alleging irregularities in voter records in the Malleswaram Assembly constituency. According to the First Information Report FIR, the complaint pertains to Polling Station No. 157 and alleges that Form 7 applications were submitted seeking deletion of the names of 778 voters from the electoral rolls. The police registered the case based on a complaint by Anoop Iyengar, a Congressman, who alleged that even though the voters had cast their votes, applications in Form 7 were submitted showing them as persons who had shifted residence or were otherwise ineligible, with the intention of having their names deleted from the electoral roll. The 778 entries were spread across eight polling parts, with 122 applications pertaining to Part 64, 233 to Part 155, 28 to Part 156, five to Part 158, 47 to Part 154, 171 to Part 205, 68 to Part 203 and 104 to Part 153, according to the complaint. The complaint further alleges that the applications were part of an attempt to interfere with the electoral rolls and disenfranchise eligible voters. It also alleges the involvement of a group of people associated with political activity in the preparation or submission of the applications. G S Vasanthalakshmi, a BJP member, has been named accused No. 1 in the FIR. Another person allegedly associated with an RSS wing has been listed as an unidentified accused. The FIR alleges that Vasanthalakshmi was associated with the preparation or submission of the disputed applications. However, the allegations are yet to be established. The complaint also raises questions about the addresses mentioned in the applications, alleging that some corresponded to multiple residences or premises. We have registered a case and are investigating, a police officer said.

articleTitle: As the Asian Games close, with a last-minute gold rush, India finish fourth
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India added five medals on 3rd October at Asian Games to finish the campaign with 21 gold. (Reuters/AP)
description: For 12 days, India had managed only 10 gold medals. Then, with the Asian Games running out of hours, the medals began to pile up. Six golds on Friday. Five more on Saturday.
body_raw: The last gold India won was also the easiest. So easy that, for the final penalty corner, the Indian hockey team had just two players standing on top of Malaysias D. And even then, Harmanpreet Singh swept into the net. No elaborate variation, no crowding of the circle. Just two players, one set piece and a gold medal that was never really in doubt. The 5-1 win was an unfussy ending to an extraordinarily complicated fortnight. For 12 days, India had managed only 10 gold medals. Then, with the Asian Games running out of hours, the medals began to pile up. Six golds on Friday. Five more on Saturday. India finished with 21 golds, 27 silvers and 37 bronzes - 85 medals in all - and, perhaps most significantly, pipped Uzbekistan to retain the fourth place it had earned in the last edition. The only rider is an unlikely gold for Uzbekistan in equestrian on Sunday. However, India finished 22 medals short overall compared to the 2023 campaign. Both India and Uzbekistan finished with 21 golds, but Indias two extra silvers made the difference. Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage The final ranking, though, barely captures the suddenness of the turnaround. On Saturday morning, recurve archer Kumkum Mohod was shooting arrows in a contest that felt like a metaphor for Indias Games. The 17-year-old had spent the week helping end South Koreas long reign in the womens recurve team event. Now, in the individual final, she found herself twice behind Oh Yejin. Twice she dragged herself level. With the title coming down to the final arrows, Oh shot an eight. Kumkum shot a 10. Gold. A few hours later, golfer Pranavi Urs nearly threw away a three-stroke advantage with a triple bogey on the third hole. The sort of mistake that can unravel a final round. Instead, she responded with birdies on the sixth, 10th and 13th, then held on to win Indias first womens individual Asian Games golf gold. I think I purely did it for my parents, Urs said, as her mother and father watched her stave off the pressure. Theyre here this week and it was always my mums dream to have me represent the country and win, and then the national anthem and stuff. That was her Bollywood style, typical Bollywood mum. She wanted all that. Paris Olympics bronze medallist Aman Sehrawats gold was harder still. He led North Koreas Han Chong-Song 6-1 in the 57 kg wrestling final, only for the world champion to claw his way back and move 7-6 ahead. Aman, who kept the Asian Games gold as his phone wallpaper, had spent much of the bout defending his left leg. Now, he had a match to rescue. He scored four unanswered points in the second period and walked away an Asian Games champion. Different sports. Different circumstances. The same late refusal to let a Games that had been drifting away end quietly. Cricket added its own drama. Abhishek Sharmas 61 and Tilak Varmas unbeaten 51 took India to 211 against Pakistan in the mens final. Pakistan got close but fell 19 runs short. It was Indias second straight mens Asian Games cricket gold, completing the gold-medal double after the womens team had won earlier. And then there was hockey, where the symbolism was impossible to miss. A year that had contained plenty of turbulence - on and off the field - had left the men needing to find a way back into the Olympic cycle. They nearly stumbled against Pakistan in the semifinal, surviving only through a late winner. Against Malaysia, there was no such drama. India won 5-1, defended its Asian Games title and secured direct qualification for Los Angeles 2028. The 21st gold therefore belonged to the sport that has long carried the weight of Indian expectations. But the 20 before it tell a more interesting story. This was not a Games rescued by one sport, one athlete or one golden generation. It was a late avalanche, after athletics, badminton and shooting underachieved compared to the previous edition. Archers who toppled a dynasty, a golfer who survived her own collapse, a wrestler who recovered from one, cricketers who handled Pakistan, hockey players who finished the job. Thats a big relief for us because how the World Cup went, it was really hard mentally and physically, hockey team vice-captain Hardik Singh said. We stood up at the Asian Games, and we fought in every match. It shows our character, and thats how we are. We want to start strong and finish stronger. For nearly two weeks, India had looked like a contingent waiting for its Games to begin. Then, suddenly, it did. Ten golds became 21 in 48 hours. And fourth place, which had seemed to be slipping away, was Indias again.

articleTitle: Flydubai FZ1073: Who were mystery pilots who saved the plane after Smit Machchhar was attacked?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Flydubai hijack, flydubai stabbing, Smit Machchhar
description: Two Flydubai pilots were travelling as passengers to operate the aircraft's return journey when the cockpit attack sent FZ1073 into a steep descent; they rushed in and helped stabilise the plane.
body_raw: Three days after flydubai flight FZ1073 plunged thousands of feet during an attack on Indian Captain Smit Machchhar, questions are now turning to two pilots who were travelling as passengers and stepped into the cockpit to help stabilise the aircraft. The two men have not been publicly identified. Flydubai has described them only as on-duty crew members travelling on the plane. Their intervention came after Smit Machchhar, despite being badly wounded, managed to unlock the cockpit door, allowing passengers to enter and subdue the co-pilot. The two pilots then took control of the aircraft and helped guide it to an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. Who were the two pilots who took control of FZ1073? According to an account given to news agency Associated Press by passenger Daniel Schlichter, the two pilots were travelling on the flight because they were supposed to operate the aircraft on its return journey from Tel Aviv to Dubai. The practice is known in aviation as deadheading, when pilots travel as passengers to reposition themselves for a subsequent assignment. The co-pilot accused of attacking a Flydubai captain has reportedly been identified as Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani national previously barred from flying over alleged extremist views. pic.twitter.comOd9nNpQ6jI - Al Jazeera English AJEnglish October 3, 2026 This is one of the miracles, Schlichter, who was seated in the second row, told AP. That not in every flight they bring two extra pilots. In this case, they brought them because they should have brought the plane back from Tel Aviv to Dubai, and this is the only reason they were there. The presence of the two pilots was crucial because both the operating captain and co-pilot were involved in the cockpit incident. The Indian Express, citing agencies, had earlier reported that four pilots were aboard the flight, the two operating pilots and the two pilots travelling as passengers, and explained how the routine practice of deadheading helped in the emergency. How did the two pilots get into the cockpit? The pilots stepped in after passengers realised something was seriously wrong. Schlichter told AP that passengers heard screaming and learned that the co-pilot was repeatedly attacking Machchhar. The captain, despite his injuries, managed to unlock the cockpit door. A passenger then grabbed the co-pilot and pulled him from the cockpit, while others helped restrain him. One of the two travelling pilots immediately moved through the group and reached the controls. He was actually kind of jumping above the guys that were handling the terrorist, and he reached out to the pilot area and started to take over, Schlichter said. And then the other guy, the other pilot, joined in and they closed the door because they didnt want anybody else to be there. The two pilots then worked to stabilise the aircraft. Flydubai has previously said that crew members travelling on the aircraft helped stabilise the plane and land it safely, but the airline has not publicly identified the two pilots. The National reported that the airline declined to comment on the deadheading crew aboard FZ1073. They had to stabilise a plane that had plunged thousands of feet The aircraft had undergone an extreme descent after the attack in the cockpit. It took the two pilots quite a lot of minutes, maybe 10 or more, to stabilise the aircraft. The descent was so severe that part of the planes rudder was torn away. The pilots made a mayday call while looking for a suitable place to land. Reuters has reported that the aircraft had been cruising at around 34,000 feet before plunging more than 16,000 feet in just over 30 seconds. The UAE has said the co-pilot attacked Machchhar with the cockpits crash axe and attempted to take control of the aircraft. The two additional pilots eventually stabilised the aircraft and helped prepare it for an emergency landing at Tabuk in Saudi Arabia. Passengers initially feared the two pilots could be hijackers Even after the two men had taken control of the aircraft, some passengers did not immediately know who they were. Schlichter said the pilots did not communicate with passengers after entering the cockpit and closing the door. After they managed to stabilize the airplane, actually they did not have any communication with us, and I have to tell you, I was worried about this, he said. Schlichter said he began worrying that the men could themselves be taking control of the aircraft for another purpose. He feared they might be hijacking the plane into maybe Iran, or I dont know where, because were actually not too far. The concern lasted around 45 minutes, according to Schlichter. The pilots eventually announced that they would land in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, and told passengers that everything would be OK. At that point, Schlichter said, he decided to trust them. And it turned out to be true. Why were the two pilots on the flight? The National reported that deadheading, formally referred to in the international aviation framework as positioning crew, is a normal practice in airline operations. Pilots can travel in uniform as passengers when an airline needs to move them to another location for a subsequent assignment. In this case, Schlichter said, the two pilots were on FZ1073 because they were expected to operate the aircraft on its return journey from Tel Aviv to Dubai. Why havent the pilots been identified? AP reported that it was not clear why Flydubai had not identified them. Schlichter described the first pilot to reach the controls as a hero. He acted really like a hero, taking over the plane and reacted like he understood exactly what is going on, and I think we owe him our lives not less than the other heroes that went on the flight, he said. With inputs from agencies

articleTitle: India can be called a developed economy if development is inclusive: V-P C P Radhakrishnan
articleFeaturedImageAlt: VICE-PRESIDENT C P Radhakrishnan, consensus and inclusivity, C P Radhakrishnan, india developed economy, Indian economy, Indian economy growth, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Speaking at the inauguration of Kautilya Economic Conclave, 2026, Radhakrishnan said India was moving towards becoming a developed economy and that development should reach every section of society.
body_raw: VICE-PRESIDENT C P Radhakrishnan on Saturday underlined the importance of consensus and inclusivity, saying India could call itself a developed economy only if its development was inclusive. Speaking at the inauguration of Kautilya Economic Conclave, 2026, Radhakrishnan said India was moving towards becoming a developed economy and that development should reach every section of society. We can call ourselves a developed economy if it is an inclusive development of everyone, he said. He emphasised the importance of policymakers understanding the ground realities of both micro and macroeconomic situations, saying China had understood the same. If we understand the ground realities of the village, we can know what we should do for the development of that village. When you want to make macroeconomic policies, then you have to understand the ground realities of the globe. That is where the success story of the Chinese is well-established. They understand the ground realities of both, and they have brought their nation to be the second largest economy of the world.Policymakers should always understand the ground realities. Speaking of the challenges being faced by economies today, he said consensus was important. In these times of flux, we need decisiveness embedded in consensus. We have to debate, we have to discuss and we have to come to a conclusion that is acceptable to everyone. Referring to the reforms undertaken by the Narendra Modi government over the past decade, including Jan Dhan accounts, direct benefit transfer and Goods and Services Tax, he highlighted financial inclusion. History proves the process of consensus-building helps reforms go forward.The process may sometimes be gradual and sometimes we may lose our patience also, but we should never show it outside. Indias experience of the last decade shows how inclusiveness is important. Inclusion can itself become an instrument of resilience, he said.

articleTitle: It rained the day after he died. For a farmer family in Yavatmal, it was too late, again
articleFeaturedImageAlt: farmer distress, Yavatmal farmer distress, farmer distress in Yavatmal, Yavatmal, Pimplapur village, farmer suicides, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Nima Malekar has now lost both her children and her husband to suicides, reportedly caused by farm distress and the wait for a borewell electricity connection
body_raw: The Tulsi plant outside her house in the brown and dry Pimplapur village in Yavatmals Ralegaon is unusually green. Nima Dnyaneshwar Malekar has barely noticed. In five years, the 58-year-old cant remember a time when she was not in mourning. First it was for her elder son Nikhil, 28, who died of suspected suicide in March 2021. Younger by three years, Tapaveen, her only other child, followed his brother in October 2024. On July 22 this year, Nimas husband Dnyaneshwar, 65, took his own life. Her voice breaking, Nima says she had no idea what was going on in their minds. We worked so hard. My children worked, their father toiled. But what was the use? There is nothing left. Nimas nephew Harish Choudhary says reasons for all three deaths, by hanging, were the same-recurring crop losses, inadequate rainfall and difficulties in securing an electricity connection to operate a borewell. The Malekars are not alone in this, as large parts of Maharashtra, including Yavatmal, again stare at drought. Last week, the state declared drought in 265 of its 358 tehsils-or about three-fourths of Maharashtra. As per official figures, between January and June this year, even before this years drought cycle actually hit, Yavatmal had witnessed 128 farmer suicides. Nima and Dnyaneshwar had built their house only this year after getting funds under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana. Left all alone in it now, Nima spends half her time at her brothers home in Kosala village, as neighbours and family help look after her land. She is just carrying on, she says. I will live for as long as God chooses to keep me. The day He takes me, I will go. I am going mad Sarpanch Ravindra Choudhary, who is related to the family, says Nikhil, who worked on the familys five-acre land, where they grow cotton, had been trying for long to get his application approved for an electricity connection to draw water from their borewell. He would say, I am going mad. I dont understand how the crop will grow, Nima recalls. Then, in 2021, excess rain washed away their crops. When Nikhil was found hanging from a tree, it was just a month to go for his marriage. Villagers cut down the tree later. Tapaveen was meant to take a different course, having finished BA and enrolled for post-graduation. But, after Nikhils death, he started helping on the land too, studying on the side and preparing for competitive examinations. But then came 2024. It was a particularly bad year, the family recalls, and their crop failed in the absence of rains. He too started saying, What should I do? My mind is not working, Nima says. One day while she and her husband were away in the field, Tapaveen hanged himself from a rope at their home. This year, they sowed three times, Nima says, putting in the seed, spending money on fertilizers. But there was no rain for nearly two months after that. The crop dried up. Her husband did not share his despair, Nima says, recalling how she slept before him that night. Sometime in the early hours, Dnyaneshwar went to the adjacent room and hanged himself. Nima discovered the body at about 5 am. Grampanchayat Adhikari of the village R R Dhage says farmers here are at the mercy of the weather. During the elder sons time, there was excess rain. During the younger sons, there was a drought. Its still the same. A familys pride Dnyaneshwar worked as a farm labourer on other peoples land for years before saving enough to buy the five acres he owned in 2018. It was all fallow land, Harish says. Dnyaneshwar made it cultivable almost single-handedly. For a few years, the family thought their troubles were behind them. But the battles with the rain-and to get electricity-just dragged on. The family says it first applied for an electricity connection in 2021, when the government came out with a scheme. The sarpanch says around 40 farmers in the village benefited, but not Dnyaneshwar. The Malekars tried again when the government came up with a solar-powered system in 2023. While Nima has written to the Tehsildar again now, Harish says solar is hardly the answer. Pointing out that the Malekar borewell is deep and requires a high-capacity pump to draw water, he says How can we run the pump on it? Solar starts dipping by around 4 pm when the sun starts going down. It does not work at night. The family also says that, without any subsidy from the government, the cost of installing a solar system is beyond their means. Sarpanch Ravindra admits only three people in the village have gone for solar. Promises and grants After all three deaths, Nima was visited by representatives from political parties. The BJP, the Congress, the Shiv Sena all came, says the sarpanch. But nothing was done. Recently, Nima was issued a certificate under the Niradhar Scheme and told she would receive Rs 1,500 a month. The payment is yet to start, family members say. A cheque of Rs 20,000 was also given by the tehsildar under the Rashtriya Kutumb Labh Yojana. Ralegaon Tehsildar Amit Bhoite says The scheme offers immediate financial support to bereaved BPL families who have lost their main bread winners. We have also sanctioned over Rs 1 lakh for her husband, under the aid for families in case of farmer suicides. The amount of Rs 1,500 has been sanctioned under the Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Yojana. Bhoite adds that he is trying to rope in some NGOs to provide additional financial assistance to Nima. The only significant aid they ever received, the family says, was Rs 1 lakh after Nikhils death. It all went into paying their debts, Harish says. Nima still goes to the farm when she can, he adds. She just goes and sits. Her eyes looking into the distance, her face blank, Nima says The day after he Dnyaneshwar died, it rained. But, since then again, there has been no water.

articleTitle: From kadhi-chawal cart to Mercedes: How a Haryana man sold a Dubai dream
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Dubai
description: Rajesh, who owns of a luxurious farmhouse and drives a Mercedes, operated via a network for duping several people across Haryana: police
body_raw: The food cart that once sustained Rajesh Kumar now lies in a corner of his plush farmhouse, while his Mercedes has been seized. The cart once meant a kadhi and cholle chawal rehri that Rajesh operated till 2019 before his and several others lives changed. Rajesh, aka Nana, entered into an investment network for allegedly duping several people across Haryana. Among those who invested across the state also include well-educated professionals, police said, with complaints lodged coming from Yamunanagar, Kaithal, Karnal, Ambala, and Kurukshetra. The seized Mercedes is in relation to the alleged fraud, which now the police estimates at around Rs 8 crore or above. From inflated digital profits to promises of Dubai flats and plots, the racket allegedly operated through a chain of local fraudsters, with the money trail now being examined by the cybercrime police in Panchkula. The four accused arrested so far are Rajesh and Udham Singh from Karnal, Sushil Kumar from Yamunanagar, and Sanjeev Kumar of Ladwa in Kurukshetra. Recoveries include Audi Q3 Q5, BMW Besides Rajeshs Mercedes, an Audi Q5, Audi Q3 and BMW linked to Sanjeev Kumar and other accused have been seized so far by the police. To recover the proceeds of crime, police have moved court seeking permission to auction these vehicles. At least six electronic devices including Apple MacBooks and iPhones and other mobile phones have been seized, which are now being examined by forensic experts for further collection of evidence. The alleged fraud surfaced when Ashok Kumar, a Panchkula-based government contractor, lodged a formal complaint against Rajesh. I initially did not believe Rajesh and his associates, but they organised an official gathering and said the companys MD and CMD would be coming to the hotel. I also saw Sushil, who introduced me to this fraud racket who initially used to come on a bike, later arriving in an Audi. I started thinking that there must really be profit in this business, Ashok told The Indian Express. I first invested Rs 8,500, and they returned the money to me. Then, in 2021, I took a loan and invested Rs 3.5 lakh. Subsequently, my brothers and other relatives also started investing in the scheme. This way they duped me of 60 lakh. Ashok alleged that more than 20-25 people whom he had brought into the network were eventually unable to withdraw their money despite repeated assurances of profits and repayment. The overall loss suffered by my contacts must be more than around Rs 7-8 crore, he claimed. An FIR lodged in July on Ashoks complaint led to their arrest. Now after two months, the investigation subsequently has widened, with police identifying suspected links to operators based in Dubai who were controlling the entire investment racket. Investors promised of flats in Dubai Among the other individuals who got arrested, Sushil, ran a security agency before 2019. He was arrested from the Delhi airport two weeks ago when he was about to board a flight to Thailand. Udham Singh and Sanjeev, arrested earlier, were unemployed and depended on farming done by family. Investors were shown growing balances on mobile applications and were allegedly led to believe that their money was multiplying rapidly. Through fake mobile apps, the figures displayed on these platforms were manipulated to sustain the illusion of profits and attract more investors. They would rather give their own example, Inspector Yudhveer Singh, SHO, Cyber Crime Police Station, Panchkula, told The Indian Express. In one instance being examined by police, an investment of around Rs 30 lakh was allegedly shown as having grown to Rs 68 lakh in about six months. Ashok alleged that whenever he sought withdrawal of his money, he was told that it had been further invested in cryptocurrency and other schemes. According to the police officials, investors were repeatedly told that Dubai flats had been booked for them, while the applications showed inflated returns. The accused subsequently introduced crypto-related schemes and persuaded investors to shift their money from one platform to another on assurances of higher returns. The police investigation centres on platforms and schemes allegedly operating under names including Bloom Drive, LPNT Cryptocurrency, MSVP Meta Soil Verse Plan, SOIL VERSE and Mechai FX. Police officers The Indian Express spoke to said that Rajesh has emerged as a key figure in the investigation. His friend Pramod Kamboj, who frequently visited him, allegedly introduced him to an online portal, Bloom Company. Rajesh initially invested Rs 7,500 and later around Rs 2 lakh in another platform after Bloom shut down. From there, he took off. He started bringing other people into such money-multiplying schemes, officials said. He attended seminars in Chandigarh, Mohali and elsewhere where people projecting themselves as promoters of such investment schemes explained the investment plans and encouraged investments through meetings and online platforms. Police claimed that Rajesh allegedly received a massive share for bringing in several investors and was later even elevated to the position of Senior Project Head. Rajesh claimed that he was gifted a Mercedes C-class and earned Rs. 2 crore in a short span, a police officer said. A luxury farmhouse and other assets linked to him are being examined as part of the proceeds of crime trail, the officer added. Several accused in Dubai too The investigation has also brought the alleged Dubai connection into focus. Police are seeking the arrest of other suspects including Ravinder Bangar, Satish Mokhra, Devinder Bangar, Karamjeet, B S Randhawa and Happy Sheikh whom the police suspect might have fled abroad. A Look-Out Circular has been issued against Bangar and Sheikh who are believed to be in Dubai, Inspector Yudhveer Singh said. Panchkula Police Commissioner Pankaj Nain has cautioned people against transferring money through online investment, cryptocurrency or stock-trading schemes promising unusually high returns.

articleTitle: Smit Machchaar narrates flydubai horror: ‘Co-pilot was praying, then attacked from behind’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Flydubai Dubai-Tel Aviv Flight News Live Updates:
description: Indian Captain Smit Machcchar has revealed chilling details of what happened inside the cockpit during the attack while speaking to Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu.
body_raw: Four days after a Flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv was thrown into an emergency, the captain who was attacked in the cockpit has begun to explain how it started. Smit Machchhar, an Indian pilot with 17 years of flying experience, has told Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu that his co-pilot stood up, saying he wanted to pray, and that within minutes he was being hit from behind with an axe. Flight FZ1073 left Dubai for Tel Aviv on 30 September with 174 people on board, most of them Israelis. Midway through the flight, the Boeing 737 Max dropped sharply after the co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, attacked the captain. Passengers and other crew took back control of the cockpit, and the plane landed in Tabuk, in north-west Saudi Arabia. Authorities in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Israel are now investigating. VIDEO Jerusalem Israel PM Benjamin Netanyahu invites PM Modi and Indian pilot Smit Machchhar to light celebratory flame on Israels next independence day. Source Israel PMO X account Full video available on PTI Videos - - Press Trust of India PTINews October 4, 2026 Machchhar gave his account in a video call with Netanyahu on Saturday, 3 October. He has been moved from Saudi Arabia to the UAE, where he is recovering from his injuries. In an earlier call with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 2 October, he spoke about his will to get up and save the passengers. The call with Netanyahu centred on the minutes before the attack, the prayer, and how he got the cockpit door open. What happened when the co-pilot stood up to pray? Machchhar said the plane was flying normally when al-Hammami stood up and said he wanted to pray. He told Netanyahu he did not think this was unusual. The co-pilot went behind him to pray, as he understood it. After about four to five minutes, Machchhar felt a hard blow to the back of his head. The prayer, in the order of events he described, came just before the first strike. Why did the captain not look behind him? Out of respect for the co-pilots prayer, Machchhar chose not to turn round. He kept his eyes forward, as he would with any colleague at prayer. That meant he was not watching al-Hammami when the blow came. Machchhar did not say he knew at the time that the prayer was a cover for the attack. But the sequence he gave shows the co-pilot picked a moment when the captain was deliberately looking away. The first blow was so sudden that he did not understand it. He thought the aircraft itself had been hit. A second blow followed, and only then did he know the attack was coming from the person behind him. How did he open the cockpit door twice? Machchhar said the blows blurred his vision, and he could feel the plane going sharply down. Hurt and unable to see well, he reached the door and opened it. Al-Hammami shut it again, and Machchhar fell to the floor. I realised I had one more chance, he told Netanyahu. He said he thought he was going to die, so he put everything he had into one more push. When the door opened, he saw people waiting outside. They rushed in, overpowered al-Hammami and helped bring the cockpit back under control. VIDEO Jerusalem Israel PM Benjamin Netanyahu calls Indian FlyDubai pilot Smit Machchhar a hero of the entire world. Source Israel PMO X account Full video available on PTI Videos - - Press Trust of India PTINews October 4, 2026 Netanyahu asked about pulling the pin on the door. Machchhar said there is no pin. Inside the cockpit the door opens with a twist of a knob, while people outside need a code. His colleagues were trying the code, but al-Hammami was stopping the door from opening. The hard part was reaching the knob. Once his hand was on it, a short, quick twist was enough. What have Netanyahu and PM Modi said to him? Netanyahu has invited Machchhar and PM Modi to Israel for the countrys Independence Day, and called the pilot a hero of Israel, India and the world. He has also said the co-pilot went through Islamist radical indoctrination. The UAE is looking into the facts, the motive and whether the attack was planned or linked to terrorism. Meanwhile, in his call with PM Modi, from his hospital bed, Machchhar said he was lying on the cockpit floor when he knew that if he did not get up, the passengers could die. He said he was fighting for his own life, but would not let others die. He also said he recited the Hanuman Chalisa during the attack and that it gave him courage.

articleTitle: Gurugram groundwater extraction hits 213% of limit, ban proposed
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The submission called for restoration of identified water bodies, their catchments and feeder channels. (File Photo)
description: The proposals are part of a case that has been before the High Court for nearly two decades.
body_raw: Gurugram is extracting 43,263 hectare metres of groundwater a year against an extractable limit of 20,333 ha m-212.77 of the limit. In view of this, environmental activist and lead petitioner Sunil Singh has proposed before the Punjab and Haryana High Court a complete ban on groundwater extraction, a freeze on new construction without an assured surface water supply and judicial oversight for restoring water bodies. The proposals are part of a case that has been before the HC for nearly two decades. Singh had approached the court in 2008 against alleged rampant and unauthorised tubewell extraction by builders in developing sectors. The case has since involved the wider issue of groundwater depletion and restoration of water bodies in Gurugram. The latest proposals come ahead of an administrative review on October 5 - to be attended by members of the GMDA, HSVP and MCG as well as the petitioners, among others - after a division bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor described the groundwater situation in Gurugram as grim on October 1. After the court was told that groundwater had plunged to 40 to 50 m across Gurugram, it had noted that annual groundwater extraction in the district was twice the replenishable resource. We expect the authorities to examine the issues threadbare and to suggest appropriate measures as would ameliorate the worsening situation of ground water in Gurugram. It is to be kept in mind that the present generation is only a trustee for the futures to come and if we loose natural resources like groundwater in the manner like it is happening, the future generation would have to face disastrous consequences, the HC had said. In his submission, Singh has said, It is suggested that all groundwater extraction through borewells in Gurugram, whether registered, permitted or unregistered, should be prohibited. All existing borewells should be identified, geo-tagged and sealed in a time-bound manner, and all existing permissionsNOCs for groundwater abstraction should remain suspended during this period. No fresh borewell, renewal of permission or enhancement of the permitted quantity should be allowed. Singh also proposed that no fresh construction be permitted unless authorities demonstrate an assured and sustainable source of water other than groundwater. The submission called for restoration of identified water bodies, their catchments and feeder channels. Citing a GMDA survey that has found 826 of 1,216 water bodies to be retrievable, the affidavit highlighted that 305 existing public water bodies covering about 393 acres and more than 140 natural low-lying water-collection areas covering about 412 acres, which have substantial potential for restoration and groundwater recharge. To overcome administrative delays, Singh proposed that restoration of the water bodies identified in the GMDA inventory be carried out under the supervision of a former judge of the highest judiciary. Further, he proposed a Zero Discharge Maximum Reuse system. Maintaining that a 300 MLD irrigation network remains underutilised because of sewage treatment shortfalls, the affidavit suggested that no untreated sewage or industrial effluent should be permitted to enter stormwater drains, natural water bodies, open land or groundwater. At present, against a working demand of 770 MLD, GMDA supplies 670 MLD. The remaining 100 MLD is drawn through tubewells operated by the municipal corporation and private builders. The October 5 meeting will examine discontinuing groundwater extraction in areas where GMDA canal supply is available. The administration is to file a compliance affidavit before the HC on October 8.

articleTitle: Karnataka youth arrested over ‘links’ to Pakistan-based terror and arms networks
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka Police
description: The Karnataka Police and central agencies continue to track the ISI-backed Shahzad Bhatti network, which uses social media to recruit local working-class conduits across states.
body_raw: A 24-year-old college dropout from a remote village in northern Karnataka has become the latest individual arrested in connection with nationwide terrorism cases involving an online conspiracy linked to Pakistan-based operative Shahzad Bhatti. Vishal Kumar Mehtre was arrested at his home in Yenkur village in the Bhalki region of Bidar district Friday. He was produced before a special court for terrorism cases in Bengaluru Saturday and remanded to 14 days of judicial custody. The arrest followed an FIR registered on October 1 at the Khataka Chincholi police station under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act UAPA, 1967, for terror conspiracy, support, and membership of a banned terrorist group after local police received a tip-off about Mehtres online activities. Social media communications point to illegal arms network Police investigation revealed that Mehtre, who dropped out of a Bachelor of Business Administration course, allegedly used social media to communicate with members of the banned terrorist syndicate to procure illegal firearms and arrange arms smuggling. Investigators extracted Instagram and WhatsApp data from Mehtres mobile phone showing direct interactions with Shahzad Bhatti, a government-banned designated terrorist of Pakistani origin. According to the Bidar police, Mehtre communicated with Bhatti associates, including Rana Hunain and Nomi Khan, joined groups suggested by them, and was being linked to illegal arms dealers identified as Ashu Sharma and Raj Bhai alias Lucky Singh. During his court appearance, Mehtre confirmed he was arrested at his house. Despite being a Hindu, this college dropout got pulled into the Bhatti network, a police source said. Broader recruitment pattern across Karnataka Mehtres arrest fits into a broader trend observed across Karnataka in recent months, where several youths, primarily from working-class backgrounds, have been targeted for recruitment through social media by the Shahzad Bhatti network. Previous arrests include Mohammed Sahil, 24, a tea stall owner from Raichur, apprehended in August for plotting civil unrest and communicating with a foreign entity named Rana Bhai for gun trading. Other cases involve migrant workers from Uttar Pradesh, such as construction worker Suhel, 20, arrested in Davanagere after saving a Pakistani number labelled Rana Bhai and joining groups named MEMON and JUTTU-333 and RANABHAI-333. Earlier in June, the Tumkur police arrested Allahbhakash and Zamir Khan for allegedly contacting a Bhatti gang member to mobilise youths and target a Pune-based businessman and right-wing leader. Nationwide crackdown According to the Ministry of Home Affairs MHA, the Shahzad Bhatti network is an ISI-backed, Pakistan-based terror syndicate that pays local conduits to conduct reconnaissance on police, defence, and religious sites, as well as install CCTV cameras for espionage. In August, the MHA reported over 80 FIRs and more than 200 arrests connected to the network, with 253 detentions recorded across 14 states, including Uttar Pradesh 62, Haryana 52, Delhi 51, Punjab 44, and Karnataka 3. Union Home Minister Amit Shah confirmed that law enforcement disrupted the groups plans for subversive attacks, recovering IEDs, grenades with Pakistan Ordnance Factory markings, pistols, live ammunition, and CCTV equipment. Designated a terrorist organisation earlier this year for arms, drugs, and explosives smuggling, the network has also been linked to the emergence of Tehreek-e-Taliban Hindustan and past operational ties with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.

articleTitle: Missing since July, Premanand Maharaj’s teen disciple traced to another ashram
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Premanand Maharaj's response, urging honesty and compassion, resonated with many for its progressive approach to a sensitive topic
description: Boy’s family staged protest near spiritual guru’s Vrindavan ashram, alleging they were not allowed to see CCTV footage
body_raw: The family of a 17-year-old disciple of Vrindavan-based spiritual guru Premanand Maharaj had been running from pillar to post for nearly three months, seeking information about his whereabouts. On Friday, the family of Anuj Chaudhary, a Hathras district native who had been missing since July, staged a protest near the Shri Radha Keli Kunj Ashram in Vrindavan of Mathura district, alleging the ashram management had been misleading them for the past three months and withholding information about his whereabouts. They later withdrew the demonstration on the assurance of senior police officials. However, their search came to an end on Saturday evening after police said Anuj was traced to an ashram in the districts Barsana area, around 45 km from Vrindavan, where he was believed to have been staying. This came days after a 25-year-old disciple of Premanand Maharaj died after falling from the fourth floor of a building located near the Vrindavan ashram. Anuj, a Class 12 student, took initiation from spiritual leader Premanand Maharaj in July in the presence of his mother. He later returned to his home in Hathras. A few days later, he left home telling his family that he was going to the ashram. But he did not return, said Anujs uncle Nirbhay Chaudhary. The family claimed that they travelled to Vrindavan several times seeking information about Anuj but received no clear response and had filed a missing complaint in Hathras. A case of kidnapping was registered at the Sahibabad police station of Hathras on July 5 in connection with Anujs disappearance. We had been asking the ashram authorities to show us CCTV footage from the premises and from the apartment building where most of the disciples stay, but they did not agree to do so, Nirbhay said. Earlier in the day, police said a preliminary inquiry found that Anuj travelled to Vrindavan in July and took initiation from the spiritual leader. He subsequently returned to his home and later went missing, they said. Anuj is the only son of Rajveer Chaudhary, a farmer. Mathura Senior Superintendent of Police SSP Shlok Kumar said they coordinated with Hathras police to trace him. Circle Officer Sandeep Kumar Singh said during the search for Anuj, police circulated his photograph on social media. A person who recognised Anuj subsequently alerted the police, leading to his recovery, the official added. We will question him to find out where he had been staying since he went missing in July, Singh said. Hathras police have been informed about the recovery, he further said. Meanwhile, the family of a 25-year-old woman from Noida who has been missing since last month approached the Mathura police for help in tracing her. Her family suspects that she might be at the spiritual leaders ashram as she was a follower of Premanand Maharaj and had visited the city in the past. Mathura Circle Officer Sandeep Kumar Singh said the womans family told police that she was a follower of Premanand Maharaj and used to carry his photograph with her. Police claimed that they checked the visitors records of the ashram but did not find the womans name. Also, police are probing the death of 25-year-old Deepak Lodhi, alias Rasik Dulari Sharan, who died after falling from the fourth floor of a building at Guru Kripa Kunj apartment in Vrindavan on September 25. The apartment, where most of the disciples of Premanand Maharaj stay, is located near Shri Radha Keli Kunj Ashram. Police have so far ruled out any foul play, based on their preliminary inquiry and a video that has since emerged. In the video, Deepak Lodhi is purportedly seen sitting on the rooftop for around 11 seconds before suddenly getting up and jumping from the building. No suicide note had been found. Police said they were examining the circumstances surrounding his death. As part of the inquiry, police examined Deepak Lodhis mobile phone and room but said they found nothing that indicated he was facing any problem or what may have prompted him to take the step. Police are awaiting the toxicology report of his blood sample before drawing any conclusions about the circumstances of his death. SSP Shlok Kumar said police are looking into the circumstances surrounding his death.

articleTitle: Can economics explain human beings? Antara Haldar’s Everyman takes on the ‘rational’ man
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Everyman: The Story of Economics in Three Acts by Cambridge economist Antara Haldar. (Generated using AI)
description: Written in part as intellectual history, part fable, Everyman is meant to be an indictment of economics, of a world caught up in its own limitations
body_raw: Imagine Homo economicus as a full-blooded character. Call him Neo. This character is a utility-maximising, or usually profit-maximising, character - rational, priding himself on a tough realism about the world, assuming everyone acts mostly on self-interest. He sees the world as a series of price points, measures every opportunity cost, and is sentimental about only his unsentimentality. He further believes that everyone acting like this rational actor will, through a miraculous feat of coordination, produce public benefits and untold prosperity. His avatars have a different machismo about them. One is called Finn, a finance bro who uses the power of money to make and unmake worlds a Davos Man, who dislocates economies in opening them up or Tek, the guy who believes that boundless technology combined with boundless capital can create a new humanity. All believe that markets will somehow coordinate these machismos. The outcome will be untold public benefit. But in reality, the world they create is Darwinian some win, some lose. The losers might want the helping hand of the State, might resent the power of the winner, might even agitate for equality. But in reality, they are whiners, holding back humanity. Imagine further an Everyman, who just might think human beings are more complex less rational, subject to behavioural influences, not single-minded in their motivations but, above all, slightly more decent and capable of cooperation. Not everything has a price cooperation can produce more public goods and a better society than gladiatorial competition, and demanding a little equality is hardly whining, but the demand of justice. Imagine if these characters collided in a psychodrama in the real world these social theories became character types who show up in historical crises, from deindustrialisation to depressions. It would make for a fascinating fable of sorts. This, broadly, is the premise of Cambridge economist, Antara Haldars engaging, Everyman The Story of Economics in Three Acts. Written in part as intellectual history, part fable, Everyman is meant to be an indictment of economics, the world of Neo, caught in its own limitations. John Stuart Mill had two critiques of Bentham. Using Carlyles memorable turn of phrase, he said Bentham had the completeness of limited men. But his second objection was that if everyone thought everyone was only self-interested, we would indeed all become only self-interested. Our construction is self-fulfilling. Something like this thought underlines Haldars fable. Neo does not describe human nature. Neo is a construct we have created and let shape us. Neo is not all bad there is a kind of tragic cast to him. As one character tells Neo, You are like Spock from Star Trek and we are like Homer Simpson from The Simpsons. But I bet it can be hard on you as well - even being the personification of reason - to live up to the ideal. But this is the only sympathy Neo will get. Neo is an imperialising figure who has no answers to deep problems of precarity, inequality, ecological devastation and economic volatility. He is deluded It is social cooperation and the visible hand of the state that is needed for the public good. But, mostly, he is psychologically stunted ignorant of the mass of literature in evolutionary biology, psychology, anthropology and behavioural economics that describes human beings in all their complexity. If humanity is to be saved, Neo must be discarded his conception of a bull run will be a rampage on what it means to be human. Everyman is inventive in constructing ideas as characters. It is breathtaking in the range of its references. There is a literary bravura in the writing, as metaphors, puns and allusions pile on each other in hurried succession, as Neo and his interlocutors are described in tropes drawn from Shakespeare to Borges. The best sections are the last third, where you get less of an indictment of economics but a representation of the kind of unintelligible pastiche of forces our world has become. As Haldar puts it, this era of superabundant information, the archive felt like a graveyard of meaning instead of a treasure. But Haldars Fable works unevenly. Some of the allusions and jokes land many dont. The books rhetorical power overwhelms its analytical acuity. The blitz of ideas is all dealt in their Twitter versions as it were. The opening intellectual history, where Neo appears as a progeny of Smith, Keynes and Hayek, borders on a caricature of these figures. It is also a punch that does not land. There is almost nothing in Everyman that these figures did not know. Even the benighted Hayek was as much a theorist of common law as he was of markets. That Neo is at root of all evil is too simplistic our penchant for cooperation and sacrifice in the form of nationalism can be more murderous and stand in the way of cooperation as much as Neos rationality. The conflict between Neo and Everyman is not a conflict between two types It is a civil war of the soul within all of us. If Neo is all that limited, why did he triumph? The rhetorical excess in the book makes you wonder, to use Shakespeare, as Haldar does Doth thou protest too much? The writer is contributing editor, The Indian Express

articleTitle: Marks withheld for extortion: How KPSC officials used merit lists to demand bribes
articleFeaturedImageAlt: KPSC exam paper leak, KPSC recruitment scam, KPSC paper leak case, Karnataka PSC scam, ED KPSC probe, Karnataka CID investigation, KPSC veterinary doctors exam, KPSC bribery case, KPSC recruitment fraud, Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, KPSC KAS recruitment, Karnataka Public Service Commission, Karnataka Public Service Commission news, Indian Express news
description: Following the arrest of former exam controller Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, the Enforcement Directorate informed a special court that 13 Karnataka PSC recruitment drives from 2024 to 2026 need to be probed for systematic extortion.
body_raw: The Karnataka Public Service Commission KPSC deliberately suppressed candidate score details in initial selection lists in recent years to allow its chairman and members to negotiate bribes using confidential performance data, an Enforcement Directorate ED investigation has revealed. The revelation followed the arrest and 14-day custody of IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, 41, who served as KPSCs controller of examinations from January 2024 to March 2026. At the conclusion of Gangwars custodial interrogation on Saturday, the agency informed a special court that as many as 13 job recruitment drives conducted during his tenure will need to be investigated. Gangwar, the primary accused in the question paper leak for the January 89, 2026, exam to recruit 400 veterinary officers, allegedly facilitated widespread corruption through a middleman who collected Rs 20 lakh to Rs 40 lakh each from at least 20 candidates. Exploitation of 13 merit lists According to ED submissions in court, the agency uncovered a systematic racket centred on preparing and finalising the 13 merit list, a preliminary shortlist containing three candidates for every available post. To enable bribe negotiations, KPSC allegedly began publishing 13 eligibility lists with only roll numbers and names, omitting candidates actual marks. KPSC members and officials then extracted performance details from Gangwar to identify high-ranking candidates, as per the agency. Once the merit of a candidate is known, the concerned member, official or middleman contacts the candidate and negotiates the bribe amount the higher the candidates chance of selection, the higher the amount demanded, the ED informed the court. During interrogation, Gangwar disclosed that after the veterinary officers 13 merit list was published on February 4, 2026, suspended KPSC chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar, along with KPSC officials B V Geetha, Shanta Hosmani, Elfreda D Silva, and others, approached him with candidate names to assess their selection prospects. Handwritten notes seized from a KPSC officials residence further corroborated the scheme, listing shortlisted candidates who paid bribes but failed to make the final list. ED seeks expanded probe ED counsel Maheshwari D M argued in court that the proceeds of crime generated across all recruitment drives during Gangwars tenure remain unquantified, requiring a comprehensive investigation into all involved officials, candidates, and transaction amounts. Defence counsel Siri R argued that the absence of separate FIRs for the other 13 recruitment drives limits the EDs jurisdiction under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act PMLA strictly to the veterinary officer recruitment scam. In response, the ED maintained that all recruitment drives during Gangwars tenure constitute a continuing money-laundering offence. The court remanded the suspended IAS officer to 14 days of judicial custody and set his bail hearing for October 8.

articleTitle: Why Maharashtra’s Green India Mission saplings died: CAG lists the failures
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Afforestation was carried out over 205 hectares at 35 sites in Goramba and Valval (Nandurbar), Rayari (Bhor) and Yerandi (Wadsa). (Express Photo by Amit Chakravarty
description: Auditing Maharashtra's Green India Mission, the CAG found inflated survival claims, Rs 12.75 crore reported as spent when barely Rs 29 lakh was used, and an agency that didn't meet once in 10 years.
body_raw: From financial misappropriation and poor survival of planted trees to a near-total collapse of institutional mechanisms, the Comptroller and Auditor General CAG of India has flagged major shortcomings in how Maharashtras forest department implemented the Green India Mission GIM. The Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change MoEFCC launched the flagship programme in 2014 to protect, restore and enhance green cover in 16 states and Union Territories between 2015-16 and 2024-25. In Maharashtra, 35 sites across four talukas in Nandurbar, Bhor and Wadsa were selected. The GIM is one of eight missions under Indias national action plan on climate change and a key part of the countrys climate commitments, since expanding forest and tree cover has been among Indias priorities under the Paris Agreement, adopted at COP21 in 2015. The CAG report states that Maharashtra failed to achieve almost all the major targets under the scheme within the timeline. The Indian Express sought comment from Milind Mhaiskar, additional chief secretary, forest department, but he is yet to respond. Agency never revamped, never met A key mandate of the GIM was to revamp each states forest development agency SFDA, the apex body that implements afforestation and eco-development programmes, receives funds from the Union ministry and represents the state nationally. The SFDA was earlier chaired by the principal chief conservator of forests PCCF, with the chairpersons and CEOs of centrally sponsored afforestation schemes on its board. Under the GIM, it was to be chaired by the chief minister or a minister nominated by the CM, and include the PCCF and key forest department officials. The CAG found the SFDA was never revamped in Maharashtra. In the 10 years between 2014-15 and 2024-25, the existing SFDA did not hold a single meeting. The state steering committee SSC, set up in April 2016 to guide district planning bodies on the GIM and afforestation, met only once till 2025, against the 18 meetings prescribed over nine years. Money claimed, money spent In 2018-19, the state released Rs 17.17 crore to the SFDA after a delay of 206 days. The SFDA told the CAG it spent Rs 12.75 crore that year, leaving an unspent balance of Rs 4.42 crore. The audit found otherwise. Audit found that Rs 12.75 crore was reported as utilised by the SFDA however, for that financial year only Rs 9.26 crore was released to five forest development agencies FDAs, of which only Rs 0.29 crore was found utilised. Meanwhile, the FDA and SFDAs claimed full utilisation of funds, the report stated. The SFDA did not open a bank account for the scheme till August 2021. Rs 1.91 crore was deposited with four district planning bodies, Gothangaon, Netali, Kosbad and Jamsher, which were not part of the mission, while eight districts that were actual beneficiaries received nothing. Saplings on paper In July 2019, 49,500 saplings were planted in the Wardha region, and their procurement cost the state Rs 33 lakh. Records relating to the supply of saplings from the nurseries were not furnished by the SFDA however, it submitted transport challans of 9,336 saplings only, the report stated. The CAG found that challans of more than 6,800 saplings related to plantation sites outside Wardha. Around 1,600 were issued after the recorded date of plantation. In all, only 116 saplings were planted at the site. Survival claims versus reality Afforestation was carried out over 205 hectares at 35 sites in Goramba and Valval Nandurbar, Rayari Bhor and Yerandi Wadsa. The SFDA claimed survival rates of 50 per cent at Goramba, 66.33 per cent at Valval, 96 per cent at Rayari and 61.20 per cent at Yerandi. The CAG found actual survival was nil at Goramba, 8.42 per cent at Valval, under 5 per cent at Rayari and under 10 per cent at Yerandi. The CAG said many saplings were destroyed largely by cattle belonging to tribal residents of nearby villages. In some cases, daily wage workers who had not been paid by local bodies left their cattle at the sites. Work to protect the saplings could not be done because funds were released late. The CAG identified the failure to carry out soil moisture conservation SMC, which prevents soil erosion, reduces evaporation and improves water infiltration, as a root cause. All 35 sites required SMC work. None of them got it, a 100 per cent shortfall.

articleTitle: No room for 135-year-old library in Central Vista plan? Supreme Court hearing today
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Space for library provided in Central Vista plan: Ministry
description: The Indian Express reported that with Shastri Bhawan set to be pulled down as part of the Central Vista revamp plan, the government has yet to find space for one of the oldest central government libraries.
body_raw: Taking suo motu cognizance of a September 30 report in The Indian Express, the Supreme Court will hear Monday the matter relating to the relocation of the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library CSL in Shastri Bhavan which is set to be torn down as part of the Central Vista revamp plan. The Indian Express reported that the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and Central Public Works Department are yet to find space for the library which houses more than 8.5 lakh books. The matter, registered under the title In Re 135-Yr-Old Library 8.5 Lakh Books-And No Room In The New Central Vista Plan, will be heard Monday by a bench of Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva. Following the publication of the report, the Ministry, in a post, said it is clarified that space for the Central Secretariat Library has been provided for in the Kartavya Path redevelopment plan. The necessary process for construction of the library is underway. Spread over four floors and covering nearly 5,500 square metres in Shastri Bhavan, the CSL contains more than 8.5 lakh books including rare books, official records and gazetteers, and continues to receive a steady stream of visitors including government officials and students preparing for competitive examinations. The oldest book, in a separate section of rare books in the library, is the compilation of a French travellers writings, dating back to 1702. On September 17, the CPWD wrote to all ministries and departments situated in Shastri Bhavan, saying the complex be vacated, including all furniture, electronic items and other belongings, at the earliest as it needs to be handed over. by the end of September 2026 for the commencement of the construction work. Sources said that in January, the Directorate of Estates allotted two rooms, with an area of 300 square metres, at Kartavya Bhavan-2 for the CSL. The Ministry of Culture, which administers the CSL, rejected this, replying that the space allotted was far from sufficient, the sources said.

articleTitle: How to test whether a compostable bag breaks down at home
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Consumers should check whether a compostable bag is certified for home or industrial composting.
description: Not every compostable bag can break down in a home compost bin. Here's how to check the certification, test the bag and dispose of it correctly.
body_raw: Compostable bags appear to be more environmentally friendly than plastic bags. But compostable doesnt necessarily mean something breaks down quickly in a home compost pile. Decomposition conditions may depend heavily on the material and the products certification. Test to ensure the bag is compostable at home Not all compostable bags decompose properly at home. Some bags need high-temperature, commercial-scale operations to break down properly. So consumers should look for the right certification on a product for use in their compost bin. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Maninder Singh Nayyar, Founder CEO, CEF Group, suggests an experiment that can help consumers determine whether bags work as expected in their compost. First, cut a piece of the bag, note its size and shape, and bury it about 10 to 15 cm deep in a well-aerated compost bin. The compost should include a combination of wet green stuff, like fruit and vegetable waste, and dry brown stuff, like leaves and shredded cardboard. It should remain damp but not soggy. Inspect the pile every four weeks and keep notes on changes. A truly compostable material should show signs of breaking down under proper conditions over time, which can take several months and depends on climate and season. Comparing it to a conventional plastic bag could help, as long as neither sample is used to make compost for food later. Consumers need to know that breaking into pieces does not equate to full biodegradation. If the bag doesnt fully decompose within the time specified by the manufacturer, it may require industrial composting. Consumers must dispose of the bags as required locally and not put them in recycling bins, as they may contaminate regular plastics. What consumers need to ensure Dr Sujit Paul, Group CEO of Zota Healthcare Ltd Davaindia, says consumers need to check the packaging carefully. Pay attention to the clear information on whether the product is home compostable or industrially compostable, instead of the labels of eco-friendly or biodegradable. Any certification testing details that may be available can also give added assurance about the claims, he adds. Dr Sujit also advises to follow manufacturers instructions for disposal, as well. A bin meant to be used for industrial composting may be aggressively managed with controlled temperatures, humidity and microbial environment which would not exist within a typical home compost pile, he says. If consumers know they should opt for certified products and know what to do with them no matter which they pick, they can make more informed environmental choices. articleTitle: Abhishek Banerjee objects to rebel TMC MP’s parliamentary panel chair post
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Abhishek Banerjee
description: Questioning the legal basis of Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar's appointment, Abhishek Banerjee urged Speaker Om Birla to restore the panel chairmanship to Trinamool Congress's official nominee.
body_raw: Trinamool Congress MP and national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee wrote to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla Saturday, objecting to the appointment of MP Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar as chairperson of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Chemicals and Fertilisers. Banerjee highlighted that Dastidar is among 20 Lok Sabha members of the Trinamool rebel faction facing pending disqualification petitions before the Speaker under the Tenth Schedule. In my letters dated September 23, I expressly requested that these Members be kept out of consideration for DRSC Department-Related Standing Committees appointments until the petitions were decided, Banerjee wrote in his letter to the Speaker. Banerjee reiterated that in his earlier communication, the party had formally requested to retain the chairmanship of one Standing Committee in the Lok Sabha and submitted its nomination for the existing chairperson to continue. He stated that the recent appointment disregards both the partys explicit objections and its official nomination. Highlighting procedural anomalies, Banerjee noted, The Digital Sansad website continues to show 28 Lok Sabha Members belonging to AITC All India Trinamool Congress. The member appointed, however, claims affiliation with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India NCPI through a purported merger disputed in the pending disqualification proceedings. He further questioned the party affiliation under which the chairmanship was allotted. If it has been allotted to AITC, on what basis has the partys nominee been replaced against its express wishes? If it has been allotted to NCPI, under what order has that affiliation been recognised, and on what basis has NCPI been given the chairmanship? he wrote. Disputed affiliation Banerjee asserted that NCPIs reported association with the National Democratic Alliance NDA cannot resolve the Tenth Schedule affiliation issue while proceedings remain pending before the Speaker. Appointing a member to a chairmanship while leaving the members disputed affiliation undecided is, in our submission, contrary to parliamentary propriety. This appointment cannot be treated as a chairmanship allotted to AITC, Banerjee submitted. Banerjee urged the Speaker to withdraw Dastidars appointment, restore the committee chairmanship to Trinamools duly nominated member, and deliver an early decision on the pending disqualification petitions.
