articleTitle: ‘Way ahead of time’: Bappi Lahiri’s grandson Rego on his disco hits in Dhurandhar, Raja Saab
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rego B, Bappi Lahiri
description: In an exclusive interview with SCREEN, late music maestro Bappi Lahiri’s grandson Rego B opened up about his new song, ‘Chand’, and reflected on his grandfather’s musical legacy.
body_raw: Bappi Lahiris musical legacy continues through his 17-year-old grandson Swastikk Bansall, who performs under the stage name Rego B. Fresh off the release of his new single, Chand, Rego sat down with SCREEN to discuss his grandfathers influence, the resurgence of his disco classics, and how Bappi Lahiris music found a global audience long before the age of social media. Speaking about Bappi Lahiris songs that continue to resonate with people, Rego B said, Granddads songs are universal, but his foot-tapping tunes that continue to resonate with younger audiences are disco songs like Auva Auva Koi Yahan Nache, Ramba Ho Ho and Jimmy Jimmy. Those songs were very different, and granddad was way ahead of his time. He knew what would work even 20 years later, and they are still working today. Shashwat Sachdev remixed Bappi Lahiri and Usha Uthups iconic disco track Ramba Ho for Aditya Dhars film Dhurandhar, headlined by Ranveer Singh. Rego admitted that he was surprised to see the cult song featured in the film. He said, I was so surprised to see his song, Ramba Ho used in Dhurandhar, and how his song Koi Yahan Nache Nache was used in Prabhas The Raja Saab. This shows that his music is still appealing to the mass audience. Its an honour to learn from him and his style of music. I feel so grateful that I have been brought up in this family, and I am lucky to be his grandson. Rego B on Bappi Lahiris international reach and his meeting with Michael Jackson Rego also offered insights into Bappi Lahiris association with international music stars and his influence beyond India. Granddad worked with many superstars, including Snoop Dogg, Lady Gaga, Elton John and Akon. It shows how influential his music was. For an artist from India, especially at that time, to have international musicians approach him and ask him to make songs for them shows just how far his music had reached, shared Rego. Also Read Inside Bappi Lahiris 40-year-old house 1,000 Ganesha idols, a gold chair, Kishore Kumars last photo and rare 100-Year-old instruments He also recalled a story his mother had told him about Bappi Lahiris meeting with Michael Jackson in 1996. Rego said, When Michael Jackson came to Bombay, my grandfather went to meet him. My mother tells me this story. She was also very young at the time and started crying when she saw Michael Jackson because who wouldnt? He is the King of Pop, hes the G.O.A.T. Even he told my granddad, I love your song Jimmy Jimmy. Its a beautiful song. So, Michael Jackson saying that to my granddad in the 90s showed how far his music had reached. Coming from a small village in West Bengal to making a name for himself in Bollywood and then becoming known worldwide shows what he achieved and how far his music travelled. Today, we have social media to showcase our music, but back then there was nothing like that. Despite that, his music travelled overseas, and that shows its reach. Its a huge thing. Rego also shared an interesting anecdote about one of Bappi Lahiris most iconic tracks, Jimmy Jimmy. He said, It was one of the most played songs in Russia. When the President and the Prime Minister come, the marching bands play Jimmy Jimmy, and they still play it. Its such an honour to see that. You are like, Oh my God Its absolutely unreal. Rego B on his new single Chand Talking about his latest release Chand, Rego expressed gratitude for the love coming his way and the opportunity to release his first independent single. I am really grateful that Chand is finally out for everyone to hear. Its really special to me because it was released on my 17th birthday September 21, during the Ganesh Chaturthi festivities. So, it truly means a lot to me as an artiste. I am grateful to my parents and my granddad, who have mentored me and raised me in that safe space of music, and helped me reach a point where I could release my own independent single. When you hear it, it gives you a homely feeling. It has that 90s and 2000s touch to it, with the nuances in the lyrics and the singing style. Watch the song Chand below Sharing his excitement over the response to the song, he said, I can feel the energy around it, and I got to know that Chand has organically made it to New Music Friday Pakistan on Spotify. It has also made it to New Music Hindi. Its really resonating with people. The word Chand is also so universal because you can connect it with anyone your girlfriend, your husband, your wife or your family. Thats one of the reasons we chose the name Chand, because not many songs are named that. Theres a special feeling behind it. Im grateful that people are giving it so much love and are also liking the video, which is very different. My friend Adrija is my co-actor in the video, and she is an impeccable dancer and actor. So, it all has a very homely feeling.

articleTitle: Mukesh Kumar and Akash Deep bowl Rest of India to Irani Cup title
articleFeaturedImageAlt: It was the first time since 2024 that the Ranji Trophy winners had failed to complete the double.
description: Set a massive target of 279, the two Bengal seamers run through Ranji champions as RoI win the title they last won in 2024
body_raw: The beauty of red-ball cricket lies in its intrinsic irony. An otherwise long, languid affair, spread across days, and yet, a few hours could be all it takes to deliver the games verdict. Basking in a Sunday sun that had found its full intensity after two subdued days, fans here at Srinagars Sher-I-Kashmir Stadium was offered a slice of that beauty, as Rest of India defeated the reigning Ranji Trophy champions, Jammu Kashmir, by 167 runs to claim the Irani Cup. What an incredible performance by the boys. Finally, it happened after two years, quipped batting coach Laxmi Ratan Shukla, relief written across his face as he entered the dressing room to join the captain Rishabh Pants birthday celebrations. Three hours earlier, the players in that very room had cut desolate figures. Chasing a target of 279 runs, the hosts had gone off to a flier. Qamran Iqbal and Shubham Khajuria batted as if they had already pencilled in a free Day 5. In accordance, 54 runs came in the first 10 overs. What followed would feel to the JK players like a fever dream. Iqbal, perhaps too eager to reach the finish line, shuffled across to deposit an Akash Deep delivery into the temporary stands past square leg. Instead, the delivery marked his deposit to the dugout, trapped lbw. Drinks were called in the 13th over, and a single conversation during that break shaped the outcome of the match. Mukesh Kumar, the least effective of his sides pacers in the first innings, pleaded with the stand-in captain, Sarfaraz Khan, for just one more over. Kumar was successful in his convincing bid. That, however, was only the first part of the job. The pacer would take two wickets in that over and turn the game on its head. An inswinger trapped Shubham Pundir lbw, and the JK captain, Paras Dogra, was undone by a peach that shaped away from the bat and disturbed the stumps. At 893, however, a semblance of parity still lingered, as it had through the first three days in the valley. Then came an hour of impeccable bowling, which made the contest look like something it never was - a one-sided affair. Shubham Khajuria, man with the most first-Class appearances for JK, would offer a shot in the very first delivery after Lunch that was not in synchronisation with his vast experience. He chased a wide delivery from Akash and could only find the edge. Kanhaiya Wadhawan, apparently untaught by the veterans misfortune, offered a near-identical stroke and was caught by the substitute wicketkeeper Aryan Juyal in the same fashion. The only difference between the two dismissals lay in the bowler - this time it was Mukesh Kumar, collecting his third wicket. He would take three more wickets. Before that, however, Akashs away movement would result in the second duck of the day - all-rounder Sahil Lotra following in the footsteps of his captain. The day belonged to the two seamers from Bengal, yet perhaps the most important dismissal came from the showstopper of the first innings, Mukesh Choudhary. Abdul Samad, who had told this paper of his ambition to score over 1,000 runs in the coming Ranji Trophy season, was a man intent on backing his words. Fresh from a first-innings half-century, he was the picture of poise in the second - batting unperturbed on 20, with the chaos surrounding him not affecting his zen. But in the 28th over, Choudhary lured him into a drive, and got him caught by Shikhar Mohan at second slip. That, effectively, was the game for Rest of India. Kumar would dismiss Abid Mushtaq, Umar Nazir and Sunil Kumar in the span of four deliveries in the next over, recording his 11th five-wicket haul in first-class cricket. It was the first time since 2024 that the Ranji Trophy winners had failed to complete the double. Save for a session of brain fade, though, Dogras men did offer a good account of themselves. They have 7 players in their team who have played for India. Bahut saari teamein sochti bhi nahin ki unko hara paayenge, but hum mein belief tha Many teams would not even have fathomed beating them, but we had belief. We fought till the last moment, Dogra said, his head held high. Outside the stadium, two young fans - Schrodingers optimist and pessimist - were locked in debate. What was the point of hosting this game involving such big players like Rishabh Pant, and then embarrassing ourselves in front of them? asked the pessimist. Rishabh Pant is here because we are the champions of India. Never forget that, replied the optimist. The debate ended in a draw. The trophy ended up in the Rest of Indias locker. Brief scores Rest of India 237 319 Ravichandran Smaran 135 Sunil Kumar 356 defeated Jammu Kashmir 278 111 Shubham Khajuria 36 Mukesh Kumar 633 by 167 runs.

articleTitle: China This Week | Rumours about Xi Jinping’s health, US jets arrive in Taiwan, and more
articleFeaturedImageAlt: US President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump with China's President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan at the White House, on September 24. (AP Photo/Alex Brandon)
description: Every week, we recap highlights of the news from China. This edition looks at the nature of rumours around Chinese President Xi Jinping's health in recent weeks, a sale of jets to Taiwan, and activity in the South China Sea.
body_raw: Over the last few days, analysts and longtime China watchers have tried to make sense of the bilateral leaders meeting in Washington, DC, in late September. What stood out was the pageantry surrounding Chinese President Xi Jinpings visit, even as many argued that the trip itself fell short on substantial outcomes. A report from The Wall Street Journal has now claimed that Xis staff requested several breaks during the visit and to cut down the duration of some events, raising questions about the 73-year-olds health. It also follows similar rumours that swirled during Xis trip to India for the BRICS summit in New Delhi earlier in September. Another noteworthy event this week was the delivery of two American F-16V fighter jets to Taiwan. The Chinese Communist Partys CCP tabloid, Global Times, commented on the fact that it came years behind schedule. The jets have also come as a major arms sale from Taiwan to the US hangs in the balance. Finally, we look at a recent Reuters report that used satellite images to find that China is building a full-scale runway at the Antelope Reef in the disputed South China Sea. Military attaches and security analysts say it could be one of Chinas most important offshore bases in the region, the report said. Here is a closer look at these developments. 1. Why Xi Jinpings health is often the centre of rumours The WSJ report cited former US officials involved in planning state visits and analysts, who said that the nature of Chinas requests for Xi was unusual. Chief among the requests was a private room inside the West Wing of the White House for Xi to take a break between events, with only his wife, Peng Liyuan, permitted to join him, the people said. No others from the Chinese delegation were allowed to use the hold room, as it was called, the report said. UPSHOT Such rumours are not exactly new. In fact, back in 2012, months before Xi was elevated as the general secretary of the CCP - the most powerful position in China - he was not seen in public for a while, sparking speculation over his health. Xi is not alone, in that many key public figures in China often draw such scrutiny given the lack of transparency in the countrys political and media systems. Information flows are heavily regulated by the government, which, in turn, heightens curiosity among observers. With a leader like Xi, who has concentrated power at the top and bypassed term limitations, China watchers are particularly interested in observing the tiniest body language shifts and movements to understand his health condition, including Xi reportedly clasping his wifes hand while using the stairs in Washington, SC. This incident may turn out to be about Xi simply requiring rest given his age and the long-duration flight to the US. The rumours of his supposed ill-health in India were also not found to have a strong basis, at least so far, but are indicative of how Chinas political system, in an attempt to project strength and infallibility, can damage those very perceptions. 2. Taiwan gets new jets, with some delays During Donald Trumps first presidential term in 2019, the United States approved an 8 billion sale of Lockheed Martin F-16V fighter jets to Taiwan, but issues such as software problems delayed delivery, Reuters reported. The arrival of the first two of 66 F-16V Block 70s strengthens Taiwans defense capabilities and safeguards our skies. We thank the United States for its longstanding support and continued security cooperation. As President ChingteLai has said, investing in defense is investing in peace. Taiwan remains committed to defending our homeland and to contributing to regional peace and stability. - DPP U.S. Mission TaiwanDPPDC October 2, 2026 The jets were to reach Taiwan between 2023 and 2026, but only two of the 65 F-16V Block 70 jets have been delivered. Commenting on the news, Global Times noted the positive reactions from Taiwans ruling Democratic Progressive Party DPP, calling it political performance. The article spoke of The DPPs alarm over the rising prevalence of abandoning Taiwan and doubting the US sentiments, particularly as China and the US have sought greater strategic stability in their relationship. Under this narrative, the arrival of two F-16Vs in Taiwan has been. cited as proof of continued US support for Taiwan island. UPSHOT The article touches on a subject that has worried some stakeholders in the US of late the countrys longstanding relationship with Taiwan. While the latest jet delivery may have been approved years ago, its delivery comes when Trump has held off on approving a 14 billion arms sale to Taiwan. Once signed, it would be the biggest such package to date. Amid the visit, Lyle Morris, Senior Fellow on Foreign Policy and National Security at the US-based Asia Society Policy Institutes Center for China Analysis, told The Indian Express that Trumps delay could be an attempt to accommodate China. Xi and the Chinese State have criticised such arms sales as part of the broader objection to any conception of Taiwanese independence. But Trumps more recent statements have also diverged from the more assured US support for Taiwan over the past few decades. In that context, it would be understandable why the DPP would see the jets as evidence of US support, and why the CCP would describe it critically. 3. New activity in South China Sea Reuters reported that a completed base at Antelope Reef would be Chinas most significant military expansion in the South China Sea in a decade, extending the reach of Chinese naval ships and military aircraft in a waterway that is an increasingly militarised arena of competition between Beijing and the United States and its allies over Taiwan. It would also help protect the approaches to Hainan Island, where China keeps its nuclear-armed ballistic missile submarines, the report said. UPSHOT In the last decade or so of increasingly assertive Chinese foreign policy, the South China Sea has been a major component. Apart from the regions vast oil and gas resources, it has also become a source of territorial contestation, with claims upto various points made by countries such as Vietnam and the Philippines. For the US, it could also emerge as a region where China incrementally increases its presence through the deployment of smaller vessels and forces, creating a strategic threat. In July, the US government issued a joint statement with countries including Japan, Australia and the Philippines on the tenth anniversary of the Philippines-China South China Sea Arbitral Tribunal Award. That award had criticised Chinas claims to the region, while China has said the tribunal was not eligible to adjudicate on the subject. We reaffirm that the Award rendered ten years ago by the Arbitral Tribunal is a significant milestone and is final, legally binding, and definitive between China and the Philippines. We reaffirm the Arbitral Tribunals decision that there is no legal basis for Chinas expansive maritime claims in the South China Sea, including those based on historic rights, it said. With continued Chinese activity even a decade after the ruling, however, there is little to suggest that tribunals and other means of adjudication will influence China to slow down its work there.

articleTitle: 4 days on road for 2 seats: Why Vijay stakes prestige for bypolls after Tamil Nadu win
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay during an election campaign for party candidate Sathyabama ahead of the upcoming Dharapuram Assembly constituency by-poll
description: In multi-cornered fights for Madurantakam and Dharapuram, TVK aims to shore up its tally and get voters to ratify its candidates who had switched to the party after winning the seats on AIADMK tickets
body_raw: Chief ministers do not ordinarily spend four days campaigning for two Assembly by-elections in Tamil Nadu. However, C Joseph Vijay has done it. With Madurantakam and Dharapuram voting on October 6, the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam TVK chief has spent two days addressing public rallies and another two on roadshows, including a 45-km journey through more than 30 villages in Madurantakam. The intensity is striking for another reason during the April Assembly election that brought him to power, Vijays own campaign appearances were comparatively limited, with several scheduled rallies cancelled and much of TVKs constituency-level campaigning left to candidates and other leaders. Inside the TVK, expectations have risen with the CMs effort. With this much campaigning by Vijay himself, we should get 50 of the votes, a senior TVK leader said. That number explains why these two bypolls have become considerably larger than two seats. The TVK is the ruling party. Both constituencies were vacated by AIADMK legislators who resigned within weeks of being elected and crossed over to Vijay. The same two leaders-Maragatham Kumaravel in Madurantakam and P Sathyabama in Dharapuram-are now contesting as TVK candidates. What is at stake? A victory would suggest that not merely politicians but at least enough of their voters have travelled with them. A defeat in even one seat would complicate the story that the TVK has been telling since it came to power in May that the centre of Tamil Nadu politics has shifted decisively towards Vijay. More immediately, senior TVK leaders acknowledge that losing a seat could slow the movement of AIADMK functionaries towards the ruling party. Since the Assembly elections, the TVK has been drawing former ministers, legislators and local functionaries from the weakened AIADMK. In Dharapuram alone, local-level AIADMK leaders have moved towards it. A victory would make further movement easier. A loss, on the other hand, would remind leaders contemplating a switch that a change of party is far simpler than transferring a constituency. That is why the bypoll is also a test of something difficult to measure until votes are counted on October 9 how much of Vijays April coalition of voters remains personally attached to him after the excitement of the general election has passed. TVK leaders believe women may be particularly important. Their assessment is that male voters could remain more firmly distributed among established party loyalties, while Vijay still has room to increase his support among women. Why Vijay has stepped in? Whether that assessment survives the ballot box is another matter. But it partly explains Vijays decision to campaign at close range rather than leave the election to ministers and local organisers. In Madurantakam, his roadshow included village stops, interactions with residents, a tractor ride and tea at a roadside shop. The Chief Minister who campaigned sparingly while seeking power is campaigning unusually hard after acquiring it. The Opposition understands the symbolism. The AIADMK has turned the circumstances of the bypoll itself into its campaign. Its supporters have repeatedly called Sathyabama a traitor for winning Dharapuram as an AIADMK candidate and then resigning to join the TVK. The argument is simple voters elected an AIADMK MLA in April, why should they be asked five months later to elect the same person for another party? Former CM and DMK chief M K Stalin has made a similar argument from the DMK, describing the elections as resulting from the death of democracy and attacking the TVK for making voters return to polling booths before, as he put it, the indelible ink from the general election had disappeared. The DMK, however, faces a different test. DMKs strength test The DMK enters these by-elections without the broad alliance that accompanied it into the Assembly election. The Congress, VCK, MDMK and IUML have moved into Vijays political orbit, while the CPI and CPIM are contesting separately. That means the DMK does not necessarily have to win to construct a favourable argument from the result. If its candidates substantially increase the partys vote share from April while contesting largely on its own, DMK leaders can argue that the defeat five months ago did not destroy the partys underlying electoral strength. A victory would be much more significant, but even a stronger second-place performance could provide Stalin with evidence that voters who deserted the DMK are beginning to reconsider. Do or die for AIADMK? For the AIADMK, the stakes are more existential. These were its seats. If its former MLAs can resign, join TVK and then defeat AIADMK candidates in the same constituencies, Vijay would have demonstrated something more damaging than attracting prominent defectors that the AIADMK label itself may no longer be necessary for some of its former representatives to win. The campaign has also acquired the familiar complications of Tamil Nadu by-elections. Leader of the Opposition in the Tamil Nadu Assembly Udhayanidhi Stalin has accused the TVK of distributing cash in Dharapuram, alleging that money was being carried in tiffin boxes. CPIM state secretary P Shanmugam has separately said villagers told Left campaigners that several parties were distributing money and that the TVK was paying the most. The TVK has categorically denied the allegations, saying it opposes cash-for-votes politics. Left adds intrigue The Lefts presence adds another peculiarity. The CPI and CPIM have supported Vijays government from outside but are now fighting his candidates. The PMK, meanwhile, has remained neutral amid discussions about a possible future relationship with the TVK. All of which makes October 6 an unusually crowded examination of a government less than five months old. By-elections are poor instruments for measuring an entire state. Local candidates, organisation, turnout and the advantages of incumbency can distort any attempt to turn two constituencies into Tamil Nadu. But these two seats have acquired importance because Vijay himself has made them important. Four days of personal campaigning has raised the price of victory. The TVK is no longer merely trying to retain two defectors. It is asking voters to ratify the political movement that brought those defectors to Vijay in the first place. In April, Vijay had to prove that his crowds could become votes. Then he returned with 108 seats, falling 10 short of the required 118 for an absolute majority in the 234-member House. Five months later, the question is narrower but perhaps more revealing. After government, Assembly debates and the ordinary frictions of power, will those votes still follow him? For the TVK, winning both seats keeps the political traffic moving towards Vijay. Losing even one could, for the first time since April, give some of those travelling in that direction a reason to check the road.

articleTitle: China or Japan, who was the biggest winner of the 2026 Asian Games
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Japan may have finished second behind China in their home Asiad, but they have cause to celebrate having increased their gold medal haul by 31 compared to last edition. (AP)
description: China finished top of the medal podium for the 12th consecutive Asiad in Aichi-Nagoya, but fell 42 medals short of what they managed in the previous edition of Hangzhou as hosts Japan gained significantly to finish in the second spot increasing their gold haul by 31
body_raw: China conquered the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, claiming a whopping 341 medals, 169 of them gold. China mined so much gold in Aichi-Nagoya, that even if Japan, South Korea, India and Uzbekistan - the next four nations on the medals tally - were to pile up their gold medals together, China would still have five more golds. China did finish on top of the medals tally for the 12th consecutive edition of Asian Games since 1982. However, Chinas total production of medals at the Aichi-Nagoya Games is still a whopping 42 medals short 341 in Nagoya compared to 383 in Hangzhou 2023 of their total haul from their home Asian Games in Hangzhou. The continental giants also fell 32 gold medals short 169 in Nagoya compared to 201 of their last Asian Games benchmark. Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage Meanwhile, Japan may have finished second in their home Asiad, but they have cause to celebrate having increased their gold medal haul by 31 83 in Aichi-Nagoya while 52 in Hangzhou and their total medal tally by 81 269 in Nagoya compared to 188 in Hangzhou. Chinas medals came in 57 different disciplines in Hangzhou but fell to 47 sports in Nagoya. In comparison, Japan claimed medals across 56 disciplines in 2026 compared to 48 in Hangzhou. So where did China miss out compared to the previous Asian Games? And what sports did Japans gains come in? Story behind Chinas tally The single biggest contributor to the 32 gold medals China was short of their Hangzhou tally was the exclusion of disciplines like dragon boat racing five golds, xiangqi three and chess three from the recently concluded Asiad. The boxers also came back four golds shorter than in Hangzhou while sailors returned with three less golds. Then there were many disciplines like athletics, badminton, rowing where they could not reclaim two golds, while there were other events like artistic gymnastics, basketball where they fell short by one gold. ALSO READ As the Asian Games close, with a last-minute gold rush, India finish fourth Five sports - swimming, athletics, shooting, diving and wushu - contributed half of Chinas gold medal haul with wushu being the one sport where Chinas 12 medals were all gold. At the Nagoya Asian Games, one sport where China made visible gains was archery, particularly compound archery. China had three medals at Hangzhou, all in recurve. Of the six archery medals China won at Nagoya, three were in compound archery, a discipline where they had none in Hangzhou. This is understandable, since compound archery will be a medalled sport at the Olympics in LA 2028. The 19-year-old swimmer Zhang Zhanshuo was Chinas athlete of the Asian Games, winning seven golds in freestyle distances ranging from the 100m relay to the 1500m solo. Swimmers Yu Yiting and Li Bingjie contributed to five golds each. In fact, if there were to be an individual medals table for medal-winning athletes, among the top 20 athletes ranked by number of medals won, 19 would be Chinese. Most of them were swimmers and shooters, and almost all of them were in the age group of 18 to 24. At this Asian Games, we have achieved our goals of testing our team, discovering new talent, identifying problems and conducting comprehensive training, further strengthening our confidence in achieving outstanding results at the Los Angeles Olympics, Zhang Xin, secretary-general of the Chinese delegation, said in a statement. China sent a 815-athlete contingent to Nagoya - which had 36 Olympic gold medalists - who broke five world records, 11 Asian records and 22 Games records, But of these athletes 548 about two-thirds were competing at their first Asian Games. Where did Japan gain? At their home Asian Games, Japans biggest gain came in athletics, where they turned their two gold medal return from Hangzhou to 10 golds. At least four of these golds were upgraded medals from Hangzhou Misaki Morota turned her womens pole vault silver from Hangzhou to gold while Yuma Maruyama converted his bronze in mens decathlon from three years back to gold. Japan actually lost five golds from the 10 it had won in track cycling in Hangzhou. But sports like judo nine golds in 2026 compared to five in 2023, fencing six golds in 2026 compared to two, wrestling seven compared to five, swimming seven compared to five helped make up for it. The total medals from fencing for Japan was not too different, but the colour changed. Japanese fencers earned 10 medals at Hangzhou, only two were gold while half of those 10 were bronze. This time in Nagoya, the fencers earned six golds in an overall haul of 12 medals on the piste. The Nagoya Games also served as a reminder of Japans inclination towards combat sports, with 19 of their gold medals and 44 total medals coming from 8 disciplines judo nine golds and 14 overall, wrestling seven gold, 15 overall, boxing one gold, four total, karate two gold, four overall, kurash two bronze, taekwondo two bronze, wushu two bronze and MMA one bronze. Japan had three golds and a silver in the triathlon in Hangzhou. At Nagoya, China took away two golds and two silvers while Japan had three medals, one of each colour. Japan had eight medals in soft tennis at Nagoya, four of them gold. China, in contrast, had no athlete representing it in the discipline, understandable since its not an Olympic sport or a discipline with any history with China. Chinas biggest medal earners at Nagoya Swimming 54 medals 30 gold Athletics 39 medals 17 gold Shooting 28 medals 16 gold Diving 16 medals 10 gold Cycling Track 14 medals 6 gold Artistic gymnastics 13 medals 7 gold Wushu 12 medals all 12 gold Canoe Sprint 10 medals 8 gold Rowing 10 medals 9 gold Japans biggest medal earners at Nagoya Swimming 37 medals 7 gold Athletics 32 medals 10 gold Artistic gymnastics 15 medals 2 gold Wrestling 15 medals 7 gold Judo 14 medals 9 gold Fencing 12 medals 6 gold

articleTitle: Gaming zone to sleeping pods: Kolkata’s Sealdah station set for major upgrade
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sealdah Station, Sealdah station upgrade,
description: The recreation zone will have three upper floors plus a terrace, while the ground floor—already developed by the railway—will remain outside the licensed area.
body_raw: Kolkatas Sealdah railway station is set for a major infrastructure upgrade with a state-of-the-art recreational centre featuring a multiplex, gaming zone, food court, retail outlets, and sleeping pods for the waiting passengers, officials said. The Eastern Railway has contracted a firm to develop, operate, and maintain the recreation zone. According to officials, this will transform the station into a modern, passenger-friendly, and commercially vibrant destination by bringing multiple lifestyle, retail, food, and entertainment services under one roof. The recreation zone will have three upper floors plus a terrace, while the ground floor-already developed by the railway-will remain outside the licensed area. The complex will house a diverse array of facilities, including grocery and daily-use products, apparel and accessories, electronics, a modern game zone, a multiplex with entertainment options, extensive food courts and cafeterias, and outlets of popular national and international food brands. Additionally, sleeping pods will be set up to offer comfortable short-term accommodation to passengers. The project will boost the local economy by creating widespread direct and indirect employment opportunities across retail, food and beverages, housekeeping, security, maintenance, and allied services, officials said. Rajeev Saxena, Divisional Railway Manager, Sealdah Division, stated that the project would offer premium facilities while improving the overall aesthetic and functional environment of the station, which has a daily footfall close to 10 lakh people. A years time has been given for the execution of the contract. First, the drawing will be approved. Then they will begin construction. So, this mart will be ready approximately by next Durga Puja. According to officials, the total value of the 10-year contract is over Rs 39 crore, including GST.

articleTitle: ‘Turn that music off’: Vijay Deverakonda’s blunt first words to Rashmika Mandanna on set
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rashmika Mandanna, Vijay Deverakonda
description: In a recent interview, Vijay Deverakonda recalled how he once dismissed love as merely a marketing term. Rashmika Mandanna, meanwhile, opened up about the importance of expressing affection and making small gestures in a relationship.
body_raw: Actors Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna recently opened up about their relationship, their journey from co-stars to life partners and how their understanding of love has evolved over the years. The couple also spoke about the little efforts that keep a relationship going. When Prakhar Gupta asked Vijay if he knew instantly that Rashmika was the one when they first met, the actor dismissed the idea of love at first sight. The Liger actor said, No. Can you ever know instantly? I dont believe in love at first sight. I need to go through a journey for love. You can know instantly that she is beautiful. But can you know instantly that she is the one? No. I knew nothing about her. I did think that she was a very beautiful girl but when I met her, I guess it was my third or fourth film. So, its more about the excitement of being on set, nervous of being on day 1 with a new team, and the aspiration of doing something successful. First day on any set is nerve-racking. Youre not comfortable enough to think about love and such. It has been eight years since we first met. Rashmika, however, corrected him about the timeline of their first meeting, saying, No, its been 9 years since we met but 8 years since our film released. Vijay jokingly responded, So, that film is my marker for how long I have known her. Vijay Deverakonda also spoke about how his perception of love was very different when he was younger. He admitted that he once considered love a marketing term and questioned the idea of falling in love more than once. The actor said, First of all, at that age, I was somebody who didnt believe in love, I was around 28-29. If you look at my interviews from then, youll see that I talk very disrespectfully about love, from a distance, and that comes from a place of young energy. I thought love is a marketing term. Weve all fallen in love multiple times in life. So, what does love mean? If I can fall in love with somebody and then I can fall in love with somebody else, then this is bullshit. So, I used to talk like this a lot. He added, You feel your mothers love, dont you? There is love where people think about you more than themselves. It took growing up and maturity to understand that. Dont disrespect the love in your life. Dont say love is a marketing term. Respect it, appreciate it, nurture it. So, for that journey, it took me many years. When I got an understanding about these things, then I started looking at love and relationships differently. Also Read Digital equivalent of sexual assault Vijay Deverakonda on Janhvi Kapoors AI deepfake video Vijay revealed that he only felt ready for marriage when he was 36, admitting that maturity played an important role in his decision. Rashmika Mandanna playfully interrupted him, telling him, Baby, you were late. Vijay said, When I was 36, I finally felt, I feel like getting married. I felt that I was ready and mature to understand this, to love it, I felt ready. Rashmika Mandanna says love is about making small efforts, Vijay Deverakonda calls her the more mature one Talking about what keeps a relationship strong, Rashmika Mandanna stressed that people often make efforts for those around them but tend to take their partners for granted. The Cocktail 2 actor said, We human beings always have to keep making efforts for the people that we love. Because most often we make a lot of efforts for people around than the people at your own house. I keep thinking that after getting married, you stop telling each other some very basic things. Something like Good morning, Are you doing well? or How was your day? It becomes, My partner already knows, so whats the point of saying it? And then, at some point, it could become, Why havent I heard this in such a long time? Meanwhile, life keeps pulling us in different directions. She further emphasised that these efforts should continue even after marriage and having children. Efforts, no matter how much into the relationship or marriage you are or even if you have kids together, I still feel like those little efforts should be made for each other, and that is love. It should be effortless but also you need to do these things because you want to do these things. Thats something that I believe in love. Vijay Deverakonda agreed with Rashmika Mandanna and called her the more mature one when it came to relationships. Vijay said, Rashmika is more mature when it comes to relationships. Look at how shes talking. She makes sure she tells me I love you at least 10-15 times a day, and she tells me that its important for me to express it too. I constantly feel it, but I shouldnt think, Okay, she knows it, so I dont need to say it. She reminds me of that, which makes me more aware because we are so caught up in life that sometimes we can forget these smaller, simpler but important things. He also opened up about being a control freak and how it took him time to trust the relationship and allow things to fall into place naturally. The Liger actor said, So, she is the one who actually made me. I was worried for the longest time whether I will be able to drive this because I am a control freak, and I was wondering if I left the steering, will it work automatically? My 4-5 years went in that laughs. She knew that the car was working, and would say, You relax. By nature, thats probably your upbringing, childhood. You are who you are because of everything that you dont even remember. Everything shapes you into the kind of person that you are. Vijay became emotional while talking about Rashmika and how she ensured that their relationship stood the test of time. He said, Shes somebody who always made sure that this relationship got through every obstacle and lasted. Rashmika Mandanna recalls Vijay Deverakonda calling her music shitty on Geetha Govindam sets Recalling her first meeting with Vijay Deverakonda on the sets of Geetha Govindam, Rashmika Mandanna revealed that she initially addressed him as sir because he was more experienced in the industry. She also remembered an incident from the first day of the shoot when Vijay asked her to turn off the music she was playing, leaving her upset. She said, I remember when I first met him on set, I used to call him sir because I was new into the industry and he had done 3-4 films by that time. On Day 1, I was playing this random music on the set, and he goes like, Turn that music off. Vijay interrupted and said, I am a blunt person, and I assume everyone to understand the intention. I feel like, we should be able to talk freely, openly but sometimes when you dont know each other fully, it was stupid of me to assume, shell get it. I just casually said, What is this shitty music that youre playing? I shouted because we had to share a locked caravan in between but because we were not big stars, so half caravan was for her, and half was for me and my team. I screamed, What is this shitty music that you are playing? Rashmika pointed out that it was hardly the ideal thing to hear from a co-actor, especially when she was new to the industry. She said, That is the first thing your co-actor is telling you, right? Vijay responded, What should I say? Rashmika added, Youre absolutely right. Now that I think about it, I wonder what that was all about. Vijay then revealed that the incident had deeply affected Rashmika, although she did not tell him about it at the time. He said, She had tears in her eyes because she thought that he doesnt like me. Rashmika explained, Because it is a new place, new industry. Vijay recalled, She thought it is going to be a torture like this. She told me this much later. Rashmika admitted, Yes, for a long time, I hadnt said it. When Vijay asked why she had not spoken about it earlier, Rashmika explained that she was extremely sensitive at the time and would get emotional over even the smallest things. However, as they began working together, their equation gradually changed. Rashmika said, I was extremely sensitive and everything would tear me up. Going to the set and there were these situations when we started working in the film, he would help me with the dialogues, and everytime I used to call him sir, he used to be like, Stop calling me that. I have a name, call me that then of course, it became Vijay, and then we became friends. She revealed that working on two consecutive films together gave them the opportunity to spend a lot of time with each other, eventually turning them into close friends. Rashmika added, Because we did two back-to-back films with each other, we sort of spent so much time with each other, we were pretty much talking to each other the whole day, you are shooting and prepping for the same film. Hence, it became like. he was my best friend back then, and then much later on, I was like, Okay, I am feeling something, and this is not. Rashmika Mandanna says God had a hand in her relationship with Vijay Deverakonda Rashmika also spoke about how her feelings for Vijay developed over time and said that she believes a higher power guided their relationship. What began as a friendship eventually turned into love, with the couple finding their way to each other. The Animal actor said, I just feel that God has his hand in our relationship, in our love. There is some sort of supreme power who has guided us into this. Hence, the wedding happened and here we are. Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna are currently gearing up for the release of their period drama Ranabaali, which marks another on-screen reunion for the actors. Directed by Rahul Sankrityan and produced by Naveen Yerneni and Y Ravi Shankar under the banner of Mythri Movie Makers, the period action drama is scheduled to release in theatres worldwide on October 16, 2026.

articleTitle: Appointing the Election Commission: An Expert Explains what Constituent Assembly said
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Election Commission
description: The controversy is really about whether the appointment process produces the appearance of independence. The system should be such that selection of Election Commissioners should not only be impartial but also appear to be so.
body_raw: On June 15, 1949, a little-remembered member of the Constituent Assembly named Shibban Lal Saxena rose to object to a deceptively simple clause. The draft Constitution said the President would appoint Indias Election Commissioners. In a parliamentary system, Saxena pointed out, that meant the government of the day would effectively be choosing the referee for its own contests. It is quite possible that some party in power who wants to win the next election may appoint a staunch party-man as the chief Election Commissioner, he warned. Saxena was careful to say he wasnt accusing anyone in the room. He even called the sitting Prime Minister lucky to have the independence and impartiality he did. But that, he said, was exactly the problem with resting a constitutional safeguard on the character of one man. We are making a Constitution for ever, and not only for today, he said. Saxena proposed that appointing an Election Commissioner should require a two-thirds majority in Parliament not to make the Commission answerable to Parliament, but to make it impossible for one party to install its own nominee. The Assembly voted his proposal down. But the warning stayed on the record. The next day, H N Kunzru pushed further. Provincial governments had been kept out of election administration because they might be politically biased. Fair enough, he said - but why assume the Central Government would be any less capable of bias? Is there no danger that the political prejudice of the Central Government may prevail where otherwise the prejudices of the provincial Government might have prevailed? Kunzru wanted safeguards strong enough that Commissioners could act fearlessly, and then delivered a stark warning Worked by people whose integrity cannot be depended upon, democracy will be poisoned at the source. How the Chief Election Commissioner is appointed Even B R Ambedkar didnt dismiss the concern. He called it one of the Drafting Committees greatest headaches. He considered borrowing the American model, where the Senate confirms presidential appointments, but worried it would import its own political games. The eventual compromise the Constitution would establish the Election Commission and shield the Chief Election Commissioner from easy removal, but leave Parliament to legislate the actual appointment mechanism. That became Article 324 - a foundation with the front door deliberately left unlocked. For 74 years, Parliament never walked through that door. No law was passed. Then, in 2023, the Supreme Court did what Parliament hadnt in Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India, it ruled that until Parliament acted, appointments should be recommended by a committee of the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition, and the Chief Justice of India CJI, a structure built to keep any one side from controlling the outcome. Parliament did act and excluded the CJI from the selection committee. The Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, replaced the CJI on the selection panel with a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister. The committee today is the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition, and a minister the Prime Minister himself picks. Two of three seats effectively answer to the same person. The perception of impartiality None of this proves an Election Commissioner appointed under the new law will act improperly, or that the Commission has turned partisan. But it does raise a legitimate constitutional question, and its almost exactly the one Saxena and Kunzru asked in 1949 does this appointment mechanism give the government enough distance from the body that referees elections involving the government itself? Simply put In an election, the government is one of the contestants. The Election Commission is the referee. The question was never whether the referee will actually favour one side. Actually, most of the time, individual Commissioners will do their jobs honestly. The question is whether a system that lets one contestant hold disproportionate sway over who gets to referee should be designed. This is precisely why Saxena refused to let the Constitutions safeguards depend on who happened to be Prime Minister at the time. His argument was structural, not personal. Its a design principle, not a character judgment, and it holds regardless of who sits in which chair today. The system should be such that the selection of the referee should not only be impartial but also appear to be so. Which is also why this controversy isnt really about any individual Commissioners competence or integrity. Its about whether the architecture of appointment produces both the right incentives and the right perception - because in institutions of this kind, the appearance of independence often matters as much as the fact of it. A referee no one fully trusts is, for practical purposes, no referee at all. Seventy-seven years after Kunzrus warning against a flawed electoral machinery, the argument has looped back to that exact source who chooses the people who run the machinery? The Constituent Assembly saw the danger clearly, debated it seriously, and then - perhaps wisely, perhaps not - left the final answer to a Parliament that would one day have to decide for itself. Whether Parliament decided well is the debate we are having today, but whats striking is how little the terms of that debate have changed. Sometimes, the sharpest commentary on the present isnt written by todays columnists at all. It was spoken, on the floor of the Constituent Assembly, by those who could not have known exactly how the future would test their words, only that it eventually would. The author is a former IAS officer and economist. He was CEO of Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana AB-PMJAY and the National Health Authority.

articleTitle: Anshul Kamboj, Auqib Nabi going to be in India’s ODI mix a lot: Shubman Gill
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gill
description: Stating that there is "not much time to experiment" before the 2027 World Cup, India captain Shubman Gill admitted the team must find a way to get its star players back on the field by the next ODI series in New Zealand
body_raw: In a series where the batting mainstays bought themselves a truckload of runs, India were still pushed for a hard reset and review by the time West Indies seized a record 352-run chase in the final ODI in New Chandigarh on Saturday. In as many games that Shubman Gill, Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and KL Rahul piled on five centuries, the bowling department has looked depleted, both in wicket-taking ability and combinations. Within six days, India fiddled with six seam-bowling options, sharing eight wickets between them. The attack often lacked a proven figurehead across phases in the absence of Jasprit Bumrah, Indias only sure-shot bowling pick in a full-strength XI. However, a spate of injuries and overlapping assignments have meant that Indias first-choice players have rarely convened in Gills first year in charge of the ODI side. Now a year left to the World Cup, Gill admitted the team must find a way to get its star players back on the field by the next ODI series in New Zealand, starting next month. I think there is not much time to experiment. The combination that we want to play, hopefully, we get all the players that are available from the next series, and we would like to start playing with the combination that we want in the World Cup, Gill told reporters after Indias five-wicket defeat. Besides Bumrah, India are missing Hardik Pandya, the cornerstone of all combinations the team adopts in the format. In their sustained absence, India have rotated with untested new-ball bowling options with an emphasis on seamers who can contribute with the bat at number eight. The team management rushed domestic First-Class performers Auqib Nabi and Anshul Kamboj for ODI debuts this week despite their limited white-ball records. Touted for the Test cap after a record-breaking Ranji Trophy season, Nabi opened the bowling on debut and leaked 84 runs in 8.4 overs on a batting paradise in Guwahati. Kamboj had seemed far from a national return after his listless Test debut in Manchester last year. Batting number 8, he struck two sixes in nine deliveries. Opening the attack, Kamboj struggled for rhythm against the West Indies top order. In a chase led by captain Shai Hopes unbeaten 162, the Haryana pacer eventually conceded 82 runs in nine overs. Notwithstanding their tough initiations, Gill backed Nabi and Kamboj to feature in the plans moving forward, offering a peek into the emphasis on seamers who can contribute with the bat. Anshul and Auqib are the kind of players who are going to be in the mix a lot. Anshul can bat at number 8. And that number is very crucial for us. We dont know who will be fit at the World Cup. And if we want someone who can bowl and can bat a bit at number 8, Anshul and even Auqib can do the job, the skipper said. They would have liked to have done a much better job. But its a little bit harsh on them. Its not easy to come and be able to deliver straight away. In international cricket, sometimes you require a bit of time. I hope that they learn from their mistakes, from the opportunities that they get, Gill added.

articleTitle: ‘Jude Bellingham can become one of the greatest players of all time’: Roy Keane
articleFeaturedImageAlt: England's Jude Bellingham in action during Nations League match against Croatia. (AP)
description: Former Manchester United captain hails England star's complete performance in 7-0 rout of Croatia, says his work off the ball inspires the entire team
body_raw: Former England footballer Roy Keane believes Jude Bellingham has it in him to become one of the finest players the game has ever seen, describing the England midfielders display in the 7-0 demolition of Croatia as a complete performance. Bellingham was at the heart of Englands biggest-ever win over Croatia, scoring once and setting up three more in Rijeka as Thomas Tuchels side ran riot in the Nations League. The 23-year-old has become the focal point of this England team, registering 13 goal involvements in his last 11 matches since the start of the World Cup. Speaking on ITV after the match, Keane was effusive in his praise for the Real Madrid star, insisting there is still more to come. Theres a lot more to come from Bellingham. He can go on to become one of the greatest players of all time, Keane was quoted as saying by Sky Sports. England thrashed Croatia in a game where skipper Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka scored braces, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers also registered their names on the scoresheet apart from Bellinghams goal. The former Manchester United captain, who was famously exacting in his assessment of players during his own career, singled out Bellinghams work rate as the quality that sets him apart. I have been praising him for being fantastic in possession, but what he is doing out of possession lifts all these players, Keane said. If you have a player who is that good in your team, who is amazing in possession and is playing for Real Madrid and doing brilliant things, but his work rate off the ball, that will inspire all the other players. Croatia, a Gibraltar-type of team Keane also had a sharp assessment of Croatias performance, suggesting England made the worlds 14th-ranked side look like minnows on the night. Keane said England made Croatia, who are ranked 14th in the world, look like a Gibraltar-type of team. Englands victory was as comprehensive as the scoreline suggests, and Keane summed up the display in typically succinct fashion. Everything you would want. A complete performance, he said.

articleTitle: US demands up to $20,000 visa bond from 50 countries; India left out
articleFeaturedImageAlt: us visa, us visa news, us visa bond
description: US visa bond programme requires eligible B1/B2 applicants from 50 countries to post financial guarantees of up to $20,000.
body_raw: The US Department of State introduced a visa-bond programme that designated nationals from 50 countries as requiring financial guarantees up to 20,000 in order to receive tourist and business visas. The mandate has encompassed South Asian nations like Bhutan, Nepal, and Bangladesh. How the US visa bond programme works Pursuant to the Immigration and Nationality Act INA Section 221g3, under which the visa bond programme has been established, a consular officer may require posting of a visa bond before visa issuance. The final rule, issued on August 3 by the State Department, states that any citizen or national travelling on a passport that falls under the list of 50 countries and is eligible for B1 B2 visa is required to post a bond for 10,000, 15,000, or 20,000, adding that the amount is determined at the time of the visa interview. Visa overstay rates determine eligibility As per the INA section, the visa overstay rates are based on the B1 B2 overstay rates from the Department of Homeland Securitys entry exit overstay report, the US State Department stated. Apart from the visa bond requirements, the applicants must also submit a Department of Homeland Security DHS Form I-352. Eligible citizens can pay the required amount through the Department of the Treasurys online payment platform, Pay.gov. US warns applicants about visa bond scams The department has alerted applicants not to post the bond on any website not specifically listed in the instructions received from the consular officer and that the administration would not be held responsible for any money paid outside of its systems. India exempt from US visa-bond requirement In a major respite for Indian nationals, holders of Indian passports have been exempted from the visa-bond obligation. The departments website shows that Nepal and Bangladesh have faced the mandate since January 21, whereas Bhutan was added beginning January 1.
