articleTitle: An old friendship renews itself through an ambitious pact
articleFeaturedImageAlt: An old friendship renews itself through an ambitious pact
description: What TEPA has delivered is not just a headline but something more durable: Tariff lines that have actually moved, and firms making decisions on the strength of it
body_raw: The last time I wrote for this newspaper was in February, when I arrived in Delhi for the AI Impact Summit. Eight months and one G7 meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi later, I am back in Delhi. This time, I am here to mark a significant anniversary The first anniversary of the entry into force of the Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement TEPA between the EFTA states and India. I am returning as a guest of the Republic of India on a state visit, demonstrating how what began as a trade negotiation has evolved into a partnership between two economies and a friendship between two democracies. Anniversaries invite summaries. I would rather treat this one as a checkpoint. What TEPA has delivered is not just a headline but something more durable Tariff lines that have actually moved, and firms making decisions on the strength of it. Switzerland is bringing precision machinery, pharmaceuticals, MedTech and specialty chemicals to this agreement - the kind of intermediate goods and technical capability that will feed into Indian manufacturing rather than compete with it. It is too early to declare results after a year, but the direction is clear. Tariff schedules and procedures do not change behaviour by themselves they only do so when companies decide that the change is substantial enough to plan around. From our conversations with Swiss businesses, we can see that they are in the early stages of making this calculation. The figure that will matter more than any other over the next decade and a half is the 100 billion investment and job-creation goal tied to TEPA - the first time an Indian trade agreement has linked market access to a concrete investment goal rather than tariff schedules alone. Beyond this is a broader ambition To deepen economic ties, encourage long-term investment, create opportunities for employment and strengthen cooperation between companies, institutions and people. The essential work of building institutions is well underway. A dedicated Desk has been set up to support EFTA companies with a smooth, informed, and confident investment experience. This is a partnership in which both sides gain. India gains capital, technology, and easier access to a market for high-value goods. Switzerland gains something we need just as much A large, fast-growing trading partner at a moment when global trade is more fragile and unpredictable than it was even a year ago. Diversification is a strategic priority. One more point deserves emphasis because it distinguishes TEPA from an older generation of trade deals. The TEPA carries meaningful provisions on labour standards, environmental protection and responsible business conduct. They reflect commitments that India and the EFTA states made together, and they show what a modern trade agreement can achieve. Alongside the trade and economic relations between our countries, there is a broader relationship Scientific and research cooperation that go back decades, a steady flow of Indian students and professionals through Swiss universities and technical institutes, growing numbers of Indian visitors to the Alps, and Swiss tourists drawn to India. There is also a substantial diplomatic relationship that has produced a dense web of bilateral agreements on science and technology, aviation, taxation, and education over the decades. None of this is reflected in the trade balance, yet it arguably makes the trade balance possible, a level of familiarity and trust between our two societies that has been quietly built up over many years, visit by visit and exchange by exchange, long before anyone thought to call it a partnership. In 2028, Switzerland and India will mark 80 years since signing their Treaty of Friendship, a document that promised perpetual peace and unalterable friendship. Those are large words for any two nations to live up to. But I think we have. Each era renewed it in the terms available to it. Scientific exchange in one decade, student visas in another, now a trade agreement with a 100-billion ambition attached to it. The TEPA, but also the Migration and Mobility Partnership and the Young Professional Agreement to be signed are simply todays answer to a promise made almost 80 years ago A practical framework that can deepen our friendship through mutual support and a shared interest in sustainable growth, prosperity, and long-term success. The writer is president, Switzerland

articleTitle: Defector MPs to dissenting MLAs: AAP cracks widen on eve of Punjab polls
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Defector MPs to dissenting MLAs: How AAP cracks widen on eve of Punjab polls
description: AAP's Sukhveer Singh Maiserkhana, suspended after flagging teacher shortage in govt schools, is among a growing number of party MLAs who have faced action after criticising the Bhagwant Mann govt's functioning.
body_raw: Sukhveer Singh Maiserkhana has now joined a growing number of the dissenting MLAs of the ruling Aam Aadmi Party AAP in Punjab, who have found themselves on the wrong side of the AAP leadership after raising questions about the functioning of the Bhagwant Mann-led party government. The AAP suspended Maur MLA Maiserkhana Saturday for alleged anti-party activities, barely an hour after he released an emotional video accusing the Mann government of failing to address teacher shortage in state-run schools, including those attended by his two children. Maiserkhana is the only MLA in the 117-member Punjab Assembly who sends his children to government schools. He said he had repeatedly raised the issue with the government and the party leadership, including Chief Minister Mann and former Delhi Deputy CM Manish Sisodia, but to no avail. I am not fighting against schools I am fighting for them, he said, adding that he could no longer accept the prevailing situation. Asking what wrong he had done to the AAP, he also indicated that he may be denied party ticket in the Punjab Assembly elections slated for February 2027. Seizing on Maiserkhanas comments, the Opposition-including the Congress, Shiromani Akali Dal SAD and BJP-slammed the Mann government, underlining that the AAPs own MLA has debunked its claims about bringing an education revolution in the state. On its part, the AAP rejected Maiserkhanas allegations as false, accusing him of attempting to defame the party. AAP discontent There are other AAP MLAs who have run into trouble after openly questioning the party dispensation on various issues. In September 2025, Sanour MLA Harmit Singh Pathanmajra had criticised the AAP governments handling of the floods and objected to what he described as interference by the partys Delhi leadership. Subsequently, his security cover was withdrawn. He was also booked by Patiala police in a three-year-old case on charges of rape, cheating and criminal intimidation. Pathanmajra claimed that this case was politically motivated and accused the government of targeting him. The Opposition, too, linked the police action to his dissent, even as the AAP maintained that law was taking its course against wrongdoing. Before Pathanmajra, Amritsar North MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh was suspended from the AAP for five years in June 2025 after he opposed the arrest of SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia in a disproportionate assets case, questioning the manner in which the Vigilance Bureau had conducted the raid. Oppn sharpens attacks The latest rumbling within the AAP has come against the backdrop of a major rupture in the party in April, when seven of its 10 Rajya Sabha MPs crossed over to the BJP. Six of them including Raghav Chadha, Sandeep Pathak, Vikramjit Singh Sahney, Rajinder Gupta, Ashok Mittal and Harbhajan Singh were from Punjab. The seven MPs invoked the two-thirds defection provision and their merger with the BJP was subsequently accepted by the Rajya Sabha Chairman. For a party that stormed to power by sweeping the Punjab polls in 2022, winning 92 of the states 117 seats, the exodus of its Rajya Sabha MPs and growing number of dissenting MLAs have led to the Opposition cornering the AAP over its internal cohesion ahead of the 2027 elections. New Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee PPCC president Pargat Singh alleged Maiserkhana had exposed the false education revolution claims and dictatorship of the AAP government. Noting that Maiserkhana was the only MLA who had enrolled his children in a government school, Singh said that like many Punjabis the former had also been influenced by the AAPs claims about the Delhi model and its education reforms. Today, the MLA Maiserkhana has himself brought out the reality of the shortage of teachers and facilities in schools, as well as how his demands for schools have been ignored, he said. Pargat Singh asked whether the voice of any AAP MLA was being heard on issues concerning Punjab and its people. He alleged that Punjab was being run by the AAP leaders from Delhi without keeping in view the interests of the state. Singh also appealed to other AAP MLAs to find the courage to stand up for Punjab and oppose what he called the dictatorship of those controlling the government. With only a few months left for the elections, the fight now is for Punjabs voice, its rights and its future, he said. Defending his party, state AAP general secretary Harchand Singh Barsat told The Indian Express that dissent surfaces even within a family. But if the leaders have any issue due to any dissatisfaction, they should raise it at the party level. They should be disciplined. If dissent is aired publicly then the party has the right to take disciplinary action, he said.

articleTitle: This building in Bastar used to house a security camp. Now, it is home to 150 students
articleFeaturedImageAlt: This building in Bastar used to house a security camp. Now, it is home to 150 students
description: The campus in Bhatpal houses two hostels for Scheduled Tribe boys studying in pre-matric and post-matric levels. Another hostel will come up for girls in Abujhmad in a few days.
body_raw: Until recently, this building in Chhattisgarhs Bastar region used to house a security camp, aiding the forces fight against Maoists. Since August, instead of paramilitary personnel, it has been home to students from nearby Maoism-hit areas, including Abujhmad that has seen over a 100 Maoists, including top leaders, being killed in the last two years. Hundreds of others have surrendered. The Bhatpal campus currently houses two hostels for Scheduled Tribe boys studying in pre-matric and post-matric levels. The objective was to address one of the key challenges faced by children from distant and difficult-to-access areas - access to safe accommodation close to school. Previously, this particular area Bhatpal had no post-matric boys hostel, making it difficult for tribal students to pursue higher education, said Narayanpur collector Namrata Jain. With the establishment of a post-matric hostel for tribal youths for the first time, students from remote areas can now continue their education with access to safe accommodation and better educational opportunities, said Jain, who recently visited the Bhatpal hostel kitchen and reviewed the quality of food. The security camp was established here 15 years ago. The pre-matric hostel caters to students from Classes 6 to 10 and is currently accommodating 114 students. The post-matric hostel, for students of Classes 11 and 12, with a sanctioned capacity of 50 students, is currently accommodating 39 students. Going by the response to the boys hostels-the pre-matric one is running beyond its sanctioned capacity of 100 students-the authorities are planning to set up more such accommodations. The next one is coming up in Kurushnar, at the entrance of Abujhmad or Maad, as it is locally known from the Narayanpur end. In 2011, a residential school was built here after permission from Maoists who demanded the school be made without a concrete ceiling or a high boundary wall to ensure forces do not start camping there. With the Maoists now gone, the security camp established less than a decade ago is being turned into a girls hostel, which is expected to be ready in a few days. Though Bhatpal hostel is away from Maad, it houses students from villages in and around the area. These include Kohkameta, Madamnaar, Orrcha, Nelwad, Chote Donger, Korenda, Chimdi, Remavand and Benoor. One such student is Komendra from Rajbeda-located around 22 kilometres away. For the Class 12 student, the opening of the post-matric hostel has provided significant relief and taken off the burden of additional expenditure on accommodation. Earlier this year, a budget of Rs 100 crore was allocated towards turning Maad and Jagargunda in the Bastar region, which were known as hotbeds of Maoism, into modern education cities.

articleTitle: Ujjain is preparing for 40 crore pilgrims. What will the ancient city lose?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Hotels, roads and the race against time: Inside Ujjain’s Simhastha 2028 makeover
description: With the state government approving 128 projects worth Rs 13,851 crore, Ujjain is being transformed at a pace rarely seen in the temple town’s modern history as it races to prepare for the 2028 Simhastha — from new highways, bridges and ghats to five-star hotels.
body_raw: Ujjain has always resisted the march of time, clinging to its ancient city of temples, ghats, bazaars and British-era offices. Now, as Ujjain prepares for Simhastha 2028, its maps are being redrawn, hurtling the sleepy temple town towards a new modernity - carved through its old streets with bulldozers, widened roads and concrete. On September 27, a crowd gathered outside the Shahi Masjid, where the administration was preparing to remove the portion of the mosque within the proposed road alignment, as protests raged over road-widening projects in Ujjain ahead of the 2028 Simhastha. Hours later, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav took an axe to his grandfathers ancestral home in Abdalpura. The demolitions came as the administration raced against time for the Simhastha Mela 2028, for which the government has approved 128 projects worth about Rs 13,851 crore across 10 departments. For Yadav, Simhastha has become his governments defining project, with the administration effectively mobilised around a single task transforming the ancient temple town before pilgrims arrive. On the ground, the transformation is unfolding on a scale rarely seen in Ujjains modern history. Highways are being carved into the citys approaches, railway lines and bypasses are being built, roads and bridges widened, kilometres of new ghats taking shape along the Shipra, and water and sewerage networks being laid underground. What is taking shape is not simply a city preparing for a festival, but a centuries-old temple town being physically remade into a modern pilgrimage city. Simhastha Mela Authority director Jagdish Aggarwals office in Kothi Road, a leafy neighbourhood, is less a conventional government chamber these days than a control room for one of Madhya Pradeshs biggest infrastructure exercises. Project officers come in with updates, meetings are held with swamis and other stakeholders, and meetings with the chief minister are woven into a schedule dominated by Simhastha. Every Thursday, Aggarwal sits with the collector and deputy collector for a review devoted to the same question how to get Ujjain ready for 2028? We are preparing keeping in mind the possibility of around 40 crore people coming to Ujjain, Aggarwal said, explaining why projects that would otherwise appear excessive for Ujjain are being taken up simultaneously. But theres also a human cost involved the eroding trust among residents. Yasin Khan, a local, welcomed the road-widening project but frowned upon the speed at which the administration proceeded. When the houses were marked in my neighbourhood, both Hindu and Muslim families came out and demolished portions of the houses ourselves. But the administration barely took us into confidence. Its better to demolish on your own than wait for the administration to come with a bulldozer. Changing Ujjain The most visible changes are on Ujjains roads. The Ujjain-Indore six-laning project, estimated at Rs 1,692 crore, is under construction, while a separate Indore-Ujjain greenfield four-lane corridor, estimated at Rs 2,935 crore, is also being developed, SMA officials said. A 98.73-km Ujjain-Jaora greenfield four-lane corridor, costing about Rs 5,017 crore, received its foundation stone in July. Planned with seven flyovers, three railway overbridges, eight major bridges, 22 medium bridges, 36 underpasses and 430 culverts, it is targeted for completion by December 2027. It is intended to provide an east-west connection towards Jaora and the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway while taking long-distance traffic away from the city, SMA officials said. More than 80 percent of road and connectivity works had reached the ground, with the road component around 70 percent complete. Around 15 bridges are under construction, and we expect five or six to be ready for inauguration by December, Aggarwal said. More than 10 five-star hotels are either coming up or planned in Ujjain, Aggarwal said, alongside smaller hotels and guest houses. Along the Shipra, the government is building approximately 29.2 km of new ghats and associated works, stretching from the Shani temple area towards the Nagda bypass. The Rs 778-crore project is intended to spread bathing and pilgrim movement over a longer stretch of the river, officials said. At Gaughat, Akram Khan, a project supervisor for a private company, said they would meet the deadline for the restored ghat by December. The restoration is taking place against an old British water works department office, built in the 1930s. Only the old English chimney remains as the Madhya Pradesh government races ahead with the modern ghat. We began work in May and employed over 100 workers per day, paying them at least Rs 800 per day to finish this work. The reason we can race through the project is that the governments fully focused on this. From making roads to providing us with electricity and water connections, they raced through all that to help our project, Akram said. The second major riverfront project is the Rs 919.94-crore Kanh closed-duct diversion scheme, intended to prevent polluted water carried by the Kanh River from entering the Shipra. The scheme involves a 30.15-km diversion system, including an 18.15-km cut-and-cover section and a 12-km tunnel. Inside Ujjain, the road programme is being executed through municipal packages, with roads widened around the old city and Mahakal area. One of the most contentious stretches is the road from Khajurwali Masjid towards Ganesh Chowk, where widening work has now moved to the ground and brought the Shahi Masjid within the road alignment. Protests - and race against time Across Ujjains old neighbourhoods, the transformation is not happening only behind construction-site barricades. It is happening at peoples front doors. Hindu and Muslim families alike have been taking hammers and pickaxes to portions of homes, shops and religious structures marked for demolition under the new road alignments. Lokendra Nigam, a cloth merchant from Chattri Chowk, lamented the removal of a small portion of his shop. We are doing it for the Simhastha. Of course, we understand the devotees need space to move. But we should be adequately compensated. We feel the authorities dont listen to us. At the Simhastha division of the Madhya Pradesh Public Works Department, Executive Engineer Praful Jain studies the map of Ujjain on his computer, tracking projects for Simhastha 2028. The PWDs Simhastha division has 20 works underway, Jain said, including an underpass, a bridge and road and connectivity projects. Among the most significant is the 629-metre Hari Phatak underpass, intended to provide an alternative route towards Mahakal Lok. More than 100 structures, on average, have been identified for impact across the underpass and elevated-corridor projects, Jain said. The focus, he said, is on resource and manpower planning, machinery planning and resolving issues on multiple fronts simultaneously, so that construction can begin at the appropriate time rather than waiting for one project to finish before another starts. Jain said the department is increasingly relying on precast technology to compress timelines. Beams, columns and girders can be prepared in advance and brought to sites for assembly. The road network is also intended to create capacity beyond the festival. Four-lane and six-lane interconnected roads are being developed at different locations, Jain said. The Simhastha works, in that sense, are being designed as infrastructure that can continue to serve the city after the festival. We want to develop international-level infrastructure across the world, like the Temple Mount in Israel or Mecca in Saudi Arabia.

articleTitle: He swore and hung up. Hours later, 3 kidnapped Gujaratis were free
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Held in Ethiopia on ‘dunki’ route to US, cousins freed as police reach out to ‘kidnapper’
description: Three cousins from Mehsana allegedly on the illegal ‘dunki’ route to the US were captured by ‘Baba Khan’, who wanted more than Rs 1 crore ransom. But Gujarat Police and the family bargained, and the Ethiopian authorities rescued the cousins in Addis Ababa.
body_raw: When cousins Mamta 30, Rutvik 23, and Mayuri 27 reached Langhnaj in Gujarats Mehsana district on October 1, their first stop, even before they went home, was the local police station. This was a procedural requirement-but the cousins also wanted to meet the officers whose remarkable negotiating skills over phone had extricated them from the clutches of a gang of abductors in Ethiopia. The cousins, all between the ages of 23 and 30 from a farming family in Vadasma village in North Gujarat, had hoped to travel to the United States. However, given the severe restrictions on migration by the Trump administration, they had allegedly chosen to take an illegal, circuitous dunki route. They never made it. The cousins were allegedly waylaid in Ethiopia, in eastern Africa, not far from the theatre of hostilities between the US and Iran, abducted, and held hostage for a week, sources in the Mehsana Police said. When they were finally able to board Ethiopian Airlines Flight ET 640 to Mumbai from Addis Ababa on September 30 evening, all that the cousins had with them were their passports-everything else had allegedly been kept by their abductors. The cousins told the police that the abductors had, however, booked the tickets for the flight back and released them without extracting a ransom. For this unexpected turn of events, the cousins have Inspector A M Gehlot to thank-and his long negotiations with the suspected leader of the kidnappers, a man who police sources said spoke in Hindi and identified himself as Baba Khan. This, in essence, is the story of an alleged attempt at illegal entry into the US by two women and a man, their abduction and, ultimately, their extraordinary escape back to India, according to Mehsana Police and Inspector Gehlot. Mehsana Superintendent of Police Himanshu Solanki and Collector S K Prajapati were not available for comment. Sources in the Ministry of External Affairs MEA told The Indian Express that three Indian nationals had been kidnapped in Ethiopia, and rescued by the local authorities there. They were rescued by Ethiopian authorities in Addis Ababa. Our Embassy in Addis Ababa was constantly in touch with the local authorities on this matter. Indian law enforcement authorities also contributed to the efforts. The three Indian nationals returned home on October 1, MEA sources said. Mehsana district is known for its residents desire to migrate to the United States, with locked homes across several villages in this region bearing testimony to this trend. Vadasma lies about halfway between Gandhinagar and Mehsana cities, and about 4.5 km from Langhnaj, which is on the main road. On September 29, members of the cousins family filed a missing persons report at Langhnaj police station, saying they had not heard from the three since their last call on September 22. The cousins had allegedly told their relatives that they were in Canada. They told their families that they would now contact them from the US. But then they went incommunicado, Inspector Gehlot said. In fact, the cousins were allegedly already in the custody of Baba Khan at the time, and had been coerced to lie to their families and not disclose that they had been abducted and were in Ethiopia. According to police sources, the three had left India on different flights from Jaipur and Delhi on September 21, and reached the Bole International Airport in Addis Ababa via the Middle East. Thereafter, investigations revealed, the agent who had booked their tickets abducted them, stole their belongings, and demanded a ransom of Rs 1 crore USD 1,05,000 for their release. The cousins extended family and police were alerted about the abduction by a youth from Kadi town in Mehsana, identified as Vansh, police sources said. This youth had returned home after being kidnapped in Ethiopia, and after having allegedly paid a ransom of Rs 40 lakh, the sources said. Officers from the Langhnaj police station immediately persuaded the families of the three cousins to file missing persons complaints. By then, Baba Khan too had reached out to a contact in Dangarva village, whom police sources identified as Aditya Panchal. This person directed the cousins family to an agent from Vadodara, identified as Bhargav Patel. But police found that Patel had already gone underground. Information on the case was shared with the Local Intelligence Branch LIB of Mehsana Police, the Gujarat Police headquarters at Gandhinagar, and the MEA in New Delhi, the sources said. They said that Langhnaj police decided to take Aditya Panchal into confidence, and get him to engage with the alleged abductor in their presence. Panchal, a member of the cousins family, and two police personnel spoke to Baba Khan continuously over several calls. They tried to convince Baba Khan that the middle-class family was engaged in farming, and couldnt afford to pay the huge ransom, especially as they had already paid Rs 60 lakh to the network-at Rs 20 lakh per person-to ferry them to the US, Inspector Gehlot said. Following the negotiations, the kidnappers brought their demand down to Rs 15 lakh. They said this was the lowest they were willing to go, at Rs 5 lakh per person, Gehlot said. By then, investigators had begun to suspect that Baba Khan was only an alias. The man on the other end would speak on WhatsApp voice calls, and would never agree to come on video, which might offer police clues as to his identity, sources said. At one point, on September 30, the family representative told Baba Khan that they could not afford to pay him even Rs 5 lakh, let alone the Rs 15 lakh that he was demanding, Gehlot said. This was followed by some tense moments. The abductor seemed very angry, and he swore and hung up, police sources said. But later that day, the family got a video call from an unknown number. When they answered, they saw Mamta, Rutvik, and Mayuri on the screen. The cousins told them they had borrowed someones phone to make the call. They said that the abductors had dropped them 2 km from the airport and had booked their tickets back to India, the sources said. The three landed in Mumbai around 2 am on October 1, and headed to Gujarat. The cousins told police that in Addis Ababa, they were taken to an isolated residence, tied and blindfolded. Rutvik was beaten but there was no mistreatment with the two women, Gehlot said. The three also told police that they did not know Vansh, the youth whose tip-off allegedly helped police get on their trail. According to sources, the family had decided to send the cousins via the dunki route after the US government rejected Mamtas visa application. Since they were sending Mamta, they thought that the two younger cousins could also start new lives in the US, and decided to send all the three together, Inspector Gehlot said. Police are now trying to trace Bhargav Patel, the alleged travel agent who is suspected to be part of Baba Khans network.

articleTitle: Omani pilot may have shut off flydubai plane’s engines after Tel Aviv crash plan failed, says report
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Flydubai Dubai-Tel Aviv Flight News
description: The Omani co-pilot may have shut off the engines of a flydubai Boeing 737 after his plan to crash it in Tel Aviv failed.
body_raw: The Omani co-pilot accused of attacking his captain on a flydubai flight may have shut off the engines of the Boeing 737 after his main plan went wrong, according to the Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera. The paper says investigators are checking whether he moved the two engine fuel switches from Run to Cutoff. The paper says the co-pilot, Hammam al-Hammami, first planned to kill Captain Smit Machchhar, an Indian national, fly the plane to Tel Aviv and crash it into a tall building, citing Israeli intelligence. When that failed, it says, he tried to crash the jet in the desert. The plane lost 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds before passengers and two off-duty pilots took control and landed it at Tabuk in Saudi Arabia. A social media account believed to be linked to Hamam al-Hammami repeatedly mentions stomping on women. Photo LinkedIn The flight was carrying 174 passengers, most of them Israeli, NBC News said. Officials say the investigation is at an early stage. US officials and a former Israeli security official told NBC News that early signs point to a lone attacker, not a group or a government. Authorities have not released the suspects name. NBC News identified him from sources. How the attack began Corriere della Sera built its account from the flight crews reports to safety authorities, people familiar with the incident, airport staff, air traffic controllers and data from flight-tracking platforms. It says al-Hammami pretended to pray in the cockpit, took out the crash axe, came up behind the captain and attacked him. Machchhar first thought a broken part of the aircraft had hit him. He understood he was under attack when the blows kept coming. His head was badly bruised and his arm was almost cut off. He tried to open the cockpit door, the co-pilot shut it, and he opened it again. A woman whose daughter was in the toilet heard thudding from the cockpit. She told other passengers and two off-duty pilots on board. Several passengers ran into the cockpit and found the captain in a pool of blood. The evidence on the engines The paper points to videos filmed during the struggle that show the cabin emergency lights on at high altitude. On a Boeing 737 these lights come on when the main electrical power is lost, which happens if the generators are off or both engines have shut down. Corriere della Sera says al-Hammami saw his plan could not work and switched off the autopilot and pushed the control stick forward. In about 30 seconds the plane lost 16,000 feet. Its speed passed 970 kilometres an hour, which damaged the tail rudder. The paper says he also tried to damage the controls before passengers overpowered him. Yaniv Hayoun, a plumber, pulled the control stick back and stopped the plane from dropping further. At one point the plane lost height again, probably because the engines were giving no thrust, the paper said. It says the two off-duty pilots then returned the plane to level flight, and the flight data fit with the engines being restarted. These points come from one newspapers account. The findings of the official investigation have not been released. I knew I couldnt let all of them die Saudi air traffic controllers told the crew to turn back and then to make an emergency landing at Tabuk. The pilots landed the plane safely. Machchhar was taken to hospital, and the co-pilot was handed to Saudi authorities, Corriere della Sera said. Machchhar spoke from a hospital in Abu Dhabi on Friday in a video call that was released by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said he could feel the plane going down before he got the cockpit door open so that passengers and crew could step in. He said he fought for his own life but knew he could not let everyone on board die, NBC News said. Lone attacker or wider plot? Emirati authorities are leading the investigation. They said on Saturday that the co-pilot attacked the captain with a crash axe and tried to take over the controls in an attempted terrorist attack. The UAE Attorney General, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, said investigators are working to establish the full circumstances, the motive and any links. Passengers embark on a FlyDubai aircraft at Ben Gurion International Airport, near Tel Aviv, Israel. AP Photo US officials briefed on the case told NBC News that early signs point to one man acting alone. Shalom Ben Hanan, a former official of Shin Bet, Israels domestic security agency, said it looks like a case inspired by content online. He said the final findings are needed to show whether a group or a state is behind it. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Friday that investigators were checking whether someone sent the attacker. President Donald Trump raised the chance of Iranian involvement on Thursday and threatened new strikes if Iran was behind it. A senior US official told NBC News earlier that there were no signs Iran directed or took part in the attack. Israel calls the incident a terror attack. It is now looking into how an Omani pilot was cleared to fly into Tel Aviv. Israel has no diplomatic relations with Oman, and the case goes against its security policy.

articleTitle: ‘Nobody’s prepared for a divorce’: Actor Shefali Shah on her first marriage
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shefali Shah was last seen in Delhi Crime 3
description: The Delhi Crime actor says her memoir, The Audacity of Being, doesn't reveal what went wrong in her first marriage. It's about what happens when any relationship falls apart.
body_raw: Im not naming anyone in the book. Im not even getting into what happened or didnt happen. Im just talking about what happens on a general scale when people get married and nobodys prepared for a divorce. Thats Shefali Shah writing about the end of her first marriage in The Audacity of Being, her memoir-in-essays published by Bloomsbury India. She spoke to The Indian Express in an exclusive interview. Shah was earlier married to actor Harsh Chhaya. In 2000, she married filmmaker-producer Vipul Amrutlal Shah, with whom she has two sons, Aryaman and Maurya. People often go into marriage with the idea of a happily-ever-after, she believes. Marriage may not necessarily pan out the way it is. And then, you just have no option but to deal with it. Asked about the candour with which she has written about her life, including the breakdown of her first marriage, Shah said, There was nothing to really hide about. I think Ive written about it very respectfully. Im just talking about any marriage falling off the brink. Theres an entire thing about when you realise your marriage is falling apart. So its, I think, about the failure of a relationship. The book covers much more. Love and its familiar aches, divorce and remarriage, friendships and community, ageing as a Bollywood actor, creative self-doubt, body image and the trials of parenting. Shah describes the book as a sort of memoir. When it was announced, she said, Nothing in my life warrants a memoir. And yet, I chose to tell a story only I have the copyright to. I dont promise an ingenious book, but what I do promise is absolute honesty. Shah has held a distinctive place in Indian entertainment for more than three decades, with films such as Satya, Monsoon Wedding, Dil Dhadakne Do, Jalsa and Darlings, and the Emmy-winning series Delhi Crime. She is aware that readers may interpret her accounts differently. When you put yourself out there in the public domain, whether its on camera or when you are writing something, or even on Instagram, people will have a point of view, she said.

articleTitle: Can gut bacteria quietly raise Alzheimer’s risk? New study has clues
articleFeaturedImageAlt: alzheimers
description: New research shows that higher levels of this bacterial product may be associated with changes in the brain linked to Alzheimer’s disease
body_raw: What happens in the gut may have consequences far beyond digestion. Scientists are increasingly discovering that the trillions of microorganisms living in our intestines produce chemicals that can enter the bloodstream and influence metabolism, inflammation and the immune system. Now, researchers are investigating whether one of these microbial chemicals could also affect the ageing brain. The molecule attracting attention is imidazole propionate, or ImP, which is produced by some gut bacteria. What is imidazole propionate? ImP is a small molecule made when certain bacteria break down an amino acid found in proteins. New research shows that higher levels of this bacterial product may be associated with changes in the brain linked to Alzheimers disease. The findings, highlighted in a University of WisconsinMadison research announcement on October 3, came from research involving both humans and mice. What did the researchers find? The researchers studied 1,196 adults who did not have cognitive impairment. People who had higher concentrations of ImP in their blood tended to perform less well on certain cognitive tests. They also had more biological markers associated with Alzheimers disease. The researchers additionally found associations between some ImP-producing gut bacteria and Alzheimers-related markers. But there is an important distinction here an association is not proof of cause and effect. Having a higher level of ImP does not mean that a person will develop Alzheimers disease. To explore whether there might be a biological mechanism behind the association, the researchers turned to mice. Could a gut chemical affect the brain? In experiments, mice exposed to ImP over prolonged periods developed changes resembling some features of Alzheimers disease. These included alterations involving beta-amyloid and tau, two proteins closely associated with Alzheimers. In Alzheimers disease, beta-amyloid can accumulate as plaques, while abnormal tau can form tangles inside brain cells. The researchers also found evidence that ImP can affect the blood-brain barrier. The blood-brain barrier is a protective system formed largely by specialised cells lining blood vessels in the brain. It helps regulate which substances in the bloodstream can enter brain tissue. If this protective barrier becomes impaired, it may contribute to processes involved in brain ageing and neurological disease. Taken together, the findings suggest a possible pathway Certain gut bacteria produce ImP. This enters the bloodstream, may affect the blood-brain barrier and brain cells, triggering changes associated with Alzheimers disease. Does this mean probiotics could prevent Alzheimers? No-not based on this study. The research did not test whether probiotic supplements can lower ImP levels or reduce the risk of Alzheimers disease. Probiotics contain different strains of bacteria, and one probiotic product cannot be assumed to have the same effects as another. In addition, the gut microbiome is extremely complex. Simply adding bacteria to the gut does not necessarily mean that the overall microbial environment will change in a predictable way. The study also did not identify a particular food or diet that can reliably eliminate ImP. Alzheimers disease has many risk factors It is also important not to view Alzheimers disease as the result of a single molecule-or even a single biological pathway. Age is the strongest known risk factor, while genetics, cardiovascular health and other factors can also influence risk. Blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes, physical activity, smoking, sleep and overall health are among the factors researchers continue to study. The gut microbiome may eventually turn out to be one piece of this much larger puzzle. Why is the finding important? Looking at the chemicals produced by those bacteria may provide a more precise way of studying the gutbrain connection. Researchers can now ask questions such as Which gut bacteria produce ImP? What causes those bacteria to make more or less of it? How much ImP enters the bloodstream? Can lowering ImP levels alter Alzheimers-related changes? Could targeting ImP or the bacteria that produce it be safe and effective in people? These are the questions that future studies will need to answer. If future research in humans shows that lowering ImP can reduce Alzheimers-related changes or help preserve cognitive function, this early finding could eventually become the basis for a new therapeutic strategy.

articleTitle: Two books to read: A family shaped by Partition, a girl who disappeared
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Book covers of No One Gets Out Of Here Alive by Ranbir Sidhu and The Fourth Girl by Arefa Tehsin
description: Ranbir Sidhu's Partition memoir No One Gets Out Of Here Alive and Arefa Tehsin's feminist thriller The Fourth Girl both earn a hit this fortnight
body_raw: Welcome to Quick Verdict, a fortnightly column where every book gets a hit or miss. This week How Ranbir Sidhus No One Gets Out Of Here Alive uses his parents deaths to ask who they might have been without Partition, and how Arefa Tehsins The Fourth Girl turns a decades-old disappearance into a feminist mystery spanning India and Sri Lanka. Ranbir Sidhus No One Gets Out Of Here Alive Verdict HIT Ranbir Sidhus No One Gets Out Of Here Alive is a Partition memoir that discusses the death and grief that followed it. The book opens with the death of Sidhus father, and then goes back in time to nine months earlier, when his mother died. In their deaths, he looks back at their lives and tries to understand who they were beyond being his parents, and who they might have been had Partition not happened. Blending elements of essay, travelogue and history, Sidhu traces the geographical space of Punjab, where his parents were born and died, against its history of violence and its demand for a masculinity that deformed the lives of both women and men. In capturing beautifully the subtle nuances of the parent-child relationship, Sidhu makes the memoir an engrossing and poignant read for anyone interested in decoding the complexities of intergenerational relationships and everything that affects them. Reviewed by Anusree K C Arefa Tehsins The Fourth Girl Verdict HIT Arefa Tehsins The Fourth Girl is a feminist mystery thriller telling the story of three women with varied backgrounds Bhairavi, a Dalit who converted to Christianity Qailah, a Muslim and Rajvi, a Rajput. The fourth girl joins their yearly trip to the fictional Sumer forest unexpectedly, and then disappears. The incident changes the course of their lives. Twenty years later, the three meet at the funeral of a famous journalist in Sri Lanka, with another journalist digging up the death. Tehsin, who has published over 20 novels, grew up in Udaipur, the novels base setting. She now shuttles between India and Sri Lanka, introducing the other setting of the novel Colombo. The author doesnt shy away from depicting the ingrained patriarchy, the systemic colourism, casteism and classism of Indian society, but it is her writing that makes the third-person narrative feel like a first-person one. Every time you think you know something, a new question pops up in your head, and you cant help but turn the page. The Fourth Girl is definitely a relevant read in this day and age. articleTitle: Fahadh Faasil says ‘won’t get half of Rs 300 cr’ as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Fahadh Faasil has responded to the worldwide box office collection of Bethlehem Kudumba Unit.
description: Fahadh Faasil, who has co-produced Nivin Pauly-starrer blockbuster romantic comedy Bethlehem Kudumba Unit, has clarified that he would get only a small fraction of the film's Rs 300 crore plus worldwide gross box office collection.
body_raw: Filmmaker Girish ADs romantic comedy Bethlehem Kudumba Unit has amassed over Rs 300 crore at the worldwide box office, emerging as the highest grossing Malayalam film ever globally. The Nivin Pauly and Mamitha Baiju-starrer has begun receding from cinemas after 40 days, and following its OTT premiere on JioHotstar this past Friday on October 2. Fahadh Faasils clarification on Bethlehem Kudumba Unit global gross Malayalam superstar Fahadh Faasil, who serves as one of the producers on Bethlehem Kudumba Unit, reacted to the unprecedented Rs 332 crore gross earned by the film, claiming that he or any of the other co-producers would end up receiving only a fraction of that figure. None of us will get even half of this Rs 300 crore that they are talking about. That is the gross collection, he argued in a chat with Cue Studio. Even though Bethlehem Kadamba Unit has earned a worldwide gross of Rs 326 crore, there are a lot of variables at pay. Out of this amount, around half of the chunk usually goes to the international agents, exhibitors, and distributors. Only after deducting the Goods Services Tax GST does the producers get the remainder of the amount. In the case of Bethlehem Kadamba Unit, its produced by Bhavana Studios, which is owned by the three producers of the film - Fahadh Faasil, actor-filmmaker Dileesh Pothan, and screenwriter Syam Pushkaran. Its distributed by Bhavana Release, Future RunUp Films, and Mythri Movie Makers, best known for backing Allu Arjuns blockbuster Telugu action thriller franchise Pushpa. The fact that Bethlehem has been a success is something that makes me very happy and proud. It is not just me. There is Girish, Shyam, and Dileesh. I see this as a collective success of all of us. I dont see it as my success alone, added Fahadh. Its co-written by Girish AD and Kiran Josey, and also features an ensemble cast including Suresh Krishna, Vinay Forrt, and Shyam Mohan among others. Bethlehem Kudumba Unit box office collection Bethlehem Kudumba Unit released in cinemas on August 21. It scored an opening day of 4.90 crore from 1507 screens at the domestic box office. It earned over Rs 20 crore during its opening weekend, and over Rs 50 crore in its opening week. It slipped down marginally to Rs 49.85 crore in its second week, and Rs 33.30 crore in the third week, as per Sacnilk. By the end of the second week, Bethlehem Kudumba Unit had crossed the Rs 100 crore mark at the domestic box office. Its fourth week earnings dropped by almost half to Rs 16.79 crore, and by another half to Rs 8.80 crore in week 5. By the end of its sixth week, the film has earned over Rs 190 crore gross and over Rs 160 crore net in India. Majority of these figures stem from the native Malayalam version, followed by the dubbed Tamil and Telugu versions in equal capacity. But Bethlehem Kudumba Unit has garnered most of its worldwide box office gross earnings from overseas, where it amassed around Rs 140 crore, only around Rs 25 crore short of its domestic net earnings. Also Read - Sanjay Dutt claims his cant feel peace in India remark was a scripted conversation In the process, Bethlehem Kudumba Units Rs 330 crore plus worldwide box office collection has made it the highest grossing Malayalam film ever globally, after surpassing that of Dominic Aruns superhero film from last year, Lokah Chapter 1 Chandra. The Kalyani Priyadarshan-starrer, produced by Dulquer Salmaans Wayfarer Films, earned around Rs 304 crore globally.

articleTitle: Sukhpal Khaira booked for sexual harassment over posts on AAP leader; cops issue notice to X
articleFeaturedImageAlt: khaira
description: Cong leader questions FIR, says police yet to inform the FIR number or the police station where the case was registered
body_raw: The Punjab Police has registered an FIR against Congress MLA Sukhpal Khaira on charges of sexually harassing and insulting modesty of a woman and criminal intimidation following a complaint by an Aam Aadmi Party leader who had flagged his posts against her on social media platform X. Khaira termed the FIR and attempt to muzzle his voice. The FIR has been registered under Sections 751iv, 753, 79, 351 and 61 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita BNS and Section 67 of the Information Technology Act, it has been learnt. Section 751iv of BNS deals with sexual harassment sexually coloured remarks. Section 753 deals with punishment for Section 751iv and prescribes imprisonment for up to one year, a fine, or both. Section 79 of BNS deals with insulting the modesty of a woman through any word, gesture, or act and covers verbal abuse, vulgar gestures, or digital messages meant to degrade a womans modesty. Section 351 for the BNS deals with the offence of threatening a person with injury, reputation, or property to cause alarm. Section 61 deals with criminal conspiracy while Section 67 of the IT Act punishes any person who publishes or transmits obscene material in electronic form. On September 27, the office of the Additional Director General of Police, State Cyber Crime Coordination Centre, Mohali, in an e-mail to X, directed the platform to take down posts by Khaira and two other accounts within three hours, stating that a criminal case has been registered. It said that the posts contained derogatory, objectionable and unsubstantiated remarks targeting the womans character, conduct and reputation. The notice said the allegations were of a personal nature and were made without credible, verifiable or supporting material, and could adversely affect her dignity, reputation and privacy. It listed six URLs, including from from Khairas account, and asked X to disable access and preserve the records. It also warned of consequences for the platforms safe-harbour protection if the content remained accessible after actual knowledge. The posts relate to a political row that began around September 25 after Khaira alleged that AAP Punjab in-charge Manish Sisodia was occupying a government house in Sector 39, Chandigarh, allotted to a Punjab minister and made certain comments about the woman AAP leader who denied the allegation and accused the Congress leader of attacking her character. Khaira subsequently objected to remarks made by her, which he described as abusive. The Punjab State Commission for Women chairperson too had criticised Khairas remarks. Khaira, meanwhile, termed the FIR an attempt by the AAP government to muzzle his voice. He questioned why the police notice to X did not mention the FIR number or the police station where the case was registered. In a post on X, Khaira said, When the AAP government cant fight me logically, it resorts to false cases and the police for support. He alleged that FIRs had been secretly registered over his two videos concerning the woman leader and claimed that while X had not removed the posts, Facebook had deleted the videos.

articleTitle: CBI probe ordered into corruption allegations against Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann’s aides
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The court ordered a probe into alleged corruption bhagwant mann
description: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has sought a report within two months on allegations against people linked to CM Mann's office.
body_raw: The Punjab and Haryana High Court Monday directed the Central Bureau of Investigation CBI to probe allegations made by the Enforcement Directorate ED against people linked to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Manns office and submit a report within two months. The order came on a PIL filed by advocate Nikhil Saraf, who sought a CBI probe into issues raised by the ED in a letter sent to Punjab Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav. The petition contended that the allegations raised serious questions about the state governments functioning and warranted an independent investigation outside the Punjab Police and Vigilance Bureau. In its earlier communication to the DGP, the agency sought registration of a criminal case against CM Manns Officer on Special Duty OSD Rajbir Singh Ghuman and his alleged associates, Nitin Gohal and Bir Devinder. According to the communication, the three allegedly interfered in the transfer and posting of government officials, government work and tender processes. The agency also referred to material purportedly indicating attempts to influence postings, access confidential government documents and interfere in administrative approvals and other official processes. The issue came to notice after investigations into alleged irregularities in the functioning of government departments and agencies in Punjab. The agencys communication to the DGP sought state police action on matters that it said had emerged during its probe. In his PIL, Saraf sought a comprehensive investigation into the claims, including the alleged financial transactions and money trail. He argued that since the allegations involved persons connected with the CMO and related to the functioning of the state government, the probe should be entrusted to an agency independent of the Punjab government. The petitioner also sought action against anyone found to be involved in the alleged offences. What CM Mann had said Last month, CM Mann called the ED letter to DGP Yadav the BJPs handiwork, saying the agencys allegations were untrue and that he did not need a certificate of honesty from people who looted the state. This is what they do. They make up cases. There is no truth in it. The Opposition is not finding any issues to raise. They are just pointing fingers. I do not need a certificate of honesty from people who have looted Punjab, Mann said, as he accused the BJP of misusing central agencies to defame, threaten and suppress its political opponents.

articleTitle: After Express report, Supreme Court notice to Centre on Central Secretariat Library relocation
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Central Secretariat Library, Supreme Court Central Secretariat Library, Central Secretariat Library relocation, Supreme Court library case, Shastri Bhavan library, Central Vista library, CSL relocation, Supreme Court, Central Secretariat Library books, Kartavya Bhavan library, Central Vista redevelopment, SC library hearing, Supreme Court news, Indian Express news
description: The Supreme Court sought details of the area proposed for the Central Secretariat Library and the actual layout plans.
body_raw: The Supreme Court Monday sought a detailed affidavit from the Centre on its plans to relocate the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library CSL from New Delhis Shastri Bhavan, which is proposed to be demolished as part of the Central Vista revamp plan. A bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva, which took note of an Indian Express report on the matter, issued notice to the Centre and sought an affidavit with full details of the area which would be allotted for housing the library along with actual layout plans. The court also asked the Centre to indicate whether the proposed library will be sufficient to house not only the books which are presently stored in Shastri Bhavan, but also the books which are stated to be lying in R K Puram.. Credit where its due. This issue was flagged by one of my former colleagues, a retired judge of the Punjab and Haryana High Court who is as fond of paper as he is now appreciative of AI and all that it has to offer, Justice Kumar said. What the court asked for Turning to Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, who appeared for the Centre, he referred to the Express report and said, Going by this newspaper report, this is a library which dates back to 1891 with writings of 1702. Its fine to say we should cut down on paper, but that doesnt mean you shouldnt take care of the valuable papers you already have. You are allotting two rooms in that Kartavya Bhavan, thats it? Bhati said that after the issue was flagged, she had taken instructions and handed over a report to the bench. As the bench said it would issue notice, she said it may not be necessary, as the reports instructions answer the doubts. Justice Kumar, however, said it would not do, and the Centre should file a proper reply, an affidavit giving an undertaking. Bhati pointed out that the report is signed by the director, Central Vista. Please see what is planned, she added. Justice Kumar also asked if the space proposed to be allocated is leaving out the 2 lakh books which are lying in R K Puram. Cartons which have not been opened since 2011. To which Bhati said, Bigger space across two floors is being planned. When Justice Kumar expressed doubt as to whether this includes the two lakh books stored in R K Puram, Bhati pointed out that the proposed area is more than the current area. The bench said it would still need an affidavit. The bench added the Centre must produce detailed plans because if you are having conference rooms etc, the actual storage area for these books, you have to tell us if there is enough area, because if you have all these trappings there, then the area for actual book storage would go down drastically. The bench fixed the matter for hearing it next on November 16. What Indian Express reported On September 30, The Indian Express report titled In Re 135-Yr-Old Library 8.5 Lakh Books-And No Room In The New Central Vista Plan explained how, when King George V announced the decision to shift the capital of British India from Calcutta, now Kolkata, to Delhi in 1911, the Central Secretariat Library, then known as the Imperial Secretariat Library, moved with it, finding its first home in the Old Secretariat Building in the Civil Lines area. After the British built a new seat of power around Raisina Hill, the library moved again to the North Block and then to Shastri Bhawan, where it has remained since 1969. The report said that with Shastri Bhawan set to be pulled down as part of the Central Vista revamp plan, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs MoHUA and Central Public Works Department CPWD were yet to find space for the Library. It added that in January, the Directorate of Estates under the MoHUA allotted two rooms totalling 300 square metres at Kartavya Bhawan-2 for the CSL, but the Ministry of Culture, which administers the CSL, rejected it, replying that the space allotted was far from sufficient.

articleTitle: Why India’s clock towers still matter in the age of smartphones and smartwatches
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mumbai's Rajabai Clock Tower
description: Clock towers may have little relevance now but they are markers of a city, its people and history
body_raw: Flanked by automobile spare parts shops and art framers, a narrow lane leads up to Sabzi Mandi Ghanta Ghar, near Kamala Nagar, in Delhi. Time moves at a different pace as we inch up to the centre of what was once the wholesale vegetable market. Workers who spent languorous hours beneath the tower dont hear the hands of time ticking away. But this clock is keeping time. At 50 ft, with its repetitive jaali pattern on its four sides, there is a plaque that calls it the Ram Roop Tower, named after the industrialist of the 1940s, who has also built a temple and schools in the area. It used to be a landmark when my father sold fruits in the market and later opened RK Dry Fruits, this shop, in 1980, says Rakesh Kumar of the recently refurbished tower. It stands testimony to time, industry and education in the area. As have many such towers over centuries. Recently, the Allahabad High Court questioned the building of one such tower in Firozabad market in Uttar Pradesh, when it asked What is the point of building one when people can check the time on their phones and wristwatches? While philosophers have contended about the illusion of time, there have been many attempts to map its transience. Gurugram-based horologist Debasish Das, author of Clock Towers of India Sentinels of Time Niyogi, 2026, has been chronicling the journey of clock towers for over six years. What began as an essay on documenting sun dials in mosques in Delhi grew to become a book that has taken him to different parts of the country, including Kochi, Mumbai, Lucknow and of course, Delhi. What fascinates me is the constant effort to measure, regulate and publicly communicate something as intangible as time. A clock tower is not merely a machine it gives time a visible and audible presence in the life of a community, says Das, who is an engineer with Nokia. He recalls his visit to the clock tower in Delhis old and well-known institutes, Shri Vishwanath Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya. Everyone spoke only in Sanskrit on the campus. They allowed me go all the way to the top of the clock tower. Its got balconies and a marble canopy, and has to be manually wound every seven days, he says. In his book, he writes, the Indian clock tower was never a single architectural type. Some of them evolved from older gateways, temple structures or civic buildings, others were purpose-built monumental towers, while in princely states they often became expressions of royal patronage and modernity. Their locations were equally varied as well, from markets and railway stations to palace precincts, municipal squares, ports and major intersections. So, although we use the common expression ghanta ghar, the structures themselves represent very different histories and purposes, says Das. While he has documented nearly 150 clock towers across the country, many with the help of friends, he sees how royal and industrial patronage, family ties and the aspirational intent of a city shaped the existence of these towers. For instance, Jodhpurs ghanta ghar was built during the reign of Maharaja Sardar Singh, while Sangramsinhji High School Gothic clock tower in Gondal was modelled on the English public schools such as Eton and Harrow. Nestled in many of these towers are stories of their origin. Mumbais famous Rajabai Clock Tower brings together Western technology and a personal story. Das writes, Its Victorian Gothic architecture and European clock mechanism were commissioned with the wealth of Indian merchant Premchand Roychand, who named it after his mother, Rajabai. She followed Jain traditions and would eat only before sunset. Its chimes helped her keep time. Though this is an oft-repeated story, it also points to the citys philanthropic and cosmopolitan character. Das takes us further back in time to the origin of the word itself. He says, The expression ghanta ghar has its roots in the sophisticated water clocks or ghatika yantras. This was a device, a hemispherical bowl made of a thin sheet of copper, with a fine hole at the centre of its base. When the bowl was placed within a large basin of water, the bowl would slowly sink as water entered through the hole. It was then lifted, emptied and placed back on the water. The bowl sank once every 24 minutes. Since the Sanskrit word for a vessel or pot is ghata, the interval of 24 minutes measured by it came to be called a ghati. Over time, ghati evolved into the familiar ghari, which is now associated with a clock or a watch. What has been fascinating is that these towers have not worked on the same mechanism. From the water clocks to weight-driven mechanical clocks and later pendulum-regulated mechanisms, depending on the period and technology, they have moved with time itself. Replacing an original mechanical movement with a cheap quartz mechanism may make the clock functional but it can also turn a living timepiece into a mere facade. When the gears stop turning and the bells fall silent, the tower may still stand but its heartbeat is gone, says Das. Many of these towers have clip-clocked through centuries, sometimes without ever stopping. Like Mumbai-based architect Brinda Somaya found out when her firm, Somaya Sampat, with a team of conservation experts, worked on the Rajabai Clock Tower. The project demanded research, patience and respect for craftsmanship. Even during the restoration process at a height of 280 feet, the clock continued to function. It reinforced a fundamental principle of conservation understand the building first, intervene sensitively, and allow it to continue its life without losing its authenticity, says Brinda. Das affirms, Strictly speaking, we no longer need clock towers to tell the time. Our smartwatches have made the clock tower redundant. But we still need them to remind us where we have come from and to give our cities a sense of place and memory.

articleTitle: ‘Completely illegal knocking out of citizen’: Former top court judge Rohinton Nariman on Bengal SIR
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Justice Rohinton Nariman Election Commission
description: The former Supreme Court judge referred to the petition challenging the 2023 law on the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and said the sooner it is decided, the better
body_raw: Former Supreme Court judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman has called for the Supreme Courts intervention in issues related to Special Intensive Revision SIR, saying, We cannot have an Election Commission that malfunctions. The senior jurist referred to The Indian Express investigation about the Election Commission and said the right to vote, which is at the heart of our democracy, is in great peril. The Express investigation, dated September 23, showed that the question of who makes it to the voters list and who is left out was being raised within the Commission itself. The former Supreme Court judge, who has also served as Solicitor General of India, spoke at the Late CA MJ Rindani Centenary Memorial Oration at Rajkot last Sunday September 27 on the subject, Constitution and the Common Man. Referring to the SIR in West Bengal ahead of the Assembly polls earlier this year, Justice Nariman said, All of you have seen that in the West Bengal election, 90 lakh voters - its an astounding figure - were disenfranchised. Now 90 lakh voters getting disenfranchised didnt somehow move the Supreme Court enough to stay this, so that these 90 lakh voters were out when the Bengal election took place. Out of those who were disenfranchised, some 22 lakh voters actually filed appeals the others have all seemed to have accepted - they must be poor people, they must be people who dont have the wherewithal or the access to justice that the others had. And of these 22 lakh voters, some one lakh voter appeals were decided, 93 per cent in favour of the voter. So can you imagine, this was a completely illegal knocking out of the common man, of the citizen of India, in order that a government obtains what it wants, and the result, as you saw in West Bengal, was something that upset the government of the day and brought in the government of the state, he said. Saying that very, very disturbing things are happening in our country today, the jurist said, Equally disturbing is the fact that we discover now, thanks to The Indian Express, that the two gentlemen on either side of the Chief Election Commissioner voiced objections to whatever was going on 14 times, and somehow or the other they didnt press their right under the new Act, Section 18, to say that look, between the three of us, its the majority vote that counts. So the two of us prevail over you, Chief Election Commissioner. They didnt do that. They were also appointees of the present government. So what do we have today? And as of right, as of today itself, todays newspaper tells us that there is some patch-up between these three gentlemen, to the nations great detriment, where they have come out with some common statement saying, yes, some of the objections you people took seem to be correct, we revert to the old Form 6, and so on and so forth, Justice Nariman said. So the first issue I wish to flag today is that the common man today under our Constitution, and at, if I may say so, the heart of our Constitution, the heart of our democracy, which is the right to vote, is at great peril. And I hope that the apex court, an institution to which I once belonged, steps in immediately and rectifies these things. You cannot have an Election Commission which functions or malfunctions like this. Its something amazing, he said. On appointment of Chief Election Commissioner The senior jurist referred to the petition challenging the 2023 law on the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner. A two-judge bench recently gave a split verdict on the petition and said that it should be referred to a five-judge Constitution bench. And the sooner the Constitution Bench decides that you have to have somebody like a Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition, coupled with the Chief Justice or his nominee, who then picks up the best name in order to see that votes actually translate into what theyre supposed to translate into happens, the sooner that happens, the better, he said. The panel that appoints the Chief Election Commissioner now has the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and a Union Cabinet minister appointed by the Prime Minister. The main opposition Congress has opposed this, saying the current system gives undue advantage to the government. The Election Commission, Justice Nariman said, originally consisted only of the Chief Election Commissioner. He was to be appointed by the government of the day, subject to a law made by Parliament. This is very important. And later, laws added two more commissioners, so that we have three commissioners as of date. This Chief Election Commissioner had a fixed tenure of 5 years, could not be removed save by impeachment in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge, which meant that you required a two-thirds majority in both houses, present and voting, in order to get rid of him. So it becomes difficult to get rid of, but the difficulty is, if the appointment is in the hands of the government of the day, then this removal procedure doesnt add very much to independence or impartiality. This is the first conundrum that we face, he said. Second, the two commissioners who are with him are also appointed by the government of the day, and they can only be removed with his concurrence, with the Chief Election Commissioners concurrence, he said. Recently, we had in Anoop Baranwals case in 2023, the Supreme Court looking into the fact that so many years have passed since the Constitution came into force and Parliament making no law whatsoever under Article 324 for appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners. So the court suggested, why dont we take a leaf out of Section 4A of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, which appoints the Director of the CBI, and for that Director you require to have a collegium consisting of the Prime Minister of India, Leader of the Opposition, and the Chief Justice of India? So the court suggested that pro tem, until Parliament makes a law, we will have these three people who will select somebody who is independent and impartial. Now what does Parliament do? Its amazing. Parliament immediately enacts in 2023 itself, an Act for the appointment of all these people, and instead of these three functionaries, the Prime Minister has his own minister as number two, and then as Leader of the Opposition, so that again you are back to square one, he said. Now the unfortunate part is that all this came before the court very recently. Two learned judges differ, and the ultimate thing is now that its gone before a bench probably of five judges in order to find out whether this is good law, not good law. But meanwhile, these appointments continue only in the hands of the government of the day, the jurist said.

articleTitle: Need to instil fear in minds of goons committing crimes against women: Supreme Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: SUPREME COURT, DELHI RAPES
description: Supreme Court said that there is a feeling that women are not safe in Delhi, especially in certain vulnerable pockets.
body_raw: The Supreme Court Monday said there was a need to instil fear in the minds of miscreants committing crimes against women, while stating that there is a feeling that women are not safe in Delhi, especially in certain vulnerable pockets. While hearing a suo motu case over the recent incidents of rape in Delhi-NCR, the apex court said What is important is to prevent a crime, not what you do after a crime is committed, the bench said, adding that the police need to create fear in the minds of goons and anti-social elements who are prone to committing such crimes. The bench, comprising Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran, said it must be ensured that every woman should feel safe, anywhere in the city at any time of the day. We have to work together. We must ensure that every woman in Delhi-NCR should feel safe even at 11 pm whether travelling on the roads or the metro, they observed, adding rape is something which is not at all acceptable to any society. On September 28, the Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance of various news reports on recent crimes against women and minor girls across Delhi-NCR and stated that such incidents highlight a systematic failure of the law enforcement agencies.

articleTitle: JEE Advanced 2026: SC qualification rate tops 50% for the first time; women reach 6-year high
articleFeaturedImageAlt: JEE Advanced 2026 exam
description: In 2018, the IITs created 800 supernumerary seats for women. That year, women made up about 15.34% of admitted candidates, above the 14% target. In last year's JEE Advanced, 3,633 female-only seats were allotted and 31 women got in through the gender-neutral pool, taking women's share to 20.15% of 18,188 seats.
body_raw: The latest JEE Advanced results show a noticeable shift in who is making it through the exam. The number of SC candidates qualifying rose from 12,499 last year to 15,856 in 2026, while the number of ST qualifiers increased from 5,008 to 6,379 - a rise of about 27 per cent in both categories. Women, too, recorded a 23.4 per cent qualification rate, the highest in the six years covered by the Joint Implementation Committee JIC report released by IIT Roorkee. The overall pool, meanwhile, grew only marginally, from 54,378 qualifiers to 56,880. The sharper change, therefore, was not in the size of the qualifying pool, but in who made it into it. Read IITs, IIMs see more women joining than before as placements, salary rises A total of 1,87,389 candidates registered this year in JEE Advanced, against 1,87,223 in last year. Of them, 1,79,694 appeared for both papers, compared with 1,80,422 last year. Qualifiers rose about 4.6 per cent, lifting the share of those who appeared and qualified from 30.1 per cent to 31.7 per cent. Qualification rate by category Category 2025 2026 Change SC 40.41 50.16 9.8 ST 33.99 42.14 8.1 General 43.0 39.8 3.2 OBC-NCL 18.2 17.5 0.7 Women-23.4 Six-year high Source JIC reports 2025, 2026 Half of SC candidates made the cut The SC qualification rate rose 9.8 percentage points to 50.16 per cent, from 40.41 per cent in the previous session. For ST candidates, it climbed 8.1 points to 42.14 per cent from 33.99 per cent. Put simply, about one in every two registered SC candidates qualified this year, compared with roughly two in five last year. Among ST candidates, more than two in five qualified, up from one in three. The headcount tells the same story. SC qualifiers grew by 3,357 and ST qualifiers by 1,371. That is nearly six times faster than the overall rise. Together, they make up 22,235 of the 56,880 qualifiers, nearly 39 per cent of the total. A year ago, that share was about 32 per cent. AlsoRead What global teacher shortage, and Indias numbers tells us Not every group moved up. The general category rate fell 3.2 points to 39.8 per cent, and OBC-NCL candidates slipped 0.7 points to 17.5 per cent. This means both SC and ST rates now sit above the general category figure, which is a notable change. Women enrolment reaches new high In 2026, 43,112 women registered for JEE Advanced. Of them, 40,562 appeared in both papers and 10,107 qualified. That works out to 23.4 per cent of registered women, the best rate in six years, and about 24.9 per cent of those who appeared. Women now make up nearly 18 per cent of all qualifiers. At the very top, the leading woman candidate scored 280 marks, with 101 in Mathematics, 86 in Physics and 93 in Chemistry, to secure All India Rank 77. In 2026, 29,983 women registered and 4,570 qualified, a rate of about 15 per cent. Ten years later, registrations are up by nearly 44 per cent, but qualifiers have more than doubled, rising by about 121 per cent. The 2026 rate is about eight points higher than in 2016.
