articleTitle: Karnataka SIR: Over 43.5 lakh notices delivered, 91,278 form 7 applications received
articleFeaturedImageAlt: According to data released by the CEO’s office, 43,82,313 notices have been generated across Karnataka. Of these, 43,55,818 have been delivered, while 26,495 are yet to be delivered, taking the delivery rate to 99.40 per cent.
description: The notices have been issued to electors whose names fall under the “No Mapping” and “Anomalies” categories during the electoral roll revision exercise.
body_raw: More than 43.5 lakh notices have been delivered to electors in Karnataka as part of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls, with 91,278 Form 7 applications received between June 16 and October 4, Chief Electoral Officer V Anbukkumar said on Monday. Form 7 is used to file an objection to the proposed inclusion or seek deletion of a name from the existing electoral roll. The notices have been issued to electors whose names fall under the No Mapping and Anomalies categories during the electoral roll revision exercise. Anbukkumar said no voter has been deleted from the electoral roll so far, and clarified that the filing of an objection does not automatically result in deletion. Just because objections have been filed, no name has been deleted so far from the electoral roll, he said at a press conference. He said objections would be examined by the concerned Electoral Registration Officers EROs, who would take necessary action according to law. On applications seeking deletion of names through Form 7, Anbukkumar said the ERO is required to issue a notice and conduct a hearing before taking any decision. The officer has to call both the objector and the voter for the hearing. The officer has to verify the documents. Only after that, once the officer is convinced, a decision can be taken whether to delete or not to delete, he said, referring to the procedure under Sections 16 to 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. The CEO said no case had been registered by his office so far. According to data released by the CEOs office, 43,82,313 notices have been generated across Karnataka. Of these, 43,55,818 have been delivered, while 26,495 are yet to be delivered, taking the delivery rate to 99.40 per cent. Of the notices delivered, hearings have been completed in 36,89,063 cases, or 84.69 per cent. Hearings in 6,66,755 cases remain pending. The CEOs office said that of the 91,278 Form 7 applications received between June 16 and October 4, none related to objections to proposed inclusion. During the same period, the state received 9,10,732 Form 6 applications, 4,677 Form 6A applications and 11,98,484 Form 8 applications. The total number of applications received across these categories stood at 22,05,171. Bidar recorded the highest number of Form 7 applications at 5,953, followed by Shivamogga with 5,936 and Dakshina Kannada with 5,534. The CEOs office said the last hearing would be conducted on October 12, while October 22 is the last date for disposal of claims and objections and the notice phase. As on October 5, Karnataka had 4,50,29,916 electors on its electoral roll, comprising 2.23 crore male, 2.26 crore female and 2,863 transgender electors. The CEOs office said that, following requests from registered and recognised political parties, lists of persons who have been issued notices under the No Mapping and Anomalies categories have been published on the CEOs website. It also said EROs had been directed to take action according to law against applicants who knowingly make false statements or declarations in Form 6, Form 6A, Form 7 or Form 8. Such action would follow an inquiry under Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and would be in accordance with Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. The CEOs office also clarified that some electors may find that their Part Number and Serial Number have changed in the draft electoral roll because of the rationalisation of polling stations and re-serialisation of electors. Electors unable to locate their names in the same part where they were previously registered have been advised to search using their EPIC number on the Election Commissions voter portal or through the ECINET mobile application. -With PTI Inputs

articleTitle: By Election 2026: Bypolls on 6 seats in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Assam; Results On Oct 9
articleFeaturedImageAlt: West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Assam By Election 2026
description: West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Assam By Election 2026 Polling - Date, Time, Streaming: The by-elections hold much significance following the BJP's victory in West Bengal ending TMC's 15 year rule, Vijay's TVK's victorious electoral debut in Tamil Nadu and it remains to be seen how the new leaders have factored in the electorate.
body_raw: West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Assam By Election 2026 The by-elections to five Assembly constituencies across West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, and one Lok Sabha constituency in Assam, will be held on Tuesday, with voting beginning at 7 am. Counting of votes will be held on October 9. The by-elections hold significance following the BJPs victory in West Bengal, ending TMCs 15-year rule, and Vijays TVKs victorious electoral debut in Tamil Nadu, and it remains to be seen how the new leaders have factored in with the electorate. By Election 2026 Live Updates Follow Here West Bengal In West Bengal, the Suvendu Adhikari-led BJP government faces its first electoral test after assuming power in the Assembly polls earlier this year. With Nandigram and Rejinagar going to polls, the Opposition faces a tough battle amid candidate withdrawals, arrests and allegations of police pressure on its workers. Nandigram The Nandigram seat paved the way for the TMCs rise in 2011 following Mamata Banerjees anti-land acquisition movement, and its where Adhikari defeated the TMC supremo in 2021. Adhikari, now chief minister, won Nandigram again in the 2026 Assembly election but retained Bhabanipur, necessitating the bypoll. The BJP has fielded Hasirani Rath, mother of Chandranath Rath, a former aide of Adhikari. Chandranath was shot dead on May 6, two days after the BJP won the Assembly elections. The Mamata Banerjee-led TMC factions nominee Sanchita Pradhan Dey withdrew her name after meeting Adhikari, following which Banerjee, left without a candidate, backed Congress candidate Milan Pradhan and described the move as an effort to strengthen the INDIA bloc. Pradhan was arrested in old cases linked to the 2007 Nandigram land-acquisition agitation but later secured interim bail and returned to campaign. The rival TMC faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee has fielded Mohammad Eteshamul Haque under the envelope symbol and a separate temporary party identity. The CPI has nominated Santigopal Giri. Rejinagar The by-election in Rejinagar was necessitated after Humayun Kabir, who won both Rejinagar and Nowda in the 2026 Assembly election, retained Nowda. His Aam Janata Unnayan Party has fielded his son Golam Nabi Azad. Kabir had won Rejinagar by nearly 59,000 votes. The contest includes BJP nominee Sakharav Sarkar, former Murshidabad district president Mamata-led TMC candidate Rabiul Alam Chowdhury rival TMC candidate Safiuzzaman Sheikh Congress nominee Mohammad Abdullahil Kafi and CPIMs Syed Asad Ali. Tamil Nadu The two seats in Tamil Nadu, Madurantakam and Dharapuram, saw four-day aggressive campaigning by TVK chief and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, as the electoral contest would be crucial for his party. It is a four-cornered contest, with the TVK, DMK, AIADMK and CPI fielding their candidates. Both constituencies were vacated by AIADMK legislators who resigned within weeks of being elected and crossed over to Vijay. The same two leaders-Maragatham Kumaravel in Madurantakam and P Sathyabama in Dharapuram-are now contesting as TVK candidates. The DMK enters these by-elections without the broad alliance that accompanied it into the Assembly election. The Congress, VCK, MDMK and IUML have moved into Vijays political orbit, while the CPI and CPIM are contesting separately. A total of 27 contestants are in the fray for the bypoll at Madurantakam, and a total of 30 contestants are in the fray in the Dharapuram Assembly constituency. In Madurantakam, a total of 2,12, 639 voters will exercise their franchise in 268 polling stations. In Dharapuram, 2,22, 406 electors will exercise their franchise in 282 polling stations. Thattanchavady in Puducherry The poll scenario is different in neighbouring Puducherry, where its a test of popularity for the four-month-old NDA government led by veteran N Rangasamy. Although a total of 11 candidates are in the fray, the battle is being seen as a three-cornered one between the ruling AINRC-led NDA, the Congress and its former ally DMK. While AINRC founder and CM Rangasamy has nominated Ashok Anand on behalf of the ruling party and the coalition it leads, the Congress has fielded E Vinayagam, who has the backing of the Tamizhaga Vetri Kazhagam TVK, which is part of the ruling alliance in neighbouring Tamil Nadu. The DMK nominee is K Sedhu Selvam. CPIs M A Saleem and S Karthikumari of actor-politician Seemans Naam Tamilar Katchi are also fighting the poll battle. Nagaon Lok Sabha seat in Assam The Nagaon Lok Sabha seat in Assam would witness a triangular contest, with the ruling BJP seeking to expand its base in this Muslim-majority constituency, and the Congress going all out to retain the seat by keeping its minority support base intact. The AIUDF, the third prominent party in the fray, is fighting to maintain its influence after it was reduced to two MLAs from 16 in the April Assembly election. A total of 15 candidates, including nine Independents, are contesting the bypoll. Among the key candidates are ex-MLA Sibamoni Bora of the Congress, former IAS officer Devasish Sharma of the BJP and sitting MLA Badruddin Ajmal of the AIUDF. The bypoll was necessitated after sitting MP Pradyut Bordoloi quit the Congress to join the BJP ahead of the Assembly elections earlier this year. Out of the eight Assembly segments under the Nagaon Lok Sabha seat, the BJP won four, the Congress three and Raijor Dal one in this years state elections. For the Congress, which won three out of 14 Lok Sabha seats in the 2024 election, retaining Nagaon is crucial to prevent further erosion of its support base. The BJP, which has been aiming to spread its base among the Muslims, has viewed the Nagaon bypoll as an attempt to establish its presence across all sections of people and further strengthen its hold in the state.

articleTitle: ‘Hollywood is a small place’: Atlee wants to take Vijay Sethupathi’s Bathttha to the Oscars
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Atlee spoke about his Oscar dreams for Baththa and the global ambitions of Raaka
description: At the Baththa success meet, producer Atlee revealed his ambition to take the Vijay Sethupathi-starrer to the Oscars, saying he would speak only in Tamil if he ever stood on the Academy stage.
body_raw: Filmmaker Atlee has declared his ambition to take the Vijay Sethupathi-starrer Baththa to the Oscars, saying he dreams of standing on the Academy stage and delivering his speech entirely in Tamil. He also revealed that Hollywood professionals working on his upcoming directorial Raaka with Allu Arjun were left stunned by the films songs, asking, Who is this guy? Speaking at the Baththa success meet on Saturday, Atlee framed his ambition with a reference to his own journey. People would have laughed at me in school if I had said that I was going to do a film with Shah Rukh Khan and Vijay Anna. But I did it. Just like that, I wish to take Baththa to the Oscars. I want to see what it feels like. Im doing everything I can to stand there, he said. He was unequivocal about one thing if the opportunity comes, the language of his speech will not be English. Im definitely going to speak in Tamil. We can do it. We can definitely do it. Hollywood is a small place, and we can go there easily. Also Read Raakas Guinness Record explained 37 performers, 92 cameras, one massive motion-capture setup Atlee then turned to his upcoming directorial Raaka, starring Allu Arjun, and revealed that international professionals working on the film were impressed by young composer Sai Abhyankkars work. Tamil people will feel really proud of Raaka. The Hollywood people working on Raaka were stunned and said, Yaarra ivan? Who is this guy?, Atlee said, referring to Sai. Recalling a music composition session for Raaka in London, Atlee said Sai worked at a studio used by acclaimed composers such as Hans Zimmer and Ludwig Goransson. We went to London for the composition of Raaka, where big music directors Hans Zimmer and Ludwig do composition, he said. According to Atlee, the international musicians present at the studio were surprised by the quality of work coming from the young Indian composer. The filmmaker also used the Baththa success meet to defend Sai Abhyankkar against the nepotism accusations the young composer has faced on social media. You are not a nepo kid, like others are saying, Atlee said, addressing Abhyankkar directly. He is not just the person who came with Katchi Sera and Aasa Kooda. He is going to bring pride to Tamil people. Also Read - Baththa movie review Vijay Sethupathi shines in a film that earns every emotion About Baththa Baththa, directed by Balaji Tharaneetharan in his third collaboration with Vijay Sethupathi after Naduvula Konjam Pakkatha Kaanom and Seethakaathi, is set in 1986 Madras and follows a feared local gangster who gets accidentally locked inside a school toilet by an eight-year-old boy. Baththa stars Vijay Sethupathi as the titular gangster Baththa, with child actor Sai playing the boy. Lijomol Jose plays Baththas wife. The supporting cast includes Ajay Ghosh, Arjun Chidambaram, Santhy Balachandran and Hari Krishnan. The film is presented by Atlee and jointly produced by A For Apple Studios and Cine1 Studios, with Murad Khetani, Priya Atlee, Alok Jain and Ajit Andhare as producers.

articleTitle: Bihar labourer arrested for sexually assaulting minor daughter in Bengaluru
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengaluru child sexual assault case
description: CCTV footage from around the rented house where the family was staying raised suspicion about the girl's father, the police said.
body_raw: The police in Bengaluru South district arrested a 30-year-old labourer from Bihar for allegedly sexually assaulting his minor daughter, who has a hearing impairment, officers said on Monday. According to the police, the incident came to light after the girl developed severe abdominal pain about a week ago. Her stepmother took her to a nearby private hospital, where doctors suspected sexual assault and alerted the District Child Protection Unit. Officials who visited the hospital subsequently confirmed that the girl had been sexually assaulted. As the girl has a hearing impairment and could not communicate verbally, a sign-language interpreter was brought in to speak to her, the police said. However, she could not provide clear information about the person responsible for the assault. The police initially registered a case against an unidentified person under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Pocso Act. During the investigation, the police questioned the girls father, who allegedly behaved as though he was unaware of the incident. However, CCTV footage from around the rented house where the family was staying raised suspicion about him, the police said. During questioning, he confessed to the crime. He was subsequently arrested and produced before a court, which remanded him to judicial custody, a police officer said. According to the police, the girl was born to the mans first wife, who died following an illness. The man and his second wife have three children, taking the total number of children in the household to four. The police said further investigations are underway.

articleTitle: From India to Global South, a Gujarat water-governance model
articleFeaturedImageAlt: From India to Global South, a Gujarat water-governance model
description: Water access gains momentum in communities equipped with effective local water governance institutions such as India’s Pani Samitis.
body_raw: New Delhi recently hosted the ninth edition of the India International Water Week under the theme of climate-resilient water management. The talk focused as much on what India has achieved in the last decade as on what comes next - keeping water supply sustainable, using water more efficiently, and treating used water as both an environmental and economic resource. Indias influence in the global water sector has grown substantially. From a country exposed to frequent climate shocks and access challenges to one now preparing for climate extremes such as floods and droughts, it offers lessons for other countries in the Global South. Over the past decade or so, India has designed and implemented some of the worlds largest programmes to improve water governance, rejuvenate rivers, increase access to water and sanitation, and enable community-driven water conservation, protection, and augmentation. And if we pause and take a step back in time, it is important to acknowledge the leadership of then Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modis initiatives between 2001 and 2014, a period that served as a laboratory for the water governance reforms that rolled out across India after 2014. These included the design and implementation of the Swachh Bharat Mission, Jal Jeevan Mission JJM, Jal Shakti Abhiyan, Namami Gange, Atal Bhujal Yojana ABY, Per Drop More Crop PDMC, etc. This 25-year journey is documented in our new case study, From Gujarat to India Water Lessons for the World, which traces water governance reforms in Gujarat and India from 2001 to 2026. Drawing on official data, policy and programme records, the literature and consultations with practitioners, the study examines how political leadership and prioritisation, public financing, institutional reform, administrative implementation and community engagement came together to strengthen water security at scale. Its central finding is that water security is as much a challenge of governance and institutions as it is of engineering - and that the Gujarat experience offers a useful lens for understanding the subsequent national journey and its relevance to the Global South. The case study distils four key lessons which, if studied and contextualised appropriately, can prove effective in the coming years and inform water governance in other countries in the Global South Lead with governance, manage the resource and the service together, root action in communities, and build for scale from the start. Lead with governance, not only hardware Political will and institutional strengthening, rather than infrastructure alone, are core to water security. India has developed a framework for putting them into action at scale, called the 4 Ps, which were articulated by PM Modi and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres through the Delhi Declaration in October 2018. The first is political leadership that prioritises water, reflected in initiatives such as universal tap water access, a cleaner Ganga, community-driven groundwater management, and communication campaigns that keep water top of the mind, such as Jal Shakti Abhiyan Catch the Rain. Second, enabling public and private financing for the capital and recurring costs of water governance. Third, developing partnerships between national, state, and local governments community-based organisations, and national and international knowledge organisations, including multilateral development banks like the World Bank. Fourth, ensuring peoples participation in local water decision-making and management, such as communities resolving to make their villages open-defecation free or preparing village-level water security plans. The 4 Ps are worth emulating in any other context or geography. Manage the water resource and the service together Taps and canals will fail if water does not flow. Addressing both water resources development and service sustainability simultaneously and at scale is paramount. Many cities in Africa are growing at a rapid rate, and industrial and irrigation demand will follow, so planning resources and services together now is cheaper than retrofitting later. As Indias experience in recent decades shows, getting ahead of the coming surge in water demand with linked water resources and services plans would help countries gain from these economic shifts with lower risk for water insecurity. A key part of getting ahead of this surge is being forward-thinking on water reuse, especially for non-potable uses, including planned data centres and semiconductor fabrication units. In India alone, the annual market revenue from the sale of treated used water is projected to reach around Rs 73,000 crore by 2047, at current prices. Root water action in community ownership Water access gains momentum in communities equipped with effective local water governance institutions such as Indias Pani Samitis, infrastructure that consistently delivers a high-quality service, and a balance of internal resources and external support. This has been demonstrated through numerous water conservation, harvesting, and recharge programmes. There is a governance linkage across scales to achieve this. As demonstrated in Gujarat during 2001-2014, the Chintan Shivirs helped prioritise water governance among key stakeholders and formulate actionable solutions to design water-related policies aligned with community expectations. A similar approach was replicated at the national level. The recent Departmental Summit on Water organised by the Ministry of Jal Shakti and addressed by the PM in September 2026 is an example. Going big and scaling up The world is off track on SDG 6 to ensure safe drinking water and sanitation for all, and to sustainably manage water resources, used water, and ecosystems by 2030. Estimates suggest an additional 500 billion in annual investment is required. To meet the scale of water governance reforms, infrastructure installation, data collection, and maintenance required for SDG 6, governments and their leaders cannot afford to slow down. Implementation of JJM across the country demonstrates that India can both think big and implement big. The global community can learn from political leadership at the highest level in India about the will, the financing and the institutions to do it at scale. Iyer is a former secretary to the Government of India at the Ministry of Jal Shakti Bassi is a fellow with the Council on Energy, Environment and Water Smith is an assistant professor at George Mason University. Views are personal

articleTitle: The knock on the Supreme Court’s door
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The knock on the Supreme Court’s door
description: Even as the Election Commission went back on its own record of inclusiveness, even as it shifted the burden of proof on the vulnerable voter and set up a hurdle race at every stage of the SIR, the Court kept giving it the benefit of every doubt. Going ahead, therefore, not just the EC, the Court is also on test .
body_raw: This newspapers investigation that shone a light on the functioning of the Election Commission of India in the context of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls has raised serious questions. They have to do with a multi-member body, a constitutional authority, shrinking, many a time, into a one-man show, undermining the checks and balances within. More fundamentally, these questions touch the citizens sacrosanct right to shape her own and the nations future through the right to vote. On Sunday, Justice Ujjal Bhuyan framed the issues in all their breadth and gravity. Large-scale disenfranchisement caused by the SIR, he said, is a violation of the Constitution, and detaching the citizen from the right to vote is like taking out the soul from the body. He referred to debates in the Constituent Assembly to underline the transformational vision and the constitutional guarantee. . years of freedom struggle and the revolt against foreign rule made the adoption of universal adult franchise a natural choice and an essential ingredient of democracy. Equal vote with equal value, regardless of identity and social location, was the first step in a new nation to achieve equality. As the Supreme Court takes up cases related to the modalities of the SIR, and the ECs appointment process and functioning, it would do well to listen in to Justice Bhuyans outlining of what is at stake. Former SC judge Rohinton Fali Nariman underlined it Also on Sunday, he said that the SIRs removal of voters put the right to vote, which is at the heart of our democracy, in great peril. These are not just the concerns of two individual judges, they reflect the disquiet the Supreme Court needs to address to repair the damage done by its troubling silence. The citizens fundamental right to participate in the electoral process has to be protected at all costs. But even as the EC went back on its own record of inclusiveness, even as it shifted the burden of proof onto the vulnerable voter and set up a hurdle race at every stage of the SIR, the Court kept giving it the benefit of every doubt. Going ahead, therefore, not just the EC, the Court is also on test. It is welcome, then, that the SC has made it clear that it did not approve of the changes made to Form 6, which made the process of registration of new voters more daunting. It is reassuring, too, that it wants answers from the EC on aspects of the decision-making within. With due respect, the Court must keep asking questions, again and again. It has a formidable record of affirming the sanctity of Article 324 that secures the Election Commission, it should ensure that remains without stain. For, as one its own members said, this is about the soul of the nation.

articleTitle: Harsimrat Badal: ‘I have not signalled Akali Dal, BJP alliance for Punjab polls’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Harsimrat Badal: 'I have not signalled Akali Dal, BJP alliance for Punjab polls'
description: “Our Mawan Dhiyan Insaaf Yatra is about feeling the pain of women who are worst-affected by drug menace in Punjab. Women tell me they are scared to send their children to schools and colleges,” says the lone SAD MP.
body_raw: With the Assembly elections in Punjab just over four months away, Shiromani Akali Dal SADs lone MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal is holding at least three meetings a day as she leads her partys women-focused Mawan Dhiyan Insaaf Yatra against drugs across the state. In an interview with The Indian Express, the four-time Bathinda MP spoke about the drug problem in the state, her partys vision for Punjab, speculations surrounding her entry into state politics, and the buzz about the SAD-BJP alliance, among other issues. Excerpts Your anti-drug campaign, which is focused on women affected by the drug problem, is in contrast to the AAPs Mawan Dhiyan Satkar Yojana. Does this make your outreach difficult? I do not intend to compete with anyone through my programme, which is about feeling the pain of women who are worst-affected by the drug menace in Punjab. Women tell me that they are scared to send their children to schools and colleges. The AAP governments scheme Mawan Dhiyan Satkar financial aid scheme for women is mere symbolism. Instead of providing an aid of Rs 60,000 over a five-year period, they started the scheme just six months before the polls. Women affected by drugs are attending my programmes voluntarily. Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann blames the previous SAD-BJP governments tenure between 2007 and 2017 for the drug problem. When we were in power, drugs were not being sold openly on the streets of Punjab nor were youngsters seen with syringe-poked arms. The AAP is just trying to defame the BJP-SAD tenure but the fact remains that chitta heroin is being sold like toffees in Punjab today. Complainants in cases of drugs are being threatened and punished rather than the suppliers of drugs. We often find policemen accused of selling heroin. There is a nexus between drug suppliers and the police. How can someone who was in power 10 years ago be responsible for todays problems? The CM often takes a dig at Nanhi Chhan, your NGO which also campaigns against drugs. What is your reaction? Nanhi Chhan is very close to my heart. I started it decades ago at a time when I was not involved in active politics. I have empowered over 14,000 women through the NGO. With regard to Manns criticism, what else can I expect from a Guru Dokhi anti-Guru CM, who has not empowered a single woman. His speeches show how much he respects women. While I brought AIIMS to Bathinda, he has not brought a single project for the state during his tenure. What is Mawan Dhiyan Di Fauj campaign that you have now launched? Mawan Dhiyan Di Fauj is to identify drug traffickers and their god-fathers across the state. We will empower our women to become the catalysts of change. I have released a form and it would be distributed in every village. I urge women to fill the form. and become active volunteers in this movement. Women should record all acts of drug trafficking around them with names of the traffickers and peddlers as well as those who were patronising them. The forms would be forwarded to a special anti-drug task force headed by a woman DGP for speedy action against the culprits when the SAD govt will come to power. What is your response to the buzz that your political activity has increased in Punjab as you may enter state politics and could be projected as the SADs CM face? These are rumours being spread by our rivals. I have always been in the state as I belong to a regional party. We understand the pain of Punjab and Punjabis. This is my state. So far, I have covered 14 Assembly constituencies through my yatra and will cover more in the coming weeks. What are your views on the possible alliance between the SAD and the BJP for the Punjab elections? Contrary to perception, I have not given any indication about this possible alliance. When asked in August by our constituency in-charge of Longowal about an educational institution in the area, I had just said if the SAD comes to power, the constituency will see development. I was just referring to former CM Parkash Singh Badals abilities to get projects for Punjab through his goodwill irrespective of who was ruling at the Centre. My statement was misinterpreted. How do you see SADs chances in the 2027 Assembly polls? The Congress won in 2017 after being out of power for 10 years. I firmly believe that public support can bring SAD to power this time as people no longer want Delhi to govern them. Ours is a party of Punjabis and for Punjabis.
