articleTitle: One Nation, One Election Bills: Supreme Court gave its nod on Sept 22, but cancelled meet with House panel late, says JPC Chairman
articleFeaturedImageAlt: SC gave its nod on Sept 22, but cancelled meet with House panel later: Chairman
description: Controversy over the proposed meeting erupted last week when Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal addressed a press conference on October 1, calling the meeting “unconstitutional” as the Bills being deliberated by the committee could someday come before the court for adjudication.
body_raw: THE CHAIRMAN of the Joint Committee of Parliament on One Nation, One Election Bills, P P Chaudhary, on Monday said the Supreme Court on September 22 wrote to the committee confirming a meeting with its members at 4.30 pm on October 6, before deciding to cancel it on October 1 following objections raised to the proposed meeting. The committee was scheduled to visit the court for a local study visit, including an informal discussion with Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and other judges of the Supreme Court on the issue of simultaneous elections, as per the programme circulated to the panel members. Controversy over the proposed meeting erupted last week when Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal addressed a press conference on October 1, calling the meeting unconstitutional as the Bills being deliberated by the committee could someday come before the court for adjudication. The Supreme Court wrote to the committee on October 1 afternoon, cancelling the meeting, saying the matter was discussed among senior judges and it was felt that it would not be desirable to have the discussion as the Bills may become a subject of judicial review. Speaking to reporters after a meeting of the Parliamentary committee on Monday, Chaudhary said the meeting was fixed by the Supreme Court after it was suggested by DMK MP and lawyer P Wilson. He said after the Supreme Court wrote to the committee on September 22, fixing the time of the meeting, all members were informed. Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal submitted material to the court the lists of members and officers who would take part in the meeting were also shared. After eight or nine days, when some issues were raised publicly, the Supreme Court felt. it would not be proper to have the meeting, so we also informed the members. If it is not appropriate, then we should not pursue the matter, Chaudhary said. He added that committees of Parliament had interacted with the Supreme Court in the past. Earlier in the day, the matter is learnt to have come up in the meeting of the committee. Wilson is learnt to have read out a letter explaining the matter. The DMK MP is learnt to have said that he had suggested the meeting with the court in the interest of broad-based consultation. He is learnt to have noted that the meeting could not take place due to political objections. Wilson is learnt to have said that seeking the judges informal views cannot amount to seeking adjudication from the court. He is also learnt to have cited past examples, including when the draft Constitution was circulated to seek views from judges in 1948, as well as some recent examples, including meetings of Parliamentary committees with judges regarding the Mediation Bill, virtual courts and National Legal Services Authority. Congress MP Manish Tewari is learnt to have said the decision to consult the Supreme Court was a grave error, given that the Bills could end up before the court. After Wilson made his point that such meetings had been held in the past, Tewari is learnt to have asked why then was the meeting cancelled. The committee is also learnt to have held interactions with Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran, Chairman, Economic Advisory Council to Prime Minister, S Mahendra Dev and Vivekananda International Foundation chairman S Gurumurthy. They are learnt to have supported the idea of simultaneous elections. The CEA, it is learnt, told the committee that frequent elections bring the focus on revenue expenditure instead of capital expenditure, and can lead to policy paralysis. Gurumurthy is learnt to have flagged that frequent elections lead to the creation of paid party workers and use of money power in elections, as opposed to voluntary cadres. The committee is examining the Constitution 129th Amendment Bill, 2024, and the Union Territories Laws Amendment Bill, 2024, that were introduced in December 2024. The Bills provide for a one-time curtailment of terms of state Assemblies to align with that of the Lok Sabha to pave the way for a simultaneous election to the Lok Sabha and all Assemblies.

articleTitle: Best-selling British novelist and former politician Jeffrey Archer dies at 86
articleFeaturedImageAlt: jeffrey archer
description: In a statement, HarperCollins' UK CEO and Archer's editor Kate Elton said: "We're all devastated to have lost a writer who has brought joy to generations of readers — and a true friend."
body_raw: Best-selling British novelist and former Tory politician Jeffrey Archer has died at the age of 86, his publisher HarperCollins said on Monday. Archer, whose international literary career spanned decades with over 300 million books sold across 119 countries, was celebrated for fast-paced thrillers like his 1976 debut Not a Penny More, Not a Penny Less and the 1979 hit Kane Abel. His final book, Adam and Eve, is scheduled for release on Tuesday, reported news agency Reuters. Archer featured on the Sunday Times bestseller lists for 14 years and five months and on the New York Times bestseller lists for five-and-a-half years. Archer is also the only author to have held the spot for No.1 Sunday Times bestseller in fiction, short stories and non-fiction. His readers meant everything to him, and just yesterday he met and signed books for hundreds of fans at a sold-out event at the Leicester Square Theatre in London, HarperCollins said in a statement. According to HarperCollins, the author passed away suddenly and peacefully between writing sessions. He had been actively promoting the project on recent radio broadcasts and was set to present at the Cheltenham Literature Festival this coming weekend. Were all devastated to have lost a writer who has brought joy to generations of readers - and a true friend, stated Kate Elton, UK CEO of HarperCollins and Archers longtime editor. Speaking about his conversation with Archer over the authors final book, Elton said When he set out to write Adam and Eve he told me from the very beginning that it would be his final novel - he was so excited about the scale of it and told me that if he could pull it off it would equal anything hed previously written, on which basis he couldnt imagine embarking on any future novels. His political career and scandal Born in north London on April 15, 1940, Archer soon moved to Weston-super-Mare in Somerset, according to the BBC. In 1969, Archer was elected MP for the Lincolnshire constituency of Louth. After serving as a lawmaker for five years, he went on to become Conservative Party deputy chairman under then-Prime Minister of the United Kingdom Margaret Thatcher in the mid-1980s, the BBC reported. However, his career was equally defined by a dramatic public scandal. In 1987, Archer won a record 500,000 660,450 in libel damages after suing the Daily Star over allegations involving a sex worker. The matter resurfaced in 1999 while he was running as the Conservative nominee for London Mayor. Following allegations from a former associate that he had fabricated evidence, Archer was convicted of perjury and perverting the course of justice, drawing a four-year sentence. He ultimately served two years, an experience that inspired his book A Prison Diary. The original libel trial achieved notoriety due to remarks made by Mr. Justice Bernard Caulfield while addressing the jury regarding Archers wife, Mary. Remember Mary Archer in the witness box, Caulfield instructed the jury. Your vision of her will probably never disappear. Has she elegance? Has she fragrance? Would she have, without the strain of this trial, radiance? Directing his comments to the author himself, the judge remarked Is he in need of cold, unloving, rubber-insulated sex in a seedy hotel? He returned to the House of Lords after being released in 2003 and served until he retired in 2024. With inputs from Reuters.

articleTitle: Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha producer claims Ranbir Kapoor film sabotaged their run
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha re release
description: Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha producer has accused the makers of Ranbir Kapoor's film for creating negative buzz around his film.
body_raw: With the success of the devotional film Hanuman Ansh, producers are now feeling more confident about making bigger bets on their mythological projects. Hanuman Ansh, which was released in August, didnt perform well for the first three weeks, but it has been in the theatres for two months now and has earned Rs 424 crore so far. Witnessing this box office trajectory, the producer of Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha is also taking a bet on his film once again, as he is planning to release his film in theatres again. In a recent conversation with India Today, producer Prakash Mahobiya claimed that his film suffered due to a negative marketing campaign and accused the makers of Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana of sabotaging his film. Producer accuses Ranbir Kapoors Ramyana of negative marketing against them Prakash Mahobiya said that competitors of his film spread negative word about Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha on social media. It was negative marketing throughout. We never got a chance to reach our audience. The ones who watched our film really enjoyed it. But if they never got to see it, how will they even have an opinion? he said. ALSO READ Ajay Devgns Drishyam 3 reminds us that more than family, the franchise is about movies Without mentioning any names, Prakash accused the makers of Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana of spreading wrong information about his film. From what we have been told, there are other movies on the same subject coming in, the big-budget film. As far as we know, a lot of negative marketing opportunities have been given to YouTubers, influencers, and other people. They are spreading wrong information and asking people not to watch our film, he claimed. When asked directly if he was accusing the makers of Nitesh Tiwaris film, he said, I dont know for sure, but thats what we are being told. Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha started receiving flak for its poor visual effects when they released their first teaser. Since then, the film has become the subject of many memes online. Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha to be re-released in theaters Prakash Mahobiya claimed that that he announced his film much before Ranbir Kapoors Ramayana. In fact, his film was even ready for release when the other one went on floors. I have made a film for the first time, and I am new to this industry. I have no idea how to market a film after making it. We are not afraid of the loss, but we are disappointed that not many people managed to watch it. And hence, we want to release the film again, he said. He said that while they knew they could not recreate the magic of Ramanand Sagars Ramayan, they were confident that their film could have done well, if given the chance. We are learning. Its our first experience. We are happy we did well. You cannot make a Ramanand Sagar Ramayan. But we wanted to make a film celebrating what we witnessed on screen as children. There is a lot of difference between your film and the other film that will arrive soon. But we are confident that, given a chance, people would have liked our film too, he said. Mahakavya Shri Ramayan Katha features Anjali Arora, Dev Sharma and Rajneish Duggal in lead roles. The film was released in theaters on September 25. Nitesh Tiwaris Ramyana is a two-part film and the first part of the film will release on Diwali. As per producer Namit Malhotra, the two films are being made on a budget of Rs 4,000 crore. The film starsRanbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash, Ravi Dubey, Adinath Kothare, Vivek Oberoi, Lara Dutta, Rakulpreet, Sunny Deol, and many more.

articleTitle: Amid heat and pollution, BMC prunes gardens budget even as 200 wait for repairs
articleFeaturedImageAlt: mahalaxmi race course
description: Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) records show that the budget allocated for the civic body’s garden and trees department, which is responsible for developing and maintaining the city’s green cover, has seen a consistent decline over the past five years.
body_raw: Mumbai is grappling with intense heat and poor air, but the citys most natural defence against both - green and open spaces - appears to be constrained by a severe funding crunch. Records accessed by The Indian Express show that at present, there is a requirement to construct and repair as many as 200 gardens and open spaces in Mumbai. However, the work couldnt be taken up due to financial crunch. Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation BMC records show that the budget allocated for the civic bodys garden and trees department, which is responsible for developing and maintaining the citys green cover, has seen a consistent decline over the past five years. According to the records, the BMC has received around 210 requests from elected representatives, including MLAs and corporators, for creating gardens, recreational grounds and playgrounds across Mumbai. Our department garden and tree has received requests for work worth Rs 710 crore. Since many of the requests are non-feasible and cant be executed on immediate basis, a technical assessment was carried out. It was found that the basic work in many of these gardens requires a funding of Rs 250 crore, an official told The Indian Express on the condition of anonymity. This amount is more than three times the Rs 68-crore budget allocated for the trees and gardens department for the current financial year. Costly affair Officials said the process of creating an open space is a multi-step method. After a land parcel is given to the BMC by the collectors office or the land and revenue department, the first step involves making the soil component fertile for grass plantation. Then utilities such as furniture, gym and playing apparatus along with compound walls are erected. Officials said that as a whole, the cost of constructing a new garden from scratch costs Rs 25-30 crore, while the cost of carrying out basic repair works costs Rs 4-5 crore as per the current rates. There are many gardens in Mumbai where no repair works have been taken up in a decade. In our latest survey, we found that there are recreational grounds where the walkways are broken, apparatus are stolen and toilets are defunct. Many of these spaces are either encroached or shut to the public, the official said. He also added that most of these gardens are located in wards M East Govandi, Deonar, M west Chembur, S Kanjurmarg and Bhandup, L Kurla and K North Jogeshwari. Most of these house the middleclass population. Budget constraints The civic bodys data shows that the budget allocated for the garden and tree department has fallen by 62 per cent in the past three years. For the financial year 2023-24, the BMC had earmarked Rs 180.83 crore for this department. However, the final budget for the garden department for this year stands at Rs 68 crore, against Rs 200 crore proposed in the budget earlier this year. The final budget for the garden and tree department was cut down by 66 per cent in the final allocation as part of it was routed towards infrastructure works, another official told The Indian Express. Budget documents also show that five key infrastructure projects have accounted for 42 per cent of the overall capital expenditure. These projects include BMCs waste water treatment facility WWTF under which the civic body aims to construct seven sewage treatment plants STP, the ongoing road concretising project, the Mumbai Coastal Road North Versova-Dahisar project, the Goregaon Mulund Link Road GMLR project and the BMCs water conveyance tunnel project. We understand that there has been a shortfall in allocation, but one has to realise that the budget estimates were prepared before the elected representatives occupied offices in BMC, according to Ganesh Khankar, leader of the house and Bharatiya Janata Party BJP corporator. We are in talks with the administration to scale up the allocation to the gardens department by 25-30 per cent for this year and correct it further next year, Khankar said. Opposition cries foul Leaders from Opposition parties said that their requests for creating new gardens are either being withheld or being sent back by the administration. Congress corporator and group leader Ashraf Azmi had sent a letter in June demanding repair works in six gardens in his constituency, Kurla. However, he didnt receive any response. In a follow-up letter in September, Azmi wrote, The jogging tracks in the park are in poor condition and the walls are in a state of collapse. The slides, swings and other materials for children have been dilapidated. In a similar letter, Shiv Sena UBT corporator Sachin Padwal requested an upgradation of a garden at Kalachowky. He is yet to get a response. Why open spaces are important Mumbai is one of the space starved cities in the world and according to civic records, the ratio of open space stands at 0.87 square metre per person, while the World Health Organisation WHO recommends that every human being should have access to 9 square meters of open space. In 2022, the union ministry of Housing and urban affairs MoHUA recommended that in India the ratio of open space should be 10-12 square meters per person. The Urban Regional Development Plans Formulation and Implementation URDPFI guidelines, 2014 recommend 10 to 12 sqm of open space per person. State and Union territories, urban development authorities and urban local bodies are expected to adopt the URDPFI guidelines in accordance with prevailing local conditions which may vary from city to city, a MoHUA statement read. Earlier this year, the BMC awarded the work of developing and maintaining a 70 hectare stretch of open space adjoining Mumbais coastal road to the Reliance group. Sources said that the Mahalaxmi Racecourse, which has been taken over by the BMC in 2024, is also likely to be developed and maintained by a private entity under corporate social responsibility CSR drive. The fact that BMC has a small budget for open spaces, clearly shows that the agency is working towards privatising open spaces. In cases like this, universal access to these spaces are usually restricted which equates, for those who are denied access, to not having an open spaces, said Hussain Indorewala, urban planner and researcher. Topographic challenges In August, during an interaction with The Indian Express editorial team, Mumbais municipal commissioner Ashwini Bhide said that considering the citys landmass and topography, the per capita green space is more than enough. As city planners, we need to strike a balance with the reality of Mumbai. We have around 30 to 32 lakh trees in the city, when we include trees from Aarey forest. Out of that 2 lakh trees are along the road. This number is good, but equitable distribution is an issue. But, we can do better, Bhide said. I fully understand that we need more open spaces. But in a city where the land itself is a scarcity, we have to be very innovative in terms of creating spaces. Maybe our buildings should utilise its podium area and create open spaces, she said.

articleTitle: As RBI rate hike looms, action beyond 25 bps a minor possibility
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Reserve Bank of India
description: Markets & economists overwhelmingly see repo rate being raised by 25 basis points on Wednesday. However, there is some speculation of the need to do more.
body_raw: The Reserve Bank of Indias RBIs Monetary Policy Committee MPC began its three-day meeting on Monday. And while most economists are predicting that a 25-basis-point bps increase in the policy repo rate to 5.5 will be announced on Wednesday, talk has emerged that a larger hike could be possible. Its not a debate that there will be a rate hike on Wednesday. But considering the MPC is now acting from behind the curve, it could even be a 50 bps increase, said a senior economist who did not wish to be named. While the six-member MPC had unanimously left the repo rate unchanged at 5.25 on August 5 and offered rather sanguine commentary to go along with it, minutes of its meeting, released two weeks later, struck a different note. Governor Sanjay Malhotra, for instance, said that while the headline retail inflation had averaged only 2 in 2025-26 - when the repo rate was brought down to 5.25 - there were signs it was now normalising. This may suggest a recalibration of policy rate. Meanwhile, Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta noted a case for a hike may emerge during the course of the year. According to Soumya Kanti Ghosh, State Bank of Indias Group Chief Economic Advisor, the RBI may raise rates by 25 bps AT LEAST emphasis Ghoshs. Madhavi Arora and Harshal Patel of Emkay Global Financial Services said that a 50 bps hike cannot be ruled out as a potential policy catch-up. The RBI last increased the repo rate way back in February 2023. As such, any rate hike on Wednesday will be the first in over three-and-a-half years. The headline inflation rate, based on the Consumer Price Index CPI, rose to 4.82 in August, as per latest data. While this is comfortably within the RBIs mandated range of 2-6, it was the third month in a row that it had come in above the medium-term target of 4. The RBIs most recent forecasts also show inflation rising to an average of 5.9 in the last three months of 2026, before cooling to 5.5 and 5.3 in the first two quarters of 2027. Long rate hike cycle? To be sure, the market overwhelmingly expects the repo rate to be raised by only 25 bps on Wednesday. However, many who do so have not only brought forward their prediction of a rate hike from December to October but also think the RBI may end up raising interest rates significantly. Morgan Stanley economists led by Upasana Chachra see the RBI on Wednesday kicking off a run of four consecutive rate hikes of 25 bps each, or 100 bps in total, which will take the repo rate to 6.25 in April. We view the rate hike cycle primarily as policy normalisation rather than disruptive tightening, Morgan Stanley said in a report last week. The word normalisation has found several takers, with some even suggesting the first 50 bps of increase in interest rate will only lead to some normalisation of monetary conditions. The last time the repo rate was 5.25 or lower was in mid-2022, when the RBI was in the middle of reversing the extraordinary measures taken to help the economy hit by the coronavirus pandemic. BofA Securities Rahul Bajoria and Smriti Mehra have not only brought forward their rate hike call of 25 bps to this week from December but also doubled their prediction of total tightening to 100 bps from 50 bps. According to them, the balance of risks is shifting away from accommodation to tightening. This essentially is no longer just about reversing the incremental cut that the RBI had delivered last December but actually taking away the monetary punchbowl before inflation risks become entrenched amid a large inflow of liquidity. Upside risks mounting While CPI inflation is well within the 2-6 mandated range, there are signs that price pressures are rising as many as 314 of the 358 items in the CPI basket saw higher prices in August compared to July. The number was 310 in July and 236 in February, before the West Asia war had begun. Inflation is being driven by a variety of forces higher energy prices due to the West Asia conflict, sub-par monsoons pushing up food prices, skyrocketing chipflation making consumer electronics more expensive, and a low base until April 2027 or so. With growth stronger than expected, demand may impart a push to inflation too. The availability of money in the banking system - or, liquidity - is also very high due to the 133 billion of foreign inflows that have come in via the highly attractive Foreign Currency Non-Resident Bank deposit scheme. These inflows, according to Sajjid Chinoy, Head-Asia Economic Research at JPMorgan, have created a liquidity overhang which has meant that monetary conditions are actually more accommodative than interest rate levels would suggest, he told Bloomberg Television. While the liquidity deluge has lowered the weighted average call rate - interest rate at which banks borrow from each other - from August onwards, the central bank has pushed it up since the second half of September through a variety of instruments, including the sale of government bonds.

articleTitle: EC protesters take over central Delhi, Rahul Gandhi stands on barricade
articleFeaturedImageAlt: rahul gandhi
description: Police said paramilitary and local cops have been deployed along several routes in New Delhi district to ensure security during the protests.
body_raw: Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi, and others were detained on Tuesday as the INDIA bloc leaders marched to the Election Commission office, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and withdrawal of the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls. Security was stepped up across the New Delhi district, and the MPs were stopped on the way, following which they sat on a dharna. After a face-off with the cops, the MPs and leaders were removed from the spot and carried away in a bus. Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi was joined by Trinamool Congress leader Derek Obrien and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. As police moved in to detain the MPs, Rahul Gandhi climbed onto the barricades and began waving the Tricolour. Police personnel then brought him down and began escorting him towards a bus. Gandhi was seen adhering to Gen-Z lingo at the protest as he carried a poster that read Gyanesh, its done bro He posted the slogan on X,too, adding Its time to resign Gyanesh, its done, bro. Time to resign. IndiaAllianceMarch - Rahul Gandhi RahulGandhi October 6, 2026 More than five companies of paramilitary personnel, along with local police, have been deployed along the route from Makar Dwar of Parliament to the Election Commission office. Around 140 Opposition MPs are expected to join the march, which is likely to begin between 10.30 am and 11 am. Multi-layered barricading has been put in place outside the main entrance of the Election Commission and around Jantar Mantar. Police said prohibitory orders under Section 163 remain in force in the district and gatherings are not allowed. Opposition steps up protests over electoral rolls The New Delhi district has been witnessing protests since October 2 by the Left and other opposition parties. On October 1, the INDIA bloc announced a joint action plan which included protests across the country, a march by the Opposition MPs to the EC headquarters, and a mega rally in Delhi on November 1. These decisions were taken at a three-and-a-half-hour meeting of the group in Delhi, which was attended by leaders of 19 parties and Independent MP Kapil Sibal. Among the Opposition faces who attended the meeting were Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi Trinamool Congress TMC chief Mamata Banerjee Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah RJDs Tejashwi Yadav NCP SP MP Supriya Sule PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti CPIM chief M A Baby CPIM-Ls Dipankar Bhattacharya and CPIs P Santosh Kumar. Earlier, around 25 MPs, including top Opposition leaders such as Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and Trinamool Congress MPs Abhishek Banerjee and Derek OBrien, were detained and taken to different police stations in buses. Several party workers from the Congress and Samajwadi Party were also detained. 9 FIRs filed in connection with anti-EC protests In connection with protests over the last five days near Jantar Mantar, police have registered nine FIRs under various sections, including those related to violation of prohibitory orders, rioting, and attacking police personnel while they were discharging their duties. Eighteen people have also been arrested, while more than 300 people were detained and later released. Police are also bracing for another protest later this week. The Cockroach Janta Party CJP has given a call for a demonstration at Jantar Mantar, as part of a nation-wide stir, on October 10, demanding the resignation of CEC Kumar. This is the groups second round of protests in the national capital after its July agitation demanding the resignation of then Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-UG paper leak.

articleTitle: Eye on regulation of student housing, Delhi Govt holds meet with PG owners
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi
description: The law was proposed two days after a five-storey boys’ private PG building collapsed in Southwest Delhi's Satya Niketan on September 6, killing seven people including five Delhi University students.
body_raw: As the Delhi government works on a regulatory framework for students housing accommodation in the Capital, Education Minister Ashish Sood on Monday held consultations with PG owners, operators and managers. Regulating private PGs, addressing safety concerns and expanding student housing have emerged as key components of the Delhi governments proposed Paying Guest Accommodation Regulation and Safety Bill, 2026, officials said on Monday. The law was proposed two days after a five-storey boys private PG building collapsed in Southwest Delhis Satya Niketan on September 6, killing seven people including five Delhi University students. Mandatory registration, safety audits, standard rental agreements and mechanisms to check arbitrary charges are among the measures being considered as part of the proposed regulatory framework, officials said. In a statement issued Monday, the government said the consultation with PG operators was aimed at understanding operational perspectives and addressing key challenges while prioritising student security and basic living standards. Officials said that the need to address the challenges arises owing to the large outstation student population in Delhi, as at least six lakh students come to the Capital annually for higher education. Following the recent unfortunate incident in Delhi, the process of regulating PGs and formulating new laws for them is ongoing. Under this initiative, a few days ago, I had engaged to understand the concerns of the students and residents living in PGs. Today, I met with PG operators, owners, and managers to understand their perspectives and stakes, Sood said in the statement. Before drafting any new law, our government is engaging with everyone through stakeholder consultations. This is true participatory governance-the very model of participatory governance we are working on, he claimed. The consultation comes nearly three weeks after the first meeting of a 20-member High-Powered Committee on Student Accommodation and Safety, chaired by Sood. The committee was constituted to examine the shortage of student housing in Delhi, safety standards and regulation of student accommodation. It is responsible to draft new laws and regulations on PGs, officials said. At its September 15 meeting, the committee discussed mandatory registration and a central database for institutional and private PGs, regulation of lease agreements, curbing arbitrary electricity surcharges and introducing zone-wise rent bands. It also proposed mandatory structural and fire-safety audits, emergency evacuation protocols and regular mock drills for PG operators and students. A centralised digital grievance mechanism was also proposed, through which students would be able to report overcrowding, building safety hazards and lease violations for time-bound resolution. The committee had decided to develop, within 15 days, a portal for PG owners to register their facilities and provide details such as the age and size of the building and fire-safety measures, officials said. A separate portal was proposed to map student data across universities and educational institutions in Delhi. The committee, which has a 60-day deadline to submit its recommendations, also would examine the shortage of university hostels and the possibility of allowing higher floor area ratio for expansion of accommodation on campuses. The Delhi Development Authority DDA and Urban Development Department have been tasked with identifying suitable land parcels for new hostels, while under-utilised government and DDA properties are also to be examined for possible conversion into student housing. Sood said the governments aim was to ensure that students had access to safe and affordable accommodation. Our concern is to ensure that people have access to safe, secure, reliable, and reasonably priced PG accommodations in Delhi, he said. As part of that responsibility, todays Monday discussions were held with the PG operators during this stakeholder consultation, he said.

articleTitle: Vote-rigging claims hit Bengal bypolls; Opposition seeks repoll
articleFeaturedImageAlt: West Bengal bypolls, Nandigram bypoll, Rejinagar bypoll, West Bengal election, Nandigram voting, Rejinagar voting, Congress repoll demand, Bengal booth capture allegations, Humayun Kabir, Suvendu Adhikari, West Bengal bypoll news, October 6 Bengal polling, Indian Express news, Bengal news
description: The BJP rejected the allegations as Opposition candidates staged protests and sought repolling in the two Bengal constituencies.
body_raw: As polling continued in West Bengals Nandigram and Rejinagar Assembly bypolls Monday, Opposition candidates and leaders alleged vote-rigging, booth capture, and the removal of their polling agents, with Congress demanding repolling in both seats. While the Bharatiya Janata Party BJP rejected the allegations, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said polling in Nandigram was peaceful. West Bengal is voting in Nandigram and Rejinagar, with both seats having fallen vacant for different reasons. Democracy is being murdered Abdullahil Kafi, Congress candidate in Rejinagar, staged a sit-in protest near the police station alleging that booths had been captured by BJP agents and that the police and administration are biased towards the ruling party. They are not allowing valid voters to cast their votes. Only BJP agents are in the booths. Our agents are driven away. Multiple agents of BJP are inside the booths looting the votes. When I tried to visit some booths, the police shoved me away. Democracy is being murdered, and votes are being looted. We will plan further agitation, Kafi told reporters. Meanwhile, West Bengal state Congress president Subhankar Sarkar demanded a repoll in Nandigram. Through the help of the administration and the police, a system is in place where common voters are not being allowed to cast their votes. Outsiders were brought into Nandigram who are looting the votes in the booths, Sarkar said. In Rejinagar, the situation is the same. Our candidate in Rejinagar was heckled. I spoke with him over the phone. We have videos and other proofs which we have shared with the Election Commission. We demand a repoll in Nandigram, Sarkar added. Senior Congress leader and former Lok Sabha MP Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury protested outside the district magistrates office in Baharampur, alleging vote loot. They are allowing Hindus to vote but not Muslims. In many areas, they are trying to loot votes. Humayun Kabirs arrest is just an eyewash. They BJP want to keep him relevant so that Muslims vote division and polarisation continue, said Chowdhury speaking with media persons. He was referring to the arrest of Aam Janata Unnayan Party AJUP founder Humayun Kabir earlier in the day in Rejinagar. Opposition wants the old days The BJP rejected the Oppositions allegations of vote-rigging and booth capture, accusing the Congress of attempting to cast doubts on the polling process after demanding repolls in the two constituencies. Congress has demanded a repoll in the two seats. They should have done this yesterday. They know they are going to lose, so they are preparing the ground to question the polling process, BJP spokesperson Debjit Sarkar said. The Opposition wants the old days to return when bombs were hurled, men kicked candidates, and cars were vandalised. That is why the Opposition is trying to instigate. But we want violence-free, peaceful polls, which we are witnessing today. We will not allow hooliganism or violence in polls. If they allege that people are not allowed to vote, why are they not going to the election commission? he asked. Nandigram Congress candidate Milan Pradhan also alleged that BJP workers and agents were being threatened. Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, Mamata All India Trinamool Congress candidate in Rejinagar, wrote a letter to the state chief electoral officer, demanding a repoll. We are observing that in several booths, the police administration cast votes in the dead of night and did not allow agents to enter. Additionally, in many areas, the police administration is driving polling agents away from the booths, casting fake votes rigging, and turning voters away from the booths claiming their votes have already been cast, Chowdhury said in his letter, a copy of which is with The Indian Express. Therefore, Sir, it is my urgent request that you kindly take immediate measures to properly arrange for a re-vote, for which I shall be grateful, he added. Law is the same for all Speaking in Nandigram, Chief Minister Adhikari said polling in the seat has been peaceful. In by-polls, generally it is seen that voting percentage is less. But I think 85 per cent of voters will turn out. I will be happy if 90 per cent of voters turn out. In 2016, I won in Nandigram by 82,000 votes. I think this time we will cross the margin, Adhikari said. He also mentioned the arrest of AJUP leader Kabir. Law is the same for all. Even for me. I can cast my vote in my booth, and now I am in the rest house. I cannot visit other booths or campaign. If I break the law, I will be arrested. That is what happened, he added. The police arrested Kabir in Rejinagar after he accused them of interfering with voting at multiple polling stations. Bengal bypolls The Nandigram seat was left vacant after Adhikari, who won from two constituencies in the Assembly elections earlier this year, decided to retain his other seat. Rejinagar became vacant after Kabir resigned from the seat after winning from Naoda as well. Kabirs son, Gulam Nabi Azad, is an AUJP candidate from Rejinagar in Murshidabad district. CPIMs Md Sayeed, Congresss Kafi, and Safiuzzaman Sheikh of the rebel Trinamool faction, Democratic Trinamool Congress, are also contesting the Rejinagar bypolls. The BJP has pitted Hansirani Rath, the mother of Chandranath Rath, Suvendu Adhikaris aide who was murdered, as its candidate in Nandigram. Votes for all the bypolls will be counted on October 9.

articleTitle: Bombay High Court fines 2 lawyers Rs 52,000 each over ‘won’t spare you’ threat to judge
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bombay High Court threat judge lawyers fine
description: According to the court records, an advocate shouted in the courtroom, alleging that their cases were being treated differently and threatened to complain against the judge and take action through the Bar Association.
body_raw: The Bombay High Court has held two advocates guilty of contempt for threatening a judicial officer during court proceedings and telling him, We will not spare you, and imposed a fine of Rs 52,000 each while referring the matter to the Bar Council for disciplinary action. The court underlined that the legal profession cannot be equated with any other traditional profession, and lawyers have contributed to the countrys independence struggle, helped frame the Constitution and assisted courts in developing the law through research and hard work. Justices Urmila Joshi Phalke and Raj D Wakode were hearing a criminal contempt reference against two advocates arising from proceedings before a civil judge, junior division and judicial magistrate first class, at Arni in Yavatmal district. The legal profession cannot be equated with any other traditional professions. It is not commercial in nature and is stated as noble considering the nature of duties to be performed and its impact on the society.lawyers have contributed in the struggle for independence of the nation. They have helped in the framing of the Constitution of India and they have also assisted the Courts in evolving jurisprudence by doing hard labour and research work, the court said on October 5. It added that the nobility of the legal system is to be ensured at all costs so that the Constitution remains vibrant and to expand its interpretation so as to meet new challenges. Thus, the lawyers who bring the cause to the Court are supposed to protect the rights of individuals of equality and freedom. The lawyers are supposed to be fearless and independent in the protection of rights of litigants. Thus, their role is significant, the court said. Dispute over warrant The case was listed before the Arni court on November 26, 2021, to check the status of a bailable warrant issued against an accused. After the judge recorded that the accused had remained absent despite the warrant, a non-bailable warrant was issued against him, following which his lawyer stated that the accused was present but had not entered the courtroom. However, when the accused was called, he was found to be absent. His lawyer then sought cancellation of the warrant and later stated that the matter had been settled between the parties. He also insisted that the informants evidence be recorded. The judge declined, noting that other accused were also absent and their presence had to be secured. According to the judicial officers account, the advocate then shouted in the courtroom, alleging that the court was troubling them, treating their cases differently and imposing higher fines, and threatened to complain against the judge and take action through the Bar Association. Later, another advocate, who was the then president of the Arni Taluka Court Bar Association, entered the courtroom while the judge was dictating an order, and allegedly told him in Marathi, , which translates to If you take anything on record and act on it, we will not spare you. We will give evidence of corruption against you to senior officials. Conduct aimed to terrorise judge The high court held that the conduct of both advocates interfered with the administration of justice. It said that if they were aggrieved by the judicial order, they had an opportunity to challenge it. Instead, the threats had the effect of pressuring the judicial officer while he was performing his duties. The due administration of law is of greater importance than the success or failure of any individual, the bench said, holding that the conduct of the advocates was aimed to terrorise, pressurise the Judicial Officer. The court said giving threats, addressing a judicial officer in a loud voice and preventing him from passing orders were serious acts, particularly when committed by an advocate who is an officer of the court. The bench held that the statements were apparently made to pressurise and terrorise him from passing an order and described the conduct as scandalous and amounting to misconduct. The advocates denied the allegations and argued that the incident occurred during the heat of arguments. They also relied on unconditional apologies tendered by them later. The court noted that the apologies were not offered at the earliest stage. It also recorded that the respondents had initially failed to appear despite service of notice in the contempt proceedings, leading to bailable warrants being issued against them. Apology is not a weapon of defence to purge the guilty of their offence, nor is it intended to operate as universal panacea, but it is intended to be evidence of real contriteness, the court said. Referring to a Supreme Court verdict, it added, Apology is an act of contrition. Unless apology is offered at the earliest opportunity and in good grace, the apology is shorn of penitence and hence it is liable to be rejected. If the apology is offered at the time when the contemnor finds that the court is going to impose punishment it ceases to be an apology and becomes an act of a cringing coward. The bench also said that where an advocate has a serious grievance against a judicial officer, the grievance can be taken to the proper authority. However, an advocate is expected to act in a dignified manner and maintain respect towards the court. The court said such respect is essential and that contempt jurisdiction protects not only the concerned judges ability to administer justice fearlessly and fairly but also the fair name of the judiciary. Rs 52,000 fine, costs The court held both advocates guilty of contempt but decided against imprisonment. It noted that while the law permits imprisonment, fine or both, fine is ordinarily the rule and imprisonment an exception. Present respondents have committed the contempt of Court, the bench held, adding that considering they were practising lawyers and had subsequently tendered apologies, a fine and reference to the Bar Council would be adequate punishment. The high court directed each advocate to pay a fine of Rs 2,000 within two weeks and referred the proceedings to the Disciplinary Committee of the Bar Council of Maharashtra and Goa for appropriate action. Each advocate was also ordered to pay Rs 50,000 as costs to the Public Welfare Account. Their total financial liability under the order was therefore Rs 52,000 each.

articleTitle: 2032 Olympic emblem officially revealed after it was leaked
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The organising committee had an official launch on Monday, just a few days after it had to hastily convene a new conference to explain the accidental leaking ahead of schedule, the 2032 organizing committee held an official launch on Monday. (Brisbane Olympics organising committee)
description: The Olympic emblem is the crest of a pink cockatoo, an Australian bird, with the color stylized to resemble an Olympic and Paralympic flame, and a shape to resemble the host state of Queensland.
body_raw: Days after an explainer video inadvertently going live resulted in emblem of the 2032 Olympics and Paralympics getting leaked, the organisers have now officially unveiled it. The cockatoo has come out as the winner for the emblem, prevailing over the kangaroo and Koala. The Olympic emblem is the crest of a pink cockatoo, an Australian bird, with the color stylized to resemble an Olympic and Paralympic flame, and a shape to resemble the host state of Queensland. The organising committee had an official launch on Monday, just a few days after it had to hastily convene a new conference to explain the accidental leaking ahead of schedule, the 2032 organizing committee held an official launch on Monday. Brisbane 2032 vice president Tim Mander and chief marketing officer Brent Hill told the weekend news conference the accidental release was a pleasant surprise. Hill embraced the unexpected opportunity, saying the publicity has been incredible. Ahead of the community launch Monday evening in the downtown Southbank parklands, Brisbane 2032 chairman Andrew Liveris said the emblems are an opportunity to promote the unique character of a Games, inviting the world to learn more, visit, invest and be part of an event unlike any other. Lachlan Kennedy, the Brisbane sprinter who set an Australian record for the 100 meters when he ran 9.85 seconds at the Commonwealth Games at Glasgow in July, attended the emblem lauch and told local TV broadcasters I love it. I think it represents Brisbane well. Its unique, he said, I think its got soul to it. For Mikaela Cojuangco Jaworski, who heads the IOCs coordination commission for the 2032 Games, the emblems represented a vibrant expression of the nature and character of the region. The Olympics and Paralympics will be centered on the state capital, Brisbane, but cities across the state, including the Gold Coast and the Sunshine Coast, will host competitions. Australia has twice previously hosted the Summer Olympics, at Melbourne in 1956 and at Sydney in 2000. The Sydney emblem design contained representations of famous landmarks including the Sydney Opera House, the citys famous harbor and beaches, as well as boomerangs, sun and rocks. Brisbanes Lord Mayor Adrian Schrinner on Monday said the emblems are a celebration of our city, our lifestyle. They reflect the Brisbane that people know and love vibrant, resilient, connected, friendly, playful and a little bit cheeky, Schrinner said. They are also a symbol of the excitement building across our city. With just under six years to go, we are already preparing to welcome the world to Australias lifestyle capital. Organizers said First Nations elements were contained within the emblems, with cockatoos seen as messengers carrying cultural meaning and linking people to place, story and ceremony. The emblems are separate to the Games mascot, which will be revealed closer to the Games. An explainer video meant to go live after a planned ceremonial event briefly appeared on the events YouTube channel on Friday night. Screenshots of images and text soon circulated on social media. With Agency inputs

articleTitle: Drain near senior citizen’s home remains clogged despite complaints, he wins Rs 15,000
articleFeaturedImageAlt: PWD sewerage consumer drain puducherry
description: The consumer commission in Puducherry was hearing a complaint filed by a man seeking directions to the authorities to inspect and resolve the blockage in the sewer system linked to his residence.
body_raw: A Puducherry district consumer commission has awarded Rs 15,000 to a 60-year-old man after a sewerage block linked to his residence allegedly went unaddressed despite repeated complaints to public works authorities. The commission directed the authorities to inspect the drain system and carry out necessary desilting, noting that prolonged blockage could cause inconvenience, discomfort and mental distress to the occupants of residential premises. President S Mouttouvel, along with members A S Suvitha and G Arumugam, while hearing the mans complaint, held that the authorities failure to attend to the blockage, despite the matter having been repeatedly brought to their notice, amounted to deficiency in service. The opposite parties PWD have not produced any material to establish that the grievance was attended to or effectively rectified and that the sewerage problem resulted in inconvenience and unhygienic conditions in and around the residential premises, we are of the considered view that the Complainant is entitled to reasonable compensation, the August 28 order read. No solution despite complaints The man claimed that he had availed himself of the sewerage service of the Public Works Department PWD under the applicable policy and paid the charges as and when claimed by the authorities. He added that on December 6, 2025, there was a blockage of the drainage line to his house, causing severe inconvenience to him and his family members and also posing a health hazard. Aggrieved, he approached the PWD and submitted a written complaint to resolve the sewerage blockage, but allegedly no action was taken despite an assurance that immediate action would be taken. He also submitted that the stagnant sewage linked to his residence had been continuously emitting foul smell and attracting mosquitoes and insects, thereby posing extremely unhygienic living conditions and causing serious health hazards to him and his family members. The man was represented by advocates S Vimal and M Dhinagaran before the commission. Sewerage, drainage and public health The commission noted that the man has specifically pleaded that the blocked sewerage line resulted in stagnant sewage, foul smell, attraction of mosquitoes and insects, and unhygienic conditions around his residence. The failure of the opposite parties department to attend to and rectify the sewerage blockage caused not merely inconvenience but also mental agony and physical hardship to the complainant, it observed. It also pointed out that sewerage and drainage are essential civic services directly connected with sanitation, public health and the maintenance of hygienic living conditions. A service provider entrusted with the maintenance of a sewerage system cannot be expected merely to receive charges from consumers it is equally incumbent upon the concerned authority to maintain the system with reasonable care and to take appropriate and timely steps when a specific complaint regarding blockage or malfunction is brought to its notice, it added. It was also noted that the department did not appear before the commission and held that this did not dispense with the commissions duty to examine whether the complainant has established his case. Accordingly, the commission directed the authorities to do a thorough inspection of the drainage system connected to the mans residence. It added that if any blockage, defect or obstruction was found, the department should undertake all remedial measures, including desilting, repair and, wherever required, restoration or replacement of the affected portion of the sewer line. The commission directed the department to ensure proper, efficient and uninterrupted functioning of the sewerage system on payment of any charges lawfully payable by the complainant. It also directed the department to pay Rs 10,000 to the complainant for the deficiency in service and attendant mental agony, physical hardship and other suffering, along with litigation expenses of Rs 5,000. Takeaway This ruling shows that government authorities responsible for sewerage maintenance can be held liable for deficiency in service when they fail to act on repeated complaints about a drain blockage. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states and union territories Puducherry 180-0425-1082 or call the National Consumer Helpline on 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: After HC rap over depleting water table, Gurugram plans borewell phase-out
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gurugram
description: In parallel, the Municipal Corporation of Gurugram (MCG) is also collaborating with IIT Gandhinagar to install water injection well systems.
body_raw: Following scrutiny from the Punjab and Haryana High Court over the rapid depletion of groundwater and unchecked extraction across the district, Gurugram authorities on Monday drew up an action plan directing government departments to gradually discontinue the use of borewells and push industrial units to switch to tertiary-treated wastewater for operational needs. At a high-level review meeting chaired by Gurugram Metropolitan Development Authority GMDA Chief Executive Officer P C Meena on Monday, departments currently reliant on groundwater were instructed to identify alternative supply channels and phase-out tube wells, officials said. All concerned agencies have been given a deadline of October 6 to submit detailed roadmaps outlining measures to cut extraction and scale up rainwater recharge. The district administration was also tasked with framing a comprehensive enforcement strategy to identify and seal unauthorised borewells across the city GMDA spokesperson Neha Sharma said. Addressing the meeting, Meena highlighted the need to replace fresh groundwater usage with tertiary-treated wastewater from sewage treatment plants STPs. Currently, the GMDA supplies 10 million litres per day MLD of treated effluent to the textile industry. Now, authorities plan to bring other industrial clusters under the treated water distribution network. To ensure accountability at the local level, the Haryana State Pollution Control Board HSPCB was directed to monitor the functioning of captive STPs in group housing societies to ensure compliance with discharge standards. Directives were also issued to mandate separate electricity connections for these treatment plants and strictly enforce the zero-liquid discharge policy in residential complexes, Sharma added. The meeting saw authorities resolve to shift focus toward retaining rainwater within the urban catchment rather than allowing run-off to discharge into storm-water drains, officials said. This strategy includes reviving water bodies facing degradation, clearing encroachments, lowering green-belt levels to trap surface run-off, and converting designated neighborhood parks into bioswales. The HC in ongoing proceedings concerning the citys shrinking groundwater reserves had directed the Mondays meeting. It had said it expects the authorities to examine the issues and to suggest appropriate measures to tackle the worsening situation of ground water in Gurugram, noting that if the situation continues unabated then the future generation would have to face disastrous consequences. In an effort to refill underground water supplies, the GMDA, in partnership with Tata Consultancy Services TCS, is also carrying out a feasibility study to construct a large underground rainwater retention reservoir beneath the football ground at the Tau Devi Lal Stadium in the city, officials said. On the recharge front, the GMDA has rolled out five advanced scientific harvesting structures designed in collaboration with IIT Delhi. Three structures, at Sectors 31 and 39, and at AIT Park in Sector 55, have been commissioned, while work on a fourth at Rezangla Chowk is underway, Sharma explained. Prof Anshuman from The Energy and Resources Institute TERI, who attended the meeting, endorsed the system as an effective mechanism to halt aquifer depletion. In parallel, the Municipal Corporation of Gurugram MCG is also collaborating with IIT Gandhinagar to install water injection well systems. A water injection well system is a deep shaft that pushes treated water deep underground to maintain reservoir pressure, or safely dispose of wastewater. Meanwhile, according to the Haryana Water Resources Authority, rejuvenation work on 142 ponds has been planned across the district, of which 68 have been completed and 74 are in progress, alongside 21 ponds revived under rural employment schemes. Within municipal limits, 32 water bodies have been restored and work on 21 others is underway in the city, officials said.

articleTitle: ‘I have done my duty’: Harmanpreet Kaur steps down as India captain in all formats
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Harmanpreet Kaur of India during the 5th T20I match between India and Sri Lanka at Greenfield International Stadium, Thiruvananthapuram, India, on December 30, 2025. (CREIMAS for BCCI)
description: Harmanpreet Kaur, India's only Women's World Cup-winning captain, has stepped down from the role in all formats.
body_raw: Harmanpreet Kaur, the only Indian captain to have won the Womens World Cup, announced on Tuesday that she has stepped down from the role with immediate effect. Harmanpreet made the announcement in a lengthy post on her Instagram account. Today, I step down as captain of the Indian Womens Cricket Team across all formats. This is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life, said Harmanpreet in her statement. Widely rated among Indias greatest cricketers of all time, Harmanpreet took over as Indias full-time captain across formats after Mithali Raj retired in 2022, having led the team periodically before that as Mithalis deputy. She has also been Indias T20I captain since 2016. Her last act as skipper of the side was leading the team to their second consecutive gold medal at the Asian Games last month. I leave the captaincy today with a heart full of emotions , but also with PEACE. Because I genuinely believe My team is in a good place. A team with talent, character, belief and a future that I am incredibly excited to watch and be a part of, Harmanpreet further said in her statement. I feel I have done my duty. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Harmann imharmanpreetkaur Harmanpreet has confirmed that she will continue to be available for India in all formats. Captaincy may end today, but my love for Indian cricket never will. Thank you to every teammate, coach, support staff, management , BCCI , family members every single fan who stood by me through the highs and lows. Blood. Sweat. Sarifice. Pride. I gave it all Now, Im ready to play for the love of the game again. Captaincy ends. The journey continues, she concluded in her statement. She has led the Indian team in five Tests, 51 ODIs and 155 T20Is. The crowning achievement of her career came last year, when under her captaincy India won their maiden Womens World Cup title, beating South Africa in the final. Notably, they had defeated the runaway favourites and record winners Australia in the semifinal before that. Harmanpreet is overall just the third Indian captain to have won the 50-over World Cup after Kapil Dev and MS Dhoni and one of five Indians to have won any World Cup as skipper, with Rohit Sharma and Suryakumar Yadav leading the mens side to victory in the T20 World Cups of 2024 and 2026 respectively. She has captained the Indian team in 155 T20I matches, the most for any player across mens or womens cricket. She has played a total of 210 T20I matches, which is also the most for any player across genders. Harmanpreet made her international debut in March 2009 in an ODI against Pakistan in the Womens World Cup that year. Her T20I debut came a couple of months after that against England. She made her Test debut against England in August 2014.

articleTitle: Noel Tata blasts 2 dissenters, repeats ‘no mandatory listing’ claim
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Tata trust
description: The four trustees of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust launched an attack on Trusts Vice-chairmen Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh, accusing them of abandoning collective decisions, airing personal views in the media, and allegedly breaching their fiduciary duties.
body_raw: The Reserve Bank of Indias RBIs communication on Tata Sons application to surrender its registration has, rather than weakened, strengthened the position of Tata Trusts and does not ask Tata Sons to pursue a listing, Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata and three trustees said. In a letter to Trusts Vice-chairmen Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh on Monday, Noel Tata and trustees Darius Khambata, Neville N Tata and Bhaskar Bhat argued that the RBIs communication did not overturn decisions taken in 2025, as it merely declined Tata Sons application and neither mandated a listing nor prescribed any specific course of action. The four trustees said the RBIs communication instead made it more urgent to find a lawful alternative to listing that would meet the settled objective of the Trusts and Tata Sons. The proposal outlined in their letter, they said, would, if implemented, take Tata Sons outside the regulatory category on which the RBIs communication was based. The Tata Trusts did what the Board of Tata Sons asked of them. The proposal set out in the Letter gives effect to the decisions unanimously taken by SDTT and SRTT on May 28, 2025 and July 28, 2025, which both of you joined, the letter said. It was sent to the Chairman of Tata Sons for the consideration of the Board and for submission to the RBI, which is exactly the course the Board itself had agreed, they said. Far from usurping the functions of the Tata Sons board, the Trusts responded to its request, they said. Whatever view is taken of the resolutions passed at the meeting of September 17, and the Trusts position on the resolution concerning the Chairman is well known, the request for the Trusts guidance was made by Tata Sons, not by the Trusts, the letter said. The four trustees of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust SDTT launched an attack on Srinivasan and Singh, accusing them of abandoning collective decisions, airing personal views in the media, and allegedly breaching their fiduciary duties. Credibility of opposition under question They questioned the credibility of Srinivasan and Singhs opposition to the Trusts stand on Tata Sons. The four trustees effectively tell the two vice-chairmen you cant first participate in unanimous decisions to keep Tata Sons unlisted and then champion listing without taking the matter back to the Trusts. Their accusation is summed up in one caustic phrase. The trustees referred to the two mens changed position in April 2026 as their epiphanies, saying they suddenly decided that listing was good for Tata Sons and its minority shareholders. Singh and Srinivasan had last week questioned Tata Trusts for sending Tata Sons reorganisation proposal without consulting them. Neville is the son of Noel Tata. They alleged that the two did not raise their changed position at any of the three SDTT meetings held after April. You chose not to raise your changed view for collective deliberation with your co-trustees, the trustees said, arguing that the conduct undermined the Trusts resolutions, as also the pending application made by Tata Sons to the RBI and amounted to a breach of your fiduciary duties. The letter makes clear that for the trustees, the dispute is not a mere difference of opinion. They are questioning whether Srinivasan and Singh acted consistently with their responsibilities as trustees. Past decisions on Tata Sons listing The issue stems from a series of unanimous decisions taken by the Trusts and Tata Sons over the past two years. In March 2024, the Tata Sons board, with Srinivasan and Singh then serving as Tata Trust-nominated directors, unanimously decided that Tata Sons should remain unlisted. Tata Sons repaid borrowings and redeemed preference shares aggregating about Rs 20,000 crore and applied to the RBI to surrender registration. On May 28, 2025, SDTT and Sir Ratan Tata Trust, with the participation of both Srinivasan and Singh, unanimously authorised the Tata Sons chairman to explore every available route to preserve its unlisted status, including discussions with the Shapoorji Pallonji Group. Two months later, on July 28, the two trusts again unanimously resolved that it should remain unlisted and engage with the RBI to achieve that objective. The four trustees now ask What happened to those decisions? Those resolutions have not been rescinded, they said. Nor does the record show that either Srinivasan or Singh asked the trustees to reconsider them or proposed that the Trusts should now support listing, they said. Charity Commissioner proceedings The trustees expressed significant concerns over the duos Charity Commissioner proceedings. They accused them of adopting a contradictory position demanding collective deliberation while approaching the Charity Commissioner to prevent the trust from meeting. The trustees said the duo filed complaints on September 25, seeking, among other things, directions preventing SDTT from convening meetings or acting through circular resolutions. They also sought restrictions concerning the Trust chairmans participation in Tata Sons matters and asked that the composition of the SDTT board be frozen. The response is scathing. We find it difficult. to reconcile the concern expressed in your letter, that SDTT should act only after deliberation at meetings of its trustees, the four trustees said, with the fact that the two had already asked the regulator to prevent the trustees from meeting at all. They said they would hope that, given the refreshing spirit of your letter, both complaints will now be withdrawn. Srinivasans conduct as Tata Sons director The letter also takes direct aim at Srinivasans conduct as a Tata Sons director. According to the trustees, SDTT had passed a circular resolution on September 16 asking Srinivasan not to participate in or vote on any item concerning the listing of Tata Sons. Srinivasan declined, maintaining that the Trust could not dictate how he exercised his judgment as a director. The trustees then accuse him of ignoring an earlier SDTT decision concerning the appointment of a new Tata Sons chairman. On August 13, SDTT had resolved to initiate the constitution of a Selection Committee under Article 118 of Tata Sons Articles of Association, they said. Yet, at the September 17 board meeting, Srinivasan voted for the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as chairman, despite the absence of a recommendation from the Selection Committee and against the vote of the Trust chairman. The four trustees said this effectively neutralised the affirmative rights granted to Tata Trust-nominated directors under Articles 118 and 121. The broader battle, however, is over Tata Sons future. The Trusts insist that the September 28 proposal was not an attempt to override the Tata Sons board. Rather, they said it was a response to a request made by the board itself after the RBI rejected Tata Sons application to surrender its registration. The letter ends with a clear challenge to Srinivasan and Singh if they genuinely want to protect Tata Sons, they should come forward with a better alternative to listing. If indeed you have anything constructive to offer, we would welcome your considered suggestions on means to avoid listing that are better than set out in the Letter. That challenge captures the extraordinary nature of the Tata Trusts internal battle. The dispute is no longer a quiet disagreement over corporate strategy. It has become a direct contest over fiduciary duty, institutional authority and who gets to speak for the Trusts. For the Tata Group, whose governance model has long been built around trusteeship and institutional continuity, the spectacle of trustees publicly accusing other trustees of abandoning collective decisions is deeply unsettling, said an observer. The question now is not merely whether Tata Sons will remain unlisted. It is whether the Tata Trusts can resolve a bitter internal battle over who has the authority to decide its future - and whose fiduciary duty comes first.

articleTitle: ‘Ritu Da’ corner, terrace den and home bar: Inside Jisshu Sengupta’s 4-storey Lake Gardens home
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Inside Jisshu Sengupta’s 4-Storey Kolkata Home
description: "I lost my mother in 2008, and since then Ritu da became a guardian to me and Nilaanjana. But what pains me the most is that he could not see this house before passing away," shared the Bhooth Bangla actor.
body_raw: Bengali actor Jisshu Sengupta-who has lived his whole life in rented places -moved into his own apartment after marrying his wife, Nilaanjana. But in 2012, when he decided to move to a bigger place, he locked down the current house-a sprawling 4-storey bungalow in the heart of Lake Gardens, Kolkata. If you look around my place, the things Nilaanjana and I were on the same page about included wooden furniture and elements, lots of greenery and muted colours. And she specifically wanted stained glass elements in the house, Sengupta shared. The living area echoes a softer colour palette, with cream upholstery and warm lighting setting a mood for cosy evenings and hosting gatherings. Brass and metal figurines, sculptures of Lord Buddha, travel memorabilia, and coffee table books keep the decor intimate. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Home bar The tour begins with the actor sharing the propertys backstory while leaning against a rustic home bar setup. Brick walls with wooden shelves holding a variety of liquor bottles, wine glasses hanging upside down, and decor elements resembling bottle caps make the space feel straight out of 60s America. From the first floor to the fourth floor, 98.98 per cent has been designed by Nilaanjana. I dont have much contribution, apart from the room on the terrace, which is my den. And the gym park, which has been designed by me, he further added. Private gym The fitness area, with state-of-the-art equipment like kettlebells, a tricep dip, a rowing machine, and a boxing bag, was one of the first spaces designed in the house. A lot of people dont know this, but there used to be a time I was heavily into fitness, because I represented Bengal under-19 in cricket. I was into sports and fitness. But since I began acting, fitness took a backseat, the actor revealed during the first episode of Asian Paints Moner Thikana. The Rituparno Ghosh corner Sengupta took us to the most special corner in his house, a space dedicated in the loving memory of his mentor and filmmaker Rituparno Ghosh. Teal walls contrast with wooden wall panels, while plush beige curtains and green plants complement two dark wooden chairs. A golden bird lamp sits inside a hanging cage, illuminating the space with a soft glow. Everything you can see here, from the chairs to the paintings to the knick-knacks on the table, all of them have been gifted by Ritu da. I lost my mother in 2008, and since then Ritu da has been a guardian to Nilaanjana and me. But what pains me the most is that he could not see this house before passing away. This is his corner, technically, he shared. Rubeena Singh, Founder of The Verve Collective, interior stylist home decorator, said that when it comes to designing a house around sentimental objects, the goal is to make it look intentional rather than cluttered. Focus on curation, not collection, she says. You dont have to display everything you own simply because it is sentimental. Choose the pieces that mean the most to you and give them enough space to be noticed, she told indianexpress.com. The terrace den Everyone is allowed here, Sengupta said, before giving us a peek into a space where his closest friends and colleagues can chat, play music and have a good time. Drums and guitars, Marvel posters and couch cushions keep the vibe casual, while the wooden wall panelling gives the space a barn-like feel. This is a place where I actually chill. I spend most of the day in this room. From reading scripts to taking meetings, I do all my work here. Especially when Im alone, no one disturbs me - which is the best part of this room, he shared As the camera zooms out, Sengupta walked up the stairs to the upper terrace, a platform where wrought-iron chairs and a wooden table make for the perfect escape to enjoy his morning coffee or evening tea, surrounded by potted plants and pink flowers.
