articleTitle: Nearly 12,000 books banned in US schools; Charlotte Bronte, Margaret Atwood among those pulled
articleFeaturedImageAlt: usa bans books across public schools
description: US public schools recorded 11,982 book bans in the 2025-26 school year, the highest annual total tracked by PEN America, with Texas reporting the most removals.
body_raw: US public schools recorded almost 12,000 book bans in the 2025-2026 school year, the highest number for a single year. The count comes from a new report, Banned in the USA, released Monday during Banned Books Week, when schools and libraries hold events to draw attention to censorship. In all, 11,982 bans were logged. They affected 7,370 individual works and more than 4,000 authors, illustrators and translators, a record number of unique titles. About 34,000 bans have been counted since 2021, which suggests removals are no longer isolated cases but a steady pattern across the country. The figures come from PEN America, a free expression group that has tracked school book removals for five years. Here are some of the titles named in the findings Book Title Author Sold most banned title, 25 removals Patricia McCormick The Handmaids Tale Margaret Atwood Speak Laurie Halse Anderson Crank Ellen Hopkins The Shining Stephen King The Green Mile Stephen King Jane Eyre Charlotte Bronte Tokyo Ghoul manga series Sui Ishida Texas recorded the most bans this year, more than 8,100. The surge is linked to a state law, SB13, which bars broad categories of books from schools. Florida had held the top spot for the previous three years. Both states have passed restrictive laws, and politicians and conservative activists there have pushed for removals. A total of 114 school districts banned books, the highest number ever in a single year. Also Read NCERTs new Art textbook covers up Mohenjodaros Dancing Girl Technology appears to be playing a growing part too, as per the report. School district administrators are relying more on artificial intelligence tools to decide which books to pull. Because such tools can scan and flag many titles at once, they may help explain how the number of removals climbed so quickly alongside the new state laws. Stephen King was the most banned author for the second year in a row, with his books pulled 312 times. The most banned single title was Sold, a young adult novel about a girl from Nepal who is sold into sexual servitude. Other frequent targets include The Handmaids Tale, Speak, a prize-winning novel about a teenager who falls silent after being raped, and Crank, a novel about drug addiction. Also Read Ram Rajya, NEP, Sengol What students will learn in NCERT in Governance and Public Policy chapter The reasons behind the bans have stayed fairly consistent. Themes of race, racism, sexuality and gender identity are still the most common grounds for challenges. More than 4,500 of the banned works were on the list for the first time, from the 19th-century classic Jane Eyre to the manga series Tokyo Ghoul. The bans also reached books that young people pick up by choice. Fiction made up more than 90 of banned young adult titles, and popular manga was among them. Supporters of school libraries argue that they make ideas available to everyone, whatever their personal or political views. The report says bans limit the freedom to read and narrow the range of voices and perspectives students can see. With inputs from AP

articleTitle: G7 to release 100 million barrels of oil, diesel: Will this bring prices under control?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A tank farm at the Klesch oil refinery in in Germany's Gelsenkirchen where diesel, gasoline and heating oil are produced. (AP)
description: Diesel is among the most important petroleum fuels globally due to its use in transportation, agriculture, construction, and other industries. This also makes it the most politically sensitive fuel amid the ongoing geopolitical crises.
body_raw: Late last week, the Group of Seven G7 countries agreed to release 100 million barrels of crude oil and petroleum products from emergency reserves, including substantial volumes of diesel, amid apparent pressure from US President Donald Trump. With diesel prices at US pumps reaching record levels, the American president had been pressuring Europe to release their diesel stockpiles, and even warned that the US could ban diesel exports amid global supply tightness and soaring prices of the fuel. Following the G7 announcement, Trump - who wants to lower diesel prices ahead of the midterm polls in the US in November - announced that the US wont ban its diesel exports. Interestingly, Trump said that a diesel export ban was never really on the table, although he himself had publicly stated over the past few days that it was under consideration and that he was inclined towards it. US and European diesel prices had surged in recent weeks amid the highly constrained fuel movement through the Strait of Hormuz as well as attacks on Russias oil and gas infrastructure. Diesel supplies are tight, inventories are low and importers are scrambling to secure the fuel from geographies not impacted by conflict or chokepoint closures. Diesel is among the most important petroleum fuels globally due to its use in transportation, agriculture, construction, and other industries. This also makes it the most politically sensitive fuel amid the ongoing geopolitical crises. While these steps wont do much to deal with the structural problems that the diesel market is grappling with, they are expected to put some downward pressure on international diesel prices, at least in the short-term, according to industry experts. Diesel prices have already drifted downwards following the announcement. The extent and duration of relief will largely depend on whether global diesel flows from West Asia and Russia improve hereon. For India, these developments are broadly positive, as a lower international diesel price would help consumers, particularly bulk and industrial buyers who are supposed to pay prices in line with global rates, even as retail consumers continue to get diesel much below international prices as public sector fuel retailers are absorbing the hit for this segment. Any cool-off in diesel prices will also reduce these companies heavy under-recoveries on retail fuel sales. If bulk diesel rates decline, it would be a positive for the Indian economy as inflationary pressure would be eased to some extent. But on the flip side, higher international supply could squeeze the supernormal margins of standalone Indian refiners - who dont have much exposure to retail fuel sales - as well as large diesel exporters, which are predominantly private sector refiners like Reliance Industries and Nayara Energy. G7 decision focused on shoring up diesel supply The G7 last week agreed to coordinate, through the International Energy Agency IEA, the release of 100 million barrels of crude oil and petroleum products over four months, including front-loaded substantial diesel release in the first 20 days. The countries also agreed to examine additional diesel releases if required by market conditions. The grouping also said that it will avoid energy export restrictions among its members, while also calling on other producers to avoid export bans. Going beyond just the emergency stocks, the group has also agreed to coordinate refinery maintenance schedules so that several refineries dont shut down for maintenance simultaneously, and also called for higher refinery utilisation wherever possible, particularly to boost production of diesel, the workhorse of the global economy. The G7 wants a substantial quantity of diesel to reach the market within days, instead of being spread-out over the four-month period, which shows that the tightness in diesel flows is among the most immediate pressure points in the global energy market. But there is a limit to what reserve releases can accomplish on their own, as strategic stocks are not endless. Releasing strategic stocks of diesel is primarily a bridge to get through a period of unusually tight physical supply, rather than a solution to the underlying disruption in refinery operations, and shipping. Europe has become increasingly dependent on diesel imports from beyond the region over the past few years as it moved away from Russian fuel amid the war in Ukraine. The West Asia war has further exacerbated the supply situation for Europe, which now depends heavily on American diesel. With the decision to release emergency diesel stockpiles, the G7 is putting additional supplies in the market, while also neutralising the threat of a US diesel export ban. Trumps diesel export ban threat Amid surging cracks or margins on diesel globally, US diesel prices jumped sharply in recent weeks, reaching record levels of about 6.5 per gallon and bringing the pain of faraway wars to the American consumer. The timing is significant as the US is set to go into mid-term polls come November, and the Trump administration is evidently feeling the pressure. Diesel is politically sensitive in the US as it is not just a transportation fuel, bit also powers long-haul trucks, agricultural machinery, construction equipment, and other heavy industrial equipment. This means that a jump in diesel prices can quickly feed into consumer-level inflation. According to experts, Trumps threat appeared driven largely by the political problem created by high pump prices in the US, and was enough to set off a good measure of panic and debate in the market. The US is one of the largest diesel exporters globally, and with diesel exports from West Asia and Russia hit due to the conflicts there, American diesel exports have surged further over the past six-seven months. In August, US diesel exports averaged at record levels of about 1.6 million barrels per day bpd, up from around 1 million bpd in February, before the West Asia war began. But the simplistic assumption that restricting diesel exports would shore up supply all over the US and in turn lower prices there doesnt really hold water. That is because there are regional disparities within the US when it comes to fuel production and supply, and the fact that US pump prices are linked to international prices. According to industry participants, analysts, and experts, a ban or major restriction of US diesel exports would have affected countries that are regular importers of American diesel, leading to a further spurt in international prices of the fuel. The adverse impact wouldnt have just been beyond American shores though. Experts point out that any significant export curb was bound to lead to a reduction in refinery production rates in the US, which would hit the USs production of other fuels like petrol as well, ultimately leading to even higher fuel prices there. To that extent, any such move could have easily become counter-productive and self-defeating, and numerous petroleum industry chambers in the US had warned Washington about these risks. The US isnt one unified fuel market. Roughly 54 of the nations refining capacity is concentrated along the Gulf Coast, where refineries produce more fuel than consumers in that region use. The West Coast produces enough diesel to meet its own demand but still imports gasoline petrol and jet fuel. The East Coast, by contrast, lacks sufficient refining capacity and relies in part on diesel supplied from elsewhere - including imports, which account for about 10 of its diesel supply, trade group American Petroleum Institute API had earlier said. According to the API, which believed that a diesel export ban would break havoc at home and abroad, if US diesel exports were blocked, surplus fuel could start filling storage on the Gulf Coast, and the only way to avoid producing even more surplus diesel would be to process less crude oil. But cutting refinery runs would not reduce diesel production alone. It would also mean producing less gasoline, jet fuel and other products at a time when global fuel supplies are already tight, it had said. Exports allow US refineries to balance their systems and maximize production. An export ban would require refineries to throttle utilization to reduce diesel production to equal domestic demand. Falling utilization would result in less gasoline and jet fuel production and higher prices for those products as well. Meanwhile, areas of the US that import fuel primarily the Northeast would face higher prices for all fuels that would now be in even shorter supply globally. This could not come at a worse time for consumers as home heating oil season is about to begin, dozens of American petroleum chambers wrote in a joint representation to Trump a couple of weeks back.

articleTitle: France school protests: 15-year-old boy loses hand after police grenade explodes
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Students on Tuesday gather on a street in Paris before a demonstration against under-resourced schools [AP Photo].
description: A teenager lost his hand after a police grenade exploded during high school protests in Lens, France. Over 5,000 arrests have been made as unrest spreads nationwide over school underfunding
body_raw: A 15-year-old boy lost his hand and part of his lower arm after a police dispersal grenade exploded during clashes between high school protesters and riot police in Lens, northern France, as nationwide student protests entered their third week. Local newspaper La Voix du Nord reported that the teenager had picked up the grenade. Pas-de-Calais prefect Francois-Xavier Lauch said an investigation had been opened but declined to comment on the exact circumstances of the incident. He said between 200 and 250 demonstrators had been throwing objects at police. The injury came on the eve of a nationwide day of student demonstrations over overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages, underfunding and deteriorating school buildings. The protests, which began in September in the Paris region, have since spread across France. Reuters ALSO READ France high school students protest What sparked violence France student protests How widespread is the unrest? The incident came as Frances high-school protests entered their third week, with students demanding action over overcrowded classrooms, staff shortages, underfunding and deteriorating school buildings. Student unions had called for a nationwide day of demonstrations on Tuesday. In Lille, clashes erupted between students and police. Cops had to fire tear gas shells in Toulouse, and demonstrators attempted to force their way into a central Paris school by setting a fire. Education Minister Edouard Geffray said that two dozen schools were targeted by arsonists and vandals. He also said 78 teachers and at least 190 students have been injured in the protests. He, however, added that student participation has declined in recent days. ALSO READ Why are thousands of French students protesting, and why is Macron worried? Protesters allege police excess The police response has drawn sharp flak from rights groups who accused authorities of using heavy-handed tactics against minors, including batons, tear gas, and rubber bullets,Reuters reported. Among several ongoing investigations into police conduct, authorities are reviewing an incident where a 16-year-old suffered a severe eye injury from a rubber bullet. Presidential election in six months With the Presidential election six months away, the unrest has triggered fierce political debate and placed further pressure on a government attempting to manage a growing Budget deficit. Government officials and Marine Le Pens far-Right Rassemblement National National Rally have accused the hard-Left La France Insoumise France Unbowed party of stoking the protests. The latter has rejected the claims, while alleging that the administration is politicising the crisis. Meanwhile, the French Justice Ministry reported that over 5,000 arrests have been made since the protests began, with 87 involving minors, and government spokesperson Maud Bregeon confirmed that fast-tracked legislation will soon make young offenders or their parents financially liable for property damage.

articleTitle: ‘Beyond healthy criticism’: Court orders takedown of Punjab Congress politician’s AI videos
articleFeaturedImageAlt: AI-generated videos, AI deepfake videos, Facebook AI videos, Batala Di Rajneeti, Kachi Laan, Thanedar Uncle, Punjab politics AI videos, Chandigarh court order, Punjab and Haryana High Court
description: A Chandigarh court restrains three Facebook pages from sharing AI-generated videos allegedly portraying Congress leader Amandeep Kumar negatively.
body_raw: A Chandigarh court has ordered three Facebook pages to remove AI-generated videos for allegedly maligning the reputation of Punjab Congress functionary Amandeep Kumar. The court said that the content appeared to go beyond healthy public criticism and could adversely affect the health of our democracy and the process of manufacturing of public consent. Kumar sought an interim injunction on the transmission of AI-generated videos in a civil case against the three Facebook pages. Judicial Magistrate First Class Kuldeep Singhnoted that the AI-generated scripted videos contained politically calculated material, in favour of the ruling party in Punjab, and against Kumar, who is from an opposition political party, and held that there was a prima facie case and irreparable loss and balance of convenience in favour of Kumar. The said pages appear to have a political agenda which is beyond healthy public criticism and apparently maligns the image of an individual without verified facts, knowingly. This is quite a serious act done in a very uncontrolled, casual manner, which may adversely affect the health of our democracy and the process of manufacturing of public consent, and the ruling party is responsible for controlling such acts, the October 5 order said. The order added, The other video links given by the plaintiff Kumar mentioned in this order show the apparent AI-generated scripted videos painting one person, namely Amandeep Jaintipua, negatively. Politics vs AI Amandeep Kumar, a lawyer and Congress political figure from Punjab, approached the Punjab and Haryana High Court alleging that three Facebook pages, namely Batale di Rajneeti, Kachi laan and Thanedar uncle, with substantial public reach with 2,200 followers, 1, 100 followers and 11,000 followers respectively, fabricated his visual representation through artificial intelligence and published it in a manner falsely portraying him in a body, dress and appearance, which he never adopted, posed for or consented to. Kumar stated that his reputation and public credibility are important to his political career. He acknowledged that his political actions, speeches, policies and public conduct are subject to fair public criticism and legitimate political disagreements, but objected to the false representation of him through the AI-generated content by these pages. Recently, Kumar came across highly objectionable videos and reels wherein his recognisable face and appearance have been digitally manipulated through Artificial Intelligence and shared on the said Facebook pages. The artificial content was calculated to ridicule and humiliate his character in order to malign his position. The material went to huge public exposure, reaching approximately 178 K, 180 K and 47.8 K views and public reactions. Every share of content exposes the fabricated representation to entire new audience, he stated. Advocates Harinder Deep Singh Bains, Jasdeep Singh Dhillon, Himmat Singh Bajwa and Abhay Singh Mann, appearing for the Congress leader, contended that due to the publishing of aforesaid AI-generated fake content from the referred Facebook pages, irreparable loss is being caused to Kumar, which necessitates the grant of ad-interim ex parte interim injunction putting restraint over the pages from further publishing the fabricated and morphed AI-generated content representing him on any social media platform. The counsel argued that Kumar, who is known as Amandeep Jaintipura, was a frontrunner for the elections of Members of Legislative Assembly under the Indian National Congress Party, from Batala constituency in Punjab in 2027. It was submitted that the Social India Platform referred to contains defamatory, falsely scripted AI-generated content calculated to malign his image, with content glorifying the image of the current MLA from Batala, to benefit the ruling political party. The scripted AI-generated content branded Kumar in a negative light, which is against the truth and strikes at the very fundamental right of the plaintiff concerning dignified public life, the counsel added. It was argued that it was not the case of healthy and fair criticism rather, it was cheap politics which uses the technology in an uncontrolled, unchecked and irresponsible manner. Therefore, there is a strong prima facie case, irreparable loss and balance of convenience in favour of Kumar. Interim injunction granted The court granted the interim injunction to Kumar against the Facebook pages, directing them to refrain from further disseminating, publishing, or uploading AI-generated content involving him until the next date of hearing. Further, the court granted an ad-interim ex parte injunction directing the concerned platform to disable public access to, or suspend, the pages, namely Thanedar uncle, Kachi laan, and Batale Di Rajneeti, linked to the AI-generated content against Kumar, until the next date of hearing. The matter will be next heard on October 22.

articleTitle: Naveen Patnaik’s BJD joins Opposition’s Election Commission protest
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Biju Janata Dal chief Naveen Patnaik: Ex Odisha CM has joined INDIA bloc protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
description: Protests against CEC Kumar and the Election Commission have gathered pace since the Express' report last month.
body_raw: Naveen Patnaiks Biju Janata Dal has joined opposition parties in demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar amid outrage over allegations of irregularities in the conduct of the Special Intensive Revision of stateUT voter rolls. Patnaik has sent Manas Mangraj and Sulata Deo to join protests that have erupted in central Delhi Tuesday, led by Congress MPs Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, who were briefly detained by police before being released. There is little love lost between the BJD and the Bharatiya Janata Party - in power at the centre and in Odisha - today, after the BJP thumped the BJP in the 2024 Assembly election, a loss the state party is now questioning. In the past, though, the BJD was a member of the BJP-led national alliance, i.e., from 1998-2009. Protests against CEC Kumar and the Election Commission have gathered pace since the Express report last month. An Express investigation found that Election Commissioners Vivek Joshi and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu had objected - formally and on record - 14 times in 10 months to the manner in which decisions were taken regarding the SIR. Among the 14 points raised were the allegedly illegal modification of Form 6 - to include questions about the voters parents or grandparents - and a push to centralise control of the ECINET software that manages the lists. BJD demands Gyanesh Kumars resignation On Monday BJD spokesperson Lenin Mohanty told reporters in Bhubaneswar that Gyanesh Kumar has no option but to resign and take moral responsibility. Mohanty insisted Kumar had to quit because he had lied about changes to Form 6 - that the alterations during the SIR had been approved by the Supreme Court. The court this week said it had not approved any modifications to Form 6 and sought a response from the EC and the government. Now, Kumar has no option. as Gyanesh Kumar had lied that Form 6 was approved by the Supreme Court, he has no moral right to continue but to step down, the BJD said in a statement. BJD leader Lekhashree Samantsinghar underlined that demand, declaring voters across the country, including those in Odisha, had lost trust in the EC.They EC must have done similar manipulation during the 2024 elections in Odisha by tampering with EVMs to make a particular party win the election, Samantsinghar alleged. Rahul Gandhi - also the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha - was joined by Trinamool Congress leader Derek Obrien and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. articleTitle: When can police refuse permission for protest? Gujarat High Court to decide
articleFeaturedImageAlt: This July, as the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP’s) protest against the NEET-UG 2026 question paper leak and issues connected with the higher education system was taking Delhi by storm, 35-year-old Subodh Kumud called a similar protest in Ahmedabad.
description: Gujarat HC is hearing a petitioner whose application for protest against the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak was rejected by Ahmedabad Police at the height of the Jantar Mantar agitation in Delhi.
body_raw: Police around the country routinely refuse permission to organisations and groups to hold protests and demonstrations. The protesters sometimes go ahead anyway, contending that the refusal of permission is arbitrary. When and under what circumstances can police lawfully refuse to permit a protest? This is the question that a petitioner has asked the Gujarat High Court to clarify in an ongoing matter. The court is scheduled to take up the petition again on Wednesday October 7. What led to the petition? This July, as the Cockroach Janta Partys CJPs protest against the NEET-UG 2026 question paper leak and issues connected with the higher education system was taking Delhi by storm, 35-year-old Subodh Kumud called a similar protest in Ahmedabad. The stated intention was to express solidarity with activist Sonam Wangchuk, who had been sitting on a hunger strike at Jantar Mantar, and other protesters who were demanding the resignation of then Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. According to Kumuds petition, filed before the High Court through Advocate B S Soparkar, Kumud emailed a Form A application under the Regulations and Conduct of Assembly and Procession Ahmedabad Police Commissioner Area Rules, 1975, to police on July 17. He said that he intended to gather together about 50 people from 6 pm to 8.30 pm on July 20 in solidarity with Wangchuk, and as an extension of the Jantar Mantar protests. He said that no loudspeakers would be used. According to the petition, Kumud was called to the Ellisbridge police station on July 19 to give a statement. He was not given a copy of the statement. On July 20, the day of the intended protest, police rejected Kumuds request for permission. Kumud has said that he received the rejection by a message sent on WhatsApp, which stated that the inconvenience that the planned protest would cause to traffic and the public cannot be ignored. But the protest took place anyway, and the protesters were detained at Paldi police station for a few hours. This was also the day of the CJPs march to Parliament in Delhi, during which youth protesters stormed the heart of the capital, provoking a violent crackdown by police. Wangchuk had been removed to hospital from the Jantar Mantar site two days earlier. However, no FIR was registered against Kumud, Advocate Soparkar clarified orally in court on September 30, the last time the matter was heard. What has Kumud argued in the petition? Kumud has argued that under Rule 81 of the Regulations and Conduct of Assembly and Procession Ahmedabad Police Commissioner Area Rules, 1975, permission can be refused only on specific listed grounds, including public order, decency, and morality. He has argued that the police communication recorded no such opinion, and treated the bare possibility of traffic inconvenience as enough to invoke public order, decency, and morality. The petition has contended that this reasoning is speculative, and not a real, immediate or apprehended danger. The petition has also submitted that a Police Inspector has no power to decide a Form A application, that power lies with the Deputy Commissioner of Police, and that the petitioner has received nothing from the office of that senior officer. Going beyond the specific case of July, Kumud has asked the HC to declare that permission cannot be refused solely over possible inconvenience to vehicular traffic without a specific Rule 81 finding. He has also sought directions that persons seeking permission for assembly must not be summoned to police stations, and that applications shall be decided at least 48 hours before the scheduled event. What is the governments argument? Public Prosecutor Hardik Dave has opposed the plea in five submissions, and asked that it be rejected with costs. He has argued that the petition was infructuous, and that Kumud had ignored Rule 42 of the 1975 Rules, which requires an application not less than seven days before the event, with reasons given for any shorter notice. Dave has told the court that Kumud had applied only three days ahead of the planned event, and had given no exceptional reason for it. Dave has said that the petitioner was trying to overreach and misuse the process of the Court. According to Dave, the prayer for blanket directions for future cases cannot be granted when the existing Rules already govern the process. The state has submitted that the Rules grant the police five days for deciding applications, but prescribe no deadline for applications filed within four days of an event. Dave also submitted that the proposed venue of the protest, M J Library, is a point at which five roads converge, and the protest could have disrupted traffic and created a public-order concern.

articleTitle: Pune water cuts from October 16? Civic body awaits state directive
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Pune, Pune Municipal Corporation, Pune water cut, Pune water cut October 16, Pune Municipal Corporation water cut, PMC water supply, Pune water shortage, Maharashtra water cut, Pune dams water storage, Khadakwasla dam, Pune drought, El Niño Pune, weekly water cuts Pune, Pune water supply news, Indian Express news
description: The Maharashtra Government has declared drought in various parts of the state, including Pune district, alerting citizens to use available water judiciously.
body_raw: A senior official of the Pune civic body said Tuesday they are likely to start weekly water cuts after the Maharashtra Government ordered local civic bodies and gram panchayats to reduce water supply by at least 10 per cent from October 16. The state government order comes amid concerns over dwindling reserves, drought-like conditions and the risk of prolonged water stress linked to El Nino. The government has declared drought in various parts of the state, including Pune district, alerting citizens to use available water judiciously. The four dams, Khadakwasla, Panshet, Varasgaon and Temghar, which supply water to Pune city, are filled to their capacity, but their water is likely to be supplied to meet the needs of drought-affected talukas of Pune district. To ensure that the available water lasts till the start of next monsoon in July next year, the Pune civic administration has prepared itself for water cuts from October 16. If there is a water cut once a week, then there will be no scarcity during summer, said Nandkishor Jagtap, in-charge of the civic water supply department, Pune Municipal Corporation PMC. However, the water cut will be considered only after written communication from the state government, Jagtap added. He said PMC Naval Kishore Ram, Mayor Manjusha Nagpure, and other senior officers are not in town, so there will be no immediate decision on a water cut. There will be a review of the situation and discussion on the water management plan before its implemented, said Jagtap. Meanwhile, the Pune civic administration has requested the Water Resource Department to reserve 21.34 TMC of water to meet the citys water demand until next monsoon. It also said that 11 villages were merged into the civic body in 2017 and 23 in 2021, increasing the population and the demand it must meet. The Pune civic body introduced water restrictions from June 15 as a precaution against a possible rainfall shortfall linked to El Nino. The cuts were temporarily lifted until July 14 to ensure adequate water availability during the annual Ashadhi Wari Palkhi processions. The decision came after heavy rains in Pune and its catchment areas boosted the water levels in the five reservoirs supplying the city to nearly 55 per cent.

articleTitle: Can Ladakh grow saffron? First-ever mass plantation drive begins in Leh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ladakh saffron cultivation
description: Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena announced the planting of 90,000 saffron corms in Leh as part of Project Him Sarovar, a government initiative to reclaim lost agrarian land in Ladakh.
body_raw: Indias saffron cultivation is set to expand beyond Kashmir, with a mass plantation drive underway in Ladakhs Leh district as the Union Territory makes its first attempt to cultivate the high-value spice on a large scale. Vinai Kumar Saxena, Governor, UT Ladakh, on Sunday announced the planting of 90,000 saffron corms, weighing 800kgs, in this region that has unique high-altitude agro-climatic conditions suitable for saffron. This pioneering project has immense potential to strengthen our local economy, creating lucrative and sustainable new livelihood opportunities for our hardworking farmers, youth, and self-help groups, he said. The experiment, spread across 4,000 square metres area in Leh, is a part of Project Him Sarovar, a government initiative to reclaim lost agrarian land in Ladakh. Whats needed to grow saffron Saffron, the dried stigma of the flower, is often used in cooking, cosmetics, and for medicinal purposes. Pampore in Kashmir is well known for cultivating the finest saffron in India. The plant can be cultivated between autumn and winter, with the ideal location having minimum temperatures ranging from 8C to 10C and benefitting from light to moderate snowfall. Only corms weighing more than 10 grams bear saffron flowers, and the number of flowers depends on the size of the corm, directly affecting saffron production. On average, an acre of saffron cultivation in Pampore is known to yield a maximum of up to 2 kg of saffron. A 2024 success story The present cultivation exercise in Leh comes in the wake of a successful experimental attempt at growing saffron in Ladakh two years ago, led by researchers at the CSIR-Indian Institute of Integrative Medicine IIIM, Jammu. Botanically known as Crocus sativus, IIIM scientists had succeeded growing saffron in open fields in Leh. In 2024, the institute inked an MoU with the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council, Leh, towards setting up demonstration farms for the cultivation of medicinal, aromatic and flowering plants in Leh. Since then, the institute has been developing protocols for cultivation, processing, and post-harvest management extendable to these crops to the farmers field and is planning to introduce more crops. A welcome step Speaking to The Indian Express, C K John, a scientist formerly with Pune-based National Chemical Laboratory, said that the Ladakh experiment is a welcome step. If it is successful, this will help the farmers of the region and also contribute in increasing the countrys saffron production, he said. John had led a team that succeeded in growing saffron under greenhouse conditions in the Pune lab and has worked with farmers across Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Sikkim for experimenting and increasing the acreage of saffron cultivation in India.

articleTitle: ‘Like straw fire’: Quoting Nepali proverb, Sikkim High Court quashes wife’s cruelty case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Straw fire Sikkim High Court husband wife cruelty Nepali proverb
description: The wife had lodged an FIR in 2022 alleging repeated misconduct and cruelty by her 50-year-old husband.
body_raw: Quashing criminal proceedings against a 50-year-old man after he and his wife settled their differences and resumed living together, the Sikkim High Court cited an old Nepali proverb that compares a quarrel between husband and wife to a straw fire that burns brightly but briefly. Justice Bhaskar Raj Pradhan was hearing the husbands plea to quash an FIR registered in 2022 on his 46-year-old wifes complaint alleging cruelty and repeated misconduct. He quashed the proceedings after the couple, who had been living together again for two years, reached a compromise. The criminal prosecution against the petitioner-husband be quashed to enable them to continue their life with an assurance from the petitioner that he shall conduct himself in a manner conducive to a peaceful and respectful matrimonial co-existence. An old Nepali proverb says Logne-swasniko jhagada paral ko aag whose English equivalent would be A quarrel between husband and wife is like a straw fire-it burns brightly but briefly, the October 1 order read. The husband expressed regret for his conduct and assured the court that he would maintain a peaceful and respectful relationship with his wife. Married in 2005 The court noted that the couple had married in 2005 and that the husband was facing criminal proceedings based on a complaint filed by his wife in 2022, alleging cruelty and detailing the alleged misconduct she had faced. An FIR was registered based on her complaint, and the investigation later led to the filing of a chargesheet. The husband then approached the high court, seeking to quash the FIR and criminal proceedings. He submitted a compromise signed by the couple in April this year, under which they agreed to live peacefully together, keeping their daughters well-being in mind. The husband also promised not to misbehave with or ill-treat his wife and to maintain a good relationship with her. The husbands counsel, advocate Rahul Rathi, and the wifes counsel, advocate Safal Sharma, told the court that they had personally spoken to their respective clients and believed that quashing the criminal proceedings would be in the familys best interest and give the couple a second chance. Husband regretted actions Court After interacting with the couple, the high court noted that the husband regretted his behaviour, repented his actions and sought forgiveness from his wife. It also noted that the couple had been living together for the past two years and that the husband said he had changed and was now a better person. Both of them state that they have a daughter who is 18 years old, who is living with them and they want to ensure that her happiness remains paramount, the court noted. The high court also noted that the compromise deed said the couple had considered their daughters well-being while resolving their differences and agreeing to maintain a good relationship. Accordingly, the court quashed the FIR and the criminal proceedings against the husband.

articleTitle: OpenAI is adding watermarks to ChatGPT text in the EU: Here’s what it means
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The EU AI Act requires developers and providers of AI systems to ensure that content generated by AI is machine-readable. (Express Image)
description: OpenAI is adding an invisible watermark to text generated by ChatGPT and Codex to comply with the EU AI Act's transparency rules.
body_raw: OpenAI has said that it will now add an invisible watermark to all text generated by ChatGPT and Codex in its bid to comply with the EU AI Acts transparency rules that require AI companies to make AI-generated content identifiable to other systems. The company announced its decision on Monday, October 6, in its official blog. The Sam Altman-led company said that the watermark will be rolled out in the next few weeks to eligible ChatGPT and Codex users on all plans. However, the rollout is currently limited to the EU. While the feature is off by default, developers using OpenAIs API worldwide can turn it on for select models. OpenAI said, while acknowledging that text watermarking and detection remain early technologies with significant limitations, that its phased approach reflects both the EU AI Act requirements and the technologies limitations. The company also said that it was opening applications to access its text watermark detector. However, this access will initially be limited to approved researchers and expert organisations that assist the company with evaluation and improvement of the technology. How does the watermark work? In its blog, OpenAI said that its technology named textGrain adds something it describes as an invisible statistical signal to the models word choices. Later, the detector scans for that signal to determine whether a passage contains an OpenAI watermark. OpenAI has published a paper, textGrain Entropy-Calibrated Watermarking for Language Model Text, shedding light on the inner workings of the technology. Further, OpenAI said that in its evaluations, textGrain matched or exceeded the performance of other approaches that it tested, including SythID Google DeepMinds digital watermarking tech for text. OpenAI also revealed that, along with strong performance, under ideal conditions, this technology could not guarantee reliable detection in everyday use. The company said that the detectors can make two kinds of errors-they can detect a watermark where none is present or miss a watermark that is present. Some of the key hurdles to watermark detection are that shorter or more constrained text is harder to detect, while editing text generated by AI can weaken its watermark. The limitations with watermarks OpenAI also pointed out factors that may deem watermarks inconclusive. It said that a watermark may not necessarily mean information about the extent of human judgement, editing or creativity. It does not establish any form of ownership or responsibility most importantly, it does not identify the user. It is also not a barometer to verify accuracy. The company claimed that the absence of a detected watermark does not translate to human authorship. Article 50 of the AI Act, which applies from August 2, 2026, sets out transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems, including generative and interactive AI systems and deepfakes. While providers are required to design AI systems that ensure individuals are explicitly informed whenever they interact with an AI system directly, they must add machine-readable marks to enable the detection of AI-generated or manipulated content. On the other hand, deployers of AI systems must inform users when they are exposed to emotion recognition and biometric categorisation tools, deepfakes, and text publications on matters of public interest without human review or editorial control. According to the Act, these obligations are aimed at building trust and integrity in the information ecosystem. OpenAIs latest announcement follows a similar measure taken by Anthropic in early August when it declared that it is adding invisible watermarks to text and files generated by its Claude models. Anthropic also made the announcement in its bid to comply with the EUs AI Act on Transparency Code. The company said that watermarks will be applied globally to all new models released after August 2, with plans to roll out support for older legacy models.

articleTitle: Jim Bakker dies at 86: Televangelist lost his multi-million empire to sex scandal, crimes
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jim Bakker death: The evangelist built a multi-million dollar empire with first wife Tammy Faye.
description: Jim Bakker Dies at 86: Infamous televangelist Jim Bakker was best known for the empire he and his first wife, Tammy Faye, built around the television show The PTL Club.
body_raw: Jim Bakker Death News Infamous televangelist Jim Bakker has died at the age of 80. While his second wife Lori Bakker didnt disclose the cause, she confirmed he was no more. It is with a broken heart that I share that my beloved husband, Jim Bakker, went home to be with the Lord this evening. He was a pioneer of Christian television, but to me, he was my husband, my best friend, and the man I was honored to walk beside through so many seasons of life and ministry, Lori said in a statement. Jim Bakker was best known for building an evangelical empire around the popular television programme The PTL Club. However, his story took a dramatic turn as sex scandals and financial crimes cost him much of his reputation and wealth. Jim Bakker and Lori Bakkerlived near Branson, Missouri, where they filmed their TV show The Jim Bakker Show since its inception in 2003. But it was Bakkers first wife Tammy Faye with whom he shot to fame. Their show fetched 13 million viewers everyday at its peak in the mid-1980s and amassed over 129 million yearly, as per AP. Their personal and professional collaborations began in college, when they began dating and dropped out to kick off their travelling ministry. Bakker preached, and Faye sang and played the accordion as they visited churches and tent revivals across the US. Televangelist Pat Robertson roped them in to launch a childrens show in 1965 and The 700 Club, a Christian talk show, in 1966. After exiting the network in 1972, Bakker formed the PTL Satellite Network in 1974, with PTL standing for Praise the Lord. Sex scandal and financial crimes galore After enjoying popularity for around 13 years, Jim Bakker admitted to a sexual encounter in 1987 with church clerk Jessica Hahn. He even paid her 265,000 from ministry funds to keep her silent. He was consequently forced to resign from his empire, with pastor and broadcaster Jerry Falwell taking over. Tammy Faye continued to stand by Bakker despite the sex scandal and subsequent fall from grace. The next year, Bakker was indicted for wire fraud, mail fraud, and conspiracy linked to PTLs finances. He was sentenced to 45 years in prison, but the jailtime was eventually reduced to eight years. Faye remained loyal to her husband even then, singing the hymn On Christ the Solid Rock I Stand at a press conference after his conviction. Also Read Fahadh Faasil says wont get half of Rs 300 cr as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr Finally, a few years later in 1992, Tammy Faye divorced Jim Bakker ahead of their 31st wedding anniversary. He was still in prison at the time of the separation. They had two children. After being released on parole in 1994, Bakker married Lori Bakker four years later. The couple adopted five children in 2002. Bakker became a television preacher again in the early 2000s, and was a staunch supporter of US President Donald Trump.

articleTitle: Delhi police arrests journalist over fake video targeting ACP Vivek Bhagat
articleFeaturedImageAlt: delhi protest
description: The arrest relates to a separate Cyber Police case over a video police said was fabricated; a woman journalist’s complaint against ACP Bhagat is being investigated by the Crime Branch.
body_raw: The Delhi Police Cyber Cell has arrested a 24-year-old independent journalist for allegedly circulating a fabricated video that falsely depicted ACP Vivek Bhagat engaging in sexually inappropriate conduct with a woman during the recent protests. Police said the video circulated on Instagram and Facebook was manipulated and falsely presented as CCTV footage. Bhagats photograph, name and designation were displayed alongside the purported footage, giving the impression that he was the police officer shown in the video. The Cyber Police case is separate from allegations made by a woman journalist against Bhagat, who has accused the officer of inappropriate conduct. The Crime Branch is looking into this complaint. The accused, Nadeem Ahmed Ameen, was apprehended from Haryanas Mewat region on October 5. Police said they recovered a mobile phone allegedly used to circulate the video. Police said he works as an independent journalist and operates an Instagram news account, News Aina Today. A case was registered on October 4 after police monitoring of social media platforms brought certain Instagram and Facebook reels to their notice. The reels showed a person dressed as a police officer allegedly engaging in sexually inappropriate conduct with a woman, while Bhagats photograph, name and designation were prominently displayed alongside the footage, said DCP New Delhi Sachin Sharma. The FIR was registered at the Cyber Police Station, New Delhi District. During the investigation, police traced one of the accounts involved in circulating the material - Instagram handle newsaaina0776 - to Ameen, a resident of Palwal district in Haryana. On examination, the Instagram account was found logged-in in the said device, the DCP said. Police also claimed photographs and other content connected with the alleged fabricated reel were found in the phones gallery. Ameen will be produced before a court. Further investigation is underway. According to police, Ameen is the sixth of seven brothers and is the son of a retired government Urdu lecturer. Police said he had studied up to Class 10 and had started the News Aaina Today Instagram account in April 2026. The account, they said, has around 24,000 subscribers. Larger conspiracy Police said they were also probing whether the circulation of the video was part of a larger conspiracy. An investigation is in progress to ascertain his source of funding and to verify if any larger pre-planned conspiracy was hatched in order to spread instigation and anarchy during the said protest, the DCP added. The Cyber Police is identifying other social media accounts allegedly involved in what the police described as an attempt to create a false narrative, tarnish the image of the Delhi Police, and spread disaffection and dissatisfaction against the government.

articleTitle: Sonu Nigam buys three office units for Rs 17 crore in Mumbai’s Andheri West
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sonu Nigam buys three office units for Rs 17 crore in Mumbai's Andheri West
description: Singer Sonu Nigam has purchased three office units in Andheri West, Mumbai, at a combined price of Rs 17 crore.
body_raw: Singer Sonu Nigam has purchased three office units in Mumbai. According to property registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix, the singer has bought commercial spaces in Andheri West at a combined price of Rs 17 crore. The transactions were registered on August 6, 2026, consisting of two adjoining units on the first floor and another office space on the ground floor of the Aston building in Sundervan Complex on Lokhandwala Road. As per the documents, Sonu Nigam purchased the first floor units from Singular Health Private Limited for Rs 16 crore. They have a combined carpet area of 3,885.77 sq ft. The transaction included a stamp duty of Rs 96 lakh. Four car parking spaces in the basement of the building were also acquired by the singer. In another transaction registered on the same date, the singer bought the ground floor unit in the same building from Singular Health Private Limited worth Rs 1 crore. The commercial space has a carpet area of 258.33 sq ft. According to property registration documents, the transaction has an attached stamp duty of Rs 6 lakh. If combined, the three office units have a carpet area of 4,144.10 sq ft, with the total value of Rs 17 crore. The average price is estimated at approximately Rs 41,021 per sq ft of carpet area if the three units are combined together. The Kal Ho Naa Ho singer expanded his portfolio in May 2026. He sold 1.067 hectares of land in Karjat part of Mumbai 3.0, for Rs 95 lakh, as per property registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix. In April 2026, Sonu sold several plots constituting more than 1.9 hectares in Karjat, a hill station in Maharashtras Raigad district near Mumbai, for a total price of Rs 1.95 crore, according to property registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix.
