articleTitle: KBC 18: Ayushmann Khurrana apologises to Amitabh Bachchan for calling him ‘budhau’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: KBC 18
description: Sara Ali Khan and Ayushmann Khurrana won Rs 12.5 lakh on KBC 18. They discussed Gulabo Sitabo, trolling and Sara’s wish to work with Amitabh Bachchan.
body_raw: KBC 18 Amitabh Bachchan-hosted Kaun Banega Crorepati 18 featured actors Sara Ali Khan and Ayushmann Khurrana in a special celebrity episode on October 5. The actors appeared on the show to promote their upcoming film Udta Teer. The money they won on the show will be donated to charity, with Sara and Ayushmann choosing different causes. The duo began their game by playing Jaldi Five, with Sara emerging as the winner. They then joined Amitabh Bachchan on the hot seat and had three lifelines available - Audience Poll, Sanket Soochak and MahaFlip. The episode also saw Amitabh Bachchan and Ayushmann revisit their 2019 film Gulabo Sitabo, while Sara spoke about her own wish to work with the veteran actor. Ayushmann apologises to Amitabh Bachchan for calling him budhau During their conversation, Amitabh Bachchan recalled working with Ayushmann in Gulabo Sitabo. The two actors shared memories from the film, with Big B also praising Ayushmann. Ayushmann then jokingly apologised to the veteran actor for calling him budhau - or old man - in the film. Aapko film mein budhau kaha, I am sorry. Aap budhau nahi hain. Really life mein aap mein 84 wali koi harkat nahi hai, 24 hain aap I called you an old man in the film, I am sorry. But you are not old. In real life, there is nothing about you that is 84. You are 24, Ayushmann told him. Big B immediately played along and asked, 84 wali kya harkatein hoti hain What are the things that an 84-year-old does? ALSO READ Fahadh Faasil says wont get half of Rs 300 cr as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr Sara Ali Khan says she is jealous of Ayushmann Sara also revealed that she was slightly jealous of Ayushmann because he had already had the opportunity to work with Amitabh Bachchan. She pointed out that several members of her family, including her mother Amrita Singh and grandmother Sharmila Tagore, had worked with the actor, but she was yet to share the screen with him. Amitabh Bachchan then complimented Saras family, saying everyone in the Pataudi family has beautiful eyes, going all the way back to her grandfather, former cricketer Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi. While talking about Saras family, he recalled seeing Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudis mother driving an open Jaguar in Delhi. He said the confidence and attitude associated with the Pataudi family appeared to have continued across generations. Ayushmann dedicates KBC Radio tribute to Amitabh Bachchan The episode also featured a special KBC Radio segment in which Ayushmann spoke about Amitabh Bachchan in a radio-style tribute. As part of the segment, Ayushmann sang a song of Amitabh Bachchan and paid tribute to the actor during his birthday week. Sara and Ayushmann answer Rs 5 lakh question The actors continued with the quiz and reached the Rs 5 lakh question. They used the Audience Poll lifeline to help them with the question and successfully gave the correct answer. The episode also saw Amitabh Bachchan revisit some of his most iconic dialogues and performances. He was asked to say a Zanjeer dialogue romantically and deliver a Deewar dialogue in a hesitant manner. He was also asked to say the famous line, Kabhi Kabhi Mere Dil Mein Khyaal aata hai.. from Kabhi Kabhie angrily, turning the segment into a playful acting challenge. Super Sandook and Amitabh Bachchans lunch promise Sara and Ayushmann then entered the Super Sandook round, in which contestants are given 90 seconds to answer 10 questions. The actors managed to answer eight questions correctly. Instead of taking the money they had earned in the round, they chose to use the 5050 lifeline. Amitabh Bachchan also revealed that if contestants answer all 10 questions correctly, he invites them to his home for lunch. He said he has invited 11 families for lunch so far. The actors continued their game after the Super Sandook round and eventually reached the Rs 7.5 lakh question. Sara and Ayushmann discuss trolling with Amitabh Bachchan The conversation also turned to social media, trolling and the pressure celebrities face online. Sara and Ayushmann shared their thoughts on dealing with criticism and trolling, while Amitabh Bachchan spoke about how public figures comments can remain online for years. Big B recalled an old social media post about rising petrol prices that he had written jokingly 10-15 years ago. I had written something about petrol prices rising 10-15 years ago, just as a joke. You wont believe it, but it is 2026 now and that post is still stuck there. Whenever petrol prices rise today, people ask why I dont say anything about it, he said. Sara and Ayushmann reach Rs 12.5 lakh question The actors eventually reached the 12th question, worth Rs 12.5 lakh. They used their MahaFlip lifeline and were presented with a question about filmmaker Christopher Nolan. The question was Which of these Christopher Nolan films has scenes set in Mumbai? A. Oppenheimer B. Tenet C. Inception D. Memento Sara and Ayushmann chose B. Tenet, which was the correct answer. The actors therefore took their winnings to Rs 12.5 lakh. The money won on the episode will go to the Balashah Foundation and UNICEF India. Mumbai in Christopher Nolans Tenet Tenet was partly filmed in Mumbai in 2019, with the city standing in for part of the films international setting. The production shot sequences at several locations across the city, including the Gateway of India, Colaba and other parts of South Mumbai. The Mumbai schedule was part of a larger international shoot that also took place in countries including the United Kingdom, Italy, Estonia, Denmark and Norway.

articleTitle: Francis Halzen wins Nobel Physics 2026 for IceCube and cosmic neutrinos
articleFeaturedImageAlt: nobel prize in physics
description: Nobel Prize in Physics 2026: Francis Halzen has won the physics laurel for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and high-energy neutrino discovery.
body_raw: Physics Nobel Prize 2026 The Nobel Prize in Physics for 2026 was announced on Tuesday by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm, and it has been awarded to Belgiums particle physicist Francis Halzen for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. The Nobel Committee, in a press release, stated that the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, conceived by Halzen, tracks neutrinos that originate in the distant cosmos. It added, The neutrino interactions that are continuously collected by IceCube will provide researchers with novel knowledge about the violent settings in which high-energy neutrinos can be created-and could even reveal previously unknown cosmic phenomena. BREAKING NEWS The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences has decided to award the 2026 NobelPrize in Physics to Francis Halzen for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. - The Nobel Prize NobelPrize October 6, 2026 The winner of Nobel Prize in Physics is poised to receive a prize sum totalling 12 million Swedish crowns 1.2 million,which is shared if there are more than one winner. The 2025 Nobel prize in physics was awarded to US-based scientists John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis for experiments that demonstrated the principles of quantum physics in action. The IceCube Neutrino Observatory-ideated by this years physics laureate Francis Halzen-tracks neutrinos that originate in the distant cosmos. The neutrino interactions that are continuously collected by IceCube will provide researchers with novel knowledge about the violent settings in which high-energy neutrinos can be created-and could even reveal previously unknown cosmic phenomena. NobelPrize - The Nobel Prize NobelPrize October 6, 2026 Halzen, who is a professor at the University of Wisconsin in United States Madison, realised that ice at the South Pole could be used to track particles known as neutrinos. He presented his vision for capturing neutrinos in 1988. When a neutrino collides with an atomic nucleus, it produces a flash of light that can be tracked by sensors in the glacial ice. Mark Pearce, Chair of the Nobel Committee for Physics, said Francis Halzen has led an international team of researchers and engineers who have provided us with a fantastic instrument. His tenacity and scientific vision has paved the way for a new kind of astronomy.

articleTitle: ‘Is baar lathi charge hua, seedha ‘Amit Shah resign’: CJP’s pre-protest note
articleFeaturedImageAlt: CJP Ashutosh Ranka Jantar Mantar protest
description: The October 10 protest will be the CJP’s second major demonstration at Jantar Mantar after July when its sit-in led to then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation.
body_raw: The Cockroach Janta Party CJP, which has called for a protest march to Delhis Jantar Mantar on October 10 demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, said it would proceed with the demonstration even if authorities denied permission for the gathering. Speaking to The Indian Express Srirupa Goswami, CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka said, Well do a march. Wherever they stop us, well sit. that place becomes Jantar Mantar. And until and unless they allow us to go in, well not get up. They can, of course, arrest us, beat us up. That they can keep doing, but we are very clear - the protest will be done at Jantar Mantar The October 10 protest will be the CJPs second major demonstration at Jantar Mantar after July when its members staged a sit-in for over a month to demand the resignation of then-Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak issue. Pradhan subsequently stepped down. Ranka also claimed that he and other CJP leaders, including founder Abhijeet Dipke and Saurav Das, could be arrested before the protest. Thats what sources from IB, Delhi Police, senior journalists. have told us. They the government want to stop us. But they are forgetting. three of us happen to be the faces of CJP, but CJP is way more than what we are, he added. Warning to Amit Shah Asked how the CJP planned to prepare for a possible crackdown on its October 10 demonstration, especially after mass detentions following the All India Students Association protest in Delhi, Ranka said, Is baar lathi charge hua.toh is baar seedha Amit Shah pe baat jayegi. Is baar seedha Amit Shah ka resignation maanga jayega. This time, if there is a lathi charge, then the matter will go straight to Amit Shah. This time, we will directly demand Amit Shahs resignation. Pointing out that the Union Home Minister is directly the person controlling Delhi Police, and orders like these cant come without his consent, Ranka added, So, he better make sure that if hes asking Delhi Police to do lathi charge, he should be ready for us going after him. EC not independent anymore Hitting out at the Centre and the Election Commission, Ranka said, They are openly manipulating elections. an election is the fundamental root of a strong democracy. Elections have been compromised in this country, EC is not independent anymore, so civil disobedience is what we are going ahead with and what we will keep doing till our demands are met. Protests against Kumar have intensified across the country, including in Delhi, over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls. An Indian Express investigation published on September 23 found that two election commissioners in the three-member ECI had recorded objections - 14 times in 10 months - to steps taken by Kumar. Ranka reiterated the CJPs demand for Kumars resignation, saying Gyanesh, beta tumse na ho payega, loosely translated as Gyanesh, you wont be able to pull this off.

articleTitle: Mother brings minor son to India flouting US order, Karnataka High Court directs return
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka HC orders mother to return to US with son, Karnataka HC sends mother and son back to US, ‘Go back to US’: Karnataka HC orders mother’s return, 2-year-old US citizen to return to America, Custody battle goes back to US, Karnataka HC sends custody fight back to US, Mother and son ordered back to US
description: The mother brought her son from US to India when he was nine months old, despite US court orders, and never went back.
body_raw: The Karnataka High Court has directed an Indian mother to return to the United States with her two-year-old American citizen son, who was brought to the state when he was nine months old despite a US court order against the childs removal from Washington. The court said the mother could not have removed the child from the US courts jurisdiction and denied him the company of his father. A bench of Justices Anu Sivaraman and T P Vivekananda observed that nothing on record suggested any imminent danger to the child from his father. The bench added, The mother had removed the child. without informing the father and in violation of the orders passed. The mother could not have removed the child from the jurisdiction of the competent Family Court in the United States of America and denied the child the company of its father, the October 1 order said, adding,The mother - respondent No.4 has to go back to the United States of America, which is the place of birth of the child and the place of its ordinary residence and work out her rights in the competent Court there. The writ petitioner husband shall make all arrangements for the return of respondent No.4 as well as the minor child to the US. The order further directed the father to bear the expenses of the mother till she finds an appropriate employment and accommodation in the United States of America. Custody fight travels from US to India The man, a US citizen and permanent resident, married the woman, who is an Indian citizen, on April 2, 2022, and they lived together in America. On February 13, 2024, their son was born and became a citizen by birth. According to the case records, on learning that his wife had made arrangements to travel to India with the child and apprehending that she would remove the child without his consent, the husband approached the jurisdictional court in the US seeking protection of his custodial rights. By an order passed on November 1, 2024, the court granted a temporary protection order in favour of the husband, restrained his wife from interfering with the custody of the minor child and directed her not to remove him from the state of Washington. Despite the order, the wife travelled to India with the nine-month-old child, and they are presently residing in Bengaluru. The wife later approached the family court in Bengaluru seeking an anti-suit injunction and under the Guardians and Wards Act,1890, and sought sole custody of the child. Meanwhile, the Superior Court of Washington, Clark County directed her on March 26, 2025, to return the child to Washington and ordered that her husband shall have the child in his exclusive care. This was reiterated by order dated May 16, 2025. Alleging that his wife had failed to comply with these directions and continues to retain the child in India unlawfully, the man instituted the present petition seeking the childs return and custody. On behalf of the father, senior counsel G L Vishwanath and advocate Meena Vargued that the custody of the minor child with the wife was unlawful, since the child was removed from the US and continues to be retained in India despite the orders passed by the Superior Court of Washington, Clark County, directing his return and placing him in the exclusive care of the father. The counsel submitted that the parties had established their matrimonial home in the US, that the child is a citizen of that country, and the custody disputes are most closely connected with that jurisdiction.It was further submitted that the wife had appeared through counsel before the Superior Court of Washington and was aware of the orders passed there, which continue to remain in force. She had obstructed her husbands access to the child and initiated proceedings before the family court in Bengaluru only after removing the child to India, the counsel added. It was also submitted that the welfare and best interests of the child would be served by restoring him to the jurisdiction of the Washington court, where the custody dispute may be finally decided. US court to decide custody Advocate Sonia Rajesh, appearing for the wife, contended that the fathers plea was not maintainable since the child, who is below five years of age, has remained in the care and custody of his mother from birth, which cannot be characterised as illegal to warrant the issue of a habeas corpus writ. Denying the allegation that the child was abducted, the counsel said her journey to India was pre-planned and undertaken with the knowledge of her husband. It was also stated that the temporary protection order relied upon by the man was dismissed on June 6, 2025, by the Washington court and cannot form the basis for treating the childs custody as unlawful. The counsel added that the wife was subjected to matrimonial cruelty, repeated abandonment and financial deprivation by the childs father, and raised concerns regarding his alleged alcohol and substance abuse, parenting ability and suitability to have the childs exclusive custody. It was submitted that the child was residing lawfully in India on a valid residence visa, was safe and well cared for, and had substantially settled in India. The father has not been denied access to the child, as video calls have been facilitated and he holds a valid visa enabling him to visit the child in India. The court observed that though the mother had approached the Bengaluru court, it passed no orders granting her custody of the son. Allowing the fathers plea, the court said that all the contentions of the parties were to be decided in the proceedings before the competent court in the US.

articleTitle: Salman Khan gets Delhi HC notice over plea to stay his suit against Kala Hiran release
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Salman Khan
description: The Delhi High Court sought Salman Khan’s response to a plea by Kala Hiran makers seeking a stay on his suit against the film’s release over personality rights.
body_raw: The Delhi High Court has sought actor Salman Khans response to an application filed by the makers of Kala Hiran The Battle for Legal, who have asked the court to stay the proceedings in the actors suit seeking to restrain the films release. According to PTI, Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani issued notice to Salman on Tuesday after producer Amit Jani argued that the dispute over the proposed film substantially overlaps with an earlier personality-rights case filed by the actor. Salman Khan has sought restrictions on the release of the film, which is purportedly based on him. The latest application by the filmmaker claims that allowing both matters to proceed separately would result in parallel litigation over the same film, its promotional material and the alleged violation of Salmans personality or publicity rights. Why have Kala Hiran makers sought a stay? According to the application, Salman Khan had already filed a suit seeking protection of his personality rights, in which the Delhi High Court granted an ex-parte ad-interim injunction on December 11, 2025. The actor later filed another application seeking an interim injunction specifically against the proposed film. According to producer Amit Janis plea, that application is still pending. The filmmaker has argued that the relief Salman is seeking in the present proceedings, including restrictions on the release, exhibition and dissemination of the film and its teasers, is substantially similar to the relief sought in the earlier case. The producer has therefore contended that the proceedings amount to parallel litigation concerning the same dispute. ALSO READ Fahadh Faasil says wont get half of Rs 300 cr as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr Delhi HC had earlier ordered removal of Kala Hiran teaser The legal dispute between Salman Khan and the makers of Kala Hiran had earlier led to an interim order from the Delhi High Court. On July 27, a coordinate bench directed online platforms to remove the films teaser and other related posts after the actor objected to the content. While passing the order, the court said the makers of Kala Hiran could not use the 59-year-old actors name, mannerisms and other distinctive attributes for commercial gains without his authorisation. It also restrained the dissemination of material that could harm his reputation. The court observed that the use of social media to circulate material allegedly violating personality rights or harming reputation can worsen the situation because of the speed, reach and permanence of digital publications. Makers say Kala Hiran is not Salman Khan biopic The makers of Kala Hiran have maintained that the proposed film is not a biopic on Salman Khan. They have also argued that the actor cannot use personality-rights protection to erase public events connected with the blackbuck controversy. The film has been linked to the blackbuck poaching case involving the actor, but its makers have maintained that their project does not amount to an unauthorised portrayal of the actors life. The filmmaker had earlier told the court that the movie was not yet ready for release as it had not received certification from the censor board. They also said that its trailer had not been released. Salman Khan accuses filmmakers of sensationalising blackbuck case Salman Khan, in his application, has accused the filmmaker of deliberately attempting to sensationalise the poaching case and generate headlines to attract public attention at the expense of his goodwill and reputation. His restraint application forms part of his broader lawsuit seeking protection of his personality rights. The actor had earlier approached the Delhi High Court seeking directions against various social media platforms and e-commerce websites over what he alleged was the unauthorised use of his name, images, persona and likeness. What happens next in Salman Khans Kala Hiran case? The Delhi High Court has now issued notice to Salman Khan on the filmmakers application seeking a stay. The actor will have to respond to the plea before the court considers submissions from both sides and decides the matter.

articleTitle: ‘Imaandar CM’ to CBI raid: Bhagwant Mann’s 2027 campaign faces a new test
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann at Fatta Maloka village during a public meeting, in Sardulgarh. (@AAPPunjab/X via PTI Photo)
description: With welfare schemes, public meetings, and digs at rivals, the Punjab CM is increasingly the face of AAP’s Assembly poll campaign.
body_raw: Imaandar CM, Lokan da CM, AAP da ikko naara, Bhagwant Mann dobara. Honest CM, peoples CM AAP has one slogan, Bhagwant Mann for the second time. As you drive down from Chandigarh to Jalandhar and then on to Kapurthala, a beaming Mann, the Punjab Chief Minister, is your constant companion, looking down at you from billboards in his trademark yellow turban. This is a far cry from late 2021, when Aam Aadmi Party AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal dominated the hoardings in Punjab, with Mann emerging later after a phone poll - Janta chunegi apna CM People will choose their CM - saw him handpicked for the top post with 93 of the votes. While other parties, except the Shiromani Akali Dal led by the Badals, remain largely non-committal about their CM face, the AAP, which swept the 2022 Assembly polls by winning 92 of 117 seats, is clearly making Mann its mascot for 2027. The flip side to this is that it puts Mann, and by extension AAP, under intense scrutiny. There was a political firestorm on Monday after the Punjab and Haryana High Court ordered a CBI probe into allegations linked to his office, following the Punjab Polices failure to act on three letters sent by the Enforcement Directorate to the Punjab DGP. The allegations involve Manns Officer on Special Duty, Rajbir Singh Ghuman, and others. On Tuesday evening, the CBI raided Ghumans residence and the CMs camp office even as the government challenged the High Court order in the Supreme Court earlier in the day. The Opposition had thought the edict would turn him into a social outcast of sorts. But Mann has remained constantly in the public eye, criss-crossing the length and breadth of the state almost every day, except for a short break in early July when he travelled to Bengaluru for what aides described as his annual wellness programme. His message changes with the audience but has two constants 300 units of free electricity a month, presented on billboards and in speeches as 600 units since bills are typically bi-monthly, and the satkar payments to women beneficiaries under the Maawan-Dheeyan Satkar Yojana that began on July 1. There is also a mandatory warning If you vote for other parties, all this will stop. Focusing on the women who have now received money for six months under the scheme, which provides Rs 1,500 a month to eligible Dalit women and Rs 1,000 to others - with the first transfers made for three months on July 1 and the second on October 1 - Mann has declared he will never let this toon-toon sound of mobile notification about money coming in stop. Kehnde Bhagwant Mann aurtan nu paise de ke sir charha reha hai . toon-toon chaldi rahegi, band nahin hon devanga. They say I am spoiling women with money. this will carry on, it wont stop. Potshots at Opposition His other favourite pitch, especially in the countryside, is the increased access to canal water under his regime, from 26 in 2022 to 86 now, and the Rs 10 lakh health insurance for all. Many billboards relay the same message, with the tagline, Jo keeta so kar ke dikhaya. He delivered what he promised. But it is his potshots at the Opposition that deliver the real sting disparaging messages cloaked in laughter. Commenting on the elevation of former India hockey captain and three-time Jalandhar Cantonment MLA Pargat Singh as Punjab Congress president on October 2, he quipped Main unhan nu hamesha Captain Sahib kehnda haan. umeed hai unhan di team vi unhan nu gend pass karegi, kyonki pass ton bina goal nahin ho sakda I always call him Captain Sahib, I hope his team will pass the ball to him so that he can score. Another favourite quip is Congress vich workers nalon vadh CM umeedwar han. Congress has more CM hopefuls than workers. At another place, he says Remember the five-point programme of Congress and Akalis Me, my son, my nephew, my brother-in-law and my sisters husband. And he almost always ends on a cautionary note Virodhi parties 2027 ton pehlan paise vi vand sakdian han. Paise le lao, par vote AAP nu pao. The Opposition parties could woo you with money, take it, but vote for AAP. The unrelenting flow of drugs is one issue where the Opposition, led by the BJP, is on the offensive. But here too, Mann plays on the front foot, reminding voters that the problem intensified during the earlier Akali Dal-BJP government and that the BJP at the Centre is responsible for manning the over-500-km international border with Pakistan, one of the routes for drug trafficking in the region. Political observers see in the billboards an AAP effort to counter the increasingly loud charge that the party is run by proxy from Delhi by Kejriwal. The billboards not only show a CM in charge but underline two things that the AAP wants voters to associate with Mann his people connect and his clean image. The flip side But its his clean image that is now under fire following the High Court order of a CBI probe. While Mann is calling it a familiar ploy by the BJP to malign him in the run-up to the Assembly polls, the Opposition is having a field day. Congress leader Partap Singh Bajwa, the Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly, said Mann cant escape blame. How is it that he was ignorant of what was transpiring in his office? The AAP government tom-toms him as an imaandaar CM. If he was so honest, why did the High Court order a CBI probe ? Punjab BJP state president Kewal Singh Dhillon went a step further and sought the CMs resignation. People in the hinterland are generally keeping an open mind. Ajaib Singh, a resident of Bagrian village in Kapurthala, who retired as a sub-inspector from the Punjab Police four months ago, says one cant say anything unless there is unassailable proof. Gurcharan Singh, a retired soldier at Bariar village, agrees. Allegations and counter-allegations are part of politics, all empty without verifiable proof. For now, though, Mann continues to do what he does best meet people with a script that he improvises on the spot to connect with them.

articleTitle: Meerut trader’s family came to bury him after ‘heart attack’, then they saw his neck
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Talib Meerut death
description: Relatives noticed a dark mark around the trader’s neck at his burial and later alleged his wife and her friend were involved in his death. Both have been booked.
body_raw: The first sign that something was wrong came when Talib was being buried. The 30-year-old traders family had been told he died of a heart attack at his Meerut home on September 28. When they arrived, they found his body covered with a bedsheet, with only his face visible, said police. They took him to his ancestral home in Muzaffarnagar for burial. There, as the cloth around his neck slipped, someone took a photograph. Police said the picture was later circulated in the family WhatsApp group. Relatives noticed a dark mark around Talibs neck and began questioning the circumstances of his death. They also learned about his wife Ilmas alleged friendship with a local youth, Aman. Police said the family now suspects the two had a role in Talibs death. Based on a complaint by Talibs cousin Akram Ali, police registered an FIR against Ilma, who works at a beauty parlour, and Aman at Lohiyanagar police station on charges of murder. The case has been registered. We will exhume the body to get a post-mortem done. We are in correspondence with Muzaffarnagar authorities, said Lohiya Nagar SHO Sumit Tomar. No one was allowed to touch the body Talib had been living with Ilma and their two-year-old son in rented accommodation in Meeruts Zakir Colony. He had moved to the city around eight years ago following a dispute within his family. Akram said relatives and friends began arriving at Talibs house after being told of his death. Ilma told them he had suffered a heart attack in his sleep. But Ilma did not allow anyone visiting the house to remove the cloth below his face. She also initially refused to let us take the body to Muzaffarnagar for burial. It was only when everyone insisted that he be taken to his hometown that she finally agreed, alleged Akram, adding that she accompanied them. It was at the burial ground that the cloth covering Talibs neck slipped off, exposing the mark that caught the familys attention. After the photograph was shared, relatives began asking neighbours in Meerut about Ilma, said Akram. The family also asked Ilma about Talibs cellphone. According to Akram, she denied having it. Relatives also noticed Ilmas unusual behaviour, finding her busy packing up household belongings.

articleTitle: No diplomatic ties, but decades of contact: Oman’s complex Israel history
articleFeaturedImageAlt: (L-r) Haitham bin Tariq Al Said, Sultan and Prime Minister of Oman; and Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel (Wikipedia)
description: Oman and Israel have no formal diplomatic relations, but their ties stretch back decades, from covert military cooperation to trade and access to airspace.
body_raw: Last week, a flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, carrying more than 170 people, plunged 17,000 feet about two and a half hours into its journey. This, however, was no turbulence incident. The co-pilot, reportedly attempting to take control of the aircraft, allegedly attacked the pilot, Captain Smit Machchhar, with a crash axe. The co-pilot was identified as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami. Among the questions being raised is how an Omani national came to be operating a flight to Israel when the two countries have no formal diplomatic relations. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has previously said that pilots from countries without diplomatic ties to Israel face restrictions. A look at Omans long history of limited engagement with Israel. 1970 a new era Open contacts between Israel and Oman did not begin until after the 1991 Madrid Conference, but Israel was no stranger to the sultanate. The roots of Omans unusual approach to Israel go back to July 1970, when the then Sultan, Qaboos bin Said, overthrew his father, Said bin Taymur, and began transforming the Sultanate of Oman. Once he consolidated his rule, Qaboos launched a major development programme focused on education, healthcare, and infrastructure. In the same decade, Jerusalem provided discreet military assistance and advice to Sultan Qaboos as he sought to suppress the Marxist-inspired rebellion in Dhofar. The Omanis were grateful for the support. In 1975, Israel sent a small advisory mission to Oman, keeping its presence hidden from Britain, Omans main military benefactor. By 1975, a sizeable infrastructure had emerged. Schools, hospitals, clinics and roads had been built and a welfare system introduced. With this infrastructure in place, Oman was able to begin to look outward and to consider its future economic development, notes Uzi Rabi in his 2006 journal article Oman and the ArabIsraeli Conflict The Reflection of a Pragmatic Foreign Policy. A distinguished foreign policy As Oman developed, it distinguished itself by entering security agreements with Western powers despite opposition from some Arab neighbours. In June 1980, for instance, Oman signed military basing agreements with Washington, the first such arrangement in the Middle East. It also consistently supported the Camp David peace accords between Egypt and Israel. What was part of an Israeli outreach to second-tier states in the region paid dividends years later when Oman decided to support the Camp David Accords, write Clive Jones and Yoel Guzansky in Fraternal Enemies Israel and the Gulf Monarchies 2020. flydubai In doing so, it became one of only three Arab states - along with Morocco and Sudan - that did not break relations with Cairo after its peace treaty with Israel. Further, in December 1983, Oman also called for the renewal of the Camp David Accords as the only means that achieved a constructive step in the direction of reaching a peaceful solution to the Middle East issue. The path to open contacts Although Oman had no formal public relations with Israel until the early 1990s, the two sides cooperated in areas where Israeli expertise was valuable, including drip irrigation and other agricultural techniques. Oman appeared increasingly open to closer ties as the Oslo negotiations progressed talks between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization. Several informal meetings between Israeli and Omani officials preceded then prime minister Yitzhak Rabins visit to Muscat in December 1994, where he received an official state welcome. The visit sparked speculation that Oman and Israel were moving towards full diplomatic relations. By spring 1995, however, Muscat made clear that further progress in the Israeli-Palestinian peace process was needed first. Still, reciprocal trade missions were established by September 1995, and Israel took on a financing role at the Middle East Desalination Research Center MEDRC, headquartered in Muscat. In October, Oman and Israel agreed to establish commercial missions, again raising hopes of formal diplomatic ties. Benjamin Netanyahu comes to power The election of Likud leader Benjamin Netanyahu as Israeli prime minister in May 1996, followed by a stalemate in the peace process, made it difficult for Oman to maintain its position. In December 1996, Foreign Minister Yusuf bin Alawi bin Abdullah announced that Oman would freeze relations with Israel. From this time onward, Oman was careful to balance its stand on the ArabIsraeli conflict with statements and actions that emphasised its concern for the Palestinians and for Syria. The position that Muscat adopted was to stress time and again that relations with Israel could not come at the expense of a comprehensive peace, which must include an Israeli withdrawal from all occupied Arab territories, writes Rabi. Oman subsequently moved closer to the Palestinian Authority. In May 1998, Sultan Qaboos welcomed Omans first ambassador from the PA, while President Yasir Arafat visited Muscat the following month to discuss developments in Arab-Israeli diplomacy. His visit was probably, at least in part, an attempt to cajole the Omanis into adopting a harder line towards Israel, Jones and Guzansky write. Oman openly condemned Israeli policies during the Netanyahu era. Israel was excluded from conferences and trade fairs in Oman, while other ties remained frozen. In November 1998, Alawi confirmed that We Oman do not have contacts with the Israeli government for the moment. Yet Oman did not close Israels trade office in Muscat. Despite its criticism of Israel, Oman continued to signal that a comprehensive peace could pave the way for full diplomatic relations. Airspace politics Oman and Israel still have no formal diplomatic relations, meaning Omani citizens lack the bilateral diplomatic and consular framework that exists between Israel and countries with which it has established relations. For years, Israeli airlines also could not use Omani airspace. In February 2023, however, Omans Civil Aviation Authority announced that it would open its airspace to all civilian airlines meeting its requirements. The move enabled Israeli carriers to use the Saudi-Omani air corridor on routes to Asia. Israel welcomed the decision, with Foreign Minister Eli Cohen calling it a significant and historic decision that would shorten flight times to Asia. Oman, however, described the decision in general terms without specifically mentioning Israel. The move reflected Omans longstanding approach of maintaining limited engagement with Israel without establishing full diplomatic ties.

articleTitle: Missing suitcase from bus: Uttarakhand Transport Corporation to pay Rs 43,000
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Uttarakhand Transport Corporation state consumer commission missing suitcase
description: The Uttarakhand State Consumer Commission held the transport corporation responsible for its conductor’s negligence and ordered Rs 43,000 compensation over a missing suitcase.
body_raw: The Uttarakhand State Consumer Dispute Redressal Commission modified an order passed by the Dehradun district commission and directed the Uttarakhand Transport Corporation to pay Rs 43,000 on behalf of a bus conductor to a man whose suitcase had gone missing in 2015 from the luggage compartment of a bus due to the negligence of the conductor. President Kumkum Rani and Member CM Singh were hearing an appeal filed by the bus conductor, who alone was held liable by the district commission for negligence and had been directed to pay Rs 75,500 as compensation, as he was the one who had kept the suitcase inside the luggage compartment of the bus. The deluxe bus was being plied by the driver under the control and instructions of respondent no 3 the Uttarakhand Transport Corporation, and the appellant the conductor is an employee of respondent No. 3, who was working under the instructions and guidance of respondent no 3, therefore, under vicarious liability, the department is entitled to pay the above-mentioned compensation, the October 3 order read. Vicarious liability is a legal rule that holds an employer liable for the wrongful or negligent actions done in the course of work of his employee. The state commission held that it was due to the negligence of the Conductor that the suitcase and clothes, jewellery etc. of the respondent no 1 the man which were kept inside it, were lost during travelling from Delhi to Dehradun. The man had claimed that he, along with his wife, was travelling from Delhi to Dehradun by a deluxe bus on November 8, 2015, at about 10 pm, and the conductor of the bus had kept his suitcase in the luggage compartment of the bus, which eventually went missing. The man alleged that his suitcase went missing because of the negligence of the conductor and filed a consumer complaint before the district commission, Dehradun, seeking the cost of the suitcase and the items kept in the suitcase. The conductor had contended before the district commission that during travelling, the passengers must take care of their own luggage and that it was due to the negligence of the man that his suitcase went missing. The driver of the bus claimed that he had no concern with the personal belongings of the man, and his only job was to drive the bus carefully. The transport corporation stated that no fare was charged for luggage and that it had only charged the fare for the passenger, because of which the man was not their customer. The district commission on November 15, 2018, allowed the complaint of the man and directed the conductor to pay Rs 57,500 to the man as the cost of the missing items of the suitcase and Rs 15,000 towards mental agony. The corporation was also asked to pay Rs 3,000 as litigation costs to the man. Subsequently, the conductor of the bus approached the state commission, appealing against the order passed by the district commission. Advocates Amit Sharma and Parul Nishad, appearing for the conductor, submitted that the man had failed to prove the deficiency on the part of the conductor and that the man was not entitled to get any relief. Advocate K Brij Bhushan appeared for the man. Advocate Saurabh Pal appeared for the driver, and Advocate AS Bisht for Uttarakhand Transport Corporation. Vicarious liability The state commission noted that the man had also sent a letter to the transport corporation, following which an inquiry was initiated, which found the conductor guilty of the disappearance of the suitcase. The state commission further noted that the order of Uttarakhand Transport Corporation properly proved that, due to the negligence of the conductor, the suitcase and its contents were lost during travel. It is also pertinent to mention that the suitcase of respondent no 1 the man was handed over to the appellant the conductor to be kept in the diggi, and even as per the version of the conductor, he locked the diggi after taking the lost suitcase along with items kept inside, but it was not found in ISBT, Dehradun and was not handed over to the respondent no 1 the man. While partly allowing the appeal of the conductor, the state commission observed that since the man had not filed any receipt or bill of any of the items, the actual cost of the items in the bag was not fully proved. Accordingly, the amount awarded to the man as a cost of the missing items of the suitcase was directed to be reduced to Rs 25,000 from Rs 57,500. There was no change in the compensation awarded for mental agony and litigation costs. Additionally, the state commission held that since the conductor was an employee of the Uttarakhand Transport Corporation and was working under the instructions and guidance of the corporation, therefore, under vicarious liability, the department would be entitled to pay the compensation. Takeaway Passengers may seek compensation for valuables that went missing during their journey from when they can establish that the loss resulted from negligence or misconduct by the staff of the transport corporation. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states and union territories Uttarakhand 1800-180-4188 or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: UP employees await pay benefits ordered in 2022, 4 IAS officers face contempt action
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The court directed them to file their responses to the charge framed within a week and remain present before it on October 13, the next date of hearing. (File Photo)
description: In 2022, the Allahabad High Court had directed the state government to revise employees’ pay, clear arrears and issue revised pension orders within four months.
body_raw: The Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court on Monday held four top IAS officers of the Uttar Pradesh government liable to be punished under the Contempt of Courts Act for allegedly failing to comply with a 2022 court order on the pay scales of government employees. The officers are Additional Chief Secretary, Finance Department, Deepak Kumar Principal Secretary, Namami Gange and Rural Water Supply and Minor Irrigation Department, Anurag Srivastava Principal Secretary, Irrigation Department, Anil Garg and Principal Secretary, Rural Engineering Department, Sorabh Babu. A single bench of Justice Saurabh Lavania, in its order, said the officers had violated the July 2022 order and were liable to be punished under the Contempt of Courts Act. The bench said the officers present before it had not produced any material showing that the July 2022 order had been complied with, even partially. Accordingly, this court finds that charge should be framed against the officers who are present before this Court, as prima facie it appears that they do not want to comply with the order passed by the writ court, it said. The court directed them to file their responses to the charge framed within a week and remain present before it on October 13, the next date of hearing. Additional Chief SecretaryPrincipal Secretary, Public Works Department, Ajay Chauhan, is also facing a contempt petition. The court directed him to remain present on October 13 for proceedings to frame charges against him. Chauhan was not present in the court on Monday he had filed an affidavit seeking exemption from personal appearance. The court had allowed it What the 2022 order said The high court has been hearing a bunch of 37 petitions from employees of various departments seeking direction to their heads to comply with the HCs 2022 order. The petitions fall into two categories. -In Category A, employees sought the pay scale of Rs 37,400-67,000 with a grade pay of Rs 8,700 in Pay Band-IV, with effect from the state government order of July 5, 2011, and on a notional basis from January 1, 2006. They also sought the benefit of similar High Court orders passed on January 28, 2014, and February 6, 2014. -In Category B, the employees challenged an April 2015 state government order which said Assistant Engineers and Executive Engineers of Engineering Services were not covered by government orders dated November 5, 2014 and May 4, 2010. They also challenged orders rejecting their representations seeking the same benefit. The court had directed the departments concerned to complete the fixation of pay, payment of salary arrears, and issuance of revised Pension Pay Orders within four months. If the benefits were not extended within that period, the employees would be entitled to simple interest at 7. Why the officers are facing contempt The employees approached the High Court with contempt petitions after the 2022 order was not complied with. These were heard on May 22, 2026. During the hearing, the Advocate General for Uttar Pradesh sought eight weeks to comply with the writ courts order. The court allowed the request and listed the matter for July 22. The state government, meanwhile, filed a special leave petition SLP in the Supreme Court against the HC order. On July 22, the Supreme Court directed the state government officers to faithfully and honestly comply with the High Court order. It also allowed officers required to appear personally before the High Court to do so virtually. The High Court then listed the contempt matter for October 5. The SLPs were heard again by the Supreme Court on September 25 and listed for October 16 to report developments.

articleTitle: Higher yields in US test India’s macro resilience
articleFeaturedImageAlt: AI
description: Considering the high yields, the possibility of an AI bubble bursting is a distinct possibility, and therefore an important risk
body_raw: By Sriram Balasubramanian and Prakash Loungani The developments dominating global markets are the 10-year US Treasury yields rising above 5 per cent and the US Federal Reserves rate hike cycle to contain inflation. These matter for India, shaping challenges and policy choices. First, the 10-year treasury yield has risen to its highest level since 2007. The immediate impact is a narrowing of the India-US yield spread to around 200 basis points, limiting the scope for further inflows compared with periods when spreads were wider. Higher yields also raise fiscal risks by increasing borrowing costs, especially for long-tenor issuances that lock in elevated costs for decades. Over the longer term, they point both to concerns about US fiscal and debt sustainability and to uncertainty around the AI infrastructure boom. They may also signal a broader higher for longer environment, closer to the pre-2000s market setting. India will therefore need to navigate these cross-currents carefully. On the issue of the Feds rate hikes, the question now is How long will this cycle last? Since inflation in the US is closer to the 2 per cent target than in the previous cycle, this one may be shorter. Even so, short-end rates are likely to stay elevated, reinforcing yield pressures through spreads, currency, and liquidity. But, Indias economy is much more resilient than in earlier episodes of high yields and rising rates in the US. The 10-year sensitivity has fallen sharply from 1.25 in 2013 to 0.43 in 2026. This points to an economy more resilient to external volatility. What explains this, and why does it matter? Several factors explain this resilience. Indias macro fundamentals are perhaps at their strongest in decades The fiscal deficit is on a glide path toward 4 per cent, inflation is within the target band, the current account is stable, and reserves remain ample, especially after the FCNR B scheme. Retail participation has risen sharply, while domestic institutional investors have overtaken foreign institutional investors in ownership, deepening Indias domestic capital base and therefore reducing the impact on capital flow volatility. There is palpable dynamism in the economy that has been the largest contributor to global growth in the last few years. These strengths provide comfort, though important concerns remain. First, considering the high yields, the possibility of an AI bubble bursting is a distinct possibility, and therefore an important risk. Indias exposure should be analysed carefully. Second, the US-Iran geopolitical conflict remains a major constraint for India, especially with respect to the price of oil and a variety of other goods imported from the Middle East. Each spike in Brent crude oil prices raises imported inflation, weakens the Indian rupee, and pushes yields higher. With the US Fed hiking, India has little room to absorb that pressure. Relief can also come quickly, as when Brent fell to about 98 per barrel and the 10-year bond yield eased toward 7 per cent. But even then, Fed tightening could keep a floor under yields. Third, state financing through the bond market needs to be monitored carefully, especially given that many of them tend to borrow in the later part of the year. State borrowing costs have risen with recent SDL auctions clearing between roughly 7.3 per cent and 7.9 per cent. These risks need to be carefully monitored. But with strong macroeconomic fundamentals, India does have the capacity to withstand changes in the global environment, if it plays its cards well. Balasubramanian is an economist and Loungani is director of the Applied Economics Programme at Johns Hopkins. Views are personal

articleTitle: How a 32-acre farm shaped Arvind Swamy’s emotional bond with Meiyazhagan: ‘Started to cry’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Arvind Swamy
description: Arvind Swamy revealed how growing up on a 32-acre farm helped him connect with Meiyazhagan, recalling the pain of leaving his childhood home and returning years later.
body_raw: Actor Arvind Swamy has revealed that his connection with Meiyazhagan went far beyond simply understanding his character. In a conversation with Gobinath, the actor spoke about the deeply personal memories that resurfaced while reading C Prem Kumars script, particularly because his character Arulmozhis emotional connection to his ancestral home reminded him of the farm where he spent his childhood. In Meiyazhagan, Arvind plays Arulmozhi, a man who is forced to leave his family home and move to Madras. Years later, he returns to his hometown for a family wedding, an experience that brings back memories he had tried to leave behind. The film, which stars Karthi alongside Arvind, revolves around his characters unexpected reunion with a relative and his gradual journey of reconnecting with his past. Arvind Swamy grew up on a 32-acre farm Speaking about why he immediately connected with the script, Arvind Swamy recalled spending his childhood on a 32-acre farm in Poonamallee. I grew up on a farm until I was 15. That is where I grew up. I didnt like city life. I wanted to go back to the farm. It was a 32-acre farm in Poonamallee. From there, I went to Sishya School. That farm was my life - the cows, dogs, plants and everything else. Arvind said growing up in that environment created an attachment that stayed with him long after he was forced to leave. When you are in such a situation, you develop an attachment to that environment. I had to leave at the age of 15. My dad was a heart patient. Back then, many facilities did not exist, and with my school and his work here, we shifted. But no one in the family was willing to go there and maintain the farm, he recalled. The actor said he even hoped that someone could temporarily look after the property so that he could eventually return. In fact, I asked if somebody could look after it for four or five years so I could come back. I couldnt even imagine my life without it. But it didnt happen. So they had to sell it to somebody who wanted to take care of it, he said. I started to cry without being aware of it Arvind Swamy admitted that returning to the place years later was emotionally difficult. He said he deliberately stayed away from it for a long time because of how traumatic leaving had been. After many years, I wanted to go back to that place. I avoided it because it was so traumatic. This was 10-15 years after my parents passed away. Once I stepped through the gate, I started to cry without being aware of it. I quickly asked for permission and went in, he said. That experience became an important point of connection when he read Meiyazhagan. Why Arvind Swamy immediately connected with Arulmozhi The actor said director Prem Kumar gave him a book rather than narrating the story when he was in Hyderabad. Prem gave me a book when I was in Hyderabad. He said he wouldnt narrate the story and asked me to read it. I was reading it and, from the first scene, I was able to connect, he recalled. When Arvind met Prem Kumar again, he told the filmmaker that he understood the emotional situation perhaps more deeply than he realised. When I met him next, I told him, You dont understand this situation as much as I do, he said. The actor admitted that even decades later, the memories remain powerful enough to overwhelm him. I will cry even today if I go there. I am a grown man, I am an old person, and it is still there today. The place - I can logically say it is only a place. But I still remember the texture of each tree. I remember which tree I used to climb or hide behind. I remember how many branches it had. That is the impact of the place where you grew up, he said. Arvind Swamy was reminded of his childhood during Meiyazhagan promotions During the films promotions, he experienced another unexpected reminder of his childhood. Arvind Swamy recalled travelling to EVP Film City, which is located close to the area where his childhood farm once stood. Usually, the team would take the bypass road, but on that occasion they took the main road through Poonamallee. After that, during the promotion of Meiyazhagan, I went to EVP. The farm is close to EVP. We went to the studio for something. We usually take the bypass road, but this time we took the main road. It went through Poonamallee town, he said. As he travelled through the area, familiar memories began returning. Automatically, I felt something. I was looking up and thinking, I know this road, even though it had been 30 years. I was looking for the Deluxe store where I used to get rubber balls. I used to ride my bicycle outside and do a lot of such things. I used to go to the shop to buy a ball, he recalled. He also found himself looking for an old theatre that he remembered from his childhood. There used to be a theatre there. I was searching for that. Back then, there used to be bedbugs on the chairs. I was searching for all these landmarks, Swamy said. The memories became so overwhelming that he began crying again. Automatically, before I went into the studio - I think there was some cooking show, and we went there for promotion - while I was going, I started to cry. This was after 30 years, he said.

articleTitle: India, Germany, Qatar & Turkiye among 7 countries interested in hosting 2036 Olympics
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India are among seven countries eyeing to get 2036 Olympics hosting rights. (FILE PHOTO)
description: India submitted their Expression of Interest to host the Games in 2024, with Ahmedabad being their city of choice to host the mega-event,
body_raw: India are among seven countries, alongside Germany, Qatar, Turkiye, and South Africa, that are interested in hosting the 2036 Olympics and have been invited to present their Games projects to the IOCs Future Host Commission next month, the International Olympic Committee IOC said on Tuesday. As per the IOC, the Games projects will be assessed on several technical factors, which include the venue master plan, athlete experience, funding strategy, political and public support, Games delivery capabilities, and legacy strategy to create long-term benefits for host communities. The Interested Parties currently in Continuous Dialogue with the IOC, with a stated interest in hosting the 2036 Olympic Games, are in alphabetical order Germany, Hungary, India, Qatar, Republic of Korea, South Africa and Turkiye, read a statement from the IOC. There are also a number of NOCs taking part in noncommittal talks with the IOC about hosting future Olympic Games beyond 2036. The Interested Parties have been invited to present their projects to the Future Host Commission in November, it added. The IOC sets out the next phase of the process for selecting the host of the 2036 Olympic Games. dhY More details ai dhY- - IOC MEDIA iocmedia October 6, 2026 The world body, however, did not share the exact timeline for these presentations. The IOC, keeping this schedule in view, said no other Interested Parties will be considered for 2036 after October 31. India submitted their Expression of Interest to host the Games in 2024, with Ahmedabad being their city of choice to host the mega-event, which has never been held in the country before. ALSO READ 2032 Olympic emblem officially revealed after it was leaked The host selection process was subsequently halted by new IOC President Kirsty Coventry, who said fresh feedback would be taken from member nations to streamline the process. The host of the 2036 Games will be known in mid-2029, and Indias negotiations will be led by the Indian Olympic Association IOA in collaboration with the Gujarat government and with the support of the Union Sports Ministry. I was fortunate to compete at five Olympic Games, across four continents. Each had their own character. Each host brought something unique through its people, its culture and the way it chose to stage the Games, said IOC President Kirsty Coventry. But wherever the Games take place, one thing must never change athletes have to be at the heart of everything we do. As an athlete, you spend years working to make your Olympic dream come true. The experience you have when you finally reach the Olympic Games stays with you for the rest of your life. That is why, for every future host, delivering the best possible experience for the athletes must always be the starting point, she added. With PTI inputs

articleTitle: Why the gloves are finally off as BJD takes on BJP, joins INDIA bloc march
articleFeaturedImageAlt: BJD insiders said the decision to join the Opposition protest was a calculated move, keeping in mind the public mood on the issue. (Express Photo)
description: Naveen Patnaik’s party says it remains outside the INDIA bloc, but its post-2024 moves show a gradual shift away from its long-standing equidistance policy.
body_raw: Its ties with former ally BJP strained since last year, the Biju Janata Dal BJD on Tuesday made an exception to its policy of maintaining equidistance from both the ruling party and the Congress-led Opposition. The Naveen Patnaik-led party joined the INDIA blocs protest march in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls. BJD chief Patnaik, who has already demanded Kumars resignation and the revisiting of the SIR exercise, asked party MPs in the Rajya Sabha to join the protest. We have joined the protest as a responsible Opposition party. The exclusion of more than 20 lakh voters in Odisha and over 13 crore voters across the country in the name of SIR has raised serious concerns and we believe this was done quite deliberately, said the BJDs leader in the Rajya Sabha, Manas Mangaraj. Mangaraj clarified that the BJD was not part of the INDIA bloc. But by joining the Opposition protest, the regional party appears to be signalling that the gloves are off in its fight against the BJP, the party that ended its 24-year rule in Odisha in June 2024. The BJP also inflicted a major blow in the Lok Sabha polls the same year as the BJD failed to win a single Lok Sabha seat, a first since the regional party came into existence in 1997. The BJP won 20 of the 21 Lok Sabha seats in the state. BJD insiders said the decision to join the Opposition protest was a calculated move, keeping in mind the public mood on the issue. The BJDs changed stance received the approval of another regional player that is in a crisis of its own key INDIA bloc ally and Mamata All India Trinamool Congress. Gratitude to bjdodisha Chief NaveenOdisha for deputing two MPs, Manas Mangaraj and Sulata Deo, and former MP Muzibulla Khan to the Oppositions protest march in Delhi today against the CEC and SIR Scam. We are on the ground. UNITED, Rajya Sabha MP Derek OBrien wrote on X. A senior BJD leader said Naveen Patnaik is a clever politician, who always reads the public mood and chose to go with the flow and the decision to join the Opposition protest is part of the same game plan. No matter the legal fallout of the SIR exercise, the Supreme Court has already intervened, but the functioning of the poll panel is under intense public scrutiny. With the poll panel facing a credibility crisis, there is a growing perception among people that a majority of its decisions tend to favour the BJP, said the leader, requesting anonymity. BJD insiders also believe that the party is also a victim of poll discrepancies during the Assembly and parliamentary elections, which contributed to its defeat. We have pointed out several discrepancies during the 2024 assembly and Lok Sabha polls in Odisha and also sought intervention of the Election Commission of India. We got no concrete reply from the poll panel, said Sulata Deo. After the 2024 polls, the BJD had flagged three major concerns the difference between the total votes polled at each booth and the number of votes counted from the corresponding Electronic Voting Machines during polling, the difference in the votes cast for Lok Sabha and Assembly elections despite them being held simultaneously, and the huge difference between voter turnouts released on polling day and the final figure, which the EC released two days later. A slow shift Besides, the BJDs shift in political strategy is not a sudden move. The party has been gradually changing course since it lost power. After the poll debacle, it announced it would stop providing issue-based support to the NDA government and subsequently joined the Opposition in staging a walkout from the Rajya Sabha over the NEET issue back in July 2024. In March 2025, Patnaik joined a meeting called by DMK leader and then Tamil Nadu CM M K Stalin against the Delimitation Bill. Earlier this year, the regional party also joined hands with Congress to field a joint candidate in the Rajya Sabha polls, though they failed to win. During the recent Gen-Z protest and amid mounting pressure on the Union government over the NEET paper leak and examination reforms, Patnaik also supported the call for Dharmendra Pradhan to resign as Union Education Minister. Patnaik also launched a direct attack on the government over the recently passed Mines and Minerals Development and Regulation Act, alleging that it deprives the state of levying any tax on mining lease holders. This was against Odishas interests, the former CM alleged. The BJD chief recently led a protest against the new law. Being a regional party, we should fight against the Centre to fulfil the regional aspirations to keep the impression of a state-based party intact. Our siding with the Centre on every issue backfired in the polls. Hence, we decided to fight the BJP, said a BJD leader. Senior BJP leader Biranchi Narayan Tripathy criticised the BJDs shift, saying, The party has been facing an existential crisis after losing power as leaders are distancing from it. It has been using non-issues to show its relevance.

articleTitle: ‘Badi gustaakhi ho gayi’: Amitabh Bachchan apologises to Madhuri Dixit on KBC 18
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Amitabh Bachchan admits mistake of dancing to Madhuri Dixit's iconic 'Ek Do Teen'
description: Actor Madhuri Dixit will make an appearance in an upcoming special episode of Amitabh Bachchan's Kaun Banega Crorepati 18.
body_raw: Madhuri Dixit, who will soon be seen hosting Kaun Banega Crorepati Marathi, recently graced the hot seat of Amitabh Bachchans Kaun Banega Crorepati Season 18. Ahead of the episodes release, Sony TV shared two interesting promos, featuring Madhuri and Amitabh.
