articleTitle: Digitising disenfranchisement: How IT systems and opaque orders are endangering the right to vote
articleFeaturedImageAlt: vote
description: There is no audit to certify the list of people within the ECI who can access or modify the electoral database, raising serious issues about oversight over unauthorised access to this system. This raises questions about the quality of the ECI’s technology-led governance strategy, which seems counter to the design of India's electoral systems
body_raw: Recent revelations about the Election Commission of Indias misconduct have exposed a deeper problem of how technology systems in government are used to reduce accountability and perhaps even subvert the law. We now know that unilateral, unauthorised changes were made to the electoral process without proper authority and in violation of the laws governing our right to vote. The ECINET, the ECIs main technology system, has played a key role in enforcing these changes in ways that are invisible and not contestable by the public. This should worry all Indians who have equated digitisation with better accountability and transparency. Left unchecked, this kind of autocratic digitisation appears designed for disenfranchisement. Three particular concerns stand out. First, they show how officials can make illegal or unauthorised changes using internal, informal orders directly into IT systems that become the de facto rules of the electoral system. Such de facto rules are almost impossible to contest. This was seen when new fields appeared in the digital Form 6 for fresh voter registration, forcing first-time voters to provide details about their parents Why is a persons right to vote dependent on their parent or grandparents identity? Yet voters could not proceed practically without filling out these fields in the form. These new fields appeared suddenly, in departure from the contents of Form 6 prescribed by the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 and the Representation of the People Act, 1950. Demanding such additional information from voters must be authorised by law, through proper amendments and modifications of the 1960 Rules that must then be laid before Parliament per Section 28 of the Representation of the People Act. Second, such autocratic digitisation through the back end of the IT system risks introducing centralisation and opacity into the electoral governance system - which was legally designed to be decentralised and transparent. This is seen in the concerns reportedly raised by two of the Election Commissioners in relation to the poor access controls for the portal and its databases. On the one hand, they flagged how key constituency-level statutory authorities responsible for preparing electoral rolls the Electoral Registration Officers struggled to get proper, complete access to the online portal from the central IT officials. On the other hand, there is no audit to certify the list of people within the ECI who can access or modify the electoral database, raising serious issues about oversight over unauthorised access to this system. This raises questions about the quality of the ECIs technology-led governance strategy, which seems counter to the design of Indias electoral systems. Under the law in India, the vision for electoral roll preparation is decentralised by design for robustness and transparency. The ECIs changes ought to aid this vision, rather than undermine it. Third, these developments highlight the failure of the IT system, and those overseeing it, to respond to technologys own shortcomings. This failure has dire consequences for the right to vote, as seen when 97 voters in Goa were incorrectly removed from the electoral roll after the software flagged them for discrepancies. They subsequently provided documents in a full legal process to establish that they were legitimate voters. Despite this, the digital system did not allow deletions to be reversed. Reports show that despite multiple requests from state-level officials to central ECI officials including the Director General of IT and Goas Senior Deputy Election Commissioner, no option to roll back these deletions was created. All 97 voters were excluded from voting. Each vote has value, and how many more are being lost to the same fate? Technology systems are often feted as being nimble, agile and responsive - with the law failing to keep up. The reality seems to be the reverse. The internal dysfunction of the ECI exposed by these revelations has laid bare the crisis of accountability and governance facing electoral governance in India. It also highlights a broader challenge, reflecting a new way in which many state institutions now operate. Officials are increasingly subverting the law from within institutions, implementing illegal changes on the fly to their IT systems using only bureaucratic orders, hidden from public view. Despite this subversion, the direct implementation of these changes through ECINET makes them binding in practice. Worryingly, the ECIs mode of autocratic digitisation is not isolated. Indeed, as my doctoral research has revealed, our experience with other technology-led systems, such as Aadhaar, shows similar dysfunctions. Over the years, many changes to Aadhaars IT system have been accompanied only by bureaucratic orders, even when they shift important legal and policy choices. For example, the adoption of facial authentication in 2018 was moved directly through the IT system and announced through bureaucratic circulars without wider public debate. Yet, this represented a major change from the earlier policy choice in 2010 not to use facial authentication, for reasons including its unreliability and privacy risks. Much like the changes within ECINET, the risk is that burying these changes in bureaucratic orders and IT systems introduces opacity that enables autocratic digitisation. Asking the public to approach the courts to review such invisible measures is like asking them to catch the wind. We must confront this reality as this public debate continues in the months ahead, to think imaginatively about the forms of accountability we demand from our digitising public institutions. The writer is a Research Fellow in Law Technology at University College London

articleTitle: ‘Emotional, impulsive’ to ‘calmer’: Evolution of Harmanpreet as leader
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down as India's captain. (CREIMAS for BCCI)
description: Former Indian player Mithali Raj spoke to The Indian Express about Harmanpreet Kaur's captaincy evolution and what lies ahead for the Indian women's team.
body_raw: Mithali Raj retired in 2022 when Harmanpreet was her deputy. Harmanpreet took charge and went on to win the first Womens World Cup in 2025. Additionally, Harmanpreet also led the T20I side from 2016 and on Tuesday she announced stepping down as captain. Mithali Raj spoke to The Indian Express about Harmanpreet Kaurs captaincy evolution and what lies ahead for the Indian womens team. Q Tell us about the evolution you have seen in her captaincy. Mithali When she took over the ODI captaincy, she was suddenly the senior-most player in the group. With me and Jhulan Goswami having retired, there was a different responsibility on her because most of the players around her were younger. You have to understand that when you are leading a younger group, you have to set the example yourself. I think she has evolved in that regard. She was more emotional, impulsive and expressive as a young captain, but with age and experience, you naturally become calmer and start looking at situations differently. Over the last few years, I have seen her become more comfortable in that senior-player role more communicative with players and making them understand what she needs from them. Q What do you think her role will be in the team going forward? Mithali The next leader can gain valuable inputs from Harman as and when required. But certainly Harman having played for so long should be able to share the experience she has gained over all these years and help the younger players navigate the next phase. Her role will also depend on where she feels she can contribute best, and that is something the captain and coach can discuss with her. She has a lot to offer as a senior player. Q What do you think her role will be as a batter? Mithali As players, we all go through different stages in our careers. When you are younger and physically at your peak, you can play a certain way and take on a lot more responsibility. As you get older, you learn to assess where you can contribute most effectively and how you can use your experience. ALSO READ Harmanpreet Kaurs real legacy is belief, not just a World Cup Harmans performance in the crunch knockout game during the 2025 World Cup was good and she has shown throughout her career that she can contribute in important situations. Going forward, I think it will be about finding the right role for her within the batting order and allowing her to contribute in the way that suits her best. Sometimes, as a senior player, you also want to take on more responsibility when you feel you havent been able to contribute as much as you would have liked. That is natural. Q Was she more into data or the man-management side as captain? Mithali I think it was a combination of both. In the current game, there is so much information available about every player, and as a captain you naturally use that to prepare and make plans. You watch videos, discuss match-ups and work out what you want to try on the field. But experience also teaches you to trust your instincts. Sometimes what you see in front of you doesnt necessarily match what the data says, and thats where a captains understanding of the game comes in. I think Harman has had her own style and has successfully balanced both data and man-management. Q What are the qualities the next Indian womens captain can imbibe from Harmanpreet? Mithali Every individual has their own personality, and that naturally reflects in the way they lead. Harmanpreets style was more aggressive and expressive and you could see her personality clearly on the field. Smriti Mandhana current vice-captain, on the other hand, is much more calm and composed. Shes a good reader of the game, analyses situations well and understands her players. Shes also been part of the leadership group for quite some time, and a lot of her contribution behind the scenes perhaps didnt get noticed enough. So, Smriti will bring her own style. It doesnt mean that one style is better than the other. It means that a new leader brings her own personality, her own attributes and her own way of looking at the game.

articleTitle: Days after newborn girl found dead in MP hospital, mother arrested: ‘Wanted a son’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Patients requiring more serious healthcare attention are referred to the second tier of the healthcare system, by the primary healthcare units, which comprises District Hospitals (DHs), Sub-divisional Hospitals (SDHs) and State General Hospitals (SGHs). (Image generated using AI)
description: The mother told investigators that she already had one daughter and had hoped that the second child would be a boy, police said
body_raw: The mother of a day-old baby girl has been arrested for allegedly strangling her daughter inside the maternity ward of the District Hospital in Madhya Pradeshs Ashoknagar, with police saying the woman, who was hoping for a son, killed her daughter in a fit of anger. Police said the case was cracked after investigators examined hospital CCTV footage, questioned family members separately, and confronted the woman with the available evidence. The development came three days after the newborn was found dead at the hospital on October 3. The baby was born late on October 2 in the Chanderi area and was admitted to the hospital shortly after for medical observation. She was subsequently found dead under suspicious circumstances. A medical examination found that the death was not natural and that the infant had died after her neck was compressed, following which a case was registered at Kotwali police station. Investigators examined CCTV footage from cameras installed at the district hospital, but the maternity ward where the incident occurred did not have a camera, leaving a crucial gap in the investigation. Ashoknagar Superintendent of Police Rajiv Kumar Mishra said the police team subsequently questioned the deceased infants relatives separately and examined the available facts and circumstantial evidence. The mother told investigators that she already had a daughter and had been hearing discussions within the family about the expectation of having a son. She had hoped that the second child would be a boy, police said. Acted in a fit of anger When she gave birth to another girl at around 11.30 pm on October 2, she became disturbed, an officer said. The woman became mentally disturbed and, in a fit of anger, strangled her newborn daughter, the officer said. The baby had blood coming from her mouth and marks resembling pressure around her neck. Given these circumstances, the hospital treated the death as suspicious and informed the police, following which the body was sent for post-mortem examination, an official had said at the time of death. The possibility of a family member being responsible for the death had emerged also because access to the child was restricted as she was admitted to the Special Newborn Care Unit SNCU. According to police, the mother was questioned after investigators found discrepancies while reconstructing the circumstances surrounding the childs death. The questioning was conducted after obtaining medical clearance and with the required sensitivity, given that the suspect was herself the mother of the deceased newborn, SP Mishra said.

articleTitle: Coming in 2030: Inter-terminal train at Delhi Airport for swift, seamless passenger movement
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport
description: Delhi airport APM will connect IGIA terminals with a 7.3-km rapid transit system by 2030, easing passenger movement between terminals.
body_raw: At Delhis Indira Gandhi International Airport, getting from Terminal 1 to Terminal 3 can mean a 15-20 minute road journey-longer during peak hours or VIP movements-despite both being part of the same airport. By 2030, that journey could be made by train. Delhi International Airport Limited DIAL, the airport operator, is planning a 7.3-km automated people mover APM or inter-terminal rapid rail system that will connect Terminal 1 with Terminal 3, with stops at Aerocity and the airports cargo area. The proposed system is estimated to cost around Rs 3,500 crore, bringing IGI - the countrys largest airport with three passenger terminals and four runways - at par with some of the leading global airports where passengers can move swiftly between terminals using driverless trains. DIAL CEO Pradeep Panicker on Tuesday expressed confidence that the intra-airport transit system would be ready by 2030, adding that its design and other modalities are under finalisation. The APM system will be 7.3 km in length, and will have six stations - Terminal 1 station, three stations at various locations in Aerocity, a cargo area station, and Terminal 3 station, which will also serve Terminal 2. According to Panicker, APM stations for Terminal 1 and Terminal 3, and one of its Aerocity stations will be built adjacent to existing stations of Delhi Metro lines, which would allow passengers and those working at the airport the option to transfer between the APM and Delhi Metro almost seamlessly. While the APM is likely to be free for passengers transiting between terminals to catch connecting flights, DIAL is yet to take a call on whether the non-passenger riders will have to pay for using the system. Panicker said the AMP track will be elevated for 5.3 km, and at grade for the remaining 2 km. The total travel time between Terminal 1 and 3 will be 13 minutes, and DIAL plans to run APM trains at a 10-minute frequency. It estimates the initial daily ridership on the APM to be 55,000, expecting it to eventually rise to 85,000. The APM, which has been in planning for years, is part of IGIAs proposed Master Plan till 2036, when the airport expects to have a passenger handling capacity of 125 million per year, which could be further increased to 129 million. IGIAs current passenger handling capacity stands at 106 million per year. The plan has been submitted to the government for stakeholder consultations, said DIAL. As per the Operation, Management and Development Agreement OMDA for the airport, the master plan is required to be updated every 10 years. Speaking on other facets of the new 10-year Master Plan, Panicker said that Terminal 1s capacity will be increased to 45 million passengers per annum from the current 42 million, while Terminal 2s capacity will remain stable at 14 million passengers. Both the terminals will continue to cater only to domestic airlines. IGIAs largest terminal - Terminal 3 - will also see significant capacity augmentation. Its domestic passenger handling capacity is expected to rise to 27 million from the current 19 million, while international passenger capacity will go up to 39 million per year from the prevailing 31 million. Panicker said a new pier is planned to be built at Terminal 3 to boost its capacity, which will take the total number of piers at the terminal to five. The new pier and related works under the Master Plan are expected to cost about Rs 2,500 crore, as per DIALs estimates. Other capacity expansion works proposed under the masterplan include additional check-in counters, security screening machines, and parking stands. The three terminals together have 230 parking stands at present the number will increase to about 260, as per the masterplan. DIAL also plans to undertake road widening projects as well as add parking space at IGIA.

articleTitle: Why cutting short-lived climate pollutants is a key climate priority
articleFeaturedImageAlt: SLCPs, India, climate change
description: Unlike CO₂, many short-lived climate pollutants (SLCPs) have shorter atmospheric lifetimes but can have severe effects on climate, health, and food security. What are the major sources of SLCPs, and how do they intensify these concerns for a country like India? And what efforts are underway to cut their emissions? See infographics.
body_raw: - Abhinav Rai Short-lived climate pollutants SLCPs are responsible for up to 45 of current global warming and also contribute significantly to air pollution. Fast and immediate action on SLCPs can, therefore, help both in climate mitigation and air quality improvement. According to a 2018 Special Report on 1.5C by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change IPCC, cutting the emission of SLCPs can help avoid over half a degree of warming by 2050 and over 50 of predicted warming in the Arctic by 2050. It can also significantly reduce the risk of triggering dangerous climate tipping points, like the irreversible release of carbon dioxide and methane from thawing Arctic permafrost. But what exactly are SLCPs, where do they come from, and how do they affect the climate? Short-lived climate pollutants and their sources Short-lived climate pollutants SLCPs are also referred to as super pollutants or short-lived climate forcers SLCFs. The IPCC defines SLCFs as a group of physical and chemical compounds that have a lifespan shorter than that of carbon dioxide CO, but have significantly higher capability to increase the rate of global warming. While CO can remain in the atmosphere for hundreds of years, many SLCPs can persist in the atmosphere from a few days to two decades. The most significant SLCPs include black carbon, methane CH4, ozone O3, hydrofluorocarbons HFCs, hydrochlorofluorocarbons HCFCs and aerosols sulphate, nitrate, ammonium, carbonaceous aerosols, mineral dust, sea spray. Black carbon It is mainly a result of anthropogenic factors like incomplete combustion of biomass, burning of fossil fuels, stubble burning and forest fires. It is a strong climate-warming agent and contributes to poor air quality. The Indo-Gangetic Plain is a black carbon hotspot because of high population density, reliance on biomass burning for cooking and heating, open burning of agricultural residue or stubble burning to clear the paddy fields, and other combustion sources. Methane It is generated primarily during agricultural activities, like rice cultivation and livestock, and during the extraction and processing of fossil fuels and waste disposal. Methane has about 80 times more warming power compared to CO2 in its first 20 years in the atmosphere. It is also the second largest contributor to global warming after CO2, and a major source of tropospheric ozone O3 production. Hydrofluorocarbons HFCs HFCs are primarily used in cooling equipment such as refrigerators and air-conditioners and they can have hundreds to thousands of times greater impact on global warming compared to CO2. Although their share in GHGs is comparatively small, HFC emissions can increase with the growing demand for cooling equipment globally and especially in sub-tropical countries like India. Ozone O3 In the atmosphere, Ozone O3 can be classified into two types Stratospheric Ozone found between 10-50km above Earths surface and the tropospheric Ozone found up to 10km above Earths surface. The stratospheric ozone acts as a protective layer from the incoming ultraviolet radiation from the Sun. In contrast, tropospheric ozone is an air pollutant and a powerful greenhouse gas that adversely affects human health and reduces crop yields and agricultural productivity. O3 does not have any direct source of emission. It is produced when volatile organic compounds VOCs, methane or nitrogen oxides interact with sunlight. Impact on climate, health, and food security Black carbon, when deposited on snow or ice, darkens its colour, which reduces albedo sunlight reflecting ability and increases the absorption of more sunlight, which further warms the snowice and enhances the rate of melting. Now the cryospheric regions are warming two to three times faster than the global average. Black carbon also affects the formation of clouds and moisture transport, reducing the amount of snowfall and seasonal nourishment of glaciers. SLCPs are a significant contributor to air pollution. Black carbon is one of the most harmful components of fine particulate matter PM 2.5 air pollution. Long-term exposure to black carbon is linked to diseases such as chronic respiratory illness, asthma, pneumonia, heart disease, lung cancer, etc. About 7 million premature deaths are globally caused by problems associated with air pollution both indoor and outdoor every year, according to the Climate and Clean Air Coalition CCAC, an initiative by the United Nations Environment Program UNEP. Moreover, air pollution also reduces the growth of staple crops like rice, corn, soya and wheat. Black carbon obstructs the incoming sunlight and also disrupts rainfall patterns, affecting crop health. Indias air pollution and water-security challenge Indias air pollution levels are among the highest in the world, posing a very serious public health and economic challenge. An estimated 1.67 million deaths or 17.8 of all deaths in the country in 2019 are attributed to air pollution, according to a Lancet Planetary Health study. The study also suggested that these diseases and premature deaths caused an economic loss of around US36.8 billion, which was equivalent to 1.36 of Indias GDP at the time. In addition, a 2025 report by Clean Air Fund, backed by the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development ICIMOD, found that black carbon is accelerating the melting of glacier ice and ice sheets across the global cryosphere, including the Arctic and the Hindu Kush-Himalaya region. It found that about 60 of South Asias black carbon comes from residential fuel combustion. While more than one-fifth of Indias GDP is underpinned by the Himalayas, the accelerating glacier ice loss is also a water-security issue for the countrys glacier-fed Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra basins. According to the Global Methane Status Report 2025, India emitted 9 of total global methane emissions, the third largest globally after the US and China, where stubble burning was identified as a growing hotspot. Notably, Indias third Biennial Update Report suggests that the countrys methane emissions in 2016 largely came from agriculture 73.96, the waste sector14.46, and the energy sector 10.62. Efforts to cut SLCPs Efforts to address SLCPs are underway. For instance, a 2016 amendment to the Montreal Protocol, adopted in 1987 for protecting Earths depleting Ozone layer, called for the phase-down of hydrofluorocarbons HFCs by more than 80 by the late 2040s. India ratified this amendment, also known as the Kigali amendment, in 2021. During COP26 2021, the Global Methane Pledge initiative was launched with the aim of significantly reducing methane emissions 30 from 2020 levels by 2030, and is currently joined by 159 countries and the European Commission. However, India has not joined it yet. Two major sources of methane emissions are paddy cultivation and livestock, and India considers them as survival emissions because a large population and food security is dependent on these. In the last couple of decades, the problem of air pollution has become severe in India, especially in northern states. Several steps have been taken since the enactment of The Air Prevention and Control of Pollution Act in 1981 and notification of National Ambient Air Quality Standards NAAQS in 2009 for 12 air pollutants, including particulate matter PM10 and PM2.5, and Ozone O. These include the launch of the National Air Quality Index AQI in 2015, the Graded Response Action Plan GRAP in 2017 in the Delhi-NCR region, joining the UNEP-led CCAC in 2019 and also launching the National Clean Air Programme NCAP in 130 cities of 24 States Under NCAP, performance-linked grants are provided to the cities for implementing pollution mitigation measures. According to the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, during 2025-26, only 65 cities under NCAP a total of 130 cities have been able to check their PM2.5 levels below the standard 40 gm under NAAQS, where Delhi recorded 102 g Similarly, regarding PM10 concentrations, even though more cities showed progress than before, only 14 cities met the NAAQS 60 gm3 during 2025-26. Way forward To slow down the current rate of global warming, decarbonisation efforts remain important. But these efforts need to be complemented by rapid reductions in SLCPs. Since many SLCPs have short lifetimes, reducing their emissions can lower their atmospheric concentrations and climate impacts within years or decades. Effective reduction in SLCPs can reduce global warming up to 0.6C by 2050. Although India has taken several steps, greater attention needs to be paid to ensuring access to cleaner cooking fuel, effective management of crop residue, and reducing air pollution levels. Schemes such as Galvanising Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan GOBARdhan can be scaled up. The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, which provided over 10.5 crore LPG connections, has expanded access to cleaner fuel, but ensuring sustained refills remains an issue. For India, cutting SLCPs can deliver multiple benefits, including cleaner air, higher crop yields, and slower ice loss in the Himalaya, alongside climate mitigation. Post read questions 1. What are Short-Lived Climate Pollutants SLCPs? Discuss their major sources and their significance in addressing climate change and air pollution. 2. What is the role of black carbon in accelerating snow and glacier melt? Discuss its implications for water security in the Himalayan region. 3. How can reduction of short-lived climate pollutants contribute to Indias climate mitigation strategy? 4. Discuss the major sources of short-lived climate pollutants in India. What measures can be adopted to reduce their emissions while ensuring energy, food and livelihood security? 5. Indias efforts to tackle air pollution have significant implications for its climate objectives. Discuss with reference to NCAP, clean cooking, crop-residue management and methane reduction. articleTitle: Pakistan, Turkey ‘military forces’ to help Saudi Arabia: Why this may not mean troops in active combat
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Pakistan
description: Does the Mecca pact statement mean Pakistani and Turkish soldiers will be in active combat alongside Saudi Arabia against the Houthis? Not exactly, and at least, not immediately. Here’s why.
body_raw: Turkey and Pakistan on Monday October 5 agreed to provide military forces to Saudi Arabia as it battles Yemens Houthis, invoking their collective defence pact, the Mecca Alliance for Defence also spelt as Makkah. The announcement came as Yemens internationally recognised government, with heavy Saudi support, claimed to have pushed back the Houthi rebels from some key areas they had captured last month, including the strategic Red Sea port of Mocha. The Houthis said they had hit airports, a refinery, and a military base in Saudi Arabia, though both sides dismissed each others claims. The Mecca Alliance parties met on Monday, after which they released a statement saying they affirmed that the security of each Party is an integral part of the collective security of the three countries, and that translating the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defense into practical measures demonstrates the credibility of the commitment to collective defense. Do does this mean Pakistani and Turkish soldiers will be in active combat alongside Saudi Arabais defence forces? Not exactly, and at least, not immediately. Heres why. What the Mecca Pact statement says Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on August 7, 2026. The Makkah agreement says an armed attack on any one of the three countries will be regarded as an attack on all three. Earlier, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan had signed the Strategic Mutual Defense Agreement SMDA on September 17, 2025. The fact that Saudi Arabia had been fighting the Houthis escalating attacks alone over the past month had raised questions about these defence pacts, specially the much-feted Mecca pact. The statement issued on Monday does speak of practical implementation, but a careful reading throws up questions. The Committee decided to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defense commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the Kingdom, in accordance with the approved arrangements and the national legislation of the Parties, thereby enhancing readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats, the statement says. Thus, any proposed action is subject to the countrys internal laws. Turkeys Parliament is yet to ratify the pact, something its officials had last month cited to explain why they hadnt acted. This seems to suggest that for now, Turkeys support will be more about intelligence sharing and training than active deployment. Pakistan has sent similar signals. After Mondays meeting, Pakistans defence minister Khawaja Asif, who had taken part in it, was asked by local TV channel Geo News about a possible operational role by Pakistan and Turkey. According to the newspaper Dawn, he replied that both nations had a presence in theatre, but only Saudi troops were involved in combat operations. Whatever assistance they require is being provided. But right now, the Turkish and Pakistani armies are playing a supportive role, he said, as quoted by Dawn. Why Pakistan and Turkey wont be keen to actively fight the Houthis While the Makkah agreement is supposed to be a defence treaty, few details about its actual operational structure are available publicly. It does not delineate the escalation ladder, or what sort of response is expected from a member at which stage when another is facing attacks. Both Pakistan and Turkey have earlier said that Saudi Arabia has not requested them to send combat forces to Yemen. Pakistan, of course, also has another mutual defence pact with Saudi Arabia. However, barring a few fighter jets it sent in April when Iran was attacking US military assets in the kingdom, Pakistan hasnt intervened militarily. Nor has Saudi Arabia come to Pakistans aid against Afghanistan, with both countries prioritising their own immediate concerns. Pakistan has a big reason to not antagonise Tehran too much - it shares a 900-km border with the Shia country, passing through the restive Balochistan region, and has the worlds second largest Shia population in the world, after Iran itself. Then is the Iran factor. The Houthis have largely been trained and armed by Iran. If other countries were to enter active fighting on Saudi Arabias behalf, Iran and its allied militias might get behind the Houthis openly, adding another dimension to the US-Israel-Iran war and risking a much wider conflagration in the region. Neither Turkey nor Pakistan wants to give up its role of mediating in the Iran conflict. Both countries have a lot more to lose if the Iran war drags on - due to oil prices and Israels stronger profile in the region - and would not wish to scuttle peace efforts there by deploying guns and boots against the Houthis.

articleTitle: After airlines push back, Centre pauses Mumbai airport’s flight cut plan
articleFeaturedImageAlt: mumbai airport flight cut plan
description: Adani-run CSMIA wanted to drop 265 weekly international departures from October 25 to make room for domestic flights. It must now draw up a fresh plan with regulatory approvals
body_raw: The Union government has put on hold a plan by Mumbais Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport CSMIA to cut international departures from Terminal 2 by 33 per cent, after airlines pushed back against the move, sources said. The decision came on Tuesday, the deadline the airport operator had set for airlines to choose which international flights they would give up from October 25. At a meeting chaired by Union Civil Aviation Secretary Samir Sinha on Tuesday afternoon, the Ministry of Civil Aviation directed Adani Airports Holdings Limited AAHL, which runs CSMIA, to call another meeting of all stakeholders and draw up a fresh transition plan, according to those familiar with the matter. Airlines and industry bodies, including the International Air Transport Association IATA and the Federation of Indian Airlines FIA, attended the meeting. AAHL will now seek approvals from the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security BCAS, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation DGCA and state authorities before it goes ahead with a revised plan, sources said. The airport operator had told airlines it would cut 265 weekly international departures from Terminal 2 from October 25, to make room for domestic flights moving in from Terminal 1B. Indian carriers accounted for 125 of these. IndiGo would have lost 74 flights, Air India 33, Akasa Air 11 and Air India Express seven. The remaining 140 belonged to foreign airlines. Airlines were asked to volunteer the slots they would temporarily drop by October 6. If they didnt, the operator said it would pick the slots itself based on operational considerations. This followed an earlier directive from the operator asking airlines to either move their Terminal 1B operations to Navi Mumbai International Airport NMIA or suspend them from October 25. Airlines objected, citing the impact on existing operations. IATA also sought a transparent assessment of NMIAs capacity before flights were shifted there, covering ground handling, cargo facilities, crew accommodation and connectivity. The changes are tied to the planned demolition of the northern section of Terminal 1B in January 2027. That section handles around five million passengers a year, nearly a third of Terminal 1s footfall. Redevelopment of the terminal is expected to be completed by 2029-30. The airport operator, airlines and other stakeholders will now discuss a fresh plan before any operational changes are made.

articleTitle: ‘Maharashtra centre of Maoist urban network’: State defends Special Public Security Act in court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The state said the law was not vague and did not violate free speech, which is subject to reasonable restrictions under the Constitution. (File Photo)
description: Defending the law against Congress, CPI and AITUC pleas, the state says other Maoist-hit states already have similar laws that have withstood judicial scrutiny
body_raw: Maharashtra, because of its highest urban population has become center of Maoist urban network, the state government has told the Bombay High Court, defending the Maharashtra Special Public Security MSPS Act. The state did not have legal framework of public security act to ban frontal organization like other Left Wing Extremism LWE affected states Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhatisgarh, said the affidavit filed by Pritamkumar Jawale, Deputy Secretary of the state Home department. The affidavit seeks dismissal of petitions by the Congress, the Communist Party of India CPI and the All India Trade Union Congress AITUC challenging the Acts constitutional validity, and questions the petitioners legal standing. It says the law was enacted to establish a robust legal framework to prevent and tackle unlawful, subversive, and extremist activities. The petitioners contend the law curbs peaceful and legitimate dissent and gives the executive wide-ranging, arbitrary, and excessive powers to ban organisations without any judicial scrutiny or oversight. The Act lists four punishable offences being a member of an unlawful organisation, collecting funds for one, helping manage one, or carrying out an unlawful activity. It authorises the state to notify any suspected body as an unlawful organisation. Citing Elgaar Parishad and other cases, the affidavit claimed Maharashtra has the highest number of frontal organisations in the country, 64. It said Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Jharkhand had banned such groups under similar laws that withstood judicial scrutiny, so Maharashtra was empowered to enact one for local security environments. Not enacting the law, it said, would affect entitlement of security related expenditure SRE fund crucial for fighting Maoist battle in LWE-affected areas. The state said the law was not vague and did not violate free speech, which is subject to reasonable restrictions under the Constitution. It balances the fundamental liberties of citizens with the paramount duty of preserving public order and national integrity, the reply said. The state also denied that appointing a government advocate to the non-judicial advisory board was illegal. The Act bridges a critical legislative gap by allowing action before any violence or loss of life, it said, as insurgencies survive not only on ideology but they require robust logistical supply chains, safe houses, covert financial pipelines, and institutional fronts. A bench led by Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi allowed the petitioners to file a rejoinder to the affidavit and posted the matter for hearing on October 16

articleTitle: ‘Sudden action seems bit strange’: Omar Abdullah after 150 flown out of J&K for deportation
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah
description: “If you look at it, their presence here has not really caused us any particular harm. However, it is also true that they cannot stay illegally,” the J&K CM said.
body_raw: A day after 150 alleged Bangladeshi nationals picked from across the Union Territory were airlifted to West Bengal, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday said the sudden action seemed a bit strange. If you look at it, their presence here has not really caused us any particular harm. However, it is also true that they cannot stay illegally, he said. Omar said that Rohingyas are being unfairly targeted, adding that it is not in the hands of the UT government but the government at the Centre, who are using the police to move them out. We gave them Rohingyas refuge here, a little space, and allowed them to stay here until conditions in their country improved. Now, suddenly taking action against them seems a bit strange to me, he said. The 150 people airlifted to Bagdogra, from where they will be deported, are among 500 who were detained from different parts of the Union Territory during a survey to identify illegal immigrants. Meanwhile, speaking to reporters, Omar commended the Supreme Court for raising questions on the issue of deletion of names from voter lists. Omar said, The good thing is that questions are being raised in the Supreme Court as well, especially the deletion of names from voter lists. The SC has sought answers regarding this from the EC and the Government of India. We will have to see how far this can be corrected by the courts. The Supreme Court on Monday issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission of India ECI on a petition accusing Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of acting in violation of the law that governs his terms of office by functioning in a unilateral manner, and seeking his removal. The notice issued by a three-judge bench, presided by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, was also directed at Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg, and ECI Director General Information Technology Seema Khanna. On INDIA blocs Delhi march, he said that after the leaders met in New Delhi, a calendar was drawn out for this month. The beginning of that was for the members of Parliament from the INDIA bloc to march toward the Election Commission, and this will go on, he added. UCC will never be implemented in JK In response to a query regarding the implementation of the UCC in Jammu and Kashmir, the CM said, A Uniform Civil Code is not truly uniform until it is implemented everywhere. It will never be implemented here. He also pointed out Bihars resistance to its implementation, stating that, Similarly, there are other governments too that have said the UCC will not be applied in their states. So, this is only being implemented by the BJP. He said it is wrong that the Bharatiya Janata Party BJP is trying to implement this step by step in states where they are in power. These matters are not handled from state to state. If you have the courage, bring a legislation in Parliament, debate it and then lets see whether it passes or not. If you look at it in the true sense of a democracy, this has to be debated at the Centre. They will not introduce this law in Parliament because they do not have the numbers, he said.

articleTitle: Expedition hopes to finally solve the Amelia Earhart mystery
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Amelia Earhart
description: Nearly 90 years after US aviator Amelia Earhart vanished over the Pacific, a new expedition to the remote island of Nikumaroro hopes a lagoon anomaly could finally reveal the fate of her missing aircraft.
body_raw: Written By Julian Ryall Amelia Earharts attempt to become the first woman to fly around the globe at the equator ended in mystery when she and her navigator, Fred Noonan, disappeared over the Pacific Ocean in July 1937. With the 90th anniversary of her disappearance on the horizon, a new expedition is setting out to finally determine what happened over the vast Pacific. This expedition has what it believes is crucial new evidence. The team from Purdue University in Indiana and the Archaeological Legacy Institute ALI is scheduled to depart for the uninhabited island of Nikumaroro on Saturday to determine if an anomaly in the islands lagoon is Earharts missing plane. Part of the low-lying Pacific island nation of Kiribati, Nikumaroro has long been considered the place where Earhart and Noonan died. The pair took off from New Guinea on July 2, 1937, on the leg to the island of Howland, where they were to refuel before continuing on to Hawaii and completing the circumnavigation in California. Something went amiss en route, however, and even though a US Coast Guard ship could hear Earharts radio transmissions and her Lockheed Electra must have been tantalizingly close, she was never found. One of the last messages said she was running on a north-south navigational line that gave her the best chance of finding land before her fuel ran out. That line went through Nikumaroro. Landing on a coral reef In 1988, researchers from the International Group for Historic Aircraft Recovery TIGHAR were the first to suggest that Earhart could have reached Nikumaroro and landed on its fringing coral reef. TIGHARs first visit to the island was in 1989, and the group has returned seven more times, turning up compelling artifacts, including lengths of aircraft aluminum and plexiglass from a windscreen. The group found a scent bottle, a zip made in Pennsylvania in the mid-1930s, parts of a pocket knife of the same brand listed in the aircraft inventory, and the heel of a womans shoe. Archive research discovered that human remains discovered on the island in 1940 were initially believed to be of Earhart or Noonan - but were lost in the chaos of the Pacific war. Despite the searches, no one has yet found the smoking gun artifact, an item that could only have come from the doomed flight. Satellite images offer fresh hope Expedition leader Rick Pettigrew, executive director of the Archaeological Legacy Institute ALI, believes the elements may have uncovered incontrovertible evidence. A powerful tropical cyclone tore through the central Pacific in 2015, shifting geographical features on the island and in its lagoon. Satellite images taken over the following years showed what might be the outline of an aircraft fuselage and wings in shallow water off the Taraia promontory. This object in the satellite images is exactly the right size to represent the fuselage and tail of the Electra, the ALI website states. It also appears to be very reflective and is likely to be metallic. It lies in very shallow water, largely covered by sediment, in a place where the current would bring an object floating into the lagoon through Tatiman Passage, the opening to the ocean and the reef. Pettigrews 17-strong team intends to focus all its efforts on the place where the images indicate debris may be located, using drone photography, remote sensing with magnetometers and sonar units. If the initial results are positive, a hydraulic dredge will excavate sediment. Once we have a sufficient portion of the object exposed, we should be able to identify it, according to the ALIs expedition plan. If it is made of aircraft aluminum and has the specific shape and rivet patterns of the Electra, we will know that we have found the remains of Earharts aircraft. In search of a smoking gun Much of the ALIs theory is based on the research and fieldwork carried out by TIGHAR, but its executive director, Ric Gillespie, is not convinced the researchers will find the smoking gun. The object visible in old satellite imagery that Pettigrew believes is aircraft wreckage does not look like aircraft wreckage, Gillespie told DW. It looks like a dead pandanus tree that was uprooted in a storm and washed up on Taraia. Pettigrew thinks the wreckage is no longer visible because it is buried in silt, Gillespie noted. He has never been to that location and does not understand that the silt there is only a few inches deep. Teams from TIGHAR searched the same location in 2001 and 2007 with metal detectors and drew blanks, he said. Yet Gillespie remains convinced that Earhart was on Nikumaroro. I think the aircraft sank immediately after being washed over the reef edge and was smashed to pieces in the surf, he said. Major components were eventually buried in underwater landslides . or grown over with coral. We have found what there is to find. Dorothy Cochrane, who has monitored progress in the search for Earhart for more than 35 years as curator at the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum in Washington, DC, and continues to do so since her recent retirement, says Earhart still holds fascination for so many people because it is the greatest unsolved mystery of the 20th and continuing into the 21st centuries. An alternative scenario She has a different view of what happened in 1937. She argues that if Earhart was nearly out of fuel while still close to Howland, it would have been impossible to fly another 640 kilometers 400 miles to Nikumaroro. Cochrane also says that items cited as evidence of a castaway on the island can be explained by other visitors and by a small settlement that existed there for several years. I believe that Earhart and Noonan were in the general vicinity of Howland Island, based on the facts of the flight, but just could not find it before they ran out of fuel, she said. Howland Island was a tiny speck in the morning light of a vast sea, she said, suggesting Earhart could not establish radio contact to guide her the last few miles to her destination. Cochrane believes the Electra lies on the seabed near Howland. Others have advanced this theory, and several searches of the area have been carried out in recent years. If Pettigrews lead pays off, however, it will conclude aviations nearly 90-year puzzle.

articleTitle: Army Subedar faces court martial for cheating civilians of Rs 51.44 lakh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: court martial case
description: The Junior Commissioned Officer (JCO) faces six charges of cheating, framed under Section 69 of the Army Act.
body_raw: A Subedar of the Corps of Electronics and Mechanical Engineers EME in the Indian Army will be facing a General Court Martial for allegedly cheating several civilians of about Rs 51.44 lakh, according to a charge sheet served on him in September. The Junior Commissioned Officer JCO, who was serving as a Subedar Clerk Inventory Management with 304 Field Workshop Company of 671 EME Battalion, attached to Headquarters 106 Infantry Brigade, faces six charges of cheating. All six charges have been framed under Section 69 of the Army Act for committing a civil offence - cheating. The charge sheet says the alleged offences came to the notice of the competent authority on September 28, 2024. At the time of the alleged offences, the Subedar was performing duties as Section In-charge, Technical Store Section, 304 Field Workshop Company. According to the particulars of the charges, the Subedar allegedly received Rs 3 lakh at field between April and May 2023 and Rs 15 lakh at Guwahati in May 2023. He is further accused of receiving Rs 5.60 lakh between August and December 2023 and Rs 10.13 lakh between September and December 2023. The remaining allegations involve receipt of Rs 3.50 lakh between August and September 2023 and Rs 14.19 lakh between December 2023 and February 2024. Directions for his trial by General Court Martial have been endorsed by Major General NS Sohal, General Officer Commanding, 71 Infantry Division. The case comes amid a series of recent court martial proceedings involving allegations of financial irregularities in the Army. In October 2025, a General Court Martial at Tibri Military Station near Gurdaspur sentenced an Army Medical Corps Subedar to seven years rigorous imprisonment and dismissal from service after finding him guilty on six charges. Three charges were under the Prevention of Corruption Act relating to disproportionate assets and three under Section 63 of the Army Act. A search had recovered Rs 8 lakh from his car and Rs 7.83 lakh from his house. Scrutiny of bank accounts also showed deposits of Rs 27.11 lakh in his account and Rs 44.27 lakh in his wifes account during his posting at a military hospital in Amritsar. Earlier that month, a General Court Martial at Fatehgarh sentenced Lieutenant Colonel Avinash Gupta of the Army Service Corps to two years rigorous imprisonment and cashiering. He was convicted on three charges under Section 52f of the Army Act relating to fraudulent transactions, including alleged misuse of railway concession vouchers issued years earlier, and one charge of unbecoming conduct. In July 2026, a Summary General Court Martial found a Major General of the Army Medical Corps, who had served as Commandant of 166 Military Hospital, Jammu, guilty on 16 of 18 charges relating to alleged irregularities and misappropriation involving medical stores worth around Rs 11 crore between August 2018 and January 2020. He was cashiered and sentenced to one years rigorous imprisonment. In August 2026, a Summary General Court Martial at Nagrota convicted Lieutenant Colonel D Maji of the Army Medical Corps on five of 14 charges arising from the same hospitals procurement of medical supplies in 2018-19. The case involved alleged projections of urgent requirements worth around Rs 3 crore. He was cashiered and sentenced to one years rigorous imprisonment.

articleTitle: Messi shines in Argentina farewell, ends 21-year career with goal, two assists
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Lionel Messi scored and assisted in his final Argentina game against Benin in Buenos Aires. (AP Photo)
description: Messi leaves the international stage as the most decorated figure in Argentine football history, having made 207 appearances, scored 126 goals and provided 67 assists, all records for La Albiceleste.
body_raw: After donning Albiceleste colours for one final time, Lionel Messi finally hung up his boots with typical flair and finesse. The 39-year-old brought the curtains down on a glittering international football career as Argentina overcame Benin 3-0 in a friendly at the Estadio Mas Monumental in Buenos Aires on Wednesday. The match, dubbed the Last Tango, saw Messi lead out Argentina one last time in front of a packed house, with members of Argentinas FIFA World Cup 2022-winning squad and their families on hand to mark the occasion. The game paused for a moment in minute 10, the digits that magically sparkled on his shirt over the years. ALSO READ Messis farewell speech I dont want to leave, not being with Argentina hurts Providing assists for teammates Nicolas Otamendi and Nico Paz in the second half and converting a 71st-minute penalty with a thunderous shot to the top-right corner, the eight-time Ballon dOr winner ensured that his final 90 minutes in the national shirt had some memorable moments. Messi had announced his retirement from international football on August 31, a little over two months after Argentinas FIFA World Cup 2026 final defeat to Spain in New Jersey. The Argentine Football Association tempted him to make one last appearance for the farewell he deserves, and thousands of fans turned up at the Estadio Monumental to show their appreciation. The AFA said the match would transcend sports and be full of emotion. His roll of honours includes the Beijing 2008 Olympic gold medal, the FIFA World Cup 2022 title, back-to-back Copa America trophies in 2021 and 2024, and the 2022 Finalissima. He appeared in a record-tying six World Cups alongside his great rival Cristiano Ronaldo.

articleTitle: ‘Fake PCS officer’ bride dupes AAP leader in Punjab; 6 booked
articleFeaturedImageAlt: aap leader wife
description: Couple got married in February. 6 months on, he alleges that his wife lied to him about being a PCS officer and also has a child from a previous marriage
body_raw: An Aam Aadmi Party AAP leader from Punjabs Fatehgarh Sahib district was allegedly duped by his wife, whom he married in February after she introduced herself as a Punjab Civil Services PCS officer posted in Jalandhar. However, over six months after their wedding, the AAP leader claimed in a police complaint that his wife was not a PCS officer and that she had lied to him. He alleged that his wife lied about her age, and that she has a teenage son from her previous marriage. The complainant, AAP leader Amrinder Singh, 33, from Mandofal village, alleged, She falsely claimed that she was posted as an ADC in Mohali. She had created a fake Instagram ID, introducing herself as a PCS officer, with the caption Serving the nation is not a post, its a purpose. Amrinder, an advocate by profession, is the market committee chairman of Sirhind and zila parishad member of Fatehgarh Sahib. He has served the AAP, Punjab, as a joint secretary and was among the founding members of the AAP in Fatehgarh Sahib. Based on his complaint, police on Monday booked Amrinders Manwinder Kaur and five other members of her family, including brother Tarlochan Singh, mother Varinderjit Kaur, cousin Narinder Singh, sister-in-law Rupinder Kaur Tarlochans wife and former sarpanch Surinder Singh Rana - residents of Sur Singh village in Tarn Taran district - under sections 318 4 cheating, 336 3 forgery, 338 forgery of valuable security, 61 2 criminal conspiracy and 340 2 using a forged document of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita BNS at the Fatehgarh Sahib police station. According to the FIR, Amrinder, in his statement, told police that both families had met at Hansali Sahib, and their wedding was fixed. He said that Manwinder and her family claimed that she was a PCS officer, with a posting in Jalandhar. He said that the bride had claimed that she was posted as PCS executive in Jalandhar. He further said that Manwinder had also claimed that her parents had died, but later he got to know that her mother was alive. Amrinder said that Manwinders family had claimed that she was 34 years old, and that their wedding was solemnised at Hansali Sahib on February 10. According to the FIR, Amrinder said that after the wedding, Manwinder would often go out, claiming that she was going to her duty. Amrinder said, When I asked her about her current posting, she said that she was posted as the Additional Deputy Commissioner in Mohali, but had been suspended due to some reasons. When I asked her to provide more details so that I could help her. I asked Manwinder to provide me with a copy of her suspension order, but she did not, Amrinder said, alleging On August 27, she left the house with 14 tolas of gold and Rs 1 lakh in cash. He further said, When I repeatedly asked her for a copy of the suspension order, she sent me a document on WhatsApp in September. According to the document, she was posted as the ADC, Mohali, in April 2022. However, the document was found to be forged later. Amrinder said that after getting suspicious, he started his investigation and found that Manwinder had never cleared the PCS, nor was she ever posted as an ADC in Mohali or Jalandhar. I found that Manwinder was 46 years old and not 34, and that she was not unmarried as claimed. Manwinder has an 18-year-old son, whom she hid. Fatehgarh SSP Shubham Aggarwal said, A probe has been initiated. The opposite party will be called to record their statement. Further proceedings will be done accordingly. The complainants allegations are yet to be verified. Amrinder did not respond to repeated calls and messages. An AAP worker from Fatehgarh Sahib said, We had attended their wedding Amrinder was really happy. Its shocking that it ended this way.

articleTitle: Woman threatens man of false rape case, extorts Rs 90 lakh; held
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengaluru gym trainer death
description: The team of officers from Sadar police station caught her red-handed as she was being handed the money, in marked currency notes, and put an end to a man’s alleged three-year extortion ordeal.
body_raw: On Sunday, a 24-year-old woman entered a cafe in Gururams Sector 47, hoping to walk out with Rs 50,000 - unaware that plainclothes policemen were watching her from a table nearby. The team of officers from Sadar police station caught her red-handed as she was being handed the money, in marked currency notes, and put an end to a mans alleged three-year extortion ordeal. The accused, identified as Suryadita Das, who hails from West Bengal and currently resides in Sushant Lok, was arrested after a corporate employee alleged that she had blackmailed him into paying approximately Rs 90 lakh having threatened him of framing him in a false rape case. ACP Crime Naveen Sharma on Tuesday said the complainant and the accused first connected around three years ago on Seeking, a dating platform. The two came in contact through the app, exchanged phone numbers and remained in touch for nearly three years. They traveled together to multiple places and developed a relationship, the ACP said. According to the police, Das later began coercing the man into parting with significant sums of money. Providing a breakdown of the extorted funds, Sharma said, The accused took approximately Rs 60-65 lakh in cash in intermittent installments and another Rs 10-15 lakh through bank transfers, totaling around Rs 90 lakh. Even after that, she continued demanding more money. Asked why the complainant waited three years before approaching the police, the ACP said the delay stemmed from a fear of public dishonour. The complainant remained in deep fear that his social standing, family name, and personal reputation would be ruined, Sharma said, adding that he eventually filed a complaint on October 4 as the woman kept pressing for more money. The police laid a trap. They asked the victim to fix a meeting with Das, a police spokesperson said. Officers in plain clothes kept a watch. Das was caught accepting the money - the notes carried pre-recorded initials and signatures put by the police, officers said. Das, who completed her MBA from SGT University, works at a private firm, police said. On whether Das was part of an organised racket, ACP Sharma said, So far, it appears that she did this alone. We are verifying if she has targeted other people as well and if any complaint or case of a similar nature has been registered against her. Das was produced before a local court Sunday that remanded her into two-day police custody. The Gurugram police have frozen around Rs 95 lakh in her bank account. Further investigation into the matter is underway, police said.

articleTitle: MPs wanted a meeting in Parliament Annexe against protocol, says Election Commission
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gyanesh Kumar resignation, gyanesh kumar, election commission of india, cec resignation protest, india bloc protest new delhi, voter list deletion row, rahul gandhi, priyanka gandhi vadra, parliament street protest, akashvani bhavan detention, vote chori allegations, india bloc, election commissioner dissent report, akashvani bhavan, election commission news
description: ‘Panel offered to send senior official to get memo but MPs declined’
body_raw: Saying that no party had sought an appointment until 4 pm Tuesday, the Election Commission EC said it was later informed by police that the Opposition Members of Parliament MPs wanted a meeting at Parliament House Annexe. It said this request was unusual, because, as per protocol, such meetings are held only on the premises of the Election Commission of India. The EC said it still offered to send a senior officer to receive their memorandum, but the MPs rejected its proposal. Earlier today, during the march of certain political parties towards the Election Commission, it was learnt through the media that some MPs wished to meet the Commission along with their delegation. With regard to todays developments, it is clarified that, till 4 pm today, no political party, through its representatives, had sought an appointment for a meeting with the Election Commission, the poll panel said in its statement on Tuesday evening. The EC said it was informed by the Delhi Police, around 4 pm that a delegation of MPs led by the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, wanted to meet the Commission to submit a memorandum. After 4 pm today, when the Election Commission was considering the above proposal for the above-mentioned meeting with the Honble MPs, it was informed by the DCP, Delhi Police, that the meeting being sought was to be held with a group of 240 MPs and that the proposed venue was the Parliament House Annexe. The Election Commission considered this request as unusual and therefore, could not be accepted, as, in accordance with ECI protocol, such meetings are held only on the premises of the Election Commission of India, it said. The EC said it still proposed to send its most senior officer on duty to the meeting venue to receive the memorandum, which in itself would have been an unprecedented step. However, this offer was also declined by the Honble MPs, the Commission said. ECI respects the parliamentary and democratic processes of the country, as well as its own protocols and conventions, which are of utmost importance. Any political party may, at any time, request for a meeting with the Election Commission and the Commission, keeping in view the suitability of time, schedules a date and time for the meeting. This is a regular practice, it said. It pointed to the procedure laid down in 2025 for meetings with political parties. All political parties had been informed of the same and they follow this procedure. Whenever a delegation of a political party, or a joint delegation of several parties, wishes to meet the Commission, it seeks an appointment through its duly authorised representative. The meeting is thereafter held at a time mutually agreed upon by both sides, it said.

articleTitle: Christa Pike is conscious and speaking after Tennessee failed execution, her attorneys say
articleFeaturedImageAlt: christa pike, Tennessee, world, christa pike alive, christa pike execution, christa pike survives, christa pike awake, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Her attorneys said they are grateful for the first responders and the medical team at the hospital “who treated Christa like a human and have provided exceptional care to her.”
body_raw: Yuvraj Manchanda murder, Christa Pike, a Tennessee inmate who survived Tennessees attempt to execute her, is awake and speaking as she receives treatment at a hospital, her attorneys said Tuesday. Against all odds, Christa Pike is conscious, speaking, and continues to receive critical medical care. Despite the severe damage she endured to her arms, she is still handcuffed and shackled to the bed. Her recovery is medically unprecedented. Her prognosis remains unclear but, at a minimum, we expect a long recovery, attorneys for Pike said in a statement. Her attorneys said they are grateful for the first responders and the medical team at the hospital who treated Christa like a human and have provided exceptional care to her. The statement was the first indication that Pike has improved since an ambulance carried her away from a Nashville prison last Wednesday. A spokeswoman for the Tennessee Department of Correction said she could provide no information other than that Pike remained hospitalized Tuesday. Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital as they attempted to put her to death for the 1995 beating and stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer. The lethal injection drug didnt kill her, but her lawyers said her arms were left burned and blistered. Dr. Joel Zivot, a professor of anesthesiology and surgery in Atlanta who consulted as an expert for Pikes legal team, said the development bodes well for a good recovery. But, he added, it could be weeks or months before anyone knows exactly what her recovery might look like, and whether her competency could be restored to a level that might enable the state to try again to execute her.

articleTitle: Karnataka Public Service Commission job racket: Flat purchased in name of family of arrested IAS officer under ED lens
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka Public Service Commission job racket, KPSC recruitment scam, Karnataka KPSC scam, KPSC chairman daughter recruitment, Suma Sahukar income certificate case, KPSC veterinary doctor paper leak .Karnataka veterinary recruitment scam. Shivashankarappa Sahukar CID probe, KPSC question paper leak, Karnataka High Court KPSC case, KPSC corruption allegations, Basavaraj Kannale KPSC scam, Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar arrest, 400 veterinary doctors recruitment scam, Karnataka government job scam, Express investigation, KPSC recruitment controversy
description: Gangwar, 41, who served as KPSC’s controller of examinations from January 2024 to March 2026, has been suspended by the Karnataka government.
body_raw: AN APARTMENT purchased in the name of family members of arrested IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar near Bengaluru airport has come under the scrutiny of the Enforcement Directorate, which is probing money laundering allegations in the recruitment for 400 veterinary officers through the Karnataka Public Service Commission KPSC. Gangwar, 41, who served as KPSCs controller of examinations from January 2024 to March 2026, has been suspended by the Karnataka government. He is alleged to have leaked the questions of the KPSC entrance exam for veterinary officers - held on January 8 and 9 this year - along with the answers to around 20 candidates who paid Rs 20 lakh to Rs 40 lakh through an arrested middleman, Basavaraj Kannale. During the investigation by the CID unit of the Karnataka police and the ED, Kannale, 36, allegedly revealed that Gangwar received around Rs 1.30 crore of Rs 1.52 crore taken from candidates as bribes for leaking the questions of the exams, said police sources. While the investigations have tracked Rs 52 lakh in bribes being funneled back to Gangwar through bank accounts of associates of the middleman, for purchase of expensive gold and diamond jewellery for a female friend of the officer from Bhima Jewellery showroom in Bengaluru, the remaining amount of bribes is still untraced, said the sources. The CID and the ED have indicated, following the arrest of Gangwar on August 29 and September 18, respectively, that some of the proceeds of the crime were used for the purchase of an apartment in the name of the brother of the officer at Godrej Royal Woods complex in the vicinity of the Bengaluru International Airport at Devanahalli. The IAS officers brother and family are unaware of the flat purchased in their name in Bengaluru. They never visited or used the property. It was used by the officer for parties and other activities since it provided privacy, said a police source familiar with the probe. The ED has indicated during court proceedings that the apartment at Devanahalli was bought with the proceeds of the KPSC recruitment racket. The funds were routed through Kannale and his associates for purchase of immovable property in the name of his brother, purchase of gold jewellery in the name of his friend, and payment of personal expenses, a special court for PMLA cases noted last week following an ED submission. Gangwar has reportedly told the ED that a part of the amount he received from Kannale for the KPSC veterinary officer job fraud was used to purchase a flat in the name of his brother, apart from the use of funds for buying gold jewellery for his female friend. The ED has also reported that an unexplained amount of Rs 26 lakh was deposited in cash between January 2025 and August 2025 in the bank accounts of a brother and sister-in-law of the IAS officer. The ED is also probing immovable assets acquired by the IAS officer - a semi-constructed house in Bareilly in 2025 for Rs 25 lakh and a real estate construction business launched by his older brothers in 2025 in UP.

articleTitle: India News Highlights, 7 October 2026: Maharashtra CM meets Amit Shah in Delhi to seek special assistance for drought

Several Opposition MPs, including Karti Chidambaram, Charanjit Singh Channi, Imran Pratapgarhi and Mukul Wasnik, attended. Police were heavily deployed outside Sagar Ratna, cordoning off the footpath around the restaurant. Additional barricades were also being brought in. After lunch, Opposition MPs started leaving Sagar Ratna and boarded two buses arranged by the INDIA bloc. The buses carrying the MPs then left Janpath for Jantar Mantar, where the bloc is scheduled to hold a protest. Speaking to the media outside the restaurant, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said the Opposition planned the protest after the Election Commissioners did not allow 300 MPs to meet them on Tuesday. Like I said yesterday, 300 MPs wanted to meet the ECs yesterday, but we were not allowed to meet them. So today, our plan is to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar. We want to tell the country that Gyanesh Kumar is not a legitimate CEC. These people are desh-drohi. Gyanesh Kumar has to resign, Gandhi said. There are 45 FIRs against me. But my aim is for 100 FIRs, he added. If you are just joining us, this is The Indian Express Realtime breaking news blog-where we bring you the latest news updates of the day in real time. Scan the top headlines of the day here, or keep scrolling to see the latest updates stream in. 5-floor Delhi building collapses, several feared trapped A five-storey building collapsed in Delhis northeast Seemapuri area on Wednesday afternoon. The incident took place at around 330 pm. Four fire tenders have been rushed to the spot, located behind a fish market. Several people are feared trapped under the debris. RJD leaders alleged that the CECs role in the Special Intensive Revision SIR process had benefited the BJP, while calling for his removal under the slogan Gyanesh Hatao, Loktantra Bachao Remove Gyanesh, Save Democracy. Im still a student PM Modi at event to mark 25 years of public life Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday marked 25 years since he first took oath as Gujarat Chief Minister on October 7, 2001, saying he never imagined he would reach this milestone and credited the people for his journey. Speaking at the culmination of the Seva Sankalp Yatra in Delhi, Modi said he still considers himself a student and seeks to keep learning. FIR against Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi over Akashvani Bhawan sit-in Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra have been booked for alleged trespassing after entering Akashvani Bhawan during Tuesdays INDIA bloc protest march against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The government made the declaration ahead of the October 31 deadline, citing the severity of the conditions and prevailing El Nino conditions.
