articleTitle: Ronaldo defers Portugal retirement, seeks apology and ‘punishment’ for walkout
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Cristiano Ronaldo was apologetic for abruptly leaving the Portugal but remained critical of coach Jorge Jesus's actions. (AP Photo)
description: Ronaldo accused Jesus of an "absolute breach of trust," first for benching him despite promising he would play, and then for reneging on an agreement to share a unified story with the media.
body_raw: On the night Lionel Messi played his final game for Argentina, Cristiano Ronaldo deferred his Portugal retirement after his recent walkout from the national side following a disagreement with coach Jorge Jesus. The 41-year-old Ronaldo left Portugals Nations League camp last week after being an unused substitute against Norway. He would also find out that he would not start against Denmark. Ronaldo had vowed in a social media post that he would reveal the full picture later, a time which arrived on Instagram on Tuesday night with six slides and an elaborate clarification running nearly 2,000 words. The Portuguese captain stated that he was seeking a punishment for leaving the national side abruptly, while stating that coach Jesus had broken his word twice. ALSO READ Jorge Jesus wont bend, and Cristiano Ronaldo cannot be bent Ronaldo accused Jesus of an absolute breach of trust, first for benching him against Norway despite promising he would play, and then for reneging on an agreement to share a unified story with the media. The Portuguese Football Federation must assess the consequences of my actions and punish me for them. I believe the punishment should not be reduced, Ronaldo said. I have already apologised, but I know that actions have consequences. On Sunday, Jesus claimed that there was no rift between him and Ronaldo, whom he had coached in his previous managerial stint at Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia. Jesus also affirmed that the five-time Ballon dOr winner is open to return to the team. Ronaldo said that he was open to continue representing the national side, given that he remained physically fit, playing with my team, and hopefully scoring goal. httpswww.instagram.compDeKiM9wAEqU?utmsourceigwebcopylinkstknNTc4MTIwNjQ2YQ After my suspension period ends, I will be available, as I always have been, to compete and win with our national team, he added. Part relenting, part critical While Ronaldo observed a relenting tone in parts, he remained critical of Jesus actions. Ronaldo revealed that under an agreement to manage his playing time, Jesus had said that he would be rested for the matches against Norway and Denmark. However, Ronaldo was told that he would be used for 30 minutes during the Norway game. Everyone knows the rest. I warmed up from half-time onwards, watched the minutes tick by and wasnt called on, Ronaldo said. The manager had broken his word to me. Ronaldo further claimed that in a later discussion with Jesus, it was agreed that the coach would reveal clarify the issues in a press conference. An eight-point was agreed upon, including statements that Ronaldo had never demanded playing time and respected Jesus decisions. The coach also made a mistake for asking someone of the stature of Pele or Maradona to warm up without bringing him on. Ronaldo said the points never reflecting in Jesus press conference, making it the second time that the coach had broken his word to me. Previously, Ronaldo had endorsed his former Al-Nassr manager as the right choice to take over the Portugal reins. Ronaldo also revealed he came close to retiring from international duty following Portugals round-of-16 exit at this summers World Cup. He had already drafted a farewell letter to the supporters, but Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proenca persuaded him to reconsider during the flight home from the United States. Ronaldo remained apologetic, but reiterated his stance on his sudden exit from the camp. I owe an apology to my national team teammates for having left the camp. I apologise to the Portuguese people once again, but a broken word has, for me, a defining impact, he wrote.

articleTitle: Sennheiser Momentum 5 review: Audiophile sound that now packs lighter
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sennheiser Momentum 5 Review: The Sennheiser Momentum 5 combines a more compact carrying case with the signature sound and comfort of the Momentum series. (Image: Nandagopal Rajan/The Indian Express)
description: The Sennheiser Momentum 5 offers great sound, strong noise cancellation and plenty of comfort, but comes at a premium price.
body_raw: On long-haul flights, I always carry a pair of over-ear noise-cancelling headphones. I prefer them to truly wireless in-ear models because they can be wired into the in-flight entertainment system and cause less ear fatigue over long hours. The one concern is the space their case takes up in cabin luggage, especially for someone who likes to travel light. I think the Sennheiser Momentum 5 addresses this to a large extent. For me, the Sennheiser Momentum is the pinnacle of audiophile headphones that also work very well for regular users, provided they can afford one. While the carrying case is now more compact, the headphones themselves retain their earlier size, though the design feels more ergonomic. The faux-leather earcups are comfortable over long hours and block out a fair amount of noise on their own, even before you switch on noise cancellation. Personally, I always thought the Alcantara on the first Momentum On-Ear, over a decade ago, was the best earcup material I have experienced on a headphone. I would have loved for Sennheiser to bring it back. The Momentum 5 is unabashedly wireless, but you can go wired with a 3.5mm cable, whether to your laptop or the in-flight entertainment system. For me, that is less about purism the wired-versus-wireless debate died down a few years back and more about practicality at 35,000 feet. The controls sit on the right earcup and help with power and noise cancellation, along with gesture controls for volume and track changes. The Sennheiser Smart Control app offers more customisation and personalisation. It lets you set custom presets, tweak bass and noise cancellation to exactly the level you want, and customise the gesture controls. There is also a find feature in case you cant remember where you left the headphones. However, none of this is different from the last time I tested a Sennheiser headphone. I was expecting something new, like personalised audio playback. httpswww.youtube.comwatch?sip9AnyWg-XsFQTU4SvF6-626dSyuEfeatureyoutu.be The moment you put the headphones on, you forget these minor niggles as the music envelops you. I was listening on a late Sunday flight into Mumbai, as the compact case had given me the confidence to stow them in my overnighter. Billie Eilishs Bad Guy is a good test for any headphone, especially a high-fidelity one like the Momentum 5, because of its bass play and distortion. The Sennheiser was in its element throughout, and I loved how the bass stayed powerful yet controlled. It booms but never overpowers the track, as some headphones are guilty of doing. With Money, I wanted to check out Pink Floyds legendary stereo imaging and instrument placement. The Momentum 5 created a soundstage that made me feel I was at a live performance, despite the cacophony of the open kitchen next to my living room. I pushed this further with Yosi Horikawas Bubbles, a masterclass in how audio can play on the mind through objects, spaces and elements within a composition. All I can say is that I have not heard it with this much clarity before, and the sense of space these headphones offer is unprecedented. The ultimate test had to be Hans Zimmers Why So Serious? I have had to take off headphones that could not handle the first minute of this dark composition. With the Momentum 5, the precision of the lows was remarkable, as was the layering of the different elements. The bass drop in the middle finally sounded like a maestro at his best, not an orchestra malfunctioning. At the other end of the spectrum, Nils Lofgrens live rendition of Keith Dont Go is where the highs are tested to their limits. The Momentum 5 handled the guitar harmonics and micro-details superbly. Many headphones wont even let you hear the latter. But all this comes at a cost, and I would not recommend the Momentum 5 for everyone. At Rs 39,990, this is a once-in-a-lifetime investment for music lovers. It is an investment worth making, though. Every time you listen to a song on these, there will be a moment that tells you what a wise purchase it was. That moment could come on the metro, in an economy seat 35,000 feet over the Atlantic, or in your living room. Cherish it.

articleTitle: Senior IPS officers must learn ChatGPT, wellness and more for pay hikes
articleFeaturedImageAlt: AI training
description: The Department of Personnel and Training directive is aimed at ensuring continuous, role-specific capacity building for officers of the All India Services, who will now have to complete prescribed courses on iGOT every year.
body_raw: Courses on emerging technologies, evidence-based policymaking, cybersecurity fundamentals, the art of storytelling, and ChatGPT and generative AI tools will now be compulsory for IPS officers, and their performance on the iGOT Karmayogi platform will be reflected in their annual performance appraisal reports APARs. In a communication recently sent to the Chief Secretaries of all States and Union Territories, the Union Ministry of Home Affairs MHA said the decision followed a Department of Personnel and Training DoPT directive aimed at ensuring continuous, role-specific capacity building for officers of the All India Services, who will now have to complete prescribed courses on iGOT every year. The iGOT Karmayogi platform is a digital learning and capacity-building portal designed for civil servants and government employees. As the cadre controlling authority for the IPS, the Ministry of Home Affairs has selected 24 courses for its officers-six for each of four categories based on years of service. Of the six courses in each bracket, the first three are mandatory, will be linked to the annual performance appraisal reports, and will form the basis of a comprehensive assessment that opens only after all mandatory courses are completed, for the financial year 2026-27. First bracket up to nine years of service In this category, comprising officers from the 2018 batch onwards, the mandatory courses are an introduction to emerging technologies, search and seizure procedures under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances NDPS Act, and cybersecurity fundamentals for leaders-offered by the Wadhwani Foundation, the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy and the National E-Governance Division of MeitY, respectively. The remaining three cover personal finance, feedback as a leadership tool, and handling of mobile devices at crime scenes Second bracket above nine and up to 16 years In this category, officers from the 2011 to 2017 batches will take an introduction to emerging technologies, an overview of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita as it replaces the CrPC, and a foundational module on the interoperable criminal justice system, along with courses on managing and leading teams, noting and drafting, and mastering feedback. Third bracket above 16 and up to 25 years In this category, officers from the 2001 to 2010 batches are introduced to emerging technologies, evidence-based policymaking, cybersecurity fundamentals, the art of storytelling, ChatGPT and generative AI tools for government officials, and change management in digital transformation projects. Seniormost category 25 years and above Under this category, officers from the 2000 batch and all prior batches will take courses that overlap substantially with the preceding group, with the addition of a module on integrative wellness from Rashtriya Raksha University.

articleTitle: ‘We rushed things’: Nani on why The Paradise, his Rs 150-cr film, got polarised reviews
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nani admits his team could've done a better job of The Paradise.
description: Nani heaped praises on The Paradise director Srikanth Odela, while admitting that he got "carried away" by the scale and expectations riding on the film.
body_raw: Srikanth Odelas period action film The Paradise scored the biggest opening of Nanis 18-year career, and also emerged as his first film to earn over Rs 100 crore at the domestic box office. However, the actor recently responded to the polarizing reviews and reactions to the film, admitting that if his team had more time during post-production, they couldve turned in a better product. Nani on The Paradises polarizing response Were in a place where were just thinking backwards, given the reactions. Were also aware of the timing. With the less post-production time, we rushed things a little bit. It was always there on the back of our mind whether well be able to achieve everything in time, confessed Nani to The Hollywood Reporter India. However, he didnt want to buy more time by pushing the film, since he had already done that twice. The Paradise was initially scheduled to release on March 26 earlier this year. It was then pushed to August 21, before finally seeing light of the day on September 25. In the process, it averted major clashes with Ranveer Singh-starrer blockbuster spy thriller Dhurandhar 2 The Revenge and Yashs action thriller Toxic A Fairytale for Grownups respectively. This was the third release date. The audience was so excited about the film that we didnt want to give up on them because of the postponement that happened so many times. So, we had an extremely tight deadline. More things would have made sense narratively with the edit and the score, if we had more time. We couldve smoothened it out, explained the actor. He acknowledged the little glitches that the audience are complaining about, like the fact that parts of The Paradise feel a little jumpy. We couldve made all of that better, but well never know I guess. We dont know if it wouldve worked better had we pushed the film, said Nani, adding,We all get carried away and do mistakes. But if we understand and learn from them, thats the best way we can go ahead. Nani lauds Srikanth Odela The Paradise also carried tall expectations given it marked the reunion of Nani and director Srikanth Odela after their 2023 action film Dasara, which amassed Rs 121 crore at the worldwide box office, on a budget of Rs 65 crore. On the other hand, the budget of The Paradise is somewhere between Rs 150 crore and Rs 200 crore, but its garnered only Rs 169.15 crore globally yet, within 13 days of its box office run. With The Paradise, Srikanth had great ideas. But when the span of the film went up, when the expectations went up, the focus shifted from storytelling to set pieces. So, the connectivity wasnt there. If he just sticks to his heart, and focuses on just telling the story, I still believe hes one of the best talents we have, said Nani. Further heaping praises on the director, Nani added, In these many years, if I have to really bet on someone, hed be on the top of the list. Hes a very, very original guy. He has a lot of ideas, but after stitching them together, his bigger vision somewhere got a little diluted. He admitted that since the expectations were sky high from him and Srikanth, the polarizing reactions hurt even more. The Paradise also stars Raghav Juyal as the chief antagonist, along with Sonali Kulkarni, Mohan Babu, and Easwari Rao among others. Set in a Secunderabad slum of the 1980s, it stars Nani plays a tribal leader called Sarakka. It opened at Rs 11.60 crore from 900 screens at the domestic box office, but has slipped down to even below Rs 1 crore - at Rs 93 lakh - by its second Tuesday day 13. Also Read - Sanjay Dutt says his cant feel peace in India remark a scripted conversation, Shekhar Suman comments The Paradise has earned Rs 138.10 crore gross and Rs 117.13 crore net at the domestic box office. Its major chunk comes from the native Telugu version, followed by the dubbed Hindi version, though Nani refused to label it as a pan-India release. Having collected Rs 31.05 crore internationally, its earned Rs 169.15 crore globally so far. Keeping all the reactions and numbers aside, we know we couldve done better, Nani reiterated.

articleTitle: Internet rallies for Jaya Bachchan amid Kangana Ranaut’s dig over ‘Nahi Bataungi’ moment
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jaya Bachchan
description: Jaya Bachchan went viral during an INDIA bloc protest in Delhi on October 6, 2026, after she pushed away a reporter’s microphone.
body_raw: Jaya Bachchan is once again in the headlines for her equation with the media. During the INDIA blocs protest over the functioning of the Election Commission, the Samajwadi Party MP and actor refused to comment on the issue that had prompted the opposition demonstration even as she was badgered by the reporter. Now, actor-politician Kangana Ranaut has taken a dig at her viral response. Sharing the video on her Instagram handle, Kangana wrote, When you sit on dharna so that you can make a point in front of the whole world but when they ask you what point you want to make? Jaya B ji. Nahi bataungi. What happened in the video? Jaya Bachchan went viral during an INDIA bloc protest in Delhi on October 6, 2026, after she pushed away a reporters microphone as he kept on asking her to respond even as she alleged that he was twisting the narrative. Members of the opposition INDIA bloc had marched towards the Election Commission of India in Delhi, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar after Indian Express investigation that revealed objections by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi to a declaration added to the online version of Form 6, the form used to enrol new voters. During the protest, a journalist questioned Jaya about a placard carried by fellow opposition members that appeared to refer to the Chief Election Commissioners office as the BJP office. Pointing to the placard being held by TMC MP Derek OBrien, the journalist asked, What is written on this? Jaya Bachchan repeatedly responded, Dont twist it. When the journalist said, I am not twisting anything, I am just asking what is written on it, Jaya sternly replied, Dont twist the matter. The reporter then asked, What is the matter? You please explain to me, prompting Jaya to simply push the microphone away. When the journalist questioned her again, Jaya said, Nahi bataungi. The reporter then asked, On what basis are you then saying that I have twisted the matter? Jaya responded, Whatever you asked Derek was twisted. She then walked away, choosing not to engage in the conversation any further. Derek, who was present throughout the exchange, also turned away. Jaya then laughed and said, I dont believe this. ALSO READ Soundarya Rajinikanth says parents changing male-dominated dynamic at home My rocks during divorce Social media users hail Jaya Bachchan for her response The video quickly went viral, prompting a wave of reactions on social media. While Jaya has often faced criticism online over her interactions with the media, several users appeared to enjoy her blunt response this time around. Many users called her a Queen and Diva for her response. One user wrote, For once, we love you Jaya Ji, while another commented, Jaya is always iconic. Only celeb politician I like. Several others turned the exchange into memes, with one user suggesting, Say Nahi bataungi and move on. Another wrote, Waiting for new memes. Jaya had made headlines just days earlier when she was seen laughing out loud at a book launch event attended by her husband, Amitabh Bachchan, and writer Gulzar. In several videos from the event, Jaya was seen sharing a light-hearted moment with Gulzar, prompting social media users to say Yeh hasti bhi hai?.

articleTitle: Nothing left in democracy if institutions are undermined: Former judge Sanjib Banerjee
articleFeaturedImageAlt: sanjib banerjee supreme court election commission of india form 6 gyanesh kumar democracy SIR
description: Former Chief Justice of Meghalaya and Madras high courts, Sanjib Banerjee says the Supreme Court does not go by public perception or any wave, but by what is constitutionally correct and it will apply the same in the case of Form 6.
body_raw: At the heart of the controversy over the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls is a simple question-who must prove that a person has the right to vote in a democracy like India? In an exclusive discussion with The Indian Express, former Meghalaya High Court Chief Justice Sanjib Banerjee says the Election Commission has fundamentally got it wrong by placing the burden on voters. Underlining that this requires a course correction, he says the poll panel must instead follow Articles 325 and 326 of the Constitution, where every citizen who has attained the age of 18 is entitled to vote unless disqualified. While hearing petitions against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and examining the functioning of the poll panel, the Supreme Court recently clarified that it had not approved changes to Form 6, which new voters are required to fill. Banerjee, who has also served as the Chief Justice of the Madras High Court, argues that the dispute over Form 6 is part of a wider concern about constitutional safeguards and public trust in electoral institutions. He adds that while the apex court had affirmed the SIR process, it had not examined or approved the specific forms or other modalities of the exercise. Edited excerpts What is the significance of the Supreme Courts statement? Sanjib Banerjee My information is based on news reports, both in the print and digital media, and I havent actually seen the order of the Supreme Court. But from what Im given to understand, the Supreme Court wanted clarity on whether the critical decisions were taken by the Election Commission unanimously or whether they were taken only by the Chief Election Commissioner. The Supreme Court, apparently, also indicated that the majority rule had to prevail as far as the Election Commission was concerned, and said that it would not stop overturning decisions that may not have been taken by the majority. Finally, the Supreme Court said that it had not expressly approved or upheld the changes made to Form 6. A press release had been issued by the Election Commission prior to the hearing, probably a few days ago, to the effect that the Supreme Court had upheld the changes made to Form 6. Probably what was misleading about the press release was that the Supreme Court affirmed the process of SIR, but did not go into the nitty-gritty of the forms or the other things, and that was sought to be kind of presented as the Supreme Court having upheld or approved the entire modality of the exercise. From what I have been given to understand from press reports, particularly the report published in The Indian Express, is that the two other election commissioners pointed out to the Chief Election Commissioner that it was within the governments domain to prepare the form, and the Election Commission could not suo motu alter its contents. And that primarily appears to be the bone of contention. The modified Form 6 is a cause for real heartburn and is at the heart of what we are calling disenfranchisement of a large number of the citizens of this country, because if youre a citizen, youre entitled to vote. The most important thing which has happened, and which requires course correction, is the Election Commissioner or the Election Commission, quite wrongly and illegally putting the burden on the citizen to prove that he has a right to vote, rather than following Articles 325 and 326 of the Constitution, where every citizen whos attained the age of 18 is entitled to vote unless disqualified by the Constitution or by any law brought by the appropriate legislature. The Supreme Court stressed on Article 324 and Section 21 3 of the Representation of the People Act to uphold the SIR exercise. Can that be invoked for any changes in Form 6, or can only the government do it? Sanjib Banerjee Every judgment has a ratio decidendi reasoning, which is the exact issue or the point of law which is decided in that case. And the long and short of the Supreme Court judgment on the SIR was that the Election Commission had due authority to conduct such an SIR so that the integrity of the voting system could be maintained. Nowhere in that judgment is the procedure actually adopted, the questions which have been put up, the various forms nowhere in that judgment is there any discussion regarding this or any approval of the forms or the modalities. It was only on the process, and that process the Election Commission has due authority to do. Theres no doubt that the Election Commission has the authority to do it. But if it is in the governments domain to indicate what the contents of any form would be, then, as the two other election commissioners have reportedly pointed out to the Chief Election Commissioner, the Chief Election Commissioner should probably have waited for the government to make that change and not gone by a unilateral kind of exercise of his position to bring about that change in the form. This is particularly harsh. What happens now? Sanjib Banerjee There are many other aspects which have to be taken into consideration. You cant expect a verdict coming out on day one when the petition is lodged or taken up for the first time. We are not talking about any other office. Its an institution which is a watchdog, and we are talking of the head of that institution. Before the Supreme Court takes any step, it has to be absolutely sure it has to go through the records, and that is exactly what the Supreme Court is doing. Now, we cannot analyse every days hearing and say that this is what ought to be done, this is what should have been done. The court functions on the basis of records and after giving reasonable opportunity to all concerned to be heard. That process takes time. Its not a quick-fix solution. Its not AI coming in, and you press a button, and you get the answer. This will take time, and the Supreme Court has taken up the matter. Im sure that all aspects will now be looked into. There are certain other features, such as the split verdict, which has been referred to, or has been required to be referred to a Constitution bench. There are certain disturbing features pertaining to that, but I am confident that at the end of the day, the Supreme Court will deliver as it has in the past and uphold what is right. The Supreme Court does not go by public view or public perception or by any wave. It goes by what is constitutionally and legally correct, and that is the approach that should always be there. If those other little things, niggles were not there, it would have been better. But when question marks are raised regarding people in high places, you cannot always be sure because sometimes its motivated, and at other times they may even be genuine. We dont have those levels of kind of morality or high conduct that ought to be expected of people in such places. The less controversy about that office, which is the watchdog, its the basic thing for a democracy the right of the people to choose their own government. On Bengal elections. Sanjib Banerjee If theres anything like what is being said about the West Bengal election, that the number of people who were left out may have changed the course of elections. I know in my home constituency of Bhabanipur, where the margin was only 15,000, there were about 40,000 or 44,000 voters left out. Some may genuinely have been non-existent voters, or dead persons, or other people, but the number of people was so large that it could have made a difference if all had participated. More disturbingly, in that constituency, more than 40 per cent of the voters excluded belong to the Muslim community, though the overall percentage of the Muslim community in that constituency is 24 per cent. These do raise some pertinent questions. They raise some other things that are not good optics. For instance, some Electronic Voting Machines EVMs were burnt when a government building in Kolkata caught fire in June, and there was a fire on the fourth and fifth floors. The other floors escaped. There was a fire on the ninth and tenth floors, and between 2,500 and 4,000 EVM machines were burnt. That evidence is lost. The chief electoral officer was catapulted to the states chief secretary, and one of the election observers became a special advisor to the chief minister. These are not good for democracy. People should eschew such steps that erode confidence in the system. We are all a sum of the systems and the institutions that are there to govern us. They are there to care for us. They are there to uphold the laws and the Constitution, and these do not augur well for the future. Im not imputing any motives to anybody if these were not there, it would have been much better. We have taken great pride despite being a new republic. Despite all the problems that we have had-the poverty that we inherited at Independence-we were not a banana republic. We have never had a coup we have never had this kind of rigging on a mass scale. Accidental omissions are there, but the system is being kind of taken over this feeling of the possibility. Im not saying it happened. It may not have happened. God willing, it never happens. But if some people get this feeling, that by itself is not good for a democracy. Most importantly, when we talk of our institutions, we must be respectful. We must use temperate language and not let emotions or anger or anything get the better of us. At the end of the day, if these institutions are undermined, there is nothing left in democracy.

articleTitle: ‘Your computer is hacked’: India-based scam targeting US seniors via Bitcoin ATMs
articleFeaturedImageAlt: bitcoin
description: The CBI said a syndicate operating from Punjab and Delhi posed as tech-support staff and sent US seniors to Bitcoin ATMs, routing crores through crypto wallets into India.
body_raw: In 2022, several senior citizens in the US began receiving calls and emails from men claiming to be Microsoft employees. Their computers had been hacked, the callers warned, and their bank accounts compromised. The callers then directed the seniors to Bitcoin ATMs - a physical kiosk that lets you buy or sell cryptocurrency using cash or a debit card, connecting directly to your digital wallet - where they were coerced into depositing cash to buy software that would supposedly fix their computers. Fearing that their money and personal information were at risk, the victims followed the instructions. They realised only later that they had been scammed. Some of them complained last year to authorities in the US, and the Central Bureau of Investigation CBI was alerted. On July 27 this year, the CBI lodged an FIR under sections of criminal conspiracy and Section 66D of the IT Act, 2000, which punishes cheating by personation using a computer resource. In August, three scammers, including alleged mastermind Saurabh Rana, were arrested by the central agency. Investigators said the accused were part of a syndicate operating from Punjab and Delhi that allegedly targeted American nationals through an organised tech-support scam by impersonating representatives of technology companies, financial institutions and law-enforcement agencies. How scam money reached India According to the CBI, the extorted money was converted into cryptocurrency and moved through a chain of crypto wallets before being consolidated into accounts controlled by the accused. The proceeds were then routed into the Indian banking system. The victims were allegedly defrauded of hundreds of crores of rupees, it said. During Ranas bail hearing last month, the agency told the court that the cryptocurrency trail provided a direct link between at least one victim and Ranas account. The CBI, in its submissions before the court, mentioned the name of a victim, Joanne Maalouf. The agency said the cryptocurrency exchange account operated by Rana received proceeds directly from the wallet associated with Maaloufs kiosk deposits on December 13, 2022, thereby establishing a direct nexus between the accused and the proceeds of the fraud. Investigators said Rana operated a Binance account linked to his Aadhaar card. The account allegedly received the largest share of the fraud proceeds - 203.30 Bitcoins, then valued at approximately 6.53 million, or over Rs 50 crore. The CBI also alleged that the fraud was operationally controlled from Delhi. It said Rana had accessed his cryptocurrency exchange account from Delhi-geolocated IP addresses on multiple dates during the period the fraud was active. Investigators also recovered incriminating WhatsApp chats between Rana and the co-accused, which, they said, pointed to his role as the main conspirator and mastermind of the fraud. Bail denied Arguing for bail before Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate ACJM Jyoti Maheshwari of the Rouse Avenue Courts Complex, Ranas counsel pointed to the delay, saying the offence dates back to 2022 while the case was registered after a four-year gap. The counsel also argued that the prosecution had failed to establish the necessity of his arrest. In an affidavit filed before the court, Ranas brother, Rishav, made allegations of torture and harassment during the investigation. He alleged that an employee, Ms S, was called to the CBI office in Chandigarh on August 22 and 23 for interrogation, where she was categorically subjected to torture and harassment by the investigating officer. The affidavit further claimed that the Investigation Officer IO had told Ms S that the court had already convicted Rana and would deny him bail, and that the court had conveyed this to the IO. Rejecting the bail plea, the ACJM held . it is apparent that the applicantaccused spearheaded the operations of the alleged cyber-fraud syndicate. Recovery of multiple digital devices from the premises connected with the applicantaccused is also indicative of his complicity in the alleged offence. . Moreover, this Court cannot turn a blind eye to the submissions on behalf of the investigating agency that various incriminating chats have been recovered from the mobile phones used by the applicant, which also reveal the modus operandi of the alleged offence, the court said. It said the offence has transnational ramifications and involves the cheating of several senior citizens of USA. .. This Court cannot turn a blind eye to the seriousness of the present offence and the alarming rise in cases of such nature, which have time and again warranted for a cautious approach, by the Honble Apex Court. Such an offence taints not just the people complicit in the crime, but also the entire country, she added in her order dated September 22. The CBI was represented in court by Public Prosecutors Saloni and Anoop Kumar. Recoveries made During simultaneous searches conducted in Delhi, Ludhiana and Mohali, Rana and co-accused Jappandeep Singh were arrested from Ludhiana, while a third man, Indermohan Singh, was arrested from Mohali. Officials said Ranas father owned the flat in Mohali from where the scam was being run. Other persons allegedly involved in the syndicate are yet to be apprehended, and the full conspiracy is still being unravelled, officials said. About 30 digital devices, including mobile phones and laptops, were seized from the Mohali premises. Digital evidence - mobile data and crypto wallets among them - form crucial evidence in the case, as per the CBI. This is still being examined.

articleTitle: University of Colorado Denver to establish India campus in Hyderabad, first cohort in August 2027
articleFeaturedImageAlt: University of Colorado Denver Telangana Campus
description: The proposed campus in Hyderabad will be CU Denver’s first degree-granting location in India. It will also be the first foreign university campus in Telangana, according to the university.
body_raw: The University of Colorado Denver CU Denver has received a letter of intent from the University Grants Commission UGC to establish a degree-granting campus in Hyderabad. The campus is expected to begin admissions for its first cohort of students in August 2027. The Hyderabad campus will offer programmes in high-demand areas including business, computing, engineering and analytics. Additional programmes are expected to be proposed to the UGC from the second year onwards. The academic model will combine subject-based learning with practical and experiential learning. Students will be expected to develop both knowledge of their chosen discipline and skills that can be applied in workplace settings. The campus will also focus on interdisciplinary learning, allowing students to work across different subject areas and apply problem-solving approaches to real-world situations. Read UWA Chennai campus gets final UGC approval, classes to begin by October-end The proposed programmes are intended to have a strong career focus, with curriculum and learning approaches linked to workforce requirements. Students will also remain connected to CU Denvers academic ecosystem in the US. The university said its Hyderabad campus will focus on areas such as consumer and business understanding, technology, applied learning and career preparation, depending on the programme. The emphasis will be on preparing students for changing workplace requirements rather than only academic study. CU Denver was established in 1973 and is governed by the University of Colorado Board of Regents. It has around 14,000 students and more than 100,000 alumni across over 100 countries. The university is classified as an R1 research institution by the Carnegie Commission on Higher Education, a classification for institutions with very high research activity, a statement notes. The proposed campus in Hyderabad will be CU Denvers first degree-granting outlet in India. It will also be the first foreign university campus in Telangana, according to the university. Also Read University of London, Northeastern University to establish offshore campuses in Hyderabad Telangana CM The campus is being planned in line with several priorities of the National Education Policy NEP 2020, including multidisciplinary education, internationalisation, learner outcomes and career readiness. The establishment of the campus is being undertaken with Emeritus as the universitys strategic joint venture partner in India. Emeritus will support the university in non-academic functions related to establishing and expanding the campus. CU Denver will now continue the regulatory process and work with academic and industry stakeholders as it develops the Hyderabad campus. The university plans to admit its first students in August 2027, with further programmes to be proposed for approval in subsequent years.

articleTitle: Pune records hottest October day since 2002
articleFeaturedImageAlt: According to the forecast of the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the maximum temperature is expected to stay around 35 degrees Celsius in Shivajinagar, Pashan and NDA till October 12. (Express File Photo)
description: The maximum temperature is above normal across Maharashtra
body_raw: Shivajinagar recorded a maximum temperature of 35.7 degrees Celsius on Tuesday, 4.4 degrees above normal, and the highest temperature to be recorded in October since 2002. Pune and its suburbs sweltered throughout the day with Lohegaon recording 5.3 degrees above normal during the day, at 36.6 degrees Celsius. In Wadgaonsheri, Chinchwad, NDA and Hadapsar, the maximum temperature was above 35 degrees Celsius. Pashan and Magarpatta recorded their maximum temperature at more than 34 degrees Celsius on Tuesday. The maximum temperature has been rising over several days. In Shivajinagar, the daytime temperature was 34.8 degrees Celsius on October 3, when the southwest monsoon withdrew from Pune. According to the forecast of the India Meteorological Department IMD, the maximum temperature is expected to stay around 35 degrees Celsius in Shivajinagar, Pashan and NDA till October 12. In Lohegaon, Chinchwad, Magarpatta, the temperature is expected to touch 36 degrees Celsius. According to IMD, no rain is expected and the skies are expected to remain clear, possibly turning cloudy, for the next few days. This is a part of the seasonal transition and it is due to an anticyclonic circulation, ie, the development of a high pressure area, which is pushing temperatures higher than normal, an expert from the organisation Vagaries of the Weather said. The maximum temperature is above normal across Maharashtra. In Amravati, the hottest place in the state, the mercury touched 39.6 degrees Celsius on Wednesday, which was 7 degrees above normal. On Wednesday, the minimum temperature was 21.8 degrees Celsius in Shivajinagar, which is 1.2 notches above normal. Lohegaon recorded 22.2 degrees Celsius. These temperature readings have been rising, but marginally, over the past few days. IMD expects the minimum temperature to continue rising till it reaches 23 degrees Celsius in Shivajinagar, Pashan, Lohegaon and Koregaon Park and upto 25 degrees Celsius in Magarpatta and Chinchwad.

articleTitle: Custodial death compensation, Rs 80,000 for students in Mumbai – Fadnavis Cabinet’s key decisions
articleFeaturedImageAlt: devendra fadnavis cabinet decisions
description: Students studying in Mumbai city, Mumbai suburban, Navi Mumbai, Thane, Pune, Pimpri-Chinchwad and Nagpur will now receive Rs 80,000 a year
body_raw: The Maharashtra Cabinet has approved a series of measures covering student welfare, police custody deaths, traditional occupations and higher education, including higher annual assistance for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe students, a compensation policy for deaths in police custody and an increase in the royalty-free minor mineral extraction limit for the Wadar community from 200 to 500 brass a year. Under the Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Swadhar Scheme, annual assistance for SC and Nav-Buddhist students who are eligible for government hostels but do not get admission has been increased. Students studying in Mumbai city, Mumbai suburban, Navi Mumbai, Thane, Pune, Pimpri-Chinchwad and Nagpur will now receive Rs 80,000 a year - Rs 42,000 as food allowance, Rs 28,000 for accommodation and Rs 10,000 as subsistence allowance. The annual assistance will be Rs 68,000 for students studying in other divisional headquarters and C-class municipal corporation areas. Students studying at other district headquarters, and in institutions within five kilometres of municipal corporation limits, will receive Rs 57,000 a year - Rs 32,000 for food, Rs 17,000 for accommodation and Rs 8,000 as subsistence allowance. Those studying attaluka headquarters have been fixed at Rs 50,000. Students pursuing medical and engineering courses will additionally get Rs 8,000 a year, while those pursuing other courses will receive Rs 4,000. Rs 5 lakh compensation for custodial deaths The Cabinet approved a policy to provide compensation to the next of kin in cases where a person dies in police custody and it is established that the death was caused by assault, torture or coercion by police personnel. The compensation in such cases will be Rs 5 lakh. The policy also provides Rs 2 lakh for permanent disability of less than 50 per cent caused by physical or mental torture in custody, and Rs 4 lakh where the disability is 50 per cent or more. Higher assistance under Swayam scheme For ST students who do not get admission to government hostels, the Cabinet approved revised assistance under the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Swayam Scheme. Students studying in Mumbai city, Mumbai suburban, Navi Mumbai, Thane, Pune, Pimpri-Chinchwad and Nagpur will now receive Rs 80,000 a year, up from Rs 60,000. At other divisional headquarters and C-class municipal corporation areas, the assistance has been raised to Rs 68,000 from Rs 51,000. For students at other district headquarters, it will be Rs 57,000. At other locations, students will receive Rs 50,000. Medical and engineering students will get an additional Rs 8,000 a year for educational material, while students in other disciplines will receive Rs 4,000.

articleTitle: ‘Give a woman that respect’: Soundarya Rajinikanth slams Katrina Kaif’s body-shamers
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Katrina Kaif
description: Soundarya Rajinikanth cited her own example while standing up for Katrina Kaif, who faced trolling for her postpartum appearance.
body_raw: When Katrina Kaif stepped out to attend the Ambani familys Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations in September, she faced intense online trolling and body-shaming over her post-pregnancy appearance. The backlash prompted several celebrities to speak out against the trolls. Now, Soundarya Rajinikanth has also addressed the issue, calling the criticism not fair and not kind. Speaking to Nayandeep Rakshit on his YouTube channel, Soundarya, who is a mother of two, said, I have two children and it is not easy. When you have to go through that process, your body changes and having a child post a particular age is even more difficult. I had my second child when I was past my 35. Not easy. You have to give that woman that respect. Because what a woman can do physically, you cant blame men because they cant. It is not biology. She added, But you need to accept and acknowledge that a woman does. We are not asking the guy, Why dont you get pregnant? But when we do go through that, my heart went out when that whole thing happened. It was not fair. It was not kind. Women go through a lot but it is special to be a woman. Previously, several celebrities, including Salman Khan, Parineeti Chopra and Khushbu Sundar, had openly supported Katrina amid the criticism. ALSO READ Virat Kohli refutes claim he visited Pemanand Ji Maharaj for Rs 5 cr Out of deep faith During an episode of Bigg Boss 20, Salman slammed social media trolls and paparazzi for commenting on Katrinas appearance, pointing out that weight gain after pregnancy is normal. I dont think the one they are trolling would mind. This shows their upbringing. You are writing bad things about those who are helping you earn. You comment on their body, weight, looks, family, and on someones smile as well as flaws. You troll someone for becoming a mother. Bhaddi lag rahi hai, moti ho gayi hai, budha ho gaya hai, all of this is going on. The troll is earning money through all this and they are enjoying it. Most of them dont even show their real faces or identities. Are they embarrassed about themselves? he said. Similarly, Parineeti Chopra called out the trolls for their comments about postpartum women. Speaking to Zoom, the actor, who is also a new mother, said, Who the hell are you to tell a postpartum woman, Abhi tumko 6 mahina ho gaya baby, abhi tum wapas aa jao Now it has been six months, now you get back to normal? She added, Please live your life and just ignore these uneducated people. How can you say something negative about something as stupid as weight? Oh lord Clearly, they dont have lives, education, or basic human decency. I dont have time for all this, and no woman should waste a single breath of hers to even listen to them. Katrina Kaif and Vicky Kaushal welcomed their first child, a baby boy, in November last year. They named him Vihaan.

articleTitle: Indian student Pratyush Prabhakar elected VP of Academic Affairs at Harvard Kennedy School
articleFeaturedImageAlt: pratyush prabhakar harvard kennedy school
description: Before joining Harvard, Prabhakar also worked with India's Ministry of Education, apart from the Ministry of Railways. His work with the ministries covered government and public-sector issues.
body_raw: A public policy professional, Pratyush Prabhakar, who previously worked as a policy and communications adviser to the Minister of Railways, with the Union Government has been elected Vice-President, Academic Affairs of the student government at the Harvard Kennedy School HKS. Students from more than 96 countries, studying across multiple programmes at the school, took part in the election. As Vice-President, Academic Affairs, Prabhakar will co-chair the HKS Academic Affairs Committee with the Dean. The role involves representing students on academic matters, including curriculum, advising and other issues related to their academic experience at the school. The committee provides a forum for student concerns to be raised with the schools leadership. Prabhakar is pursuing a Masters in Public Administration at HKS as an Edward S Mason Fellow. The Mason Fellowship is aimed at public-sector professionals and leaders from developing countries. His current programme focuses on public administration and policy, and follows his earlier work in the Indian government. Also Read Harvard Executive Education programmes to launch in Hyderabad from December Before joining Harvard, Prabhakar also worked with Indias Ministry of Education, in addition to the Ministry of Railways. His work with the ministries covered government and public-sector issues. He has also founded two organisations, Communeeti and thriWe, alongside his government work. During the campaign, Prabhakar cited Mahatma Gandhi as an inspiration. The results were announced on October 2, which is observed as Gandhi Jayanti in India, and Prabhakar referred to the date in a message following the announcement. Also Read Chinese universities surge in global rankings as US schools slip The election brings Prabhakar into a student representative role that will involve working with the schools academic leadership. The Academic Affairs Committee deals with issues concerning students academic experience, giving student representatives a role in raising concerns and contributing to discussions on curriculum and advising. For Prabhakar, the position combines his studies at HKS with the public-sector experience he brought to the school. It also gives him a platform to bring the perspectives of a diverse student body, drawn from more than 96 countries, into those conversations. Harvard Kennedy School is Harvard Universitys graduate school focused on public policy and government. It offers graduate programmes in areas including public policy, public administration, international development and political governance. The school is named after former US president and Harvard alumnus himself, John F Kennedy.

articleTitle: Gautam Gambhir lauds Ajit Agarkar: ‘3 ICC trophies…testimony of your conviction’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Agarkar
description: During Agarkar's tenure, India reached the final of the ODI World Cup before winning the 2024 T20 World Cup and the 2025 Champions Trophy. India also retained the T20 World Cup earlier this year
body_raw: Ajit Agarkars tenure as chief selector at the Board of Control for Cricket in India BCCI has been quite a mixed one. He won silverware but also drew heavy criticism for the tough calls he made. Taking the reins in July 2023, Agarkars tenure officially ended on Tuesday, with the BCCI calling for applications. Head coach Gautam Gambhir lauded Agarkar and praised his conviction. Dear Ajit Bhai, an absolute honour to work with you. Those 3 ICC trophies are a testimony of your conviction Team first Team ahead, always. I must say, History will be kinder to you. Thank you for everything. My heartfelt wishes for your future endeavours , Gambhir wrote on X formerly Twitter. It was not just Gambhir earlier former Indian cricketer R Ashwin, on his YouTube channel, was empathetic to Agarkars situation as the selector. The fact is that Ajit Agarkar had the responsibility to take a lot of big decisions in this stint he had to phase out the senior players, and it cannot be easy. I was one of the senior players phased out during his tenure, but still by keeping some distance from that, I want to say that he has been a very good chairman of selectors. If we look at what all he has done with the team, Ashwin said on his YouTube channel. During Agarkars tenure, India reached the final of the ODI World Cup before winning the 2024 T20 World Cup and the 2025 Champions Trophy. India also retained the T20 World Cup earlier this year. Agarkar didnt ask for an extension. As there was no interest from his side, the BCCI has decided to look for a new chief selector, a source told The Indian Express at the time. This paper had reported in August that BCCI officials would meet Agarkar to discuss a one-year extension to his term after India tours Sri Lanka amid differences over Rohit Sharmas ODI future in the lead-up to the 2027 ODI World Cup.

articleTitle: In own state, ‘upset’ Fadnavis cites ‘pathetic’ school, hostel infra for protests
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis
description: Directing questions at the officials, Fadnavis made his displeasure known at the meeting and said, "If schools and hostels are in such poor condition, agitation will happen."
body_raw: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has expressed displeasure over the pathetic infrastructure of schools and hostels, pointing to it as the reason for protests across the state. Visibly angry during the meeting, Fadnavis directed the concerned department to take immediate steps and make necessary changes to improve infrastructure. If the schoolhostel condition is so pathetic, why will there be no agitation? How can the department overlook the basic amenities, Fadnavis, it is learnt, asked at the infrastructure review meeting held this week. Directing questions at the officials, Fadnavis made his displeasure known at the meeting and said, If schools and hostels are in such poor condition, agitation will happen. Following the chief ministers remarks on pathetic infrastructure, the ministries of social justice, tribal department and OBC department decided to work out a plan to make necessary corrections. The three ministries have decided to conduct an audit and address the problems. Generally, a sub-committee for infrastructure would focus on mega projects. However, this weeks review meeting saw the government focusing on school and hostel infrastructure. The governments decision to review school hostel infrastructure also comes in the wake of the Cockroach Janta Partys CJP protest in Maharashtra against poor school and hostel conditions in several districts of the state. Sources said, The social justice, school and tribal department was trying to push positive images during the meetings. But the skill department, during the presentation, showed images of dilapidated hostel structures and inadequate facilities. We cannot continue like this. Things will have to change, sources quoted Fadnavis as saying during the meeting. He directed the Departments to allocate funds for infrastructure upgradation from the District Planning Development Committee DPDC immediately. Earlier, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had launched a school thik karo agitation in Maharashtra. He visited several government-aided schools in the Marathwada region.
