articleTitle: Rahul Gandhi stood guard, Priyanka lay on the road — then the police moved in
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rahul stood guard, Priyanka lay on the road — then the police moved in
description: The Opposition is learnt to be planning another protest on Thursday, keeping the details under wraps so that it can catch the police off guard.
body_raw: The dramatic events on Wednesday started off rather innocuously with a lunch for Opposition INDIA bloc leaders hosted by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge at the Sagar Ratna restaurant in Janpath in central Delhi. While the police outside the restaurant prepared to stall any movement of the MPs, the mood inside was full of optimism. The leaders of the INDIA bloc spoke of how they were moving ahead in the right direction and that the government was on the back foot. Most of the leaders belonging to South Indian states ordered dishes associated with North Indian states, while those from the North and other parts of the country ordered what is broadly clubbed as South Indian cuisine, sources said. The variety on the plates ranged from idli and dosa to uttapam and North Indian and South Indian thalis. Twelve leaders sat on the main table, including the Gandhi siblings, Kharge, K C Venugopal, RJDs Manoj Jha, IUMLs E T Mohammed Basheer, CPIs P Sandosh Kumar, CPIMs John Brittas, and representatives of other parties. Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi shared with others the food he had ordered, said those present at the lunch. Following the lunch, the MPs exited the restaurant and announced to the media contingent that had gathered outside that they would make their way to Jantar Mantar in three deluxe buses parked outside to keep up the pressure on the government for the second straight day, demanding that they be allowed to meet Chief Election Commissioner CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the Election Commissioners. The Opposition, it seemed, was prepared for the long haul, stacking the buses with energy drinks, snacks, and plenty of water. As the buses left Janpath and slowly inched towards Jantar Mantar, less than a kilometre away, the word had gone around among Congress workers that the top leadership was heading towards a flash protest. Hundreds of Congress workers joined them, walking alongside the buses and raising slogans. Soon afterwards, several Congress MPs, including Imran Masood, Deepender Hooda, Imran Pratapgarhi, and Amrinder Singh Raja Warring of the Congress, climbed atop their bus and waved a Tricolour, giving the protest march the colour of a celebratory roadshow. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were dragged away by Delhi Police-for a second time in as many days-after opposition MPs kick-started Day 2 of protests demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar quit over irregularities in the SIR process. Read - The Indian Express IndianExpress October 7, 2026 Once the destination was just metres away, the mood changed and became more confrontational as the police stopped the buses from entering the road to Jantar Mantar. The police had already barricaded it and a face-off appeared on the cards. Then came the tipping point, as the situation hurtled towards a skirmish. Near the Windsor Place roundabout, Congress workers, including those from the partys student and youth wings, were pushed back as the police tried to stop them from progressing. As several Congress workers sustained minor injuries in the ensuing melee, those in the buses decided to get down. How could we stay inside when our workers were being bashed up? asked an MP. This, sources said, marked a change of plan. We thought we would sit in the bus till night, said an Opposition leader. Sit-in and punctured tyres The parliamentarians led by Rahul Gandhi got off their buses and attempted to begin an impromptu sit-in. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra lay on the road, shielded by other MPs and party workers, while her brother stood guard, pushing back the police personnel attempting to break up the protest. This is my sister, the LoP shouted at the police. He became a shield, said a Congress MP. But as it unfolded on Tuesday, both the LoP, Priyanka Gandhi, and other Opposition leaders were eventually pushed into police buses amid allegations that the police used force on them. Trinamool MP Mahua Moitra sustained injuries to her face and hands, and was seen showing her counterparts that she had been left bloodied. As the police bus carrying Rahul Gandhi made its way to the Barakhamba police station, some Congress workers punctured one of its tyres, bringing it to a screeching halt. As the police waited for backup, the LoP sent out a video message saying the fight would continue till Gyanesh Kumar resigns. This is a fight to protect the most sacred thing in this country, he said. We are not going to stop protesting till Gyanesh Kumar resigns. This is a fight to protect the most sacred thing in this country. There is nothing that Narendra Modi and Amit Shah can do that will stop us. - Rahul Gandhi RahulGandhi October 7, 2026 Priyanka and other MPs and Opposition leaders were taken to far-off Chhatrasal Stadium in Model Town. Eventually, all were released after hours of dramatic scenes. The INDIA bloc is learnt to be planning another protest on Thursday and has kept the details under wraps, sharing them with only a few select leaders, to catch the police off guard. More MPs, more parties will come on Thursday, claimed a senior MP.

articleTitle: Second day, second Opposition protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, detentions again
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Second day, second Opposition protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, detentions again
description: Samajwadi Party absent at Kharge lunch for INDIA bloc leaders; Cong for more protests today
body_raw: Pressing for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Opposition leaders staged a protest for the second consecutive day in the heart of the Capital Wednesday before they were stopped and detained by police. The Samajwadi Party, however, stayed away from the INDIA bloc protest. On Tuesday, after the Opposition protest, Congress allies had expressed concern that it had been turned into a Rahul Gandhi show. The SP skipped the lunch hosted Wednesday by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge at the Sagar Ratna restaurant on Janpath. From the restaurant, Opposition MPs, including Gandhi, Mamata TMCs Derek OBrien, CPIMs John Brittas and CPIs P Sandosh Kumar, boarded three buses to head towards Jantar Mantar. Over the next couple of hours, as the buses crawled forward, Congress workers walked alongside. Police, however, blocked the way and the march came to a halt near Windsor Place. Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra lay on the road, clutching a copy of the Constitution, along with other women leaders. Later, police forcibly removed Congress workers and detained the Gandhi siblings and other senior leaders. Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan was among those who had joined the protest. We are not going to stop protesting till Gyanesh Kumar resigns. This is a fight to protect the most sacred thing in this country. There is nothing that Narendra Modi and Amit Shah can do that will stop us, Gandhi said. He thanked all INDIA bloc MPs standing firm in defence of our democracy-in Parliament, outside on the streets, and today near Jantar Mantar. The Congress called for more protests at state, district and block levels on Thursday. The party also played down the absence of SP MPs from Wednesdays lunch meeting, saying they had left Delhi the night before or early Wednesday. The SPs absence, it is learnt, also came up during the discussions over lunch. Later in the day, INDIA bloc leaders reached out to the SP, which agreed to send its representatives for the protest Thursday, sources said. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh, in a post on X, said all alliance parties were invited to the lunch. But the decision for lunch had been taken late last night and communicated. It was therefore natural that some parties could not be represented. There is needless comment in some sections of the media on it. INDIA and other Opposition parties are united and stand in solidarity against Vote Chori, SIR and Delimitation, he said. SP leaders whom The Indian Express spoke to blamed the patchy coordination by the Congress. A party MP said, The Samajwadi Party did not attend the lunch by the Congress because of lack of proper coordination from the Congress side. Samajwadi Party MPs left for their constituencies on Tuesday evening after the protest against the CEC ended. Until then, there was no information about the lunch. Sources in the SP said the party leadership and the MPs were upset with the Gandhi siblings for stealing the show Tuesday. It is true that we are not happy with the poor coordination by the Congress regarding the protest at Akashvani Bhavan. It was supposed to be a joint protest by the INDIA bloc, and not by the Gandhis. The next big election in the country is in Uttar Pradesh, where the Samajwadi Party has a bigger stake than the Congress. Akhilesh Yadav raised the concerns about SIR in Uttar Pradesh more aggressively and effectively, while the Congress leadership only took symbolic steps during the SIR in UP earlier this year. But the Congress in Delhi tried to portray that only it was serious about SIR, an SP leader said. The developments are playing out against a key backdrop the UP Assembly elections early next year. In the politically significant heartland state, the SP and the Congress are allies and as the polls approach, a tussle over seat distribution has begun.

articleTitle: I&B Ministry notifies names of 13 journalists as Press Council members
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ministry of information and broadcasting, Press Council of India operating at half strength, Press Council of India, Press Council of India (PCI) staff, Press Council of India (PCI) strength, Indian express news, current affairs
description: The Indian Express reported on Wednesday that the I&B Ministry has not yet notified the names of 13 of the 28 PCI members, despite nominating them earlier this year and the council sending three reminders to the government.
body_raw: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting IB on Wednesday officially notified the names of 13 journalists as members of the Press Council of India PCI - Indias key media watchdog. The names comprise six newspaper editors and seven working journalists other than editors. The Indian Express reported on Wednesday that the IB Ministry has not yet notified the names of 13 of the 28 PCI members, despite nominating them earlier this year and the council sending three reminders to the government. The gazette notification has been long pending, with the PCI operating at half its sanctioned strength for nearly a year and without a single working journalist or newspaper editor. The PCI operates under the Press Council Act, 1978, which stipulates that the Council must consist of a chairperson and 28 members, each serving a three-year term. So far, only 14 of the 28 members have been appointed five MPs, three nominees and six from among newspaper owners and management, aside from the chairperson. Earlier in the day, the Editors Guild of India also demanded the immediate reconstitution of the 15th Press Council in conformity with the Press Council Act, 1978, including the prompt filling of all 13 seats reserved for professional journalists.

articleTitle: DDA begins process to rehabilitate 45 slum clusters housing 1 lakh people
articleFeaturedImageAlt: DDA begins process to rehabilitate slum clusters, delhi slum clusters, rehabilitate delhi slum clusters,Master Plan for Delhi, Delhi Development Authority (DDA), Indian express news, current affairs
description: The slum clusters in Badli, Shahdara, Pitampura and Tilak Nagar house the largest number of households to be considered for rehabilitation.
body_raw: The Delhi Development Authority DDA on Wednesday initiated the process of rehabilitation of more than one lakh slum dwellers, in what is seen as one of the first big movements under the Master Plan for Delhi MPD-2047. The agency floated Request for Proposals RFP for appointment of three Transaction Advisors for preparing feasibility reports for 15 projects covering 45 slum clusters across the city. The clusters comprise approximately 21,229 households spread over 135.74 acres of land. The slum clusters in Badli, Shahdara, Pitampura and Tilak Nagar house the largest number of households to be considered for rehabilitation. The move comes over three months after Union Home Minister Amit Shah chaired a meeting on slum rehabilitation in the city and directed the DDA and the Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board DUSIB to issue tenders for five slum clusters within 45 days, and to float tenders for at least five public-private partnership PPP-based rehabilitation projects every month. A DDA spokesperson said that the transaction advisors will assess rehabilitation requirements, development potential, infrastructure needs, financial viability and suitable implementation models for systematic and sustainable implementation of the projects. The government claims that there are about 675 slums in the Capital. Of these, around half are set up on land owned by various Central agencies, such as Railways, Land and Development Office LDO, and the DDA. The nodal agency for rehabilitation of these slums is DDA. The rest are located on land owned by the Delhi government, where the nodal agency is the Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board DUSIB, which comes under the Urban Development Department. The rehabilitation process has progressed at an excruciatingly slow pace over the past decade, with only two in-situ projects - Ashok Vihar and Kalkaji, together providing around 4,700 flats - completed so far, both by DDA. Under the PPP model, which the government says it will use, private developers come in to construct housing to rehabilitate slum dwellers on a part of the slum land while the remaining land is commercially developed. The underlying rationale is that the developer recovers the cost of building units for slum dwellers by making profits from the free sale component. The model was expected to work well since slums are typically located on high-value land. However, the DDA has struggled to attract private developers who cited small land parcels, difficult locations near drains and railway tracks, and frequent litigation. Recent changes to rehab framework How Delhi handles slum rehabilitation has undergone big changes over the past couple of months. Amendments were made to the citys slum policy, making slum dwellers eligible for getting a flat in place of their current home. Changes were also made in the MPD-2047. In a bid to attract participation of private developers in slum rehabilitation, developers were allowed to build taller buildings on slum land parcels and sell a higher proportion of that land for profit. Transferable Development Rights TDR were also introduced in the MPD-2047. In the free sale component, a developer may not be able to use all the development rights available to build flats, shops, or offices for profit because of the size or location of the land parcel in question, or due to height restrictions. Under the new TDR mechanism, these unused development rights can be used on another plot, or sold to another developer. TDR has been used extensively in Mumbai, particularly to accelerate slum rehabilitation and redevelopment.

articleTitle: ‘They ask me over and over’: Bengal BLOs fear tribunal questions in special drive
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengal BLOs fear tribunal questions, Bengal sir, Bengal sir special drive, SIR of electoral roll, nationwide SIR, Special Intensive Revision (SIR), Assembly elections, Assembly polls, nationwide Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, nationwide SIR of of electoral rolls, Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, SIR of of electoral rolls, Election Commission, Election Commission of India, Indian express news, current affairs
description: CEO notice says BLOs should refer to list of those deleted on grounds of being absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, hints tribunal cases not covered; BLOs wait for clarity
body_raw: An organisation representing Booth Level Officers BLOs has expressed apprehension that they may face the ire of deleted voters. Others wonder how long the latest turn in the Special Intensive Revision SIR exercise, of re-checking those voters left out, will keep them away from their day jobs. Some point out that it entails them doing an exercise done by them once already. However, the biggest question hanging over BLOs in West Bengal as they set out again is this how do they tackle questions regarding those whose cases are hanging fire in appellate tribunals? They also hope that clarity will be forthcoming in training sessions to be held for them after the Durga Puja holidays. With questions swirling, the state CEOs office put out a notice Tuesday saying that the special drive announced by the Election Commission of India ECI applies to left out eligible voters, adding that BLOs should refer to the list of ASDD Absentee, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate voters. Any person in this list may submit Form 6 online or through BLO for inclusion of hisher name in the Electoral Roll, the notice said, apart from first-time voters who have now reached 18 years of age. As reported by The Indian Express first, under fire over the scale of voter deletions, the ECI directed on September 29 that in the 20 states and Union Territories where the SIR was completed, a special drive will be held to enrol voters left out of the rolls. At a subsequent video conference with all state Chief Electoral Officers, the Deputy Election Commissioner present said pre-SIR and post-SIR rolls should be compared to draw up the list of those deleted, and identify any who may have been left out, as per officers who attended. In the final electoral roll of West Bengal published on February 28 this year, 63.66 lakh voters were deleted, nearly 1.9 lakh added, while the cases of 60.06 lakh were listed as under adjudication. Of these, while 33 lakh-odd voters were restored to the electoral roll, cases of 27 lakh were referred to tribunals, which also took up around 16 lakh applications against inclusion. Speaking to The Indian Express over the phone, Md Sahabuddin Mondol, a BLO of Barasat, North 24 Parganas, said Before the SIR, there were 1,279 voters in my booth. During the SIR, we found 120 either absent, shifted or dead. I think now there is a chance for such voters to apply again. Additionally, from his booth, 586 cases were referred to the tribunals. Of these, 86 have been deleted so far, Sahabuddin says. I am not sure whether these 86 can apply again, and I dont think those whose cases are still being heard by tribunals can apply either. But I am waiting for the training session. The ECI also said in its September 29 order that the Form 6 for enrolment of voters now will no longer require them to show linkage to the 2002 SIR. Sahabuddin says he has heard of this change, but is waiting for clear instructions. Pinki Jaiswal, a BLO at Kolkatas Narkeldanga, says of the 191 voters deleted in her booth, 100 were removed as they are dead. The rest I will re-check. Basically, we have to check the shifted and absentee voters. In my case, I had found that most of them were now in Bihar. Jaiswal adds The main problem is with the cases referred to tribunals. I have 28 in my booth who appealed, but there is no news regarding their hearings. The BLO believes they cannot be included in the exercise. Khurshid Anwar, a BLO from Srirampur in Hooghly district, says he has heard that we will have to visit and re-check the documents. He mentions that it will take time, and adds But the main problem is the tribunal cases. People are stuck there, and they ask me about it over and over. Habibur Rehman, a BLO from Deganga in South 24 Parganas, says All I am hearing is that there will be training. Only after that can I tell you anything. A BLO from Central Kolkata who did not want to be named expresses his frustration. After completing the SIR and then helping with the Assembly elections, we have now been enrolled for Census. That itself is a mammoth task, and the process will only be completed next February. Meanwhile, this special ECI drive has started. When will we do these jobs and when do we do our school duties? Earlier, an organisation representing BLOs called Votekormi and BLO Aikya Mancha wrote to the Bengal CEO seeking appropriate measures for complete security. for BLOs working in sensitive areas. where a huge number of voters have been deleted during SIR. Referring to South and North 24 Parganas, Howrah, parts of Hooghly and Kolkata, Malda, Murshidabad and Uttar Dinajpur, the letter said In these districts, a huge number of voters were deleted for no reason. They the BLOs may be the target of attacks by furious deleted voters. The BLOs themselves had no role in the mass deletion, the letter said, blaming it on the ECI system flagging logical discrepancies that had raised the question of credentials of these deleted voters. Then Chief Minister Mamata Banerjees decision to go to court led to their cases coming under adjudication and finally being referred to tribunals, the organisation wrote. The entire process was faulty and then we drew the attention of the concerned authority, but without result. Asked about the BLOs fears, a senior ECI official said, In this process, they dont have to go to every applicants house. All District Electoral Officers will organise camps where applicants can apply through Form 6. They can also apply online. Then, if an Electoral Registration Officer or District Electoral Officer thinks that in a particular case physical verification is needed, in only those, BLOs would have to go to the applicants residence. On the tribunal cases, the official said No applicant who was deleted after hearing in a tribunal or whose case is under tribunals jurisdiction can apply because the Calcutta High Court earlier said that such cases can only go to an appellate court. The ECI has no role in their cases.

articleTitle: OpenAI rolls out GPT-6 with visuals, interactive features and faster responses
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ChatGPT can now respond with more visual and interactive elements, instead of relying mainly on text.
description: GPT-6 brings a new ChatGPT experience with faster responses and interactive features, allowing users to explore information through charts, graphics, forms and other tools directly in a conversation.
body_raw: OpenAI has begun rolling out its much-awaited GPT-6 globally in ChatGPT. The company is introducing a new Intelligent UI that allows the chatbot to combine text with visuals and interactive elements. The update was initially available to Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users, while Free and Go users will start receiving it on Thursday, October 8. GPT6 in ChatGPT introduces Intelligent UI, a new capability that allows ChatGPT to answer quickly with fully interactive user interfaces that make everyday answers more visual, make learning complex topics easier, and can swiftly create a tool to solve a task right in the moment, the company said in its blog announcing the development. What is Intelligent UI? According to OpenAI, GPT-6 has been designed to move ChatGPT beyond a text-based interface. Intelligent UI allows ChatGPT to generate graphics, charts, forms, tappable buttons, and interactive experiences directly within a conversation. OpenAI said that now ChatGPT can automatically choose a format based on a question at the same time, it can offer a conventional text response when deemed necessary. For instance, a user asking about a bicycle will get an interactive diagram that breaks it down into its different parts. ChatGPT can also create tools like calculators, bill splitters, and simple games within the conversation. The company claims that the feature could also make complex topics easier to understand by allowing users to change inputs and explore how the results change. OpenAI said that it has built an intelligent UI based on a library of native, streamable components and a compiler that processes interfaces as GPT-6 generates them. As an outcome, interactive elements appear progressively instead of waiting for the entire response to be generated. The company also said that it trained GPT-6 to make decisions about the content, layout and level of interactivity required for a particular question. Reasoning delivered more quickly Another key highlight is how GPT-6 manages reasoning. OpenAI said that the model can begin answering while it continues to think or use tools, meaning it adds useful information progressively instead of waiting until its reasoning process is complete. Further, the company revealed that during an internal evaluation of high-value everyday agentic tasks, GPT-6 Extra High began responding in roughly the same amount of time as GPT-5.6 Medium while achieving a higher overall score than GPT-5.6 Extra High. The Sam Altman-led company also claims improvements in web-based research. GPT-6 Instant begins responding 44 per cent sooner on average than GPT-5.6 Instant when web search is required. According to the company, the new model is also better at determining when a search is necessary and finding information that supports its answers. On safety measures OpenAI said that GPT-6 comes with updated safety measures. The model is said to be more resistant to multi-turn attempts to bypass safeguards and has improved protections against high-risk misuse involving cyberattacks, biological threats, etc. Besides, it is also trained to better recognise its limitations and communicate when it does not have the information or tools needed to answer a question. For ChatGPT, paid plans use GPT-6 Sol, while free and Go users will get GPT-6 Luna. The latest rollout applies to the chat experience OpenAI says the models powering ChatGPT Work and Codex are not changing as part of this release. According to OpenAI, GPT-6 is part of its longer-term effort to make software adapt to users rather than forcing users to navigate fixed interfaces. The company claimed that over 1.2 billion people use ChatGPT each week.

articleTitle: What if your cooking gas came from water? Meet India’s hydrogen stove
articleFeaturedImageAlt: hydrogen stove
description: As LPG supply chains face fresh vulnerabilities, companies are experimenting with hydrogen-powered stoves — but high costs, efficiency and the lack of long-term data remain hurdles
body_raw: Vikash Kumar grew up in a house where cooking was always cumbersome-it meant either getting bundles of firewood or cow dung arranged, or running around for LPG cylinders. For the 33-year-olds household in Bihars Vaishali district, the LPG crisis in the aftermath of the West Asia conflict magnified the problem severalfold the family had to shell out Rs 8,000 per cylinder. We had to stand in a queue for hours, he says. So, I thought of a solution - let me make a one-time investment so that we dont have to stand in line for gas again and again every month. Thats when he came across hydrogen stovetops on Instagram and YouTube from a Faridabad-based, research-driven company that aims to revolutionise carbon neutrality with cutting-edge green technologies. The stovetop uses water and separates H2O into hydrogen fuel, which can then be used for cooking roti sabzi every day. The stovetop is one of several experimental products that strive to optimise hydrogen-the most abundant element in the universe. Companies hope to push hydrogen as a clean-energy replacement for fossil fuels-not only because of the ongoing climate crisis and the decarbonisation problem that electricity and batteries cant easily solve, but also, more recently, the West Asia conflict, which has caused cooking gas prices to spiral. For millions of Indians like Vikash, the technology could be significant - the country imports almost 60 of its LPG, with over 90 coming via the Strait of Hormuz. The West Asia conflict significantly impacted LPG supply - Indias monthly imports dropped from two million tonnes to less than a million, a decline of over 50. Globally, approximately 2.1 billion people still cook using biomass, coal, or kerosene, with severe health consequences, particularly for women and children. LPG, while cleaner than solid fuels, remains dependent on fossil supply chains with volatile pricing. Hydrogen cooking - where the only combustion product is water vapour - eliminates indoor air pollution and carbon emissions, provided the hydrogen source is renewable. For companies exploring this avenue, the possibilities are immense-but so are the challenges. At the World Hydrogen Summit in Rotterdam in May 2026, Indian deep-tech company Vision Mechatronics and Netherlands-based HyCooker BV signed a strategic cooperation agreement for international commercial sales of hydrogen-burning cooking stoves. The agreement positions India as the manufacturing base for hydrogen cookstoves under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat programme, with the partnership targeting industrial-scale production to bring costs down. Among those exploring the field is Prakash Chandra Ghosh, a professor in IIT Bombays Department of Energy Science and Engineering, who is collaborating with Powai-based Zest Clean Power Pvt. Ltd to take hydrogen cooking stoves to villages using indigenously developed and internationally patented technologies. Ghosh, who has a PhD in hydrogen technology from Germany and over two decades of experience, is developing hydrogen cooking systems using alkaline electrolysis, with a focus on community-scale solutions. A 25 kW solar-powered green hydrogen production unit was demonstrated at IIT Bombay during the recent West Asia crisis. We showed that it was capable of producing 2.53 kg of green hydrogen a day to prepare 200250 meals. IIT Bombays canteen relied on the system for daily meal preparation, Ghosh says. Strategically, this technology reduces dependency on imported fossil fuels and strengthens national energy security. Our research highlights that this technology eliminates indoor air pollution, reduces heat stress by lowering cooking temperatures, and advances gender equality. Users believe that while these products are somewhat pricey at the moment, the investment could be worth it. Vikash bought the domestic double-burner model from GreenVize a few months ago-and believes the investment was worth it. Its design and operation are very simple. Its not bulky and doesnt take up space. I dont have to worry about gas running out or becoming expensive, he says. How it works Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe, but on Earth, it exists almost entirely bound to other atoms - most commonly in water. It is an energy carrier, not an energy source, meaning it must be produced. When produced using renewable electricity, it is called green hydrogen, and when burned, its only by-product is water vapour. Its this that GreenVize hopes to leverage through its hydrogen cooking stove, which uses an integrated on-site generation process. Co-founder Sanjeev Kumar, a mechanical engineer by qualification with an M.Tech in design engineering, says he began looking for a sustainable alternative to standard cooking gases, and that search led him to hydrogen energy-based products. As you see nowadays, there is a huge dependency on LPG, fossil fuels, and Gulf countries, so we were looking for an alternative for a long time. Two years ago, we started with the thought that nothing needs to be imported and we shouldnt be dependent on foreign countries, Sanjeev says over a call on a sunny Monday afternoon. We wanted to build a practical hydrogen-based system so that we could easily adopt things and wouldnt need to source things from anywhere else. The mechanics are fairly straightforward. You add water to the stoves internal tank, which a built-in Proton Exchange Membrane PEM electrolyser splits into hydrogen and oxygen using electricity. Hydrogen then passes through safety and conditioning stages, including a bubbler, a buffer tank and a multi-stage flame back arrestor, before reaching the catalytic burner, where it combusts to produce a clean, smokeless flame. Electrolysis, the process at the heart of the stove, typically operates at 6286 efficiency depending on the technology used. PEM electrolysers use a polymer membrane to split water and are known for their compact design and ability to operate at varying loads, though they require high-purity water. Once the system is switched on and the required operating conditions are reached, hydrogen generation starts within 30 seconds. The only by-product of this combustion is pure water vapour, says Sanjeev. Oxygen is also released into the air, which is good for indoor air quality improvement, Sanjeev says, adding that the company also has other variations, the Hydrooxy and Alkaline electrolysers, which serve the same purpose. Sanjeev says he first conceived the idea of a company in 2024. But why hydrogen? He says it was because of its versatility. We wanted to explore how hydrogen could be converted from an emerging clean-energy concept into a usable solution for everyday energy applications. Cooking and industrial heating are two areas where LPG, PNG and other conventional fuels are still used. If hydrogen can be used as a clean fuel here too, why should it be limited to large industrial plants, laboratories or mobility applications? he asks. The device is expensive at the moment - a domestic model with a 3-litre tank costs Rs 1,05,000 for a single burner and Rs 1,50,000 for a double burner, while the commercial stove is priced at Rs 3,50,000. For an average user like Vikash, the 3-litre tank lasts about a month. GreenVize estimates this translates to approximately 3 tons of CO savings per year and eliminates the need for external hydrogen storage or LPG cylinders. The company was officially registered in January 2025. Two years and several safety trials later, GreenVize made its first sale of the stove in March 2026 - to the Indian Army. The armys stove is being used in the high altitudes of Jammu right now, says Sanjeev. They also sell hydrogen dispensers, hydrogen fuel-cell systems, biomass power plants, and pressure swing absorption PSA oxygen and nitrogen generators. Future of hydrogen cooktops Under its National Green Hydrogen Mission, India aims to produce 5 million tonnes of green hydrogen by 2030, install 10100 GW of electrolyser capacity, and create 5 lakh new green jobs. The Centre has allocated Rs. 17,490 crore until 2030 to incentivise electrolyser and green hydrogen production. GreenVize has also applied for the Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme BIG, which supports young start-ups in biotechnology innovation and research. Sanjeev believes the grant will help the company scale up as well as improve quality. We aim to integrate smart tech and AI to make a smart stove. That would mean your stove could be connected to your Wi-Fi network, controlled by your phone via an app, and even have voice integration, he says. At a workshop organised by the Bureau of Indian Standards BIS in collaboration with Standards Australia SA under the Australia-India Standards Trade Enabling Project AI-STEP in August, GreenVizes hydrogen cooktops were presented as a case study. The company is also planning to distribute the hydrogen stovetop across other countries, starting with the Maldives. For now, however, there are limitations, chief among them the high cost. Sanjeev knows that this could be a challenge but believes theres some way to go. If anything is exclusive, it tends to be expensive. To make it affordable, we need to make it non-exclusive. Once it goes into mass production, we will bring the cost down, he says. Then there are the repair and replacement costs. While the company says that it depends on individual products, theres no data on long-term use yet. Sanjeev understands he has a long way to go, especially if he wants to scale up production. The company has still not broken even yet, he says. The priority right now is to establish it as a commercially viable product first, and then scale up manufacturing. His clients agree. At their restaurant in Khliehtyrshi, a small town in Meghalayas West Jaintia Hills, Alpana Bareh and her husband, Marphalangki Chyrmang, have been using GreenVizes commercial hydrogen stove for the last few months and now swear by it. This stove is quicker than the LPG one we had before, and the safety of the valves is built into the system itself, which is a plus. We bought two commercial single-burner cooktops after the LPG crisis hit, and found it to be very cost-effective, Alpana says.

articleTitle: Death toll in Delhi building collapse rises to 4, more feared trapped
articleFeaturedImageAlt: delhi building collapse
description: Delhi building collapse in Seemapuri: Four-storey building developed cracks during Tuesday's earthquake
body_raw: A day after a four-storey building collapsed in Northeast Delhis New Seemapuri Wednesday afternoon, police officials said one more body was recovered in the wee hours of Thursday, taking the death toll to four. On Tuesday, when Delhi experienced earthquake tremors in the evening, the building had developed cracks, officials said. Rescue operations still continue at the site, with officials saying that they fear that 1-2 people might still be trapped. A Municipal Corporation of Delhi MCD official said that 75 of the debris has been cleared but it might be a couple of hours more before the area could be fully cleared The collapse took place near the Idgah Machhli Mandi area. Four fire tenders were rushed to the spot. Within minutes of the collapse, residents started pulling people out of the rubble and took them to hospitals. The building measured 225 sq ft. Some people have been rescued and sent to hospitals, but we suspect that two to three people are still trapped under the debris. They are talking. rescue operation is underway, DCP Northeast R P Meena said. In a statement, the MCD described the structure as a ground-plus-three-floor building located in a jhuggi jhopri area on about 25 square yards of DUSIB land. It said the building was around 20-25 years old and occupied. The building stood next to the mosque in the densely packed locality. The boundary wall of the mosque also collapsed in the impact, while walls of an adjoining building were damaged, the MCD added. Officials said demolition work was being carried out in the adjoining building. Three- and four-storey structures surround the mosque on three sides, leaving little open space. Much of the debris fell inside the mosque compound, said local residents. The building was owned by Anwar. His family members who stayed on the first three floors included his wife Salma, 50 son Rehman, 28, and wife Sakeena his daughters Nushrat and Ameena as well as Nushrats three-year-old son Abdaan. While Anwar, Ameena and Rehmans wife were not at home when the building collapsed, Nushrat is stuck under the debris, officials said. A tenant, also named Sakeena 35, lived on the upper floor, according to relatives.

articleTitle: ‘I settled 8 wars’: Trump renews Nobel Peace Prize bid ahead of Friday announcement
articleFeaturedImageAlt: US President Donald Trump renewed his pitch for the Nobel Peace Prize
description: Donald Trump renewed his Nobel Peace Prize pitch, claiming he settled eight wars and prevented global destruction during remarks at the Oval Office.
body_raw: US President Donald Trump renewed his pitch for the Nobel Peace Prize at the Oval Office, claiming he had settled eight wars and done stuff that nobody else has ever done. Trump made the fresh bid at the Oval Office on Wednesday afternoon, ahead of Fridays announcement of the coveted award by the Norwegian Nobel Committee. Ive done stuff that nobody else has ever done. Im not bragging, Im just telling you the facts. No president has probably ever settled any wars. I settled eight wars, Trump told reporters here. He then said that it would be a great discredit to the Nobel Committee not to honour him. They have a reputation for maybe not giving it to people like me. But, whether I get it or not, I have done far more. And I think it would be a great discredit to them. And Im not saying that out of scorn, Im saying that when you settle eight wars, and nobodys never, the US president said. He said that his peacemaking efforts were continuing and hinted that he was on course to settle another war, apparently referring to the US-Iran conflict, which has now entered its eighth month. Look, Obama got it, and he didnt do anything, says Trump Trump then moved on to criticise former US President Barack Obamas 2009 Nobel Peace Prize win, claiming Obama did not know why he had received the award. Look, Obama got it, and he didnt do anything. He still doesnt know what he got it for. He got it when he got elected, right at the beginning, and he had no idea why he got it, the US President said. He further recalled that last years Nobel laureate, Venezuelas Maria Corina Machado, handed her peace prize to him during a meeting at the Oval Office. Last time they gave it to a young lady whos a fabulous person, and she said she didnt deserve it, that I deserved it, and she gave it to me, the US President said. I was very honoured to receive it indirectly. Last time by the recipient, who said nobody in history deserves it more than President Trump, he said. POTUS then repeated that in the past year he had settled eight wars, secured the return of all hostages and used tariff threats to prevent conflicts.

articleTitle: Nana Patekar, the actor who redefined the tough cop, the psychotic villain, and Hindi cinema
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Film star Nana Patekar in film WAJOOD. Express archive photo
description: In a film industry that traditionally handed out important roles to clean-cut, chocolate-box heroes, Nana Patekar stood out in both appearance-- rough-hewn, son-of-the-Maratha-soil who could pull bombast with believability.
body_raw: Apne ko sochne ka allowed nahin hai, apne ko sirf ungli hai, ghoda kheechne ka. That single dialogue, in a 2004 film filled with snappy one-liners, cemented the image of the encounter cop in Hindi cinema. Scenery-chewing tough-talking cops had always been a Bollywood staple, with Amitabh Bachchan giving his Vijay in the 1973 Zanjeer the kind of smouldering swag we hadnt encountered before. But when Nana Patekar came swinging out in Shimit Amins 2004 Ab Tak Chappan, owning the part of a Maharashtrian cop in his own way, he became equally unforgettable. Patekar didnt have to act the part of his iconic Inspector Sadhu Agashe, based on a real-life figure he just became the man so obsessed with cleaning up crime that all semblance of balance disappeared. His other, even more iconic line that everyone remembers, belongs to another cop he played in the 1991Yashwant ek machchar saala aadmi ko hijra bana deta hai, delivered in that distinctive voice, rumbling out from the screen. Its one of those lines that became viral before virality was a thing, and it is as resonant today. In a film industry which had traditionally handed out important roles to clean-cut, chocolate-box heroes, Nana Patekar stood out in both appearance- rough-hewn, son-of-the-Maratha-soil-who-never-forgot-his-roots, as well as his ability to pull off bombast with believability. While he did lean into socialist-realist-middle-of-the-road cinema and broad comedy Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman, Natasamrat, Welcome, his most striking streak saw him both in villain and hero roles, a tough divide to straddle think Vidhu Vinod Chopras 1987 Parinda, in which Patekars psychotic crime lord Anna Seth ruled the roost, right up there with the 1991 Prahaar in which he plays the righteous armyman Major Pratap Chauhan, which he directed himself without making it a vanity project interestingly, both films had Madhuri Dixit in the lead. ALSO READ Nana Patekar Death Updates Nana Patekar will be accorded state funeral, PM Narendra Modi remembers his intensity, individuality Craggy looks and the crime landscape goes hand in hand, especially when it comes to hidebound casting choices in Bollywood his first appearance that brought him recognition was Mira Nairs 1988 Salaam Bombay, in which he plays Baba, the hard-nosed drug dealer without an ounce of empathy for the women he pimps out. And he could have got typecast in such roles, especially after Parinda, a film which gave him a maniacal laugh as his signature mannerism. But Patekar refused to get boxed in. There were a clutch of other roles that he will be remembered for, especially the 1994 Krantiveer, in which he got to play his own brand of angry young man, fighting against injustice and corruption. And then there came a time when his film appearances dwindled- in 2018, he was faced with a sexual harassment charge- but even when he remained on the periphery, his unshakeable stature as one of the most popular actors in Maharashtra, ensured that his Ganapati celebrations continued to be crowded with netas and abhinetas alike. Speaking of, Patekars reluctance to join active politics was an enduring mystery. Given his constant, almost bordering on reverence, connection with Marathi manoos, he could easily have become a mascot of parties like the Shiv Shena that spoke to Marathi asmita, or of BJPs brand of nationalism. But he stayed far away, almost as if it was an area he didnt want to have anything to do with it. One of those reality-is-stranger-than-fiction things, even more ironic because he played, with great conviction, savvy king-makers in highly-political films like Prakash Jhas 2010 Rajneeti. His being at the right place at the right time ensured he became one of the busiest actors of the era. With his powerful performances, and stylised delivery, he cemented a place in the post-Satya late 90s world, giving us a clutch of characters we could enjoy and take home with us. Patekar never tried to be anything he couldnt channel with authenticity, even when doing loud nationalistic dramas like the 1993 Tiranga. Corrosive anger and a kind of derision, which felt, often, self-directed, as well as slung out at the audience, was a quality that ran through his highly-performative roles, the ones his fans loved him for. But he could also underplay. One of my most favourite performances of his in Bollywoods only true musical, the criminally forgotten Amol Palekar-helmed Thoda Sa Roomani Ho Jaaye, in which he plays the rare romantic hero who spreads joy without being cheesy. His other hatke part was in 1996 Sanjay Leela Bhansali Khamoshi, in which he plays the deaf-mute Joseph Braganza as a husband-and-parent, to Seema Biswas and Manisha Koirala respectively. This was the film in which Patekar channelled his softer, vulnerable side, and he was quite wonderful in it no clutches of dialogue, just pure performance, the hallmark of a true actor.

articleTitle: ‘Baseless and misconceived’: Centre after Elon Musk claims ‘oligarchs’ blocking Starlink in India
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The Centre said India’s satellite communication regulatory framework is fair and non-discriminatory, rejecting Elon Musk’s claim that “certain oligarchs” were blocking Starlink’s plans.
description: The Centre said India’s satellite communication policy is fair and non-discriminatory. The statement came after Elon Musk alleged that “certain oligarchs” were blocking Starlink’s plans in the country.
body_raw: The Ministry of Communications on Thursday said Indias regulatory framework for satellite communication services is fair and non-discriminatory. This comes a day after SpaceX CEO Elon Musk alleged that certain oligarchs were blocking Starlinks plans in India. The Centre said that any suggestion of Indias regulatory framework for satellite communication services is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived. In a statement issued by the Press Information Bureau, the Ministry said that licences have been granted to three satellite communication companies and all are required to meet security conditions. Their security assessments are currently underway. Under the terms and conditions of license, every such licensee is required to demonstrate compliance with security conditions. This is aimed at ensuring that services provided meet various security requirements to ensure safety of all users and their data, the statement read. As and when this security process is completed for a licensed entity, it may proceed to the next step of seeking assignment of spectrum. At present, all the three entities are at broadly the same regulatory stage, the Ministry further said. At present, all the three entities are at broadly the same regulatory stage, the ministry said, calling claims of discrimination baseless and misconceived, a statement issued by the Press Information Bureau said. Earlier, Elon Musk had alleged on X that Starlink was being blocked to protect a monopolistic chokehold over Indian consumers. His comments came in response to a post arguing that Starlink could provide high-speed internet to underserved and remote communities. Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. You can guess who they are . This is a crime against the people of India - Elon Musk elonmusk October 7, 2026 Starlink has a licence to offer satellite internet services in India, but it is still awaiting security clearances and spectrum band allocation before it can start commercial services, Bloomberg reported. India has given satellite communication licences to three companies Starlink, Jio and OneWeb. None of them has yet switched on a full commercial service, Bloomberg said. At the India Mobile Congress on Wednesday, Starlink vice-president Lauren Dreyer said the company had built 20 gateway sites in India and developed India-specific security controls. She said Starlink was keeping Indian users data within the country and had invested in ground infrastructure to begin commercial services. Dreyer also said Starlink had been working with Indian regulators and industry stakeholders for five years. In June, she had denied reports that the approval process had been frozen, saying the company remained in talks with the government over its commercial launch.

articleTitle: Amazon layoffs: E-commerce giant cuts jobs in Stores business amid AI spending push
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Amazon has cut jobs again as the tech industry continues to see layoffs and restructuring. (Image for representation/Magnific)
description: Amazon has cut a small number of jobs in its Stores business as the company continues to reduce costs while ramping up spending on AI.
body_raw: The tech industry is witnessing another round of layoffs. E-commerce giant Amazon, on Wednesday, October 7, said it was cutting some jobs in its Stores business, which works with its main website. The announcement comes close on the heels of Amazons biggest shopping days. The fresh round of job cuts at Amazon is part of a larger round of layoffs that began last year and affected around 30,000 employees, with the latest cuts reportedly affecting fewer than 1,000 employees. Reportedly, affected employees wrote in an internal Slack channel that they received emails informing them that their roles were being eliminated. According to a report in Business Insider, the channel with 37,000 members subsequently saw queries about severance, internal job postings, and if more notifications were in the offing. The messages on Slack indicated job cuts across multiple business units, including marketplace support, customer service, and engineering roles in retail business, in both India and the UK. The layoffs suggest that Amazons cost-cutting drive is continuing to reshape its corporate workforce. This is coinciding with the companys plans to dramatically increase spending on AI. The e-commerce giant slashed around 30,000 jobs in late 2025, and it is now looking at a mammoth 220 billion investment in data centres, chips, and other AI infrastructure. Meanwhile, an Amazon spokesperson confirmed that the company cut a small number of jobs on Tuesday, mainly in its stores business. The company said it had changed the structure of the business to better support its priorities and that the affected employees would receive support during the transition. The tech sector continues to see significant job cuts. Amazon is not the only tech giant cutting jobs while increasing its focus on AI. Meta laid off around 8,000 employees in May while moving 7,000 other workers to new AI-focused initiatives. Microsoft has cut 5,300 jobs so far this year, including 4,800 in July and another 500 in September. According to Layoffs.fyi, 131,382 tech employees have been laid off across 314 companies so far in 2026. In September, companies including Uber, Oracle, Microsoft, Workday, Apple, Expedia, Thinkific and Trustly announced job cuts. Uber announced one of the largest rounds, affecting about 3,300 employees, while Workday cut 525 and Microsoft 500. The cuts reflect a mix of restructuring, cost reduction and changing business priorities, with AI increasingly influencing how major technology companies organise their workforces.

articleTitle: When Vidhu Vinod Chopra tore Nana Patekar’s kurta on set, late actor spoke about ‘bad memories’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nana Patekar and Vidhu Vinod Chopra's infamous feud during Parinda
description: Nana Patekar once recalled his 'bad memories' from Parinda. Director Vidhu Vinod Chopra admitted that he tore the late actor's kurta on set.
body_raw: Late actor Nana Patekar was known to be quite temperamental on film sets and during one of his best-known films, Parinda, he had a scuffle with director Vidhu Vinod Chopra. In an interview, Nana recalled the memories of shooting for Parinda and said that he had bad memories from the film. Vidhu, in another interview, admitted that the argument on the set got heated up to such an extent that he tore Nanas kurta after they started swearing at each other. Nana Patekar has no control over his anger Nana Patekar shared his side of the story in an interview with The Lallantop and said that he did not like Vidhu Vinod Chopra. He accepted that even back then, he could not control his anger, which resulted in a tiff between the two. I dont like Vidhu Vinod Chopra. I have no control over my anger. I am still the same. That aspect of my life hasnt changed yet. Every scene has its setting, tune, and note, there is a way to talk. Now, I dont know if you watched Parinda, I was in the character, so when the director says, Lights, camera, clap, if you aggressively say action, it starts to linger in your ears. It echoes and hurts your ears. ALSO READ Nana Patekars wife financially supported him son died at the age of 2 I never cried Nana said that since Vinod would yell out action, it would distract his performance just before the take. Let us be in our character please. What happens, when someone shouts, we forget the note that is required for the scene and unknowingly pick directors note. Just say action calmly. Let us get into our character and note. It is because of this we must have had a tiff. I have very bad memories of him Vidhu Vinod Chopra and his habits, he said. Nana then looked into the camera to address Vidhu directly. He said, Vidhu, please hear this. I want to tell you all this to your face and not behind your back. When Nana was asked about his last meeting with the director, he said, Every time I meet him, I wish it to be the last meeting. No, seriously, he added as his response made the studio audience laugh. Vidhu Vinod Chopra claimed Nana Patekar would hurl abuses Vidhu Vinod Chopra shared his side of the story during an appearance on the singing reality show Sa Re Ga Ma Pa in 2023 where he said that he was a very well-behaved young man from Kashmir but it changed after he met Nana Patekar. Vidhu said that Nana would hurl abuses at him when he directed the actor. I wondered how I would direct him at all. So, thats when I started abusing him back. I started swearing only because I had to direct Nana, he claimed. Vidhu shared that their first fight happened over food. Since the film was being made on a tight budget, all the actors were told to bring their own food, but Nana did not adhere to these directions. The first fight we had was over food, because he asked for lunch. I asked him, Ghar se nahi laaya khaana Didnt you get food from home?, he recalled. ALSO READ Nana Patekar Death Updates Last rites to be held with full state honours, relatives gather at Goa hospital Sachin Tendulkar, Alia Bhatt, Kiara Advani mourn actor Vidhu Vinod Chopra tore Nana Patekars kurta Recalling their infamous scuffle where the director tore Nana Patekars kurta, Vidhu Vinod Chopra shared, Theres a scene in the film where Nana asks if he has tears in his eyes after his wife has died. Wed been shooting all day, and it was late in the evening. Nana declared that he was too tired to continue and that he was going home. I told him, Sure, you pay for the overheads then. He started swearing at me, I swore back, and in the scuffle, I tore his kurta. The cops on set said, Were here to protect you, and youre fighting among yourselves. Vidhu said that when they filmed the scene, Nana was just wearing a vest as Vidhu had destroyed his kurta. If you watch the scene, hes wearing a vest in it because his kurta had just been torn. The tears that you see in his eyes are real because wed just fought. Later, we hugged it out and he told me, I was nervous about the scene. Thats how Parinda was made, he shared. Nana Patekar won the National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor for his work in Parinda. Nana and Vidhu never collaborated again. About Nana Patekars death Nana Patekar died on Thursday, October 8, at his residence in Goa. He was 75. His son Malhar shared with The Indian Express, Yes, the information is true. I am in Pune right now and reaching Goa. I will come up with detailed statement. He died due to natural reasons.
